name: thm:main
statement: Let $E/\Q$ be an elliptic curve and let $q$ be any prime. If $s_q(E)\in\{0,1\}$, then \[ r(E)=a(E)=s_q(E),\qquad \#\Sha(E/\Q)<\infty, \] and, with $r=r(E)$ and the preceding normalizations, \begin{equation} \frac{L^{(r)}(E,1)}{r!} =\frac{\Omega_E\Reg_E\,\#\Sha(E/\Q) \prod_{\ell\text{ finite}}c_\ell(E)} {\#E(\Q)_{\rm tors}^{2}}. \end{equation} There are no additional hypotheses on reduction, rational torsion, isogenies, complex multiplication, or residual Galois representations.
why: Goal statement; not graded.

name: Unrestricted low-corank converse
statement: For every elliptic curve $A/\Q$, every prime $q$, and $u\in\{0,1\}$, the equality $s_q(A)=u$ implies \[ a(A)=r(A)=u,\qquad \#\Sha(A/\Q)<\infty. \]
why: Cited theorems or standard normalizations (Cassels/Milne isogeny and restriction of scalars; Gross-Zagier; 006 twist density).

name: Two-primary leading term
statement: For every elliptic curve $A/\Q$ with $s_2(A)\leq1$, the quotient $Q_A$ of \eqref{eq:normalized-quotient}, with the total real period and the full-lattice regulator of \eqref{eq:height-convention}, is a positive rational number, and \[ v_2(Q_A)=v_2(\#\Sha(A/\Q)). \]
why: Cited theorems or standard normalizations (Cassels/Milne isogeny and restriction of scalars; Gross-Zagier; 006 twist density).

name: Analytic rank zero and one
statement: If an elliptic curve $A/\Q$ has $a(A)\leq1$, then $r(A)=a(A)$ and the entire group $\Sha(A/\Q)$ is finite.
why: Cited theorems or standard normalizations (Cassels/Milne isogeny and restriction of scalars; Gross-Zagier; 006 twist density).

name: Isogeny invariance
statement: Suppose $A$ and $A'$ are isogenous elliptic curves over $\Q$ of analytic rank at most one. Then \[ \frac{Q_A}{\#\Sha(A/\Q)} =\frac{Q_{A'}}{\#\Sha(A'/\Q)}. \] In particular $X(A)=X(A')$. Over a number field, the corresponding analytic-to-arithmetic BSD ratio is likewise invariant under isogeny when the Tate--Shafarevich groups are finite. It is compatible with products and restriction of scalars.
why: Cited theorems or standard normalizations (Cassels/Milne isogeny and restriction of scalars; Gross-Zagier; 006 twist density).

name: Analytic twist densities
statement: For every elliptic curve $A/\Q$, among nonzero squarefree integers $d$ ordered by $|d|$, the twists $A^d$ of analytic rank zero and one each have density $1/2$. Consequently the set of $d$ with $a(A^d)\geq2$ has density zero.
why: Cited theorems or standard normalizations (Cassels/Milne isogeny and restriction of scalars; Gross-Zagier; 006 twist density).

name: Compatible auxiliary fields
statement: Let $E/\Q$ have conductor $N$ and analytic rank $r\in\{0,1\}$. There exist coprime negative odd fundamental discriminants $D,D'<-4$ such that, for \[ K=\Q(\sqrt D),\qquad F=\Q(\sqrt{DD'}),\qquad L=\Q(\sqrt D,\sqrt{D'}), \] the following statements hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item Every prime dividing $2Np$ splits in both imaginary quadratic fields, and $\left(\frac{D}{|D'|}\right)=1$. \item The analytic ranks of $E^D,E^{D'},E^{DD'}$ are respectively $1-r,1-r,r$. \item The…
why: Auxiliary-field choice from the density theorem (the argument of [C, Sec. 2]).

name: Split Gross--Zagier normalization
statement: With the preceding conventions, $D$ odd fundamental, $(D,N)=1$, all level primes split, and $\mathcal O_K^\times=\{\pm1\}$, one has \begin{align} \frac{\sqrt{d_K}}{8\pi^2(f,f)_N}L'(f/K,1) &=2H_{\rm abs,f}(P_X),\\ L'(E/K,1)&=\frac{A_E}{\sqrt{d_K}\,c_E^2}\cdot 2H_{\rm abs}(P_K). \end{align} In the simple-zero case $P_K$ is nontorsion.
why: Cited theorems or standard normalizations (Cassels/Milne isogeny and restriction of scalars; Gross-Zagier; 006 twist density).

name: Full-index discrepancy identity
statement: Assume $L(E/K,s)$ has a simple zero under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{classical:gross-zagier}. Then \begin{equation} \frac{Q_E}{\#\Sha(E/\Q)} \frac{Q_{E^D}}{\#\Sha(E^D/\Q)} =\frac{[E(K):\Z P_K]^2} {c_E^2\prod_\ell c_\ell(E)^2\,\#\Sha(E/K)}. \end{equation} The index on the right is the full group index, including torsion. Consequently, at any prime $p$, if \[ n_P=v_p\bigl([E(K)/E(K)_{\rm tors}:\Z\overline P_K]\bigr), \qquad \tau_g=v_p(\#E(K)_{\rm tors}), \] then \begin{equation} X_p(E)+X_p(E^…
why: Restriction of scalars + Gross-Zagier; the same identity as JSW 2017 / Zhang 2014 / [B, Sec. 2], here noted to hold at every p.

name: Finite models and marked operations
statement: Consider continuous-cochain diagrams over finite local Artin rings of $p$-power characteristic, with finite free coefficient modules and compatible coefficient lifts. Assume that residual cohomology dimensions are bounded uniformly, and vanish outside a uniformly bounded range for every complex for which a bounded model is required. Then the diagrams admit bounded finite free models with derived base change. Restriction, unramified inflation, local cones, cup products, invariant maps, conjugati…
cited_or_new: new proof of standard-type homological lemma
why: Homological perturbation lemma (finite series formulas (3.2)) plus ultrafilter limits of finite matrix data; no new mathematics beyond the ultraproduct packaging, which belongs to EC2.

name: Exact local complements
statement: Let paired perfect local maps $U_v\to L_v$ and $U'_v\to L'_v$ have a specified nullhomotopy of their cup restriction. Suppose the induced morphism \[ L'_v/U'_v\longrightarrow U_v^\vee[-2] \] is an equivalence, where $\vee$ denotes derived linear dual before shifting. Then their Selmer complexes are perfect duals with shift $-3$. The localization boundaries for nested such conditions are adjoint under this duality. These assertions hold over the model rings and after localization or derived spec…
cited_or_new: new proof of standard-type homological lemma
why: Homological perturbation lemma + ultraproduct of finite matrix data; determinant-line bookkeeping as in Nekovar Selmer complexes and Mazur-Rubin finite/singular comparisons.

name: Evaluation detection
statement: Let $G_R(M)$ be an unrestricted limiting global model as in Lemma~\ref{models:finite-models}. After any field specialization, including $R\to\Frac(\F_p[[\mathbf u]])$, its degree-one cohomology injects into abstract crossed-homomorphism classes on the product of the stage absolute Galois groups. The action is obtained by taking entrywise coefficient limits before specialization. Invariants are detected in the same way. The assertion holds for a Selmer complex whenever its local conditions conta…
cited_or_new: new proof of standard-type homological lemma
why: Homological perturbation lemma + ultraproduct of finite matrix data; determinant-line bookkeeping as in Nekovar Selmer complexes and Mazur-Rubin finite/singular comparisons.

name: Line switch
statement: Over a DVR $A$ with residue field $k$, suppose local finite and transverse coordinates are split free lines in degree one, with perfect mixed pairing. The lower condition contains all $H^0$, the upper condition omits $H^2$, and the global lower and upper diagrams have exact complementary duality. Assume the finite and transverse global complexes have amplitude $[1,2]$ on the generic and residual tests. Suppose the finite complex has only a generic degree-one line. At a fiber with $\dim H^1(C_f\…
cited_or_new: new proof of standard-type homological lemma
why: Determinant change under a change of local condition (Mazur-Rubin finite/singular comparison).

name: Square switch
statement: In the preceding local diagram over a DVR $A$ with residue field $k$, let $F,S$ be split free planes. Retain all $H^0$ in the lower condition and omit $H^2$ from the upper condition. Assume amplitude $[1,2]$ for both switched global complexes on their generic and residual tests, exact self-duality of the lower and upper diagrams, and perfect mixed pairing. The pure finite and transverse planes are isotropic, with their compatible cup nullhomotopies retained. On a common plane let $e$ be unimodu…
cited_or_new: new proof of standard-type homological lemma
why: Rank-two version of the line switch.

name: Strict versus finite conditions
statement: At a split pair $w,\bar w$, let $C_*$ be strict at $w$ and full at $\bar w$, and let $C_F$ impose exactly complementary finite conditions $U_w,U_{\bar w}$. Keep all other conditions fixed with conjugate duality. Suppose these comparisons are perfect over a DVR, $U_w$ is generically a line in degree one, $C_*$ is generically acyclic, and $Y\in H^1(C_F)$ has nonzero localization. If $\operatorname{loc}_wY=a e$ in a generic basis $e$ of $U_w$, then \begin{equation} d(C_F,(Y,Y^\vee))=d(C_*,1)+2\big…
cited_or_new: new proof of standard-type homological lemma
why: Homological perturbation lemma + ultraproduct of finite matrix data; determinant-line bookkeeping as in Nekovar Selmer complexes and Mazur-Rubin finite/singular comparisons.

name: Local Haar factors
statement: For the minimal differential, write $P_\ell(1)=L_\ell(E,1)^{-1}$, $\tau_\ell=\length E(\Q_\ell)[p^\infty]$, and $\log_{\omega_E}E(\Q_p)=p^l\Z_p$. Then \begin{equation} \tau_\ell=v_p(c_\ell P_\ell(1))\quad(\ell\ne p),\qquad \tau_p-l=v_p(c_pP_p(1)). \end{equation} The connected real period $\Omega_0$ on a primitive positive Betti cycle satisfies $\Omega_E/\Omega_0=\#\pi_0(E(\R))$, a $p$-adic unit.
cited_or_new: new proof of standard-type homological lemma
why: Standard local Tamagawa/Haar identities (Bloch-Kato, Fontaine-Perrin-Riou).

name: Global Kummer volume
statement: Let $K$ be imaginary quadratic, suppose $E(K)$ has rank one and $\Sha(E/K)$ is finite, and let $C_{\rm Kum}$ impose the full integral Kummer conditions. Put $\tau_g=v_p(\#E(K)_{\rm tors})$ and $s_K=v_p(\#\Sha(E/K))$. For a nontorsion point $P$ let $n_P$ be the valuation of its index in $E(K)/E(K)_{\rm tors}$. Then \begin{equation} d(C_{\rm Kum},(P,P^\vee))=2n_P+2\tau_g-s_K. \end{equation}
cited_or_new: new proof of standard-type homological lemma
why: Global Kummer volume = Tamagawa number formalism.

name: Division from high characters
statement: Let $\mathcal O$ be one of these complete integer DVRs and let $L,B\in\mathcal O[[t,\mathbf u]]$. Suppose $L\not\equiv0\pmod{(\varpi,t)}$, where $\varpi$ is a uniformizer. If, for every sufficiently high finite $p$-power character $\theta$ of $1+t$, the specialization $B(\theta,\mathbf u)$ is divisible by $L(\theta,\mathbf u)$ after inversion of $p$, then $L$ divides $B$ integrally. The assertion applies simultaneously to finite products of such divisors and after the fixed constant extensions …
cited_or_new: new proof of standard-type homological lemma
why: Integral Weierstrass division from divisibility at infinitely many finite characters (classical Iwasawa-theory lemma).

name: Persistence of poles
statement: Suppose integral stage numerators and denominators in a genuine variable converge coefficientwise along the ultrafilter, with nonzero limiting denominator. If every stage numerator is divisible by its denominator after inversion of $p$, each zero of the limiting denominator in the open unit disk is a zero of the limiting numerator with at least the same multiplicity.
cited_or_new: new proof of standard-type homological lemma
why: Hurwitz-type persistence of zeros under coefficientwise convergence.

name: Points on a horizontal divisor
statement: For a characteristic-zero height-one divisor in a bounded $\Z_p$-power-series ring, finitely many functions nonzero on that divisor can be kept nonzero at a point whose coordinates lie in the open unit disk of a finite extension of $\Q_p$.
cited_or_new: new proof of standard-type homological lemma
why: Homological perturbation lemma + ultraproduct of finite matrix data; determinant-line bookkeeping as in Nekovar Selmer complexes and Mazur-Rubin finite/singular comparisons.

name: Auxiliary tuples
statement: For any finite list of fixed split support and test primes, the tame tuple may be chosen to have the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item Its limiting elliptic Frobenius actions have determinant one and $V(\gamma_j)-1$ invertible. Over $K$ the same holds for the companion. The weight character $\mathcal C$ used in the theta construction has nontorsion value on each $\gamma_j$, and its $\Gamma$ value is nonzero. \item The vectors of Frobenius exponents in the artificial variables at the…
why: Auxiliary-prime choice by Chebotarev to kill residual Selmer classes is the Ramakrishna / Taylor-Wiles / Kolyvagin-prime pattern; the Heisenberg-commutator addressing inside it is the candidate EC1.

name: Residual concentration
statement: After adjoining finitely many more tame variables, the separate rational and imaginary tuples satisfy \begin{equation}\tag{1} \begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{(a)}&G\otimes_RR_{(p)}\text{ is a free line in degree one};\\[2pt] \mathrm{(b)}&L_w,L'_w\not\equiv0\pmod{(p,t)} \quad\text{for both }w\mid p. \end{array} \end{equation}
why: Residual concentration: determinants nonzero mod (p,t) after adjoining tame variables; the outcome of EC1+EC2 at the residual level.

name: Scalar localization
statement: For the constant roots coefficient, global degree-two localization is injective on these residual tests. In particular a cup of two paired classes which is locally zero has a global cochain primitive.
why: Auxiliary-prime choice by Chebotarev to kill residual Selmer classes is the Ramakrishna / Taylor-Wiles / Kolyvagin-prime pattern; the Heisenberg-commutator addressing inside it is the candidate EC1.

name: Conjugate parity
statement: For an absolutely simple residual elliptic plane over $K$, each one-sided strict space above has even dimension. The same alternation statement holds on characteristic-zero localizations with unramified conditions at fixed non-$p$ places and constant inertia action.
why: Conjugate self-duality forces even-dimensional strict spaces (Flach/Nekovar alternation).

name: Necessary first-order lift test
statement: Let $x$ be an old strict class and $d$ a class in its paired opposite space. Choose a primitive $u$ of their scalar cup, $du=x\cup d$. For whole spaces of such classes, fix cochain representatives on bases, choose the primitives on pairs of basis elements, and extend these choices bilinearly. Suppose $x$ lifts in the new direction, with derivative satisfying $dx_1=-\lambda\cup x$ in the chosen character convention. Put \[ A=(M_x(\gamma)-1)^{-1}x(\gamma), \] where $M_x$ is the coefficient repres…
why: Same object as M2 lem:obstruction-necessary (cup-primitive evaluated at the limiting Frobenius); EC1 cluster.

name: Obstruction span
statement: For the residual tests above, finitely many new tame directions have necessary lift matrices whose linear span contains every $s\times(s+a)$ matrix over $k_r$ in the rational problem, every $s\times s$ matrix for a reducible constituent in the imaginary problem, and every alternating $s\times s$ matrix for an absolutely simple plane in the imaginary problem. Previously prescribed Tate actions, radical data, old character actions, and acyclicity of the new local complexes can all be retained.
why: EC1: commutator-modified Frobenius addresses whose lift matrices span all s x (s+a), s x s, or alternating s x s matrices.

name: Preservation under enlargement
statement: Property~\eqref{eq:source-1}(b) persists when further tame primes are adjoined, provided each has a nonzero Frobenius exponent in the preceding artificial variables. On setting the new variables to zero, unramified inflation identifies the old diagram, with the full new-place singular factors retained. Those factors have nonzero reduction on the residual test.
why: Auxiliary-prime choice by Chebotarev to kill residual Selmer classes is the Ramakrishna / Taylor-Wiles / Kolyvagin-prime pattern; the Heisenberg-commutator addressing inside it is the candidate EC1.

name: Directions at horizontal tests
statement: Fix finitely many characteristic-zero height-one field tests of a tuple satisfying~\eqref{eq:source-1}(b), with at least two old artificial variables. One may adjoin finitely many tame directions, locally zero on all old support, so that the new prime complexes are acyclic at all these fields and the necessary lift tests of Lemma~\ref{vertical:lift-test} retain their commutator-spanning property. The construction is compatible with further field extension and with the primitive unramified condi…
why: Auxiliary-prime choice by Chebotarev to kill residual Selmer classes is the Ramakrishna / Taylor-Wiles / Kolyvagin-prime pattern; the Heisenberg-commutator addressing inside it is the candidate EC1.

name: The relative lattice
statement: Relative pullback and Poincare duality give an integral Galois map \[ H^1(\overline{Y_1(L_0)},\Z_p)(1)\longrightarrow T. \] For \(A=1\), an integral combination \(\delta=\sum_\xi n_\xi\delta_\xi\) of finitely many symbols satisfies \(\delta(a)=1\).
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Kato Euler system made integral at all odd p; single:logarithm/height-direction/cup/spectral form candidate EC5 (tame-height route to Perrin-Riou formula).

name: Integrality and traces
statement: The classes just constructed are integral away from \(pn_2\infty\) and compatible with division traces and with corestriction as the \(p\)-part of \(M\) grows with \(A,c,d,\xi\) fixed. If \(\ell\nmid cdn_2L_0\) is a fresh prime and is adjoined to both orders and the root index, the rational norm multiplier is \begin{equation} 1-\frac{a_\ell(f)[\ell]}{\ell}+\frac{[\ell]^2}{\ell}, \end{equation} where \([\ell]\) sends the determinant root to its \(\ell\)-th power. For \(q_0^a\parallel b\), \(q_0\…
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Kato Euler system made integral at all odd p; single:logarithm/height-direction/cup/spectral form candidate EC5 (tame-height route to Perrin-Riou formula).

name: Full-level calibration
statement: In square order, before projection to the elliptic curve, the dual exponential of \eqref{single:K1} is \begin{equation} \pm M^{-2}(c^2E_P-cE_{cP})(d^2E_Q-dE_{dQ})\,\frac{dq}{q}. \end{equation} The sign is determined by cup, pairing, and orientation conventions and is common to the determinant components.
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Kato Euler system made integral at all odd p; single:logarithm/height-direction/cup/spectral form candidate EC5 (tame-height route to Perrin-Riou formula).

cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Kato Euler system made integral at all odd p; single:logarithm/height-direction/cup/spectral form candidate EC5 (tame-height route to Perrin-Riou formula).

name: Integral normalized coordinate
statement: The generic cohomology of \(G\) is a line in degree one, and \(z\) is nonzero on that line. If \(U_0\in\Frac R\) is its coordinate in the inverse determinant relative to an integral generator, then \begin{equation} U=\frac{U_0}{\Delta} \prod_{q\in S_f\setminus\{p\}}\frac{D_q}{P_q} \ \in R\setminus\{0\}. \tag{3} \end{equation}
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Kato Euler system made integral at all odd p; single:logarithm/height-direction/cup/spectral form candidate EC5 (tame-height route to Perrin-Riou formula).

name: Line comparison for a smoothed system
statement: In any of these three settings, suppose that the chosen square or rectangular system class \(z_{\rm sys}\) is generically nonzero. Then the global complex has a single generic cohomology line in degree one. At each of the indicated DVRs, \begin{equation} d(G_{\rm test},z_{\rm sys})\geq0. \tag{4} \end{equation} In the third setting, \(G_{\rm test}\) denotes the complex with the unramified old local conditions.
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Kato Euler system made integral at all odd p; single:logarithm/height-direction/cup/spectral form candidate EC5 (tame-height route to Perrin-Riou formula).

name: Exact logarithmic comparison
statement: If \(\ord_{s=1}L(E,s)=1\) and \(P\in E(\Q)\) is nontorsion, then \begin{equation} \frac{\log_\omega z_b}{(\log_\omega P)^2} =\pm d_0\frac{L'(E,1)}{\Omega_0H(P)}. \tag{5} \end{equation} The right-hand quotient is rational, and is interpreted in \(\Q_p\). The height is exactly the height \(H\) fixed in the introduction.
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Perrin-Riou's Kato-class logarithm formula, here claimed at every odd p and every reduction type via tame heights (EC5). Statement is a known conjecture (proved by BDV and others under hypotheses); the route is the candidate.

name: A nonzero height direction
statement: The horizontal sequence can be chosen to define bilinear tame heights whose rational limits satisfy \[ h_\lambda^{K_b}(P_1,P_2)=2h_\lambda^\Q(P_1,P_2) \quad(P_1,P_2\in E(\Q)),\qquad h_\lambda^\Q(P,P)\ne0. \] These heights are compatible with trace in the second argument.
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Mazur-Tate tame height via Poincare biextension, with a Heisenberg-commutator choice making h_lambda(P,P) nonzero (EC1 again).

name: Cup comparison
statement: For the sequence of Lemma~\ref{single:height-direction}, \begin{equation} Z'\log_\omega P =\pm(2-a_*)\frac{\log_\omega z_b}{\log_\omega P} h_\lambda^\Q(P,P). \tag{6} \end{equation}
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Kato Euler system made integral at all odd p; single:logarithm/height-direction/cup/spectral form candidate EC5 (tame-height route to Perrin-Riou formula).

name: Spectral-height identity
statement: For the horizontal sequence just constructed, \begin{equation} C_0\Omega_0L(f\otimes\varepsilon,1)\frac{Z'}{d_0} =\pm(2-a_*)\frac{h_\lambda^{K_b}(Q_X,Q_X)}{\delta_\phi}. \tag{7} \end{equation}
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Tame Gross-Zagier-type identity (proof via [B] Sec. 6 intersection calculation); EC5.

name: Central coordinate
statement: The element \(U\) of Proposition~\ref{single:integral} satisfies \begin{equation} X(E)=v_p(U(0))\ge0. \tag{8} \end{equation} This holds at every odd coefficient prime, for all reduction types and all residual representations of the non-CM curve.
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Assembly: X(E)=v_p(U(0))>=0.

name: Integral logarithmic primitive
statement: On the canonical ordinary locus define \[ f^{[p]}=(1-a_pV_p+p\epsilon_pV_p^2)f,\qquad F_0=\lim_{j\to\infty}d_{\rm mod}^{(p-1)p^j-1}f^{[p]},\qquad F=\prod_{q\in S^\circ}P_q(V_q)F_0. \] The limits are integral weight-zero functions. They satisfy \[ d_{\rm mod}F_0=f^{[p]},\qquad F=\sum_{\substack{n\ge1\\(n,p\prod_{q\in S^\circ}q)=1}} \frac{a_n}{n}q_{\rm Tate}^n \] at a Tate cusp with all cyclic groups of multiplicative type. If \(z\) is a Serre--Tate coordinate with \(z=1\) at the canonical lift, …
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Bertolini-Darmon-Prasanna p-adic L-function and its comparison with a Greenberg/strict determinant (Castella, CGLS, JSW pattern), extended with tame variables.

name: Finite characters and the center
statement: Let \(\theta\) be a sufficiently high finite character of \(\Gamma\), and let \(\theta_l=\theta\circ\eta_\Gamma\) have primitive conductor \(p^m\). Put \(\chi=\theta\psi_s\), and let \(X\) be the point with parameter \(\zeta_{p^m}\) in the base disk at the original primitive level. Then \begin{equation} \left(\sum_{j\bmod p^m}\theta_l(j)\zeta_{p^m}^{\,j}\right) b_s(\theta,\mathbf u) = \left(\sum_{\rho\in\Gal(H_{p^ms}/K)} \chi(\rho)G(X^\rho)\right) \prod_{q\in S^\circ}P_q(\chi(\sigma_q)). \tag{1…
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Bertolini-Darmon-Prasanna p-adic L-function and its comparison with a Greenberg/strict determinant (Castella, CGLS, JSW pattern), extended with tame variables.

name: Removal of tame conductor variables
statement: Choose each new base disk by a descending isogeny from the preceding conductor. Setting a new tame variable equal to zero multiplies each single analytic series by \begin{equation} a_r-\chi_{\rm old}(\Frob_{v_r}) -\chi_{\rm old}(\Frob_{v_r})^{-1}. \tag{13} \end{equation} The notation denotes the limit of the stage coefficients and character values. The determinant \(L_w\) is multiplied by the square of this factor up to an integral unit. These assertions hold successively for any subset of the …
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Bertolini-Darmon-Prasanna p-adic L-function and its comparison with a Greenberg/strict determinant (Castella, CGLS, JSW pattern), extended with tame variables.

name: Descent of the analytic ideals
statement: The principal ideals generated by \(b_w^+\), \(b_w^-\), \(b_w^0\), and \(B_w\) descend to \(R\). Each actual series differs from a generator over \(R\) by an integral unit.
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Bertolini-Darmon-Prasanna p-adic L-function and its comparison with a Greenberg/strict determinant (Castella, CGLS, JSW pattern), extended with tame variables.

name: Vertical analytic primitivity
statement: For each of the tuples under consideration and either \(p\)-adic place, \begin{equation} p\nmid B_w. \tag{14} \end{equation}
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: p does not divide B_w by linear independence on the ordinary locus (Chai-Hida rigidity / Hida mu=0 method); transfer N0 of Hida 2010 technique.

name: Divisibility at high finite characters
statement: For every sufficiently high finite \(\theta\), \begin{equation} B_w(\theta,\mathbf u)\in L_w(\theta,\mathbf u)A_\theta'. \tag{15} \end{equation} With the same global character variable, the two nonzero quotients for \(w\) and \(\bar w\) are associates in \(A_\theta'\).
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Characterwise divisibility from local-condition comparison (BDP explicit reciprocity).

name: The two local Kummer lines
statement: At each \(p\)-adic place and after fixing \(\theta\) as above, degree-one local cohomology splits over \(A_\theta\) into a free Kummer line and its free complementary line. The paired Kummer conditions at conjugate places are exactly orthogonal. After extension to \(A_\theta'\), the logarithm identifies the Kummer line with a free line, and its value on the weighted CM point classes is \eqref{eq:source-10}, with the factor \(c_E\) restored for \(\log_{\omega_E}\). These assertions hold for bad …
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Bertolini-Darmon-Prasanna p-adic L-function and its comparison with a Greenberg/strict determinant (Castella, CGLS, JSW pattern), extended with tame variables.

name: Inert derivative coordinates
statement: There are fresh inert good prime sequences \(\ell\), with \(\ell\to-1\) and Tate Frobenius tending to \(J=\rho_T(\tau)\) for complex conjugation \(\tau\), for which the limiting local degree-one cohomology splits into finite and transverse planes. Their mixed pairing is, up to a unit, \(\langle x,Jy\rangle\), and both planes are self-annihilating. For each fixed finite sequence of switches, there is a compatible family of descended weighted Kummer classes \(Z_I\), indexed by the subsets occurri…
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Bertolini-Darmon-Prasanna p-adic L-function and its comparison with a Greenberg/strict determinant (Castella, CGLS, JSW pattern), extended with tame variables.

name: The integral comparison quotient
statement: Using the descended analytic ideals, the fraction \[ U_w=B_w/L_w \] is represented by an integral series, and \(p\nmid U_w\). Removing any newly added tame variables specializes it to the old quotient times an integral unit. This includes removal of all tame variables, leaving the genuine anticyclotomic line.
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Bertolini-Darmon-Prasanna p-adic L-function and its comparison with a Greenberg/strict determinant (Castella, CGLS, JSW pattern), extended with tame variables.

name: Auxiliary tests
statement: One may choose two sets of fixed finite theta data with the following properties. Their extra rational good primes requiring nonspherical target controls are split completely in $L$, are different from $p$, and the two sets are disjoint. Outside these sets and the elliptic bad primes, the target tests are spherical. At an unramified-twist Steinberg place the source vector is Iwahori invariant and the target test has line-stabilizer parahoric level. At an additive place fixed nonspherical tests …
why: Kudla-Rallis theta family on U(3,1) with bounded position-cut moments; close variant of [C] Sections 4-5 and of CLW GU(3,1) Eisenstein congruences.

name: Choice of a point
statement: Let $\mathfrak p$ be a horizontal divisor on which $b_w^0$ vanishes. Fix a strict side for each of the two elliptic representations, and suppose both corresponding primitive strict cohomology groups vanish generically on $\mathfrak p$. There is an interior point $z_0=(t_0,\mathbf u_0)$ on this divisor, over a fixed finite extension $k/\Q_p$, retaining their vanishing and the following properties. The local $H^0,H^2$ vanishings at $p$ and the acyclicity of the moving local complexes hold for bot…
why: Kudla-Rallis theta family on U(3,1) with bounded position-cut moments; close variant of [C] Sections 4-5 and of CLW GU(3,1) Eisenstein congruences.

name: Canonical levels
statement: At each finite depth $s$, the ordinary branch of the normalization in level $J(s)$ on which the rank-three flag is multiplicative adds only finite etale character-group flags and frames. At a toroidal cusp it does not ramify the center Fourier parameter. Every component of this branch meets a compatible ordinary cusp, and reduction of all Fourier--Jacobi expansions detects divisibility of an integral section by the uniformizer. These assertions hold after every finite coefficient extension, wit…
why: Kudla-Rallis theta family on U(3,1) with bounded position-cut moments; close variant of [C] Sections 4-5 and of CLW GU(3,1) Eisenstein congruences.

name: The two $p$-operators
statement: For every $i,m$, the unnormalized right-coset operators $U_j=[J(s_i)\operatorname{diag}(1_j,p^{-1}1_{4-j})J(s_i)]$, $j=2,3$, act on \eqref{eq:source-18} by $p^2$. In weight $(m,m,1;-1)$ the integral ordinary normalization is $p^{-2}U_j$, so both normalized comparison values are $1$.
why: Kudla-Rallis theta family on U(3,1) with bounded position-cut moments; close variant of [C] Sections 4-5 and of CLW GU(3,1) Eisenstein congruences.

name: Bounded cuts of unary moments
statement: Fix the integral position lattices, additive characters, Igusa frames, and the finite tests away from $p$ used for a finite product of unary theta functions. Moving tame tests may have bounded group-ring coefficients and additive Fourier normalizations that are $p$-units. At $p$ let $c$ be any locally constant function on the position lattices, with coefficients in any finite extension or finite group algebra and $\|c\|\leq1$. Its conductor is unrestricted. For every finite polynomial combinati…
why: Kudla-Rallis theta family on U(3,1) with bounded position-cut moments; close variant of [C] Sections 4-5 and of CLW GU(3,1) Eisenstein congruences.

name: Integral theta sections
statement: There is a fixed integer $c\geq0$ such that $p^c\Theta_{i,m}$ is an integral ordinary section on the canonical branch, coefficientwise in $\mathcal O[G_i]$. The same $c$ works for all increasing depths $s_i$, all sufficiently large positive weights on the fixed branch, all the fixed test variants, and bounded locally constant cuts in the head of \eqref{eq:source-18} that retain the source determinant equivariance on a fixed compact. The two trailing columns keep their full integral lattice test…
why: Kudla-Rallis theta family on U(3,1) with bounded position-cut moments; close variant of [C] Sections 4-5 and of CLW GU(3,1) Eisenstein congruences.

name: CM translations and bounded Fourier projection
statement: Choose connected and etale Tate coordinates $e_p,f_p$ at a split ordinary CM point. The translation $n(j/p^b)$ gives the lattice \[ \Z_pe_p+\Z_p\bigl(f_p+(j/p^b)e_p\bigr). \] It corresponds, up to a fixed sign and a unit root-basis choice, to the Serre--Tate parameter $\zeta_{p^b}^{cj}$ with $c\in\Z_p^\times$, and preserves the connected differential frame integrally. Suppose $F(z)=\int_{\Z_p}z^y\,d\mu(y)$ for a bounded measure $\mu$, and $\chi$ has conductor dividing $p^b$ on units. For every …
why: Kudla-Rallis theta family on U(3,1) with bounded position-cut moments; close variant of [C] Sections 4-5 and of CLW GU(3,1) Eisenstein congruences.

name: The toric weight limits
statement: At every fixed stage $i$, the periods $P_{j,i}(m)$ have coefficientwise limits as positive $m$ tends to zero on the chosen $p$-adic branch and tends to infinity ordinarily. The limits, as group polynomials, have uniformly bounded coefficients as $i$ varies. Up to a fixed nonzero scalar and group-like units, the limit of $P_{0,i}(m)$ is the stage image of the undepleted series $b_w^0$. Consequently, when $b_w^0(z_0)=0$, weights may be chosen at each stage with arbitrary prescribed additional pre…
why: Kudla-Rallis theta family on U(3,1) with bounded position-cut moments; close variant of [C] Sections 4-5 and of CLW GU(3,1) Eisenstein congruences.

name: Vanishing of all constant terms
statement: Assume $b_w^0(z_0)=0$, and choose the auxiliary tests and local parameters of Lemma~\ref{theta:test-point}. After the fixed clearing of Proposition~\ref{theta:integral-family}, weights $m_i$ may be chosen so that all constant Fourier--Jacobi coefficients of $\Theta_{i,m_i}$ at $z_0$ tend uniformly to zero. The weights tend to zero on the fixed $p$-adic branch and to infinity ordinarily. At each fixed stage they can satisfy arbitrarily strong additional weight-approximation requirements. The ass…
why: Kudla-Rallis theta family on U(3,1) with bounded position-cut moments; close variant of [C] Sections 4-5 and of CLW GU(3,1) Eisenstein congruences.

name: Theta implication
statement: Let $\mathfrak p$ be a horizontal height-one prime of the deformation ring, with the auxiliary tuple conditions of Section~\ref{sec:theta}. If $b_w^0\in\mathfrak p$, then, over $\Frac(R/\mathfrak p)$, at least one of \[ H^1_{\mathrm{prim},a}(K,V\chi),\qquad H^1_{\mathrm{prim},a}(K,V'\chi) \] is nonzero. Here $a$ is one fixed side determined by the reciprocity convention of Section~\ref{sec:theta}. Replacing $w$ by $\bar w$ replaces $a$ by its conjugate. Both alternatives use the scalar characte…
why: Theta implication: vanishing of the undepleted CM series on a horizontal divisor forces a one-sided strict jump. Close variant of [C]'s extraction at the augmentation, extended to nontrivial test characters and growing p-level.

name: Content with the local controls
statement: There are controlled theta sections at $z_0$, of weights $m_i$ as above and depths $s_i$, whose constant terms tend uniformly to zero and whose ordinary positive Fourier--Jacobi content has valuation bounded above by a constant independent of $i$.
why: Ribet-Wiles lattice/GMA extraction; variant of [C] Sections 7-9 at growing p-level.

name: Uniform cusp congruence
statement: After one fixed reduction of precision, the sections in Lemma~\ref{extraction:content} give finite integral operator orders $\mathbb T_i^0$ on classical cusp spaces and maps \[ \lambda_i^0:\mathbb T_i^0\longrightarrow \mathcal O_k/(p^{M_i}),\qquad M_i\longrightarrow\infty. \] The maps have the tested theta values on the split good and controlled operators. Both normalized $p$-operators have value one. No upper bound on $s_i$ is required.
why: Ribet-Wiles lattice/GMA extraction; variant of [C] Sections 7-9 at growing p-level.

name: Binary separation at an inertia test
statement: On an actual system with $\Delta_v\ne0$, the generalized $1$-primary projection $P_v^{\mathrm{bin}}$ of $\rho_\pi(\iota_v)$ is defined and satisfies \[ (\rho_\pi(\iota)-1)P_v^{\mathrm{bin}}=0 \qquad(\iota\in I_v). \] Together with the Frobenius-separated projections, these identities give an exponent $C_0$ independent of stage and depth for which \[ \Delta^{C_0}\ker(\mathbb T_i^0\longrightarrow\mathbb T_i)=0, \] where $\mathbb T_i$ is the image order in characteristic-zero eigensystems.
why: Ribet-Wiles lattice/GMA extraction; variant of [C] Sections 7-9 at growing p-level.

name: The cyclotomic corner
statement: The corner modules satisfy $D_{xy}=D_{xf}D_{fy}$.
why: Ribet-Wiles lattice/GMA extraction; variant of [C] Sections 7-9 at growing p-level.

name: Exclusion of the last stable line at arbitrary depth
statement: The image of $D_{fy}$ is nonzero in every characteristic-zero field evaluation of the ambient ring. Consequently $\operatorname{Fitt}_{0,\mathscr T}(D_{fy})=0$.
why: Ribet-Wiles lattice/GMA extraction; variant of [C] Sections 7-9 at growing p-level.

name: unit:quotient-regularity
statement: At a horizontal height-one prime the primitive one-sided complexes are perfect of amplitude $[1,2]$ and Euler characteristic zero. If $M_{a,w}$ is the determinant of their differential, then \[ L_{0,w}=D_0M_{0,w},\qquad L_{1,w}=D_1M_{1,w} \] up to units in the testing DVR. Here $L_{0,w}=L_w$, $L_{1,w}=L'_w$, and $D_a$ is the product of the singular Euler determinants at the fixed non-$p$ places. Every irreducible divisor of either $U_w$ is horizontal and has nonzero reduction modulo $(p,t)$.
why: Candidate EC4. Codimension facts are standard determinantal algebra; the device of adding tame directions to push simultaneous-jump loci to codimension two is the new element.

name: Equality of the two quotient ideals
statement: For every auxiliary tuple satisfying the preceding requirements, \begin{equation} (U_w)=(U_{\bar w}) \tag{17} \end{equation} in $R$.
why: Candidate EC4. Codimension facts are standard determinantal algebra; the device of adding tame directions to push simultaneous-jump loci to codimension two is the new element.

name: Augmented alternating matrices
statement: Let $k$ have characteristic zero and let $s\geq1$. On \[ W_s=\operatorname{Alt}_s(k)\oplus\operatorname{Mat}_{s,2}(k) \] the locus where $[A\mid B]$ has rank less than $s$ has codimension at least two. If $s_0,s_1$ are positive even integers, the locus \[ \{(A_0,A_1):\det A_0=\det A_1=0\} \subseteq\operatorname{Alt}_{s_0}(k)\oplus \operatorname{Alt}_{s_1}(k) \] also has codimension at least two.
why: Codimension of rank-deficient loci of [A|B] with A alternating; elementary determinantal algebra.

name: First-order tests and formal codimension
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a regular local ring with $\operatorname{char}k=0$. Let $D:A^s\to A^r$, $r\geq s\geq1$, have entries in $\mathfrak m$, and let $D_1$ be its linear part on the tangent space $T_A=\Hom_k(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2,k)$. Suppose there is a linear injection $\iota:W_s\to T_A$ such that, over every extension field $k'/k$, \[ \ker D_1(\iota(A_0,B)) \subseteq\ker[A_0\mid B]^{\mathsf t}. \] Then the maximal-minor ideal $I_s(D)$ has height at least two. There is also a simultane…
why: Initial-ideal/tangent-cone height bound for maximal-minor ideals; standard commutative algebra.

name: unit:simultaneous-jumps
statement: The new tame directions can be chosen so that, for every such $\mathfrak q$, the following two loci have codimension at least two in $\Spec S_{(\mathfrak q,\mathbf y)}$: \begin{enumerate} \item the locus where both one-sided primitive complexes for a single representation jump; \item for each allocation of sides, the locus where one one-sided primitive complex for each of $V_0,V_1$ jumps. \end{enumerate} The old complexes are recovered on setting $\mathbf y=0$, and the determinant and analytic …
why: EC4: choose new tame directions so that simultaneous one-sided jump loci have codimension >= 2; combined with EC1 commutator spanning.

name: unit:unit-comparison
statement: The two quotients $U_w$ are units. Their specialization with all artificial variables zero gives an integral unit comparison between the analytic series and strict determinant on the true anticyclotomic line.
why: Unit conclusion: a height-one divisor of U cannot sit inside a codimension-two locus. The final step of EC4.

name: center:exact-factor
statement: Let $C_w^{s=1}(0)$ be the actual central strict/full complex after all artificial variables have been removed. Its differential determinant satisfies \begin{equation} \begin{split} -v_p(L_w^{s=1}(0)) &=d(C_w^{s=1}(0),1)\\ &=2n_P+2\tau_g-s_K -2\bigl(v_p(\log_{\omega_E}P_K)-l+\tau_p\bigr) -2\sum_{q\in S^\circ}\tau_q . \end{split} \tag{22} \end{equation} Consequently \begin{equation} 2(n_P+\tau_g)=s_K+2v_p(c_E)+2\sum_q v_p(c_q(E)), \tag{23} \end{equation} where the last sum ranges over all rationa…
why: Determinant-volume computation in the style of Bloch-Kato/Fontaine-Perrin-Riou; CM rank-zero is Burungale-Flach.

name: center:pair-discrepancy
statement: For every elliptic curve of analytic rank zero or one, including CM curves, and for the imaginary twist in Lemma~\ref{classical:auxiliary-fields}, \begin{equation} X(E)+X(E^D)=0. \tag{24} \end{equation}
why: Substitution of (23) into (2.12).

name: center:cm-zero
statement: If $E/\Q$ has complex multiplication and $L(E,1)\ne0$, the exact BSD formula holds for $E$ with the normalizations of Section~\ref{sec:intro}.
why: Burungale-Flach Thm 1.1/Cor 1-2; isogeny to maximal order is standard.

name: center:odd-valuations
statement: For every elliptic curve $E/\Q$ of analytic rank zero or one and every odd prime $p$, \[ v_p(Q_E)=v_p(\#\Sha(E/\Q)). \]
why: Sandwich X>=0 for E and E^D plus X(E)+X(E^D)=0. Note: proved for EVERY E of analytic rank <=1 and every odd p.

name: The unrestricted low-corank Selmer converse
statement: For every elliptic curve $A_0/\Q$, every prime $p$, and $r\in\{0,1\}$, \[ s_p(A_0)=r \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a(A_0)=\rank_{\Z}A_0(\Q)=r, \qquad \#\Sha(A_0/\Q)<\infty. \] There is no restriction on reduction type, complex multiplication, the residual representation, rational torsion, or rational isogenies.
why: Goal statement.

name: Established converse at $2$
statement: If $E/\Q$ is any elliptic curve and $\corank_{\Z_2}\Sel_{2^\infty}(E/\Q)=r\in\{0,1\}$, then \[ \ord_{s=1}L(E,s)=\rank E(\Q)=r, \qquad \Sha(E/\Q)\text{ is finite}. \]
why: Cited from release sibling 006 (model-produced, unreviewed).

name: Established analytic twist-density theorem
statement: For any elliptic curve $E/\Q$, among nonzero squarefree integers $d$ ordered by $|d|$, the quadratic twists $E^{(d)}$ of analytic rank zero and one each have density $1/2$. In particular the exceptional set of twists of analytic rank at least two has density zero.
why: Cited from 006.

name: lem:auxiliary-fields
statement: There are coprime negative odd fundamental discriminants $D,D'$ such that every prime dividing $2Np$ splits in both quadratic fields, \[ \left(\frac{D}{|D'|}\right)=1, \] and each of $A_0^D,A_0^{D'},A_0^{DD'}$ has the smallest analytic rank permitted by its sign. They may also be chosen so that \[ K=\Q(\sqrt D),\qquad F=\Q(\sqrt{DD'}),\qquad L=\Q(\sqrt D,\sqrt{D'}) \] satisfy the following properties: $L/F$ is CM and unramified at every finite prime, $L$ has only the roots of unity $\{\pm1\}$, …
why: Standard auxiliary-field selection (cf. BFH, Murty-Murty, Skinner), here via density theorem.

name: prop:arithmetic-reduction
statement: With these choices, \[ \dim H^1_f(K,V)=1, \qquad \dim H^1_f(K,V^{DD'})=1. \] The second line localizes nontrivially at both places of $K$ over $p$. Let $y\in A_0(K)$ be the norm of the conductor-one Heegner point under a modular parametrization taking the cusp $\infty$ to zero. If $y$ is non-torsion, Theorem~\ref{thm:main} follows.
why: Standard reduction of the p-converse to Heegner non-torsion.

name: lem:base-green
statement: If the compact Selmer line of $W/K$ has nonzero localization, then $H^1_{\Gr}(K,W)=H^1_{\overline{\Gr}}(K,W)=0$. The only remaining possibility is the following \emph{strict case} in the $V$ summand: $r=1$, and the compact Selmer space is generated by a class $a$ such that $a^c=a$ and every localization of $a$ is zero. In that case \begin{equation} H^1_{\Gr}(K,V)=\langle a,h\rangle, \qquad H^1_{\overline{\Gr}}(K,V)=\langle a,h^c\rangle, \end{equation} where $h$ has nonzero localization at $v$ a…
why: Standard Poitou-Tate computation; the "strict case" is the zero-localization case that Skinner 2020 excluded by hypothesis.

name: prop:tame-primes
statement: There are rational primes $q_i\notin S$, split completely in $L$, distinguished places $\mathfrak q_i$ of $K$ above them, cyclic $p$-quotients $\Delta_i$ of the ring class group of conductor $q_i$, and surjections \[ \ell_i:G_K\longrightarrow\Delta_i\simeq\Z/p^{n_i}\Z, \qquad n_i\longrightarrow\infty, \] with the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item $\ell_i$ is unramified outside the pair above $q_i$, its restriction to inertia at $\mathfrak q_i$ is surjective…
why: Chebotarev selection of auxiliary primes with prescribed Frobenius (Kolyvagin/Taylor-Wiles/Ramakrishna pattern) plus radical conditions; part of EC2.

name: def:admissible
statement: An \emph{admissible cochain} with coefficients in $M_b^{\eta}$ is a function on sequences of Galois elements which is the coefficientwise ultralimit of continuous finite-stage cochains, in the fixed basis of $V\otimes R_b$, with one denominator $p^C$ independent of $i$. Finite-stage cochain identities are required modulo precisions $A_i\longrightarrow\infty$ along $\cU$, with $A_i\le n_i-c_b$. Equivalently, the limiting identity holds on \emph{every} sequence of arguments. Cohomology is the coh…
why: Ultralimit cochains over varying moving primes: close variant of Sweeting ultrapatching / Loeffler-Zerbes ultra-Kolyvagin systems; candidate EC2.

name: lem:admissible-specialization
statement: For constant coefficients $V$, admissible $H^1$ is precisely $H^1(G_{K,S},V)$, and likewise over $L$. For $\Q_p(1)$ the same assertion holds when unramifiedness at the moving primes is imposed. The fixed local conditions specialize to the usual rational local conditions. Coefficient reduction and multiplication by $t$ give short exact sequences of admissible cochain complexes \begin{equation} 0\longrightarrow C^\bullet(M_{b-1}^{\eta}) \xrightarrow{\ t\ } C^\bullet(M_b^{\eta}) \longrightarrow C^…
why: Compactness/finiteness argument; routine once EC2 is set up.

name: lem:obstruction-necessary
statement: The expression $H_\gamma$ is independent of the primitive and bilinear. If a nonzero class $x\in H^1_{\Gr}(K,V\otimes k)$ is the specialization of an admissible class in $\GrH(K,M_2^{\eta})$, then \begin{equation} H_\gamma(x,d)=0 \quad\text{for every }d\in H^1_{\overline{\Gr}}(K,V\otimes k). \end{equation} The same necessary condition holds for either $\eta$.
why: Tame-pairing evaluation of a cup-product primitive at Frobenius: a derived/tame height pairing (Mazur-Tate, Bertolini-Darmon) used as a deformation obstruction.

name: lem:nonzero-obstruction
statement: The element $\gamma$ in \cref{prop:tame-primes} can be chosen so that, in the bases of \cref{eq:base-green-bases}, the obstruction matrix is \begin{equation} \begin{pmatrix}0&\kappa\\-\kappa&0\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \kappa\in\Q_p^\times. \end{equation} Thus no nonzero base Greenberg class lifts to order two.
why: Candidate EC1 (Heisenberg-commutator Frobenius addressing).

name: prop:green-length
statement: For the primes of \cref{prop:tame-primes}, chosen in the strict case as in \cref{lem:nonzero-obstruction}, every fixed $b\ge1$, and either $\eta=1$ or $\eta=-1$, one has \begin{equation} \length_{R_b}\GrH(L,V\otimes\psi^{\eta}) \begin{cases} =0,&\text{outside the strict case},\\ \le2,&\text{in the strict case}. \end{cases} \end{equation} In the strict case this module is killed by $t$ and is the image of its two-dimensional base space under multiplication by $t^{b-1}$. Put \begin{equation} b_*=…
why: Dévissage along t-filtration; the new input is EC1.

name: lem:uniform-local-log
statement: Fix an integer $d_0\ge0$. There is a constant $c$ such that, for every finite unramified extension $E/\Q_p$ with $v_p([E:\Q_p])\le d_0$, \begin{equation} \log_{A_0,p}(A_0(E))\subseteq p^{-c}\cO_E. \end{equation} If $P\in A_0(E)$ and the Kummer class of $p^C P$ vanishes in $H^1(E,A_0[p^n])$, where $C,n\ge0$ are integers, then \[ v_p(\log_{A_0,p}P)\ge n-C-c. \]
why: Formal-group logarithm bounds.

name: prop:heegner-log
statement: At the distinguished place over $p$, and for either sign, \begin{equation} \sum_{g\in\mathcal G_i}(1+t)^{\pm\ell_i(g)} \log_{A_0,p}(y_i^g) \longrightarrow0\pmod {t^{b_*}}. \end{equation} More precisely, every coefficient of degree less than $b_*$ has valuation tending to $+\infty$ along $\cU$. The coefficients through any other fixed degree have a common lower valuation bound. These assertions hold in a common $p$-adic algebraic closure, with its fixed extension of the valuation.
why: Weighted ring-class Heegner logarithm sums (Bertolini-Darmon / Kolyvagin derivative style).

name: lem:split-u-operators
statement: Every test \eqref{eq:p-pivot-test} satisfies $U_2\Phi_p=p^2\Phi_p$ and $U_3\Phi_p=p^2\Phi_p$. Thus both operators $p^{-2}U_j$ have value $1$ on the theta form of weight \eqref{eq:theta-weight}.
why: Hecke operator computation.

name: lem:theta-eigenparameters
statement: At a split spherical place the standard parameter of the theta form, in unitary normalization, is \begin{equation} (\pi\otimes\eta)\ \oplus\ |\cdot|^{-1/2} \ \oplus\ |\cdot|^{1/2}. \end{equation} Here $\pi\otimes\eta$ means tensoring the standard two-dimensional parameter by the determinant-twist character.
why: Standard theta-correspondence local parameter.

name: prop:theta-family
statement: For the characters \eqref{eq:theta-character} and every sufficiently large positive $m$ on the prescribed branch, the theta construction gives holomorphic algebraic forms $\Theta_{i,m}$ of weight \eqref{eq:theta-weight}. In the canonical ordinary monomial-dual lattice their coefficients have a common bounded denominator, coefficientwise in the tame group algebra and in every fixed truncated substitution $R_b$. They have spherical parameters \eqref{eq:theta-eigenparameters}, and at both distingu…
why: Holomorphic theta lift to GU(3,1); close neighbour Castella-Liu-Wan Klingen Eisenstein congruences on GU(3,1).

name: conv:scaled-support
statement: The position-moment functional is defined first in fixed Igusa differential frames. Fixed powers of algebraic unit scales arising from conversion to another CM frame are restored afterwards. An equivalent formulation puts the polynomial norm on the actual scaled compact support. We do not identify that support with $\Z_p$ merely because the scale is an algebraic $p$-unit: a unit in a coefficient extension need not belong to $\Z_p$. The restored unit powers are analytic on a sufficiently narrow …
why: Convention.

name: Uniform unary moments
statement: Fix the integral position supports, the locally constant tests at $p$, and their levels. At a fixed ordinary CM test object, the period-normalized unary jets, in the frames of Convention~\ref{conv:scaled-support}, are the moments of a bounded measure on the product of their integral position lattices. Its norm is bounded in terms of the coefficients of the fixed tests and their $p$-levels. The bound is independent of the moment degrees and of the moving tame level $q_i$. Cutting a position meas…
why: Bounded-measure moments of unary theta series; Katz/Hida p-adic measure technique.

name: lem:mixed-expansions
statement: The mixed Fourier--Jacobi expansions of \eqref{eq:upper-theta-integral}, in algebraic ordinary differential frames and in the monomial-dual lattice, have a common bounded denominator. The bound is independent of $m$, $i$, and the tame character, and is coefficientwise in the tame group ring. The same assertion holds after substitution into any fixed $R_b$.
why: Fourier-Jacobi expansion bookkeeping.

name: prop:constant-term-small
statement: Assume that the conductor-one Heegner point $y$ is torsion. The positive weights $m_i$ in Proposition~\ref{prop:theta-family} can be chosen with $m_i\to+\infty$ and $m_i\to0$ on the prescribed $p$-adic branch so that every constant Fourier--Jacobi coefficient of the upper theta form tends coefficientwise to zero modulo $t^{b_*}$. The assertion holds in bounded algebraic ordinary differential bases, uniformly over all boundary representatives and all polynomial components. The weights may be req…
why: Square identity linking constant terms to toric periods and BDP-type Heegner logarithm (BDP 2013).

name: Cleared period comparison
statement: There are group-ring polynomial factors $A_i(m),B_i(m)$ with uniformly bounded coefficients such that \begin{equation} A_i(m)S_i(m)^2 =B_i(m)P_{0,i}(m)^2P_{1,i}(m)^2. \end{equation} For each $i$, after taking $m$ sufficiently close to zero on its branch, $A_i(m)$ has nonzero augmentation whose valuation is bounded above by a constant independent of $i$. The required neighborhood of zero may depend on $i$. The identity holds in the full characteristic-zero tame group algebra, including at zeros …
why: Toric-period square identity (Waldspurger, BDP); variant.

name: lem:one-index-unfolding
statement: There are finite tests satisfying the $p$- and $q_i$-requirements of Section~\ref{sec:theta} for which the coefficient \eqref{eq:primitive-monomial}, at index $(e_1,e_1)$, unfolds into the product of a fixed row-one Heisenberg theta function and \begin{equation} \int_{[T]}\varphi(s)\eta^{-1}(s) \vartheta_{1,d_1}(sb_1)\vartheta_{2,d_2}(sb_2)\,ds. \end{equation} Here $b_1,b_2\in U(1)(\A_F)$ translate the binary lines, and known splitting-character factors in $b_j$ have been removed. At $q_i$ the …
why: Rallis-type unfolding.

name: lem:simultaneous-unary-nonvanishing
statement: The fixed finite-order parts of $\xi_1,\xi_2$ can be chosen, preserving \eqref{eq:unary-character-product}, so that suitable permitted local tests give $T_j(d_{j0})\ne0$ at positive classical cut weights $d_{10},d_{20}$. The weights can be chosen so that $d_{10}+d_{20}+1$ is divisible by every prescribed torsion order and a prescribed sufficiently large fixed power of $p$.
why: Uses Burungale-He-Tian-Ye 2026.

name: lem:bounded-uncontrolled-content
statement: Before imposing the additional fixed-place controls, there are positive $d_{1i},d_{2i}$, with $m_i=d_{1i}+d_{2i}+1$ tending to zero $p$-adically and to infinity archimedeanly, for which the theta forms have a nonconstant Fourier--Jacobi coefficient of valuation bounded above at augmentation. The choices can simultaneously satisfy the constant-term precision of Proposition~\ref{prop:constant-term-small}.
why: Bounded-divisibility Fourier-Jacobi coefficient; standard requirement in Ribet/SU method.

name: lem:fixed-place-spanning
statement: At each such fixed split place, the tests just prescribed and their translates span the tests used in Lemma~\ref{lem:bounded-uncontrolled-content} in theta coinvariants, after inverting a Laurent polynomial nonzero at weight zero. For weights tending to zero, this spanning uses finitely many translates and a common bounded denominator. All replacements can be made independently while leaving the $p$- and $q_i$-tests unchanged.
why: Local representation theory.

name: The combined theta output
statement: Fix the truncation $b_*$ selected in Section~\ref{sec:tame}. There exist positive integers $m_i\to\infty$, tending $p$-adically to zero on the prescribed torsion branch, and theta forms $\Theta_i$ of weight $(m_i,m_i,1;-1)$ with the following simultaneous properties. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item Their ordinary monomial-dual lattices have a uniform denominator bound, coefficientwise in the full tame group algebra and after every fixed truncated substitution used in the argum…
why: Assembly of SU-style congruence input with tame truncation b_*.

name: Canonical ordinary level
statement: Over the ordinary formal completion, the locus on which the rank-three flag equals the multiplicative subgroup is an open and closed branch of $Y^{\mathrm{tor}}$. Its residual flag and frame data are finite etale data on the Cartier-dual character group. On a toroidal cusp chart this branch adds finite etale covers of the abelian extension-data scheme and does not ramify the center Fourier variable.
why: Lan / Katz Serre-Tate.

name: Integral operations on the coefficient lattice
statement: The functor $\mathcal D_d$ is finite locally free and commutes with base change. Integral changes of Hodge frame preserve its lattice. If a map on $\mathcal H$ is diagonal with entries $c_1,c_2,c_3$, its action on the basis dual to the minor monomials has entries \[ (c_1c_2)^{a_{12}}(c_1c_3)^{a_{13}} (c_2c_3)^{a_{23}}, \qquad a_{12}+a_{13}+a_{23}=d. \] A filtration of $\mathcal H$ by subbundles with constant locally free graded pieces induces such a filtration on $\mathcal D_d(\mathcal H)$.
why: Integral automorphic vector-bundle lattice.

name: Cusp base change on the canonical branch
statement: An ordinary section modulo $p^M$ on the canonical branch whose constant terms vanish, extended by zero on the other branches, is a section of $\mathcal M_\lambda/p^M$ over the ordinary open. The assertion remains true with coefficients in $\cO[t]/(p^M,t^b)$ and after finite extension of coefficients.
why: Hida-theoretic base change.

name: Integral trace calculation
statement: The operators in \cref{eq:ordinary-normalization} preserve the dual-Fock differential lattice on the canonical ordinary branch and its reductions modulo every power of $p$. After the Hasse shift, both comparison eigenvalues are $1$ modulo the prescribed precision.
why: Ordinary projector computation.

name: Uniform cancellation in a truncated ring
statement: Let $K'/k$ be a finite extension, and let $a(t)\in\mathcal O_{K'}[t]/(t^b)$ satisfy $v_p(a(0))\leq C$, where $C$ is a fixed nonnegative integer. If $a(t)r(t)$ belongs to $p^M\mathcal O_{K'}[t]/(t^b)$, then \[ r(t)\in p^{M-bC}\mathcal O_{K'}[t]/(t^b). \] The bound is independent of the extension and of $a$.
why: Elementary content cancellation in O[t]/t^b; role is part of EC2/EC3 architecture.

name: Classical cusp congruence
statement: After reducing $M_i$ by a fixed constant and relabeling it, there are homomorphisms of $\cO$-algebras \begin{equation} \lambda_i^0:T_i^0\longrightarrow (\cO/p^{M_i}\cO)[t]/(t^{b_*}), \qquad M_i\longrightarrow\infty, \end{equation} which send every indicated operator to its theta comparison eigenvalue, in the full truncated ring. The weights are \cref{eq:shifted-weight}, and the two normalized $p$-operators have value $1$ at each distinguished place. One may restrict $T_i^0$ to the local summand…
why: Congruence over truncated tame ring; variant of SU/CLW.

name: Weak transfer with full infinite characters
statement: There is a conjugate-dual formal parameter \[ \Psi=\boxplus_\beta\tau_\beta[a_\beta], \qquad \sum_\beta d_\beta a_\beta=4, \] with unitary cuspidal factors, the standard transferred full infinitesimal character of $\pi$ at both real places, and the transferred Satake parameter at every finite place outside a finite set $S$ whose finite places split in $L/F$. Every cuspidal factor is unramified at every nonsplit finite place.
why: Labesse base change; sign property verified.

name: Algebraicity of the cuspidal factors
statement: Every cuspidal factor in \cref{lem:weak-transfer} is conjugate-self-dual and tempered at infinity. After a unitary parity-correcting character twist it is regular algebraic. The formal parameter is elliptic: its conjugate-self-dual blocks occur without repetition.
why: Clozel/BGHT.

name: Simultaneous transfer
statement: There is a formal parameter \[ \Psi=\boxplus_\beta\tau_\beta[a_\beta], \qquad \sum_\beta d_\beta a_\beta=4, \] with unitary cuspidal factors on $\GL_{d_\beta}(\A_L)$, such that: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item its archimedean infinitesimal character is the standard transfer of that of $\pi$; \item at every split finite place $v=ww^c$, the representation $\pi_v$, viewed on $\GL_4(F_v)$ using $w$, is the representation attached to $\Psi_w$; \item at every nonsplit finite place, …
why: Labesse + Moeglin-Waldspurger.

name: Regular algebraic conjugate-self-dual Galois input
statement: Let $\Pi$ be a regular algebraic conjugate-self-dual cuspidal representation of $\GL_d(\A_L)$ and fix $\iota:\overline{\Q}_p\simeq\C$. There is a continuous semisimple representation $r_p(\Pi)$ of $G_L$, with \[ r_p(\Pi)^c\simeq r_p(\Pi)^\vee\eps^{1-d}. \] It is de Rham above $p$. If its first infinitesimal coordinates at an embedding are $b_1,\ldots,b_d$, its de Rham weights there are $(d-1)/2-b_j$. At every finite place $w$, \begin{equation} \iota\WD\bigl(r_p(\Pi)|_{G_{L_w}}\bigr)^{\mathrm{F\…
why: BGHT, Caraiani, Shin.

name: Galois representations of the cusp systems
statement: For every characteristic-zero cusp eigensystem in \cref{prop:cusp-congruence}, there is a continuous semisimple representation \[ \rho_\pi:G_L\longrightarrow\GL_4(\overline{\Q}_p), \qquad \rho_\pi^c\simeq\rho_\pi^\vee\eps^{-3}. \] It is unramified at every finite place nonsplit over $F$. At every split finite place $v=ww^c$, \begin{equation} \iota\WD\bigl(\rho_\pi|_{G_{L_w}}\bigr)^{\mathrm{F\text{-}ss}} \preceq \operatorname{rec}_w \bigl(\pi_v\otimes|\det|_w^{-3/2}\bigr). \end{equation} The rep…
why: Standard package.

name: The two Hodge--Newton contacts
statement: At each distinguished $w\mid p$, every $\rho_\pi$ under consideration has a $G_{L_w}$-stable flag of dimensions $2,3,4$. Its last quotient is \begin{equation} X_w=\eps^{-h_4}\operatorname{unr}(\widetilde U_3^{-1}), \end{equation} where $\operatorname{unr}(a)$ takes geometric Frobenius to $a$. At the conjugate place it has a first subline of character \begin{equation} Y_{\bar w}=X_w^{-c}\eps^{-3}. \end{equation} Under \cref{eq:hecke-congruence} their values tend, uniformly on local Galois elemen…
why: Hodge-Newton decomposition from ordinary U_p values.

name: Separation and inertia
statement: The augmentation values of $\Delta$ are nonzero with uniformly bounded valuation. On any characteristic-zero system where $\Delta\ne0$, the Frobenius primary projection $P_v^{\mathrm{bin}}$ onto the roots of $A_v$ is defined and satisfies \begin{equation} (\rho_\pi(\iota)-1)P_v^{\mathrm{bin}}=0 \qquad(\iota\in I_{L_v}). \end{equation} The assertion concerns actual inertia, without a semisimplicity assumption on Frobenius.
why: Local monodromy separation; variant of SU local analysis.

name: The Steinberg control
statement: At a split place with the specified $(3,1)$ parahoric level, $\rho_\pi|_I$ is unipotent and \[ \rank(\rho_\pi(\iota)-1)\leq1\qquad(\iota\in I). \]
why: Local Langlands compatibility.

name: Uniform nilpotent control
statement: Let $T_i$ be the image of $T_i^0$ in its characteristic-zero cusp eigensystems. There is an integer $C$, independent of $i$, the weights and $q_i$, such that \begin{equation} \Delta^C\ker(T_i^0\longrightarrow T_i)=0. \end{equation} After decreasing the precisions by a fixed constant, \cref{eq:hecke-congruence} descends to \begin{equation} \lambda_i:T_i\longrightarrow \cO/(p^{M_i})[t]/(t^{b_*}),\qquad M_i\longrightarrow\infty. \end{equation}
why: Uniform version of Hecke-algebra nilpotent control.

name: Uniformly many module generators
statement: There is an integer $N$ independent of $i$ such that the $T_i$-module $B_i$ is generated by $N$ monomials in images of Galois elements.
why: Uniform GMA generation; needed only because of the ultralimit framework.

name: Finite-value admissibility
statement: If $\Phi:B\to M_4(R_b)$ is a $T$-linear algebra homomorphism with scalar map $\lambda$, then $\Phi\rho_*$ has admissible matrix coefficients. The same holds with $k$ in place of $R_b$. Algebraic local identities holding on all local sequences have the uniform increasing-precision meaning in \cref{def:admissible}.
why: Bookkeeping for EC2.

name: Corner determinant identities
statement: Choose four rows of a stack of $4\times4$ matrices in $B$, with column indices $1,2,x,y$. If the row indices consist of the column indices with $y$ replaced by $u$, then its signed determinant is a well-defined element of $D_{uy}$. The same assertion holds for a square minor whenever canceling common row and column indices leaves precisely one surplus row and one surplus column; if no indices remain, its value lies in $T$. If the ordinary determinant is zero in every ambient field, this corner …
why: GMA algebra.

name: prop:cyclotomic-corner
statement: The corner modules satisfy \begin{equation} D_{xy}=D_{xf}D_{fy}. \end{equation}
why: Variant of SU/BC extension-elimination.

name: Excluding a stable last line
statement: The image of $D_{fy}$ is nonzero at every field evaluation of $\mathcal R$.
why: Variant of Ribet/SU irreducibility step.

name: cor:fitting-vanishing
statement: One has \begin{equation} \Fitt_{0,T}(D_{fy})=0. \end{equation}
why: Fitting ideal calculation.

name: Extension extraction
statement: There is an injective $R_b$-linear map \begin{equation} \Hom_{R_b}(D_{fy}\otimes_{T,\lambda}R_b,R_b) \hookrightarrow \GrH(L,V\otimes\psi^{\pm1}). \end{equation} Its source has $R_b$-length at least $b$.
why: Ribet-SU lower bound for Greenberg Selmer, over the truncated tame ring R_b.

name: Comparison of global torus factors
statement: Let $K=\mathbb F_q(X)$, where $X$ is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus $g$, and let $\Gamma_K$ be its absolute Galois group. Let $T_1,T_2$ be $K$-tori with isomorphic rational character modules as Galois representations, and let $\ell:\operatorname{Lie}T_1\simeq\operatorname{Lie}T_2$ be a $K$-linear isomorphism. Choose local Haar measures $\eta_{i,v}$ compatible under $\ell$ on the Lie algebras, and give the smooth integral compact subgroups volume one at almost all pla…
why: Unused appendix; relies on an undated author draft (Halleck-Dube).

name: Change of characteristic for fixed nonstandard data
statement: Fix a finite collection of paired based root data with rational root-ray maps $\psi$, matching Levi data, and compatible finite cyclic outer actions. Suppose the nonstandard weighted fundamental lemma holds over local fields of sufficiently large positive characteristic for their unramified forms, including all cyclic-generator variants. Then it holds over characteristic-zero local fields of sufficiently large residue characteristic, uniformly for this collection and for all integral genericall…
why: Transfer principle (Cluckers-Loeser) application; unused.

name: Sylvester's positive prime cases
statement: Let $\ell$ be a rational prime with $\ell\equiv4,7,8\pmod 9$, and equip the projective cubic \[ E_\ell:\quad X^3+Y^3=\ell Z^3 \] with origin $(1:-1:0)$. Then \[ \ord_{s=1}L(E_\ell,s)=\rank_\Z E_\ell(\Q)=1, \qquad \#\Sha(E_\ell/\Q)<\infty. \] In particular, there are $x,y\in\Q$ such that $x^3+y^3=\ell$.
why: Corollary of Thm 1.1 + Satge descent; same cases claimed by Yin 2026 and Burungale-Tian 2026 (2609.14893).

name: thm:main
statement: Let \(E/\mathbb Q\) be any elliptic curve with \(s_2(E)\leq1\). Then \[ r:=\operatorname{rank}E(\mathbb Q) =\operatorname{ord}_{s=1}L(E,s)=s_2(E), \qquad \#\Sha(E/\mathbb Q)<\infty. \] Moreover, \[ Q_E=\frac{L^{(r)}(E,1)\,(\#T_E)^2} {r!\,\Omega_E\Reg_E\prod_{\ell\ \mathrm{finite}}c_\ell(E)} \in\mathbb Q_{>0}, \qquad v_2(Q_E)=v_2\bigl(\#\Sha(E/\mathbb Q)\bigr). \] There is no restriction on \(E[2]\) or on the reduction of \(E\) at two.
why: Goal.

name: An any-prime input criterion
statement: Let \(E/\mathbb Q\) be an elliptic curve. Suppose that, for some prime \(p\), its full \(p\)-power Selmer group with the usual local Kummer conditions at every place satisfies \[ s_p(E):=\corank_{\mathbb Z_p}\Sel_{p^\infty}(E/\mathbb Q)\le1. \] Then all conclusions of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} hold, with common rank \(r=s_p(E)\).
why: Combination with M2.

name: Positive comparison
statement: Let \(A/\mathbb Q\) be non-CM. If \(\an(A)\leq1\), then \(X(A)\geq0\). Suppose a positive fundamental discriminant \(a\) prime to \(2N_A\), or \(a=1\), satisfies \(\an(A^a)\leq1\) and \(X(A^a)=0\). Then \(s_2(A)\leq1\) implies \(\an(A)=s_2(A)\) and \(X(A)=0\).
why: Kato-type one-sided divisibility at 2.

name: Split-pair anchor
statement: Let \(A/\mathbb Q\) be non-CM. There exist a fundamental discriminant \(h\) prime to \(2N_A\), allowing \(h=1\), and an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant \(k\) prime to \(2hN_A\), in which all primes dividing \(2hN_A\) split, such that \[ \an(A^h)+\an(A^{hk})=1, \qquad X(A^h)+X(A^{hk})=0. \]
why: Same pair architecture as M1 at p=2.

name: CM comparison
statement: If \(A/\mathbb Q\) has complex multiplication and \(s_2(A)\leq1\), then \(\an(A)=s_2(A)\) and \(X(A)=0\).
why: CM Iwasawa theory at 2.

name: Two-primary parity
statement: For every elliptic curve \(A/\mathbb Q\), \[ (-1)^{s_2(A)}=w(A). \] For a quadratic field \(K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{k})\), \[ s_2(A/K)=s_2(A)+s_2(A^k). \] Moreover, \(\dim_{\mathbb F_2}\Sel_2(A)-\dim_{\mathbb F_2}A(\mathbb Q)[2]-s_2(A)\) is a nonnegative even integer. These statements do not require finiteness of \(\Sha(A)\).
why: Known.

name: Split Gross--Zagier formula
statement: With the preceding hypotheses and units modulo signs one, \[ \frac{\sqrt D}{8\pi^2(f,f)_N}\,L'(f/K,1)=2H_{\rm abs,f}(P_X). \tag{GZ} \]
why: Gross-Zagier.

name: The full-index discrepancy
statement: Under these assumptions, the single Hilbert-class trace satisfies \[ X(E)+X(E^k) =v_2\!\left(\frac{[E(K):\mathbb ZP]^2} {c_E^2\,\prod_\ell c_\ell(E)^2\ \#\Sha(E/K)}\right). \tag{G} \] Here \([E(K):\mathbb ZP]\) is the full group index, including torsion.
why: Same as M1 classical:discrepancy-identity.

name: Finite models and matrix limits
statement: Consider diagrams of the global, local, and mapping-fiber cochain complexes above over finite local Artin coefficient rings of 2-power characteristic, with modules finite free (and compatible lifts), in systems with fixed finite residue field and only boundedly many moving places. Assume the dimensions of the residual cohomology of each complex to be modeled are uniformly bounded per degree; if a bounded perfect model is used integrally, assume these dimensions vanish outside uniformly bounded …
why: Homological perturbation + ultrafilter limits; finite/singular switches as in Mazur-Rubin.

name: Complementary local conditions
statement: If paired perfect local maps \(U\to L,\ U'\to L'\) (possibly only over a localized test ring after the limit) have a paired restriction nullhomotopy and induce \(L'/U'\simeq U^\vee[-2]\), the two Selmer complexes are perfect duals with shift \(-3\). \end{lemma} \begin{proof} Dualize \(G_c\to C(U)\to U\) and use the localization adjunction to identify the dual fiber. The comparison boundaries for nested local conditions with compatible orthogonality data are localization adjoints by the same tri…
why: Homological perturbation + ultrafilter limits; finite/singular switches as in Mazur-Rubin.

name: Line switch
statement: Assume that the local quotient ranks are \(1,1\). Suppose \(C_f\) has just one generic cohomology line in degree one. At the fiber, if \(h=\dim H^1(C_f)>1\), arrange nonzero finite evaluations for both a primitive fiber reduction of that generic line and some degree-one class for the old dual condition. Then the switch lowers the fiber dimension from \(h\) to \(h-1\), and \(C_s\) again has a single generic cohomology line in degree one. If \(Y,Y'\) are classes for the finite and transverse cond…
why: Homological perturbation + ultrafilter limits; finite/singular switches as in Mazur-Rubin.

name: Square switch
statement: Assume that the local quotient ranks are \(2,2\), in the self-dual global setting with exact lower/upper duality. The localization image for upper in the four coordinates is self-annihilating: its annihilator is the kernel of the boundary into \(H^2(C_-)\), by adjunction, hence is the same image. Suppose \(C_f\) has generic rank one in degree one with a class \(Y\) and nonzero \(f(Y)=v_0\); then \(H^1(C_-)\) there vanishes. Suppose \(Y'\) for \(C_s\) has \(s(Y')=J v_0\) up to a unit, where \(J\…
why: Homological perturbation + ultrafilter limits; finite/singular switches as in Mazur-Rubin.

name: The global Kummer volume
statement: For the actual all-finite Kummer complex \(C_{\rm Kum}\) over an imaginary quadratic \(K\), with enough support, derived base change to finite coefficients gives the usual Selmer in degree one by these assertions, and likewise passage to divisible coefficients. If \(\Sha(E/K)\) is finite, degree one integrally is the compact Mordell--Weil module, degree-two torsion has length \(s_K=v_2(\#\Sha(E/K))\) (the residual finite quotient in the change to \(\mathbb Q_2/\mathbb Z_2\)), and degree-three t…
why: Homological perturbation + ultrafilter limits; finite/singular switches as in Mazur-Rubin.

name: Tame division from character tests
statement: In a DVR-integer bounded power-series ring in \(t,\mathbf u\), a divisor \(L\) with nonzero reduction at uniformizer \(=t=0\) becomes distinguished up to a unit in one tame variable after a tame group-power coordinate change. The change may retain any fixed finite list of characteristic-zero generic ranks and nonvanishings at \(t=0\). If a bounded series \(B\) is divisible by \(L\) after inverting two at every sufficiently high two-power character in \(t\), then \(L\mid B\) integrally.
why: Homological perturbation + ultrafilter limits; finite/singular switches as in Mazur-Rubin.

name: The pole test
statement: Let \(\mathcal O\) be a complete dyadic integer DVR. Suppose \(f_i,g_i\in\mathcal O[[t]]\) converge coefficientwise along the fixed ultrafilter to \(f,g\in\mathcal O[[t]]\), with \(f\ne0\). Assume, on a filter-large set of stages, that \(f_i\ne0\) and \[ g_i/f_i\in\mathcal O[[t]][1/2]. \] No uniform bound on the denominators of these quotients is required. Every zero of \(f\) in the open unit disk, taken in an algebraic closure of \(\operatorname{Frac}\mathcal O\), is a zero of \(g\) with at le…
why: Homological perturbation + ultrafilter limits; finite/singular switches as in Mazur-Rubin.

name: The integral relative lattice
statement: There is an integral Galois-equivariant map \[ H^1(\overline{Y_1(L)},\mathbb Z_2)(1)\longrightarrow T \] dual to pullback on relative cohomology. When \(A=1\), there are finitely many integers \(n_\xi\) such that \[ \delta=\sum_\xi n_\xi\delta_\xi,\qquad \delta(a)=1. \]
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Kato Euler system at p=2 with dyadic integrality.

name: Integral classes and dyadic compatibility
statement: The classes obtained from \eqref{eq:K1} are integral for support containing the primes of \(2n_2\) and infinity. They are compatible with the dyadic division traces and, after the mark and determinant projection, with corestriction as the dyadic part of \(M\) increases with \(c,d,A,\xi\) fixed. The projected smoothed classes on \(\mathbb Q\), with group or character coefficients, admit integral lifts to ordinary positive cohomology.
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Kato at p=2.

name: The full-level differential
statement: In square order, the dual exponential of the inverse-root-twisted trace \eqref{eq:K1}, before cuspidal projection, is on each determinant component a scalar multiple of \[ (c^2 E_P-c E_{cP})(d^2 E_Q-d E_{dQ})\,\frac{dq}{q}. \tag{K2} \] The scalar is \[ \pm M^{-2}, \tag{K3} \] with one common sign determined by the cup, pairing, and orientation conventions. The statement holds for all \(c,d\) prime to \(6M\).
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Kato at p=2.

name: Good-prime norms and rectangular filling
statement:
For either order pattern, adjoining a fresh prime \(\ell
mid cdn_2L\) to both orders and to \(M\) gives, after the elliptic projection, the rational norm multiplier \[ 1- rac{a_\ell(f)[\ell]}{\ell} + rac{[\ell]^2}{\ell}. \] The trace defining this norm is integral. At complete splitting in a lower abelian field the scalar is \(\det(1-ho_T(\mathrm{Fr}_\ell))/\ell\). In rectangular order, let \(q_0^a\parallel b\), \(q_0
mid b_1\). At a finite even field character \(
u\) of conductor dividi…
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Kato at p=2.

statement:
Use square order or first-row-unfilled rectangular order \(b_1=1\). Suppose \(c,d\equiv1\pmod L\), and let \(
u\) be an even finite character of \(\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb Q(\mu_M)/\mathbb Q)\). For the projected, weighted class \(z_
