cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Kato at p=2.

name: A nonzero rectangular symbol
statement: In rectangular order one can choose \(A=2^k\) and \(\xi\in\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\) with lower row \((Ns,1)\) so that \(\delta_\xi(a)\ne0\).
cited_or_new: new integral version of cited construction
why: Kato Euler system at p=2 with dyadic integrality.

name: Primitive evaluation and positive twisting
statement: For the square construction with \(A=1\), one may use an integral combination of symbols with \(\delta(a)=1\) and common smoothing integers. If a fixed positive fundamental quadratic character \(\chi_h\), prime to \(2N\), is included in the field weight, the integral coefficient identification with the twist \(E'^{\,h}\) transports \eqref{eq:K4} to the corresponding twist-period formula, with its actual smoothing factors and omissions.
why: Kato at p=2.

name: Integral positive determinant
statement: The auxiliary tuples \(R_i\) can be chosen with the following properties. The construction permits one prescribed sequence among their entries, provided that it satisfies the varying-support and cyclic-quotient conditions above, splits on \(W\) and in the fixed twisting field, and has a limiting Tate Frobenius matrix of determinant one and trace different from two. The complex \(C^+\otimes_B B_{(2)}\) is a free module of rank two in degree one, up to homotopy. Generically over \(B\), the tensor…
why: Determinant of Kato complex with tame tuples.

name: The fixed factors
statement: The factors \(\Delta,D_q,P_q\) in \eqref{eq:L1} are integral and remain nonzero modulo two after all tame parameters are set to zero. Each \(D_q/P_q\) has central value one and reduces to a group-like unit in the residual fraction field.
why: Residual concentration at 2 (same device family as M1 vertical:*).

name: Residual concentration
statement: The auxiliary primes in Proposition~\ref{prop:positive-determinant:integral} can be chosen so that the positive complex is free of rank two in degree one over \(B_{(2)}\), up to homotopy. The two raw determinant tensors in a simultaneous positive-twist comparison have identical reductions in the residual fraction field.
why: Residual concentration at 2 (same device family as M1 vertical:*).

name: Horizontal switching
statement: In any of the three test settings, let \(z_{\rm sys}\) be the indicated square or rectangular class, satisfying the old local conditions. If its generic image is nonzero, the ordinary complex has a single generic cohomology line, in degree one. At every indicated horizontal test DVR the determinant coordinate of \(z_{\rm sys}\) has nonnegative valuation.
why: Residual concentration at 2 (same device family as M1 vertical:*).

name: Generic nonvanishing and the first divisibilities
statement: The positive complex has only degree-one generic cohomology, of dimension two, and \(a\wedge z\ne0\). The coordinate \(U\) has nonnegative order at every height-one prime outside the fixed factors \(2\Delta\prod_{q\in S_f,\,q\ne2}D_qP_q\).

name: Division at the fixed factors
statement: The coordinate \(U\) has nonnegative order at every horizontal height-one prime dividing \(\Delta\prod_{q\in S_f,\,q\ne2}D_qP_q\).
why: Residual concentration at 2 (same device family as M1 vertical:*).

name: Corank-zero central specialization
statement: For either branch \(A_0\) of the construction, if \(\mathrm{an}(A_0)=0\), then the normalized determinant satisfies \[ v_2 U(0)=X(A_0) . \tag{L5} \] In particular \(X(A_0)\ge0\). If only \(s_2(A_0)=0\) is known and \(U\) is a unit, then \(L(A_0,1)\ne0\), and hence \(X(A_0)=0\).
why: Residual concentration at 2 (same device family as M1 vertical:*).

name: Tame logarithmic comparison
statement: Suppose \(\an(E)=1\), and let \(P\in E(\Q)\) be nontorsion. Then \[ \frac{\log_\omega z}{(\log_\omega P)^2} =\pm d_0\,\frac{L'(f,1)}{\Omega_0H(P)}. \tag{T1} \] The complex-side quotient is rational, and is viewed in a fixed dyadic embedding. Here \(H\) is the height fixed in the introduction.
why: EC5 statement at 2 (Perrin-Riou formula, all reduction types at 2).

name: Horizontal data
statement: A horizontal sequence consists of primes \(r_i\), integers \(m_i\to\infty\), and even surjective residue exponents \[ \lambda_i:(\Z/r_i)^\times\longrightarrow\Z/2^{m_i}, \] with the following properties. The primes avoid the fixed data, \(r_i\equiv1\pmod{ND}\), \(r_i\to1\) dyadically, and \(r_i\) splits in the Hilbert class field of \(K\) and in any fixed twisting field in use. The characters kill every prime of \(S_f\) and of the fixed smoothing integers \(c,d\), including \(2\). We may requir…
why: Candidate EC5 cluster: tame (Mazur-Tate) heights + tame Gross-Zagier intersection computation.

name: Spectral-height comparison
statement: For the horizontal data of Definition~\ref{tame:data}, and the tame height defined below, one has \begin{equation} C\Omega_0L(f\otimes\varepsilon,1)\frac{Z'}{d_0} =\pm(2-a_*)\,\frac{h_\lambda^K(Q_X,Q_X)}{\delta}. \end{equation} This assertion requires the odd functional sign and the nonzero companion value, but does not assume \(\an(E)=1\) or that \(E(\Q)\) spans the rational Selmer group. In particular, if \(Q_X\) is torsion, then \(Z'=0\).
why: Tame Gross-Zagier-type spectral-height identity; EC5.

name: A direction detecting a self-cup primitive
statement: Let \(V=T_2E\otimes\Q_2\), and let \(x\in Z^1(G_{\Q,S},V)\) represent a nonzero class. Let \(\beta\) be a cocycle on the Tate dual representing \(\operatorname{pol}([x])\), and suppose that a continuous cochain \(k\in C^1(G_{\Q,S},\Q_2(1))\) satisfies \[ dk=-\beta\cup x. \] Fix a finite normal extension \(F/\Q\) enforcing the splitting and congruence conditions of Definition~\ref{tame:data}, including the Hilbert class field of \(K\), the fixed twisting data, and \(E[2]\). Let \(\mathcal P\) be…
why: EC1 at p=2: commutator multiplies g so that eta=k(g)-beta(g)g_T(g_T-1)^{-1}x(g) is nonzero.

name: A direction with nonzero height
statement: If \(P\in E(\Q)\) is nontorsion, the horizontal data can be chosen so that \(h_\lambda^\Q(P,P)\ne0\).
why: Candidate EC5 cluster: tame (Mazur-Tate) heights + tame Gross-Zagier intersection computation.

name: Tame heights and trace compatibility
statement: Let \(F'\supset K\) contain the ring class field \(H_{r^j}\), \(j\ge1\). The norm of \(\lambda_i\) to \(F'\) is finite-unramified. On the polarized abelian varieties in use it defines a bilinear biextension height \(h_i^{F'}\) modulo \(2^{m_i}\). After multiplying the first argument by one fixed power of \(2\), there are compatible heights on \(E/K\) and \(E/\Q\), even at the ramified character place \(r_i\). Their rational limits satisfy trace compatibility and \[ h_\lambda^K(P_1,P_2)=2h_\lamb…
why: Candidate EC5 cluster: tame (Mazur-Tate) heights + tame Gross-Zagier intersection computation.

name: Cup reciprocity in analytic rank one
statement: If \(\an(E)=1\) and \(P\in E(\Q)\) is nontorsion, then \[ Z'\log_\omega P =\pm(2-a_*)\frac{\log_\omega z}{\log_\omega P} h_\lambda^\Q(P,P). \tag{T2} \]
why: Candidate EC5 cluster: tame (Mazur-Tate) heights + tame Gross-Zagier intersection computation.

name: tame:holomorphic
statement: The continuation in \eqref{tame:kernel} at \(s=0\) is a holomorphic weight-two form of level \(Nr^2\), with trivial character.
why: Candidate EC5 cluster: tame (Mazur-Tate) heights + tame Gross-Zagier intersection computation.

name: The traced coefficient
statement: At the indicated character evaluation, the coefficient of \(q^{nr^h}\) in \(I_\chi\) is \begin{equation} \begin{split} D_{i,h}(n) &=\frac12\sum_{\substack{C_0,\ y_0\in C_0,\ b>0\\ a=\mathrm Ny_0/a_C>0\\a+Nb=nr^hD}} \ \sum_{\substack{kl=b\\\gcd(k,l,D)=1}} W(k)\chi(a/D)\bar\chi^2(Nk),\\ W(k) &=\prod_{\substack{p\mid D\\p\mid k}}\epsilon_p(l) \prod_{\substack{p\mid D\\p\nmid k}}\epsilon_p(-a_CNk). \end{split} \end{equation} Only terms with \(a\) a unit at \(r\) occur. Its linear coefficient is the…
why: Candidate EC5 cluster: tame (Mazur-Tate) heights + tame Gross-Zagier intersection computation.

name: Removal of the mask
why: Candidate EC5 cluster: tame (Mazur-Tate) heights + tame Gross-Zagier intersection computation.

name: The projected holomorphic coefficient
statement: For all sufficiently large \(h\), \[ \begin{split} \big[\mathcal A(D'_{h+2}-D'_h)\big](\ell) ={}&\mathcal A_fa_f(\ell) \frac{\gamma_{h+2}-\gamma_h}{(a_*-2)(a_*+2)} C\Omega_0\,\frac{Z'}{d_0}\\ &{}\cdot(2-a_*)L(f\otimes\varepsilon,1). \end{split} \tag{T5} \]
why: Candidate EC5 cluster: tame (Mazur-Tate) heights + tame Gross-Zagier intersection computation.

name: The local divisor sum
statement: Fix \(C_0,y_0,b\) in the unmasked sum, and put \(d_q=v_q(b)\). Its contribution with weight \(-2v_q(k)\), including the factor \(1/2\), is zero unless \(q\) is inert, \(d_q\) is odd, and \(\varepsilon_{K,p}(-bNa_C)=1\) for every \(p\mid D\). In that case it is \[ -\frac{1+d_q}{2}\,\rho(b/q)\, 2^{\#\{p\mid D:p\mid b\}}. \tag{T6} \]
why: Candidate EC5 cluster: tame (Mazur-Tate) heights + tame Gross-Zagier intersection computation.

name: Intersection realization
statement: The negative of the local sum in Lemma~\ref{tame:local-divisor}, summed over \(C_0,y_0,b\), is the intersection of the oriented Hilbert-class sum based at \(\infty\) with \(T_m\) of the same sum based at \(0\), at the places of \(K\) over \(q\), weighted by their residue degrees over \(q\).
why: Gross-Zagier-style intersection computation at level N r^2 (quaternion lattice counts).

name: The rank-one central value
statement: Suppose a branch \(A_0\) of the positive determinant construction has analytic rank one. Then \(U(0)\ne0\) and \[ v_2 U(0)=X(A_0). \] Thus \eqref{eq:L5} holds in both analytic ranks zero and one.
why: Selmer Bockstein / Rubin height formula variant.

name: Positivity and transfer of a central unit
statement: The following assertions hold for a non-CM curve \(A\). \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item If \(\mathrm{an}(A)\le1\), then \(X(A)\ge0\). \item Suppose the positive twist hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{prop:positive} holds, without assuming the analytic rank of \(A\). Then the positive determinant of \(E'\) is a unit for every completed auxiliary-prime construction permitted by Proposition~\ref{prop:positive-determinant:integral}, including those with one prescribed admissible sequence. If…

name: A primitive for the self-cup
statement: Let \(x\) be a cocycle representing a nonzero class in the rational compact Selmer line at fixed support, with coefficients \(T\otimes\mathbb Q_2\), and let \(\beta=\operatorname{pol}(x)\) on the Tate dual. There is a continuous scalar \(1\)-cochain \(k\) on \(G_{\mathbb Q,S}\) such that \[ dk=-\beta\cup x. \] After multiplying \(x,\beta\) by the same nonzero dyadic integer and \(k\) by its square, all three cochains can be taken integral.
why: Selmer Bockstein / Rubin height formula variant.

name: A compatible nonzero direction
statement: The prescribed auxiliary sequence can be chosen to satisfy the spectral-height hypotheses of Section~\ref{sec:tame} and the fixed splitting conditions for both positive-determinant branches. Its Frobenius lifts can be chosen to tend on the fixed data to an element \(g\in G_L\) whose Tate action \(g_T\) has determinant one, trace \(a_*\ne\pm2\), and two non-root-of-unity eigenvalues, and which satisfies \[ k(g)-\beta(g)g_T(g_T-1)^{-1}x(g)\ne0. \tag{P2} \]
why: Selmer Bockstein / Rubin height formula variant.

name: Nonzero Selmer Bockstein
statement: For the direction of Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-completion:direction}, \(\operatorname{ord}_v\delta(v)=1\). In particular, \(C_f^{\rm Sel}\) is generically acyclic over \(\mathcal R\).
why: Selmer Bockstein / Rubin height formula variant.

name: Reducible split-product comparison
statement: Let \(E/\mathbb Q\) be a non-CM elliptic curve with \(E(\mathbb Q)[2]\ne0\), and put \(N=\mathrm{cond}(E)\). Let \(d\equiv7\pmod {16}\) be prime and suppose that every prime dividing \(2N\) splits in \(K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d})\). If \(s_2(E/K)=1\), then \(L(E/K,s)=L(E,s)L(E^{-d},s)\) has a simple zero at \(1\), and \[ X(E)+X(E^{-d})=0 . \] If the product is already known to have a simple zero at \(1\), the same valuation identity holds without separately assuming the Selmer corank condition.
why: BDP at p=2.

name: Scalar residual order
statement: For an odd prime \(q\mid N\), let \(b_q\in\mathbb Z_2\setminus\{0\}\) be the \(\Gamma\)-Frobenius exponent at one of the places over \(q\), and put \(g_q=2^{v_2(b_q)}\). Then \[ \operatorname{ord}_t\overline L_{\rm alg}(C(t)) =4\sum_{\substack{q\mid N\\q\ne2}}g_q. \tag{A1} \]
why: BDP at p=2.

name: Auxiliary primes and Frobenius exponents
statement: There is a sequence of split good primes \(r_i\), leaving every fixed finite set, with principal places \(R_i=(\pi_i)\), such that: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item \(\pi_i\) tends to \(1\) at both dyadic places, and its residue modulo \(\sqrt{-d}\) is a nonzero nonsquare; \item \(\sqrt2\) exists and is a nonsquare modulo \(R_i\), and \((q/r_i)=-1\) for every odd \(q\mid N\); \item the Tate Frobenius at \(R_i\) tends to a matrix \(g\) with \(\det g=1\) and \(a_*:=\operatorname{…
why: BDP at p=2.

name: Transverse regularity
statement: The determinants satisfy \[ L_{\rm alg,r}(t,0) =(2-a_*)^2 L_{\rm alg}(C(t))\cdot{\rm unit}, \tag{A2} \] and \[ L_{\rm alg,r}\big|_{(2,t)=0}\ne0. \tag{A3} \]
why: BDP at p=2.

name: Integral depleted primitive
statement: The displayed limit defining \(F_0\) converges to an integral weight-zero function on the ordinary locus, including when \(2\mid N\), and \(d_{\rm mod}F_0=f^{[2]}\). At a Tate cusp with cyclic \(\mu\)-level, \[ F_0=\sum_{\substack{m\ge1\\2\nmid m}}\frac{a_m}{m}q_{\rm Tate}^m, \qquad F=\sum_{\substack{m\ge1\\(m,\,2\prod_{\ell\in S^\circ}\ell)=1}} \frac{a_m}{m}q_{\rm Tate}^m. \] Congruences between such fully depleted primitives can be checked by their Tate expansions on a common raised tame leve…
why: BDP at p=2.

name: Support of the disk measure
statement: There is a bounded integral measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb Z_2\) with \[ \mathcal F(z)=\int_{\mathbb Z_2}z^x\,d\mu(x). \] It is supported on \(\mathbb Z_2^\times\).
why: BDP at p=2.

name: The exact logarithmic primitive
statement: The modular logarithm \(G\) is analytic on each interior ordinary CM disk, and on these disks \[ F_0=P_2(V_2)G. \tag{M1} \] With the branch of the logarithm satisfying \(\log 2=0\), the Eisenstein primitive is \[ F_{{\rm Eis},0} =-\frac1{48}\log\left( \frac{\Delta^2V_2^2\Delta}{(V_2\Delta)^3}\right). \]
why: BDP at p=2.

name: CM disk coordinates
statement: The conductor-\(s\) CM points are canonical lifts. In their Serre--Tate disks, the points \(z=\zeta_{2^m}^j\), for \(j\) odd, have endomorphism order \(\mathcal O_{2^ms}\) and are defined over \(H_{2^ms}\) with the specified cyclic level. The kernel of the order-class map to conductor \(s\) acts on them through the unit ratio \((\mathbb Z/2^m\mathbb Z)^\times\), simply transitively on the primitive roots in each disk. Its inverse-limit map to \(\Gamma\) is a fixed map \(\eta:\mathbb Z_2^\times\…
why: BDP at p=2.

name: Character and central interpolation
statement: Let \(\theta\) be a sufficiently high finite character of \(\Gamma\), and let \(\theta_l=\theta\circ\eta\) have primitive conductor \(2^m\). Let \(X\) be the point with \(z=\zeta_{2^m}\) in the base disk, at the original primitive level, and put \(\chi=\theta\psi_s\). Then \[ \left(\sum_{j\ {\rm odd}\bmod 2^m}\theta_l(j)\zeta_{2^m}^{j}\right) b_s(\theta,u) = \left(\sum_{\rho\in\operatorname{Pic}(\mathcal O_{2^m s})} \chi(\rho)\,G(X^\rho)\right) \prod_{\ell\in S^\circ}P_\ell(\chi(\sigma_\ell)). …
why: BDP at p=2.

name: The split trace and residual order
statement: Return to the geometric setting of Proposition~\ref{split-measures:reducible-input}, without imposing its Selmer-corank hypothesis, and take \(S^\circ\) to be exactly the odd primes dividing \(N\). For the auxiliary sequence of Lemma~\ref{split-measures:auxiliary-primes}, \[ B_r(t,0)=(a_*-2)^2B(t), \tag{M4} \] and \[ \operatorname{ord}_t\overline B =4\sum_{\substack{q\mid N\\q\ne2}}g_q. \tag{M5} \]
why: BDP at p=2.

name: Odd local conditions
statement: At the places over the moving primes \(r\), the full local complexes are acyclic over \(A\). At each fixed odd place \(v\), the characteristic-zero unramified condition \[ U_v=[M^{I_v}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Fr}_v-1}M^{I_v}] \qquad\text{in degrees }0,1 \] contains local \(H^0\), injects into local \(H^1\), and is exactly complementary to the corresponding condition on the conjugate Tate dual. The product of the singular determinants at the two places over \(q\in S^\circ\) is, up to a unit, \[ D_q=…
why: Greenberg/BDP determinant comparison at 2.

name: Projected Kummer lines
statement: At each \(v=w,\bar w\) there is a projected Kummer condition \(U_v\), a split free line in \(H^1(K_v,M)[-1]\) (placed in degree one) mapping into \(R\Gamma(K_v,M)\), over \(A\). Here \(H^1(K_v,M)\) and the full complex refer to the limiting local model; the latter is itself split free of rank two in degree one only. The lines are exactly self-annihilating with conjugate transport and Weil pairing. The same assertion holds for a fixed characteristic-zero Hecke plane of a modular abelian variety,…
why: Greenberg/BDP determinant comparison at 2.

name: Logarithmic coordinate and finite-level transfer
statement: The scalar-extended Kummer line at \(w\) has an \(A'\)-linear isomorphism \(\lambda_w\) given by weighted logarithms. At finite cyclic quotients of the conductor variables, this line specializes to the usual projected Kummer condition. A sequence of corestricted twisted classes satisfying the finite-level Kummer conditions to growing precision therefore belongs to the limiting Kummer line. For classes arising from global points, \(\lambda_w\) is the unnormalized character-weighted orbit sum of …
why: Greenberg/BDP determinant comparison at 2.

name: The unramified center
statement: Set \(t=0\) and localize, after inverting \(2\), at the tame center \((u)\). At both dyadic places the full local complex again has a direct Kummer line and a complementary quotient line in degree one. They specialize to the ordinary Kummer condition and its quotient at \(u=0\). After the same measure-side scalar extension used for \(\lambda_w\), the weighted logarithm is a line isomorphism over the center local ring, and the transfer and membership assertions of Lemma~\ref{split-local:log-tran…
why: Greenberg/BDP determinant comparison at 2.

name: The finite and transverse planes
statement: At an auxiliary inert prime satisfying the preceding full-Tate approximation conditions, the limiting local complex has split free cohomology \[ M,\qquad M\oplus M,\qquad M \quad\text{in degrees }0,1,2. \] Here \(M\) denotes the underlying coefficient plane. The finite and transverse conditions have complementary pure degree-one coordinates, both include degree zero, and both omit degree two. They are exactly self-annihilating for conjugate duality. Their mixed pairing is, up to a unit, \(\lang…
why: Greenberg/BDP determinant comparison at 2.

name: CM derivatives and uniform descent
statement: For a finite collection of auxiliary inert prime sequences satisfying the full-Tate approximation conditions, choose the CM points compatibly over their conductor-product ring class fields. After multiplication by one common nonzero integer \(L\), their derivative Kummer classes descend to the lower conductor fields to arbitrarily high retained \(2\)-power precision. They satisfy Kummer conditions at the fixed places over \(2N\), and unramified conditions at the fixed odd places after a further…
why: Greenberg/BDP determinant comparison at 2.

name: Inert derivative identity
statement: Fix a finite collection of auxiliary inert prime sequences satisfying the full-Tate approximation conditions above Lemma~\ref{split-local:inert-planes}. Over the lower conductor fields \(H_{b_i}\), form the compatible CM points and derivative operators \(D_I\) of Lemma~\ref{split-local:descent}, using its common nonzero multiplier \(L\) for this collection. Let \(Z_I\) be their descended, \(\chi\)-weighted corestrictions to \(K\), transferred to the limiting coefficient model. In the finite and…
why: Greenberg/BDP determinant comparison at 2.

name: Selmer membership and the logarithmic comparison
statement: For the horizontal test currently considered the \(Z_I\) over \(A\) lie in the Selmer problems with \(U_v\) at \(2N\), full at \(r\), and the switched planes as indicated (finite at additional unswitched derivative places). For \(Z=Z_\varnothing\), their logarithmic comparison with the paired measure is \[ B_r(\theta,u)=\epsilon\, \lambda_w(\operatorname{loc}_wZ)^2\prod_{q\in S^\circ}D_q, \qquad \epsilon\in(A')^\times.\tag{B1} \]
why: Greenberg/BDP determinant comparison at 2.

name: The horizontal determinant inequality
statement: For a sufficiently high finite character \(\theta\), suppose \(B_r(\theta,u)\ne0\). Impose the unramified conditions \(U_v\) at the fixed odd places and the Kummer conditions at both dyadic places, and call the resulting Selmer complex \(C_F\). Let \(Z=Z_\varnothing\) and write \(\operatorname{loc}_wZ=p_0e\) for a basis \(e\) of the Kummer line over \(A\). Put \[ L_{\rm prim}=\frac{L_{\rm alg,r}(\theta,u)}{\prod_{q\in S^\circ}D_q}. \] At every height-one valuation \(v\) of \(A\), the complex ha…
why: Greenberg/BDP determinant comparison at 2.

name: Integral unit comparison
statement: For the reducible split-product construction, \[ B_r=L_{\rm alg,r}\,U_r, \qquad U_r\in\mathcal V^*[[t,u]]^\times. \] Likewise \(B/L_{\rm alg}(C(t))\) is a unit in \(\mathcal V^*[[t]]\).
why: Greenberg/BDP determinant comparison at 2.

name: Rank detection from Selmer corank one
statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{split-measures:reducible-input}, assume \(s_2(E/K)=1\). The conductor-one Hilbert trace \(P\) in \eqref{eq:M3} is nontorsion. Consequently \(L(E/K,s)\) has a simple zero at \(s=1\).
why: Greenberg/BDP determinant comparison at 2.

name: The exact factor at the center
statement: In the reducible split-product setting, assume that \(L(E/K,s)\) has a simple zero at \(1\), either as a hypothesis or by Proposition~\ref{split-local:center-rank}. Then \[ X(E)+X(E^{-d})=0. \] In the notation of \eqref{eq:Kum}, the exact arithmetic identity producing this equality is \[ 2(n_P+\tau_g)=2v_2(c_E)+2\sum_\ell v_2(c_\ell)+s_K. \tag{E} \]
why: Greenberg/BDP determinant comparison at 2.

name: Characteristic-zero Heegner rank test
statement: Let \(f\) be a normalized primitive weight-two newform of trivial nebentypus and level \(N_f\), and let \(\mathcal A\) be its modular abelian factor. Let \(K\) have odd fundamental discriminant \(-D<-4\), prime to \(N_f\), and suppose every prime dividing \(N_f\) splits in \(K\). Thus \(\mathcal O_K^\times=\{\pm1\}\), and the split height formula \eqref{eq:GZ} applies. Let \(F_f\) be a finite extension of \(\mathbb Q_2\) containing the image of a fixed Hecke coefficient embedding, and let \(V_f…
why: Greenberg/BDP determinant comparison at 2.

name: Finite Selmer seed
statement: There are a permitted twisting factor \(h\) and an elliptic curve \(E_0\), isogenous over \(\mathbb Q\) to \(E^h\), with rational two-torsion and \[ \dim{\rm Sel}_2(E_0)=\dim E_0(\mathbb Q)[2]. \tag{seed} \]
why: Finite 2-descent graph/matrix model; known technique.

name: Realization of labels and edges
statement: There is a linear map \(\xi:H^*\to V\) such that \(\operatorname{loc}_S(p_i^*)=\xi(l_i)\), and the map \[ (z,y)\longmapsto\operatorname{loc}_S(z)+\xi(y), \qquad H\oplus H^*\longrightarrow V, \] is injective. Arbitrary finite label lists and edge values are realizable by distinct fresh primes, subject only to \[ e_{ij}+e_{ji}=l_i(-1)l_j(-1). \]
why: Graph model of 2-Selmer under twisting (Monsky matrices).

name: Finite change inequalities
statement: Suppose self-orthogonal local conditions on a fixed self-dual module are changed at finitely many places. Let \(b_0\) be the sum of the old local dimensions modulo the intersections with the new conditions, and let \(j_0\) be the rank of old Selmer localization in that sum. Then \[ \dim\operatorname{Sel}_{\rm new} \le\dim\operatorname{Sel}_{\rm old}+b_0-2j_0. \] For a pair of dual scalar problems, suppose transverse lines are switched at \(n\) odd places of local dimension two. If their old loc…
why: Graph model of 2-Selmer under twisting (Monsky matrices).

name: The finite graph model
statement: For \(h=\prod_{i=1}^n p_i^*\) in this family, every global two-Selmer class has unique coordinates \(w\in H\otimes W\) and \(u_i\in W\). They satisfy \[ \begin{split} {\rm loc}_S(w)+\textstyle\sum_i \xi(l_i)\otimes u_i &\in L:=\bigoplus_{v\in S}\operatorname{im}(\delta_{2,E^h,v}) \ \subset V\otimes W,\\ w(l_i)&=B(l_i)u_i+\sum_{j\ne i}e_{ij}(u_i+u_j) \qquad(1\le i\le n). \end{split}\tag{graph} \] Here \(L\) is fixed throughout the family. The torsion subspace is \(u_i=t,\ w=Bt\), for \(t\in W\),…
why: Graph model of 2-Selmer under twisting (Monsky matrices).

name: Orientation by isogeny
statement: We may replace \(E\) by a rationally isogenous curve with full rational two-torsion, and apply that isogeny to all its twists, so that \[ k_A\le m\qquad\text{for every }f_A=0. \tag{orient} \] The conductor and the prescribed family of local squareclasses are preserved.
why: Graph model of 2-Selmer under twisting (Monsky matrices).

name: Full-plane minimization
statement: For the oriented curve of Lemma~\ref{lem:reducible-orientation}, some allowed nonempty twist has pure dimension zero. In particular, Proposition~\ref{prop:reducible-seed} holds when the initial curve has full rational two-torsion.
why: Graph model of 2-Selmer under twisting (Monsky matrices).

name: One-line construction
statement: Proposition~\ref{prop:reducible-seed} also holds when \(\dim E(\mathbb Q)[2]=1\).
why: Graph model of 2-Selmer under twisting (Monsky matrices).

name: Split imaginary Selmer partner
statement: For \(h,E_0\) in Proposition~\ref{prop:reducible-seed}, there is a fresh prime \(d\equiv7\pmod{16}\) such that \(K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d})\) splits all primes of \(2hN_E\), and \[ d_2(E_0^{-d})=s_2(E_0^{-d})=1,\qquad s_2(E_0)=0,\qquad s_2(E_0/K)=1. \]
why: Finite 2-descent graph/matrix model; known technique.

name: The reducible split-pair anchor
statement: Proposition~\ref{prop:anchor} holds for every non-CM elliptic curve over \(\mathbb Q\) with rational two-torsion.
why: Assembly.

name: CM realizations
statement: The field \(F\) is real, the Hecke-character value field is \(F_c\), and the characteristic-zero Tate plane at each Hecke embedding is absolutely irreducible over \(\mathbb Q\). The variety \(A\) is \(\mathbb Q\)-simple, with endomorphism algebra \(F\); over \(L\) its endomorphism algebra is \(F_c\), and its CM type is induced from \(L\).
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: A CM lift of an imaginary residual plane
statement: If an \(S_3\) residual plane \(W/\mathbb F_2\) has imaginary quadratic subfield \(L\), there is a form \(f\) as above for which \(M^*/\pi\simeq W\otimes_{\mathbb F_2}\mathcal O/\pi\).
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: Individual-character elliptic-unit comparison
statement: Let \(\Gamma\simeq\mathbb Z_2^2\) be the free pro-\(2\) factor of the ray-tower group, let \(\Lambda_{\mathcal O}=\mathcal O[[\Gamma]]\), and let \(\Lambda(\chi)(1)\) have the finite-character and regular variable actions of \cite[Section~4.1]{BF23}. If \(\mathfrak f_\chi\mid\mathfrak f\), then, inside generic rank-one cohomology, \[ \Lambda_{\mathcal O}z_{2^\infty\mathfrak f} = \det_{\Lambda_{\mathcal O}}^{-1} R\Gamma\bigl(\mathcal O_L[1/2\mathfrak f],\Lambda(\chi)(1)\bigr). \] For the charact…
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: Specialization under concentration
statement: Let \(\psi\) be an additional finite allowed character, possibly trivial. Suppose that \[ R\Gamma\bigl(\mathcal O_L[1/2\mathfrak f],T_\alpha\psi\bigr)[1/2] \] has a one-dimensional \(H^1\) and no other cohomology. Then the unsmoothed elliptic-unit class satisfies \[ \mathcal O z(T_\alpha\psi)= \mathcal D\bigl(R\Gamma(\mathcal O_L[1/2\mathfrak f], T_\alpha\psi)\bigr). \tag{C2} \] Here the determinant is identified with the rational cohomology line. No nonvanishing hypothesis on a complex \(L\)-v…
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: Shapiro and the CM period equation
statement: Suppose \(\psi\) comes from a Dirichlet character on \(\mathbb Q\), is locally trivial at \(2\), and the omissions are conjugation-stable. Allow all ramification primes and write \(z\) also for the Shapiro class in \(M^*\psi\) over \(\mathbb Q\). After trivializing at \(2\) by a compatible geometric Artin basis, \[ \exp^*z=\frac{L_{2\mathfrak f}(f,\psi^\pm,1)}{p_\gamma}\,\omega . \tag{C3} \] The sign \(\pm\) fixes the reciprocal convention on the finite character; one may invert the variable th…
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: Nonvanishing of the eigendifferential logarithm
statement: For every nontorsion \(P\in B(\mathbb Q)\), one has \(\log_\omega P\ne0\).
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: Horizontal CM logarithm
statement: Suppose that \(L(f_B,s)\) has a simple zero at \(1\). Then the rational compact Selmer group at the chosen coefficient embedding is one-dimensional, generated by any nontorsion rational point \(P\) after extension of scalars. Write \(z_B=\alpha\lambda_{B,*}(P)\) in projected Kummer notation. With the absolute \(F\)-valued Poincar\'e height pairing, \[ \alpha=\pm e_S\log_\omega P\, \frac{L'(f_B,1)}{p_\gamma H_{\lambda_B,F}(P,P)}. \tag{C4} \] The height-normalized complex expression is interprete…
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: The torsion-trace implication
statement: In the CM elliptic setting, suppose only that the functional sign is odd. Choose a split Heegner companion \(K'\) with nonzero central value and form the same horizontal exponential coordinate \(Z\). The prime choices need satisfy the spectral conditions above, but need not satisfy the additional prescription involving a rational point \(P\). If the projected Hilbert trace \(P_0\) is torsion, then \(Z'=0\).
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: The exact CM lattice index
statement: If \(E\) has analytic order zero or one, then \[ d\bigl(C^+(M),a^*(1)\wedge z\bigr)=v_2(\gamma(a)). \tag{C5} \]
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: The CM leading coefficient in known low rank
statement: If \(E/\mathbb Q\) is CM and \(\an(E)\le1\), then \(X(E)=0\).
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: CM corank zero
statement: If \(E/\mathbb Q\) is CM and \(s_2(E)=0\), then \(\an(E)=0\) and \(X(E)=0\).
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: Paired CM comparison
statement: Let \(A=e_fJ_0(N)\) have the normalization \eqref{eq:C1}. Suppose \(K\) has odd fundamental discriminant \(-D<-4\), splitting \(2N\), and \(L(f/K,s)\) has a simple zero at 1. Use \(S\) above finite rational primes splitting in \(K\), including \(2N\) in the prime-support sense, archimedean places understood, and \(e_S\) for the omission multiplier of \(f\) over \(\mathbb Q\). Put \(P=e_f P_X\) on \(A(K)_{\mathbb Q}\) for the Hilbert trace of \eqref{eq:GZ}. Over \(K\) consider the complex \(C_*\…
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: Horizontal nonnegativity for elliptic units
statement: Let \(E/\mathbb Q\) be CM by \(L\), with character lattice \(T_\alpha\), and fix a support \(S_f\) containing two and all bad primes. Choose good primes \(r_i\) split in \(L\), tending to one dyadically, and even surjective residue characters \[ \lambda_i:(\mathbb Z/r_i\mathbb Z)^\times \longrightarrow\mathbb Z/2^{m_i}\mathbb Z, \qquad m_i\longrightarrow\infty. \] Suppose these characters kill the fixed support and smoothing norms, and the Tate Frobenii at \(r_i\) tend to a determinant-one elem…
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: CM corank one
statement: If \(E/\mathbb Q\) is CM and \(s_2(E)=1\), then \(\an(E)=1\) and \(X(E)=0\).
why: CM main conjecture inputs (Rubin, JLK, BF, LTYZ) applied at 2.

name: Conjugate Bockstein alternation
statement: With the coefficient module, local conditions, and isotropy data just specified, let \(s\in R\) be a regular scalar. On degree one for coefficients mod \(s\), with \(\partial\) the Bockstein from mod \(s^2\), one has \[ \langle x,\partial x\rangle=0 . \tag{H1} \]
why: Heisenberg-central-extension proof that a Bockstein pairing is alternating: technique of Poonen-Stoll (theta groups) / Flach; variant for conjugate-induced coefficients.

name: Parity of special and generic ranks
statement: For a perfect two-term DVR complex in degrees \(1,2\) with perfect self-duality of shift \(-3\), arising from the preceding local conditions and satisfying \eqref{eq:H1}, the generic and special first-cohomology dimensions have the same parity.
why: Elementary-divisor parity from an alternating perfect pairing.

name: Imaginary \(S_3\) anchor
statement: Proposition~\ref{prop:anchor} holds for every non-CM elliptic curve \(E/\mathbb Q\) whose residual image is \(S_3\) and whose quadratic residual subfield is imaginary.
why: Alternation of a Bockstein pairing via a Heisenberg central extension = Poonen-Stoll / Flach technique transplanted to conjugate-induced coefficients.

name: Choice of comparator
statement: Let \(W=E[2]\) have image \(S_3\) and imaginary quadratic subfield \(L\). There exist a primitive CM newform \(f_0\) of weight two and trivial nebentypus, lifting \(W\) on the plane \(M^*\) of Section~\ref{sec:cm}, and an imaginary quadratic field \(K\) of odd fundamental discriminant \(k<-4\), such that \[ L(f_0,1)\ne0,\qquad \ord_{s=1}L(f_0/K,s)=1, \qquad q\mid 2N_E N_{f_0}\Longrightarrow q\text{ splits in }K. \] Moreover, \(K\ne L\), and \(W|_{G_K}\) still has image \(S_3\).
why: Alternation of a Bockstein pairing via a Heisenberg central extension = Poonen-Stoll / Flach technique transplanted to conjugate-induced coefficients.

name: Simultaneous Selmer seed
statement: For the field \(K\) above, there is a squarefree product \(h\) of fresh primes congruent to \(1\pmod8\), coprime to \(2N_Ek\) and split in \(K\), such that \[ \dim_{\mathbb F_2}\Sel_2(E^h/\mathbb Q) +\dim_{\mathbb F_2}\Sel_2(E^{hk}/\mathbb Q)=1, \qquad s_2(E^h/K)=1. \]
why: Alternation of a Bockstein pairing via a Heisenberg central extension = Poonen-Stoll / Flach technique transplanted to conjugate-induced coefficients.

name: CM local factorization
statement: For auxiliary primes satisfying these prescriptions, put \(v_j=(1+u_j)^{\alpha_j}-1\), where \(\alpha_j\in\mathbb Z_2^\times\) is the relative inertia exponent. Replacing the full local condition by the pure singular condition on the CM problem removes a factor \(v_j^2\) from its strict determinant. Each paired measure vanishes when \(u_j=0\).
why: Alternation of a Bockstein pairing via a Heisenberg central extension = Poonen-Stoll / Flach technique transplanted to conjugate-induced coefficients.

name: Exact central switch
statement: Suppose the auxiliary primes satisfy the Frobenius prescriptions above. At each step \(I\to I\cup\{j\}\), require nonzero finite evaluations of \(Y_I\) and of a class \(z\) of opposite conjugation sign in the problem obtained from \(C_{F,I}\) by relaxing both dyadic conditions. Then at every step the strict complex is rationally acyclic, \(C_{F,I}\) has cohomological ranks \((1,1)\), and \(Y_I\) spans degree one with nonzero logarithms at both dyadic places. Moreover, \[ 2v_2(\log_{\omega,w}Y_I…
why: Alternation of a Bockstein pairing via a Heisenberg central extension = Poonen-Stoll / Flach technique transplanted to conjugate-induced coefficients.

name: Compatible primes and residual concentration
statement: A finite collection of auxiliary prime sequences can be chosen to satisfy all prescriptions of Lemmas~\ref{alternation-imaginary:local-factors} and~\ref{alternation-imaginary:central-switch}, to have nonzero fixed-place Frobenius exponents in one tame variable, and to satisfy \[ D\big|_{t=\pi=0}\ne0 \] for both the CM comparator and the elliptic curve. The non-CM limiting traces \(a_{j,*}\) can all be required to be nonzero.
why: Alternation of a Bockstein pairing via a Heisenberg central extension = Poonen-Stoll / Flach technique transplanted to conjugate-induced coefficients.

name: The central mixed coefficient
statement: For \(f_0\), with \(I\) the set of all tame indices and with the same common multiplier \(H\) as in Lemma~\ref{alternation-imaginary:central-switch}, one has \[ v_2\left(\left.\frac{b^\pm}{\prod u_j}\right|_{t=\mathbf u=0}\right) =v_2(e_S\log_{\omega,w}Y_I/H). \tag{I4} \] Consequently both \(\widetilde B(0,\mathbf0)\) and \(\widetilde D(0,\mathbf0)\) are nonzero, and their ratio is a dyadic unit: \[ v_2\!\left( \frac{\widetilde B(0,\mathbf0)}{\widetilde D(0,\mathbf0)} \right)=0. \]
why: Alternation of a Bockstein pairing via a Heisenberg central extension = Poonen-Stoll / Flach technique transplanted to conjugate-induced coefficients.

name: Integral quotient and its unit value
statement: Embed the arithmetic coefficient ring into the common integral measure coefficient ring. For each of the two coefficient planes, \(D\mid B\) in the resulting integral series ring, and both quotients in that ring are units.
why: Alternation of a Bockstein pairing via a Heisenberg central extension = Poonen-Stoll / Flach technique transplanted to conjugate-induced coefficients.

name: The real \(S_3\) anchor
statement: There are a fundamental discriminant \(h\) prime to \(2N_E\), allowing \(h=1\), and an imaginary quadratic field \(K\) of discriminant \(-d\) prime to \(2hN_E\), in which every prime dividing \(2hN_E\) splits, such that \[ \an(E^h)+\an(E^{h(-d)})=1, \qquad X(E^h)+X(E^{h(-d)})=0. \]
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: A level supporting the real character
statement: The character \(\psi\) is a character of an ordinary ring class group of \(L\). If \(b\) is its ring conductor, then its character conductor ideal is \(b\mathcal O_L\), and the odd part of the Artin conductor of \(W\) is \(d_L^{\rm odd}(b^{\rm odd})^2\). Choose a good prime \(\ell_0\equiv3\pmod4\), outside the conductor support, whose Frobenius on \(W\) is a \(3\)-cycle. Then \begin{equation} n=2^\delta d_L^{\rm odd}(b^{\rm odd}\ell_0)^2, \qquad \delta=v_2(d_L)\bmod2 \end{equation} satisfies \(…
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: A pair with Selmer corank one
statement: There is an odd fundamental discriminant \(h\), prime to \(2nN_E\) and allowing \(h=1\), such that \(E_0=E^h\) has trivial two-Selmer group. There is also a fresh prime \(d\equiv7\pmod8\) such that \(K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d})\) splits every prime dividing \(2nhN_E\), \(W(\mathrm{Fr}_d)\) is a \(3\)-cycle, and \[ s_2(E_0/K)=1. \] The class number of \(K\) is odd and its units are precisely the signs.
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: The detector at infinity
statement: There is an \(\mathbb F_2\)-linear functional \[ \Theta:H^1(\langle\sigma\rangle,T_2J)\to\mathbb F_2,\quad \Theta T_p=\operatorname{tr}W(\mathrm{Fr}_p)\Theta\ (p\nmid2n), \qquad \Theta([Y'])\ne0 . \tag{R0} \] where \([Y']\) denotes the twisted real Kummer class.
why: EC3: Theta weights each real circle of X_0(n) under sigma=w_n c by psi(a)+psi(a)^{-1}, a = ideal class of the anti-linear isogeny S (S^2=n) in a real quadratic order; Hecke eigenlaw Theta T_p = tr W(Frob_p) Theta. Paper itself flags it as "The new ingredient". No neighbour found in searches (see novelty).

name: The rank-two Hecke module
statement: There is a free rank-two \(A\)-module \(P\), with Galois action of cyclotomic determinant and residual representation \(W\), such that \begin{equation} M=P\otimes_A D. \end{equation} Here Galois acts only on \(P\), \(D\) is a multiplicity lattice free over \(\mathbb Z_2\), and \(P\) rationally carries the primitive newform representations in the Hecke factor. No freeness of \(D\) over \(A\) is asserted or needed. All these primitive forms are non-CM. Their levels equal the specified level away …
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: Parity on the primitive components
statement: If \(g\) is one of the primitive components or its quadratic twist and has odd functional sign, its two-adic characteristic-zero Kummer Selmer dimension over \(\mathbb Q\) at the chosen embedding is odd.
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: The modified local conditions
statement: For \(j>0\), the subcomplex \(U_j\) splits off and is exactly self-orthogonal for conjugate local duality. The resulting complex \(C\) has a perfect self-duality and a minimal square model \(\delta_C:F\to G\) in degrees \(1,2\). The full strict problem also has square amplitude \(1,2\).
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: Residual transversality
statement: The moving inert primes can be chosen so that \[ (\det\delta_C)|_{t=\mathfrak m_A=0}\ne0 \tag{R1} \] and likewise for the full strict determinants on \(P\) and \(T_2E_0\).
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: An integral alternating presentation
statement: There is an integral matrix \(H\) such that \begin{equation} K'=K_b+\delta_C^tH\quad\hbox{is invertible}, \qquad K'\delta_C\quad\hbox{is alternating}. \end{equation} The common rank of \(F,G\) is even. The element \[ \mathcal P=\operatorname{Pf}(K'\delta_C) \] is regular and remains nonzero after reduction in \eqref{eq:R1}. Its Pfaffian adjugate, denoted \(\#(K'\delta_C)\), satisfies \[ \#(K'\delta_C)K'\delta_C=\mathcal P\,1. \]
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: The cofactor lift
statement: Let \(\eta\) be a closed degree-one input at \(w\), and let \(\beta:C_w[-1]\to C\) be the strict-place boundary map. Put \begin{equation} y=\#(K'\delta_C)K'\beta\eta. \end{equation} There is a global cycle \(z\), obtained from \(y\) by integral maps and an integral correction multiplied by \(\mathcal P\), such that \[ \delta_Cy=\mathcal P\,\beta\eta, \qquad \operatorname{loc}_w z=\mathcal P\eta \] in cohomology, after a consistent choice of sign. If a scalar \(c\) clears \(\eta\), it also clear…
why: Pfaffian cofactor lift of a closed input keeping the full product of auxiliary traces; integral device built on the textbook Pfaffian identity.

name: Pfaffian divisibility with repeated factors
statement: Let \(R_0\) be a commutative ring, let \(\mathsf A,\mathsf B\) be alternating matrices of even size, and let \(\Delta=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_{2r})\). Suppose \[ \mathsf A=\Delta\mathsf B\Delta,\qquad v=\Delta b, \qquad L=H\Delta \] with all matrices integral. The target of \(L\) may be any \(R_0\)-module. If \(Q_\Delta=\prod_kd_k\), then \begin{align} \operatorname{Pf}(\mathsf A)&=Q_\Delta\operatorname{Pf}(\mathsf B), \\ L\#\mathsf A\,v&=Q_\Delta H\#\mathsf B\,b. \end{align} Thus \(L\…
why: Pf(DBD)=det(D)Pf(B) and its adjugate analogue are textbook identities (Pf(X B X^T)=det X Pf B).

name: Integral cofactor divisibility
statement: Further specialize \(u_j=0\) for every \(j>0\), so that the coefficient ring is \(R_1=A[[u_0]]\). For an integral input \(\eta\), the global coordinates of the cycle in Lemma~\ref{real:cofactor-lift} are divisible by \[ Q_{\rm aux}=\prod_{j>0}\alpha_j.\tag{R2} \] For an input cleared by \(c\), the same assertion holds for \(cz\). The assertion also holds with multiplicity coefficients \(D\).
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: Inflation at the center
statement: At the all-zero center, inflation from fixed support identifies the integral degree-one global groups, including with \(M\) coefficients, and is compatible with the transport actions.
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: Divisibility over a coefficient order
statement: Let \(B\hookrightarrow\prod_\lambda B_\lambda\) be an injective map of complete Noetherian local rings, with each component map local. Put \(R_B=B[[\mathbf z,x]]\) and \(R_\lambda=B_\lambda[[\mathbf z,x]]\). Suppose \(f\in R_B\) is \(x\)-distinguished up to a unit, of degree \(d\). Then \begin{equation} R_B/(f)\longrightarrow\prod_\lambda R_\lambda/(f_\lambda) \end{equation} is injective. If \(B\) and all \(B_\lambda\) are two-torsion-free, divisibility of an integral series by \(f_\lambda\) in…
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: Paired and Pfaffian division
statement: The quotients \[ V_A=b^+ b^- /s_F,\qquad V_*=b_*^+ b_*^-/s_*,\qquad R_b=b^+/\mathcal P \tag{R3} \] are integral in the power-series rings just described. If \(V_*\) is a nonunit, then \(R_b\) is a nonunit.
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: The horizontal local logarithm
statement: There are perfect local maps \(U_w,U_{\bar w}\), exact orthogonals over the test DVR. At the generic field they are lines in degree one injecting in full local cohomology (of rank two in degree one only). At \(w\) we identify that generic line by weighted log and claim \[ d(U_w,e_{\log})=v(P_2^f(x^{-1})) \tag{R4} \] for the generic basis of log coordinate one. On the test residue field the maps inject in degree zero with no negative degrees in the conditions. At the characteristic-zero center o…
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: An integrally controlled logarithmic input
statement: There is a closed input \(\zeta\) in the degree-one \(w\)-model, in the generic Kummer lines of Lemma~\ref{real:local-log} on all primitive projections, whose weighted logarithm is \(\mathcal L\). There is a scalar clearing series \(c\) for \(\zeta\) such that \[ \overline c(u_0) :=c\big|_{2=u_j=0\ (j>0)}\ne0. \] The construction and clearing assertion are compatible with the multiplicity comparison \(M=P\otimes_A D\).
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: Identification with the Heegner class
statement: Over the generic fields, \[ Y(\mathbf u)=R_b z . \tag{R5} \]
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: Horizontal integrality and Fricke invariance
statement: Before further specialization, the global coordinates of \(z\) are integral after inverting two. Its all-zero specialization is invariant under \(w_nc\), componentwise. On a primitive component whose ordinary characteristic-zero Selmer dimension over \(K\) exceeds one, this specialization vanishes.
why: Supporting lemmas around the detector.

name: Removing the last denominator
statement: Let \(\mathcal O\) be a discrete valuation ring of residue characteristic two, with uniformizer \(\varpi\), and let \(B=\mathcal O[[u]]\). Let \(N\) be a finite free \(B\)-module. If \(v\in N[1/\varpi]\), \(cv\in N\), and the image of \(c\in B\) in \((\mathcal O/\varpi)[[u]]\) is nonzero, then \(v\in N\).
why: B[1/varpi] cap B[1/c] = B; elementary.

name: Primitivity detected at infinity
statement: The paired elliptic quotient \(V_*\) of \eqref{eq:R3} is an integral unit.
why: Unit via detector: a nonunit would give zero detector value. Uses EC3.

name: Cyclic-cubic Selmer seed
statement: There are a prime \(d\equiv7\pmod8\), a field \(K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d})\), and a positive fundamental discriminant \(h\), allowing \(h=1\), such that: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item every prime dividing \(2mN_{E_0}\) splits in \(K\), and \(\rho(d)\ne1\); \item \(h\) is a product of fresh primes congruent to one modulo eight, good for \(E_0\), split in \(K\), and prime to \(d\); \item the finite two-Selmer dimensions of \(E_0^h\) and \(E_0^{-dh}\) are zero and one, in some orde…
why: Ray-unit/Stark-unit comparison for cyclic cubic residual image.

name: Addressed conductor variables
statement: The inert prime sequences and order-conductor variables can be chosen so that \[ \rho(r_j)=1,\qquad a_{r_j}(E)\longrightarrow a_{j,*}\ne0, \qquad D\big|_{2=t=0}\ne0. \] Moreover, the old split places have nonzero Frobenius exponents, and each new place has a primitive relative inertia exponent.
why: Ray-unit/Stark-unit comparison for cyclic cubic residual image.

name: Curve divisibility
statement: With these choices, \(D_E\mid B_E\) in the integral power-series ring.
why: Ray-unit/Stark-unit comparison for cyclic cubic residual image.

name: Primitive ray determinant
statement: The class \[ z_S=e_Sz_{\rm ray} \] is a basis of the inverse determinant of the unrestricted global complex on \(\mathcal O(\tau)(1)\tau\), with support \(S'\), over the dyadic character integers. Rationally this determinant is its single \(H^1\)-line.
why: Ray-unit/Stark-unit comparison for cyclic cubic residual image.

name: Unramified logarithm lattice at two
statement: The evaluated free logarithm lattice of \(H^1(K_w,\mathcal O(\tau)(1)\tau)\) has valuation \(1+a_w\). Its torsion and the local \(H^2\) each have normalized length \(a_w\). Consequently, the strict determinant on this summand has valuation \[ v_2(\ell_wz_S)-1-a_w. \]
why: Ray-unit/Stark-unit comparison for cyclic cubic residual image.

name: Comparator determinant
statement: At every stage and high-order character selected above, \[ v_2(D)=2v_2(\ell_w z_{\rm ray})+ \sum_{q\in S,\,v_0\mid q} v_2(P_q(\chi(\mathrm{Fr}_{v_0}))). \tag{Y2} \] The two terms above the rational prime two sum to \(2a_w-2\).
why: Ray-unit/Stark-unit comparison for cyclic cubic residual image.

name: Eisenstein primitive
statement: The function \(G\) has Tate coefficients \(a_l/l\), and its three degree-two quotient logs sum to \(a_2G\). Hence \(P_2(V_2)G\) is the two-depleted antiderivative on the ordinary CM disks.
why: Ray-unit/Stark-unit comparison for cyclic cubic residual image.

name: Order labels and ray labels
statement: In either orientation, the primitive weighted order-conductor sum of \(G\) has valuation \(v_2(\ell_wz_{\rm ray})\).
why: Ray-unit/Stark-unit comparison for cyclic cubic residual image.

name: cyclic:anchor
statement: For the original curve \(E_0\), the discriminants \(h\) and \(-d\) of Lemma~\ref{cyclic:seed} satisfy \[ \an(E_0^h)+\an(E_0^{-dh})=1,\qquad X(E_0^h)+X(E_0^{-dh})=0. \] Thus Proposition~\ref{prop:anchor} holds for cyclic-cubic residual image.
why: Ray-unit/Stark-unit comparison for cyclic cubic residual image.

name: Exact two-primary BSD for almost all quadratic twists
statement: Fix an elliptic curve \(E/\mathbb Q\). For each nonzero squarefree integer \(d\), write \(E^d\) for the quadratic twist of \(E\) by \(d\), and put \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal D(X)&=\{d\in\mathbb Z:0<|d|\le X,\ d\text{ squarefree}\},\\ \mathcal D_j(E;X)&=\{d\in\mathcal D(X):s_2(E^d)=j\} \qquad(j=0,1). \end{aligned} \] Then \[ \lim_{X\to\infty}\frac{\#\mathcal D_j(E;X)}{\#\mathcal D(X)} =\frac12\qquad(j=0,1). \] For every nonzero squarefree \(d\) with \(s_2(E^d)=j\in\{0,1\}\), put \(F=E^d\). Then…
why: Corollary combining Thm 1.1 with Smith/006 Selmer distribution.

name: Discrepancy X_p(E) and normalized quotient Q_E
statement: Q_E = L^{(r)}(E,1) #E(Q)_tors^2 / (r! Omega_E Reg_E prod c_l); X_p(E)=v_p(Q_E)-v_p(#Sha).
why: Renaming of the BSD ratio (same device in M3, JSW).

name: Tame variables u_j and R=Z_p[[t,u_1..u_m]]
statement: u_j: limit along an ultrafilter of cyclic p-power characters of conductor r_{j,i} (moving primes tending p-adically to 1); 1+u_j represents a chosen generator.
why: EC2; neighbours: Taylor-Wiles patching variables, Sweeting ultrapatching, Loeffler-Zerbes ultra-Kolyvagin systems.

name: necessary lift matrix
statement: Matrix of first-order lift tests H(x,d) for a new tame direction.
why: Matrix of tame/derived height pairings.

name: jump
statement: A nonzero degree-one cohomology group of a one-sided primitive complex on a field fiber.
why: Renaming of cohomology jump locus.

name: U_w = B_w / L_w (pair quotient)
statement: Quotient of BDP-type analytic series by strict/full determinant.
cited_or_new: new instance of standard main-conjecture quotient
why: Ratio of p-adic L-function to characteristic power series = main conjecture formulation.

name: strict case
statement: r=1 and the compact Selmer line is generated by a c-invariant class a with all localizations zero.
why: The zero-localization case excluded by hypothesis in Skinner 2020 and handled by Zhang 2014 via Kolyvagin.

name: psi=(1+t)^ell, M_b^eta = V tensor R_b(psi^eta), R_b=k[t]/(t^b)
statement: Tame deformation of V over a truncated Artin ring via the ultralimit additive character ell.
why: EC2.

name: b_* (1 or 3) and the two incompatible lengths
statement: Upper bound length < b_* vs lower bound length >= b_*.
why: Length-comparison contradiction is the SU/Ribet template, here over R_b.

name: square order / rectangular order (Kato class smoothing)
statement: Two orderings of smoothing data for Siegel-unit Kato classes.
why: Kato smoothing (c,d) conventions.

name: label / pure dimension (graph model of 2-Selmer)
statement: Combinatorial labels and edges for twist-by-product 2-Selmer computations.
why: Monsky-matrix / graph models of 2-descent (Heath-Brown, Swinnerton-Dyer, Kane, Smith).

statement: Given Selmer classes x (strict) and d (opposite strict) with locally trivial cup product and a cochain primitive u (du = x cup d), the first-order obstruction to deforming x along a tame character ell_i at a moving prime q_i is H_gamma(x,d) = z_gamma(x,d;u) - z_gamma(x^c,d^c;u^c), z_gamma = u(gamma) - e((V(gamma)-1)^{-1}x(gamma), d(gamma)), gamma = limiting Frobenius. Multiplying gamma by a commutator sigma=[g,g'] in ker(G->GL(V)) changes u(gamma) by -e(a(g),d(g'))+e(a(g'),d(g)) without changin…

id: EC3: real-component detector Theta at p…
statement: An F_2-linear functional Theta on H^1(<sigma>, T_2 J), sigma = w_n c (Fricke involution composed with complex conjugation), defined by weighting each real circle of X_0(n)^sigma by psi(a)+psi(a)^{-1}, where a in Pic(O) is the ideal class of the anti-linear isogeny S (S^2=n) attached to a real point and psi is the cubic character of the real quadratic field L cutting out E[2]; it satisfies Theta T_p = tr W(Frob_p) Theta and is nonzero on the twisted real Kummer class of a Heegner trace.

Embed the pair quotient U_w in S=R[[y_1..y_n]] with new tame variables chosen so that, at every possible divisor q of U_w, the loci of simultaneous one-sided jumps have codimension >=2 in Spec S_(q,y); a height-one divisor of the enlarged quotient would force such a jump (theta implication), so the quotient is a unit, and specialization y=0 is integral.

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter on sequences of moving primes q_i with ring-class (or cyclotomic) characters of order p^{n_i}, n_i -> infinity; the p-adic ultralimit ell of these characters is an additive character on sequences of Galois elements; cohomology is computed with 'admissible' cochains (ultralimits of finite-stage cochains with one fixed denominator, identities holding to precision -> infinity). This yields Selmer complexes over Z_p[[t,u_1..u_m]] or k[t]/t^b in which t (or u_j) is a p…

id: EC5: tame-height route to the rank-one …
statement: log_omega z_b / (log_omega P)^2 = +- d_0 L'(E,1)/(Omega_0 H(P)) for the Kato class z_b and a nontorsion P, at every odd p (M1) and at 2 (M3), for all reduction types, proved by differentiating Kato classes along a tame direction, identifying the derivative with a Mazur-Tate tame height (cup reciprocity), and computing that height for Heegner points by a tame Gross-Zagier-type intersection computation at level N r^2 (spectral-height identity).

name: Heisenberg-commutator Frobenius addressing of tame directions (first-order obstruction control)
statement: For Selmer classes x, d with everywhere-locally-trivial cup product and a primitive u (du = x cup d), the obstruction to lifting x to first order along a tame character at a moving prime with limiting Frobenius gamma is H_gamma(x,d) = [u(gamma) - e((V(gamma)-1)^{-1}x(gamma), d(gamma))] - [conjugate]. On N_V = ker(G -> GL(V)) the primitive satisfies u([g,g']) = -e(x(g),d(g')) + e(x(g'),d(g)); replacing gamma by gamma [g,g']^m changes only u(gamma). Hence the obstruction matrix can be made nondeg…
why: Passes tests 2 and 3 and partially test 1: no equivalent found, but the object is a Mazur-Tate/derived tame pairing and the move (Chebotarev in a Heisenberg extension to set a cup-primitive value) is a known Massey-product technique; given the obstruction pairing, the commutator step is a one-line consequence (low pivot distance). Upgrade to N3 (F3) if an expert confirms that controlling tame first-order obstructions of Selmer classes this way has no precedent AND Test 4 (directed arm, given H_…

name: Ultralimit tame deformation variables and admissible cochains (p-unramified Iwasawa variable)
statement: Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter on sequences of moving primes q_i (r_i) with cyclic p-power characters of order -> infinity; the p-adic ultralimit ell is an additive character on sequences of Galois elements; cohomology over R_b=k[t]/t^b or Z_p[[t,u_1..u_m]] is computed by admissible cochains (ultralimits of finite-stage cochains with one denominator, identities to precision -> infinity). The resulting variable is unramified at p, so local conditions at p are those of V itself.
why: Close variant of ultrapatching and Taylor-Wiles variables; the transplant into Selmer-complex Iwasawa theory is a new use (bridge) but the concept exists. Could be argued N0 transfer; kept at N2 because the admissible-cochain cohomology over R_b with Greenberg conditions is not literally present in the neighbours (snippet-level check only).

statement: An F_2-linear functional Theta on H^1(<sigma>,T_2 J), sigma = w_n c, built by weighting every real circle of X_0(n)^sigma with psi(a)+psi(a)^{-1}, where a is the ideal class (in a real quadratic order O containing Z[sqrt n]) of the anti-linear isogeny S with S^2 = n attached to a real point, and psi is the cubic character of the real quadratic field cutting out E[2]. Proved: Theta T_p = tr W(Frob_p) Theta (p not dividing 2n), and Theta([Y']) != 0 on the twisted real Kummer class of a Hilbert-cl…

Low confidence: searches were snippet-level, real points of modular curves are a classical topic, and the device serves one residual sub-case at p=2 (limited downstream reach, so a downstream speedup is unlikely). Correctness of the Hecke eigenlaw at branch points is unchecked. Falls to N2 if an expert identifies a known Hecke-equivariant …

name: Codimension-two divisor removal by adjoining tame directions
statement: Every irreducible divisor of the integral quotient U_w is horizontal and corresponds to a one-sided Selmer jump (theta implication). After adjoining tame variables y chosen by C1 so that the tangent slices span Alt_s + Mat_{s,2} (resp. Alt_{s0} + Alt_{s1}), the simultaneous jump loci have codimension >= 2 in Spec S_(q,y); hence the enlarged quotient has no height-one divisor and is a unit; specializing y=0 keeps it a unit.
why: A new use of standard principles (pseudo-null support, generic determinantal codimension, adding variables). Depends on C1 for its spanning. Would rise to N3 (F5) only if experts find no precedent for removing horizontal divisors of a main-conjecture quotient by enlarging the tame parameter space.

name: Tame-height route to the rank-one logarithm-squared (Perrin-Riou) formula at every prime and reduction type
statement: log_omega z_b/(log_omega P)^2 = +- d_0 L'(E,1)/(Omega_0 H(P)) for the Kato class z_b, proved by differentiating Kato classes along a tame direction, identifying the derivative with a Mazur-Tate tame height via cup reciprocity, and evaluating that height on Heegner points by a tame Gross-Zagier-type intersection computation at level N r^2.
why: Known target statement, new bridge (tame heights -> Kato logarithm) built from known parts. Recorded under bridge_novelty as a candidate new bridge.

name: U(3,1) theta implication with nonaugmentation tests and growing p-level (theta-to-cusp congruence over a truncated tame ring)
statement: Holomorphic Kudla-Rallis theta family on GU(3,1) over the CM biquadratic field L, with constant terms tied to toric/Heegner periods and a bounded nonconstant Fourier-Jacobi coefficient, lifted to cusp forms mod p^M with coefficients in (O/p^M)[t]/t^b; Galois representations via Labesse transfer and BGHT; extension extraction via generalized matrix algebras gives one-sided Greenberg classes of length >= b.
why: Paper names its close antecedent (CLW); deep transfer of SU/CLW/BDP machinery with technical extensions.

name: Conjugate Bockstein alternation at 2
statement: For induced conjugate-dual coefficients over an imaginary quadratic field with split/unramified local conditions, the Bockstein pairing <x, dx> vanishes, proved via a Heisenberg central extension with commutator B.
why: Variant of the Poonen-Stoll/Flach alternation argument.

name: Pfaffian cofactor lift with repeated factors
statement: Pf(DBD) = det(D) Pf(B) and Delta #A Delta = Q_Delta #B, used to show global coordinates of a cofactor-lifted cycle are divisible by the full product of auxiliary traces, even when the traces are not coprime.
why: Textbook Pfaffian identity; the 'repeated factors' remark is a direct consequence.

name: finite-order Hecke character over F=Q(sqrt-3) and L_F(s,eta)
statement: Ray class character mod f extended by zero; L_F(s,eta)=sum eta(a)Na^{-s}=Euler product, continued meromorphically. Dirichlet L(s,chi), zeta = character mod 1.
why: Textbook (Hecke 1920).

name: quasi-Riemann hypothesis / uniform exclusion
statement: Find sigma_0<1, independent of character, conductor and height, with no zeros in Re s>sigma_0 ([BCSS] for zeta; [FG] uniform Dirichlet form).
why: The posed problem.

name: beta_*: family supremum of real parts of zeros of primitive Hecke L-functions over F (sentinel 1/2)
statement: beta_* = sup({1/2} U {Re rho: 1/2<=Re rho<=1, L_F(rho,eta)=0 for some primitive finite-order eta}).
why: Abbreviation of the classical Theta=sup Re rho, taken over a family.

name: Continuation from a common signal (Prop 2.1)
statement: If beta_*>sigma_0 and for every primitive eta a probe J_eta(Z) satisfies |J|<<Z^{C(sigma_0)+omega} and |J - f_eta|<<Z^{C(beta_*)-sigma}, with f_eta the Mellin integral of Z^{C(s)}e^{(s-5/6)^2}H_eta/L^S_F, omega,sigma uniform in eta, then contradiction.
why: Landau-type: a power saving for a Mellin-signal gives holomorphic continuation of 1/L; the uniform-in-eta margin against the family supremum is a routine packaging.

name: The 11/12 half-plane (Part I)
statement: Every finite-order Hecke L over F and every Dirichlet L is zero-free in Re s>11/12.
why: It is a (weaker) form of the goal; not a device.

name: Fixed numerators give ray characters
statement: For fixed a, n -> (a/n)_6 is a finite-order ray character (Kummer theory, Frobenius on a^{1/6}).
why: Classical Kummer theory.

name: Prime Gauss identities gamma_2(p)^3=-alpha(p); gamma_1 gamma_2 = conj(H(4)) gamma_3 gamma_2^3
statement: For primary prime p: normalized cubic Gauss sum cubed is -p/|p|; Hasse-Davenport-type relation between sextic, cubic and quadratic Gauss sums.
why: Classical cubic Gauss-sum evaluation and Davenport-Hasse product formula.

name: Quadratic four-term formula; sextic reciprocity and fixed Gauss phase
statement: Evaluation of quadratic Gauss sums Gamma(c) and a fixed finite ray phase R(a,b), G(a) absorbing sextic reciprocity.
why: Classical reciprocity / Gauss sums.

name: Smooth calculus, Gaussian annular decomposition, kernel seminorms
statement: Calculus for smooth norm profiles and Mellin/Fourier kernel bounds.
why: Routine analysis.

name: Hecke strip growth, logarithmic control, deleted Euler factors
statement: Convexity-type growth, Borel-Caratheodory log-derivative control on zero-free disks, bounds for finitely many deleted Euler factors.
why: Textbook complex analysis.

name: Completed cubic reflection (theta transformation retaining character zeros)
statement: Kubota-Patterson cubic theta: completed sums over indices cn^3 twisted by sextic symbols transform into dual sums of cusp coefficients twisted by a quadratic character, with all zero-on-nonunit restrictions retained.
why: Close variant of DR's level-aspect Voronoi formula (DR Sec. 5; Patterson-Yoshimoto).

name: Completion: indices cn^3 with c squarefree, full cube factor retained; target and ray phase acting on the whole product
statement: Completed index A=cn^3 (c sf, n arbitrary, possibly sharing primes); 'completion means retaining the full cubic factor n^3'.
why: DR cube completion.

name: Unmarked reflected block; unmarked completed-row moment
statement: Mean square over rows of reflected completed theta sums, bounded by the quadratic large sieve.
why: DR + GL combination.

name: Planar additive large sieve; balanced additive norm
statement: Large sieve for well-spaced points in C/O.
why: Huxley; Baier-Bansal.

name: Balanced low estimate
statement: At X=Y=Z^{1/2}: I_eta << Z^{1/4+eps}, via Cauchy-Schwarz of Q13 and Q14.
why: Cauchy-Schwarz of two known-type norms.

name: The base probe I_eta(X,Y,Z)
statement: Average over s (sextic Gauss sums g_{chi_s}(s,-m)) and m in O of smoothed Mellin integrals of corrected completed cubic-theta rows T_{m,s,eta}(t), twisted by target eta and fixed ray phases. Has two exact representations: reflected (low) and Poisson-in-m (high), and the principal Poisson row contains 1/L_F(s,eta).
why: Constructed auxiliary probe; same core duality as A03/A04 (candidate C1).

name: Exact Poisson series: rows H=ua^6, u sixth-power-free
statement: Poisson in m (modulus s b_* A); frequencies factor as u a^6; strict positivity M(1/6)>0 of a radial Mellin transform.
why: Standard Poisson summation over Z[omega].

name: The complete local identity (scalar Euler identity)
statement: For each sixth-power-free row u and good prime p, the local factor of the high series is an explicit rational function; for u=1 the global product is a nonzero scalar times 1/L_F(s,eta) times a holomorphic Euler product.
why: Explicit local computation enabled by the C1 duality; local-factor bookkeeping is standard.

name: Buffered zero-free bins; pointwise dyadic estimates
statement: Each non-principal row gets a buffered zero-free rectangle for its finite family of Hecke twists, with bins (i,a), a<=beta_*.
why: Bookkeeping for zero detection.

name: Two saturated witnesses (zero detector)
statement: A row with a zero in a bin a>51/100 yields an inverse (Mobius) polynomial M_r and a plain polynomial S_m with the same row character and twist height, each individually large: |M_r|^2>>U^{delta r-eps}, |S_m|^2>>U^{delta m-eps}.
why: Montgomery-Halasz zero detector; 'simultaneous saturated' pair is a refinement.

name: Sextic large sieve (primary convention)
statement: Sum_k |sum_n c_n chi_n(k)|^2 << (KD)^eps (K+D+(KD)^{2/3}) sum|c_n|^2.
why: Specialization of BGL Theorem 1.3.

name: Sextic-sieve row envelope
statement: Count of physical rows with a large inverse witness, after fixing the powerful part.
why: Standard large-sieve counting.

name: High-expansion analytics: contour moves, external tails, principal signal extraction, outer row norms
statement: Contour shifts per bin, extraction of principal residues giving a nonzero scalar times f_eta, small/large row norms.
why: Contour bookkeeping.

name: Balanced high estimate (saving 1/4800)
why: Numerical assembly.

name: Measuring row contributions against the hypothetical rightmost zero C(beta_*) (family bootstrap)
statement: 'The high estimate is measured relative to C(beta_*), not to C(sigma_0).' Rows of the Poisson side are Hecke twists of the target whose zeros are themselves bounded by beta_*; this replaces the GRH used by DR.
why: Self-referential family bootstrap; GRH replaced by the hypothetical supremum. Close to standard 'rightmost zero' arguments.

name: Quadratic transfer to Dirichlet L-functions
statement: L_F(s,chi o N) = L(s,chi) L(s,chi chi_{-3}) up to Euler factors nonzero in Re s>0; pole handled by L(1,chi_{-3})>0.

name: The compensated probe (Part II): marked-minus-rescaled prime slots with asymmetric scales
statement: I_mod(Z)=sum over slot-prime tuples of prod W_i * sum_J (-1)^{|J|} q_{p_J}^{-3/2} conj(eta(p_{J^c})) I_{eta;p_{J^c}}(X/q_{p_J},Y/q_{p_J},Z q_{p_{J^c}}); X=Z^{17/48}, Y=Z^{23/48}, slots of total length 1/6; C_II(s)=s-11/16.

name: Fixed-ray prime normalizer; prime-power Fourier sums; full finite correlations
statement: Prime counting in a fixed ray class [TZ]; local Fourier correlations retaining shared prime powers.
why: Routine.

name: Marked completion; whole-index marked reflection; quadratic-cubic norm bound; reflected energy
statement: Reflection and energy bounds for completed rows carrying prime marks.

name: Compensated low estimate; additive Gram bound; dynamic local errors
statement: Low side and local error terms for the compensated probe.

name: Marked inverse moment + canonical marked estimate (recursive two-Poisson descent)
statement: sum_{0<q_u<<Z^m} |M_u(Z^r;W) Q_u|^2 << Z^{m+eps} under r+2z<=m-c1, 2r+8z<=3m-c2, M_u a Mobius polynomial twisted by sextic symbols chi_n(u), Q_u prime-slot polynomials. Proved via a canonical family with an extra averaged squarefree label f (fourth-power symbol), closed by two masked Poisson transforms shortening the row range, terminal bound by reflected energy.

name: Masked primitive Poisson
statement: Finite Poisson summation with a coprimality mask.
why: Routine.

statement: sum_{q_u<=H} |D^{-1/2} sum_n mu(n)nu(n)chi_n(u)^{+-1} W(q_n/D)|^2 << H (HD)^eps for H>=D^{1+c} (identical to A04); amplification to sixth-power-free rows: sum_u|M_u|^2 << (H/P)(UD)^eps, P=(H/U)^{1/6}.

name: Fourth moment with short prime factors; centered coefficient; masked rectangle cancellation
statement: Mean square of products of two plain polynomials and short prime polynomials, excluding rows whose inducing character lies in the fixed finite group Theta; centered differences cancel main terms.

name: Prime amplitudes, bin prime bound, row counts from witnesses
statement: Combines inverse and plain moment bounds with selected prime slots to count rows above the floor.
why: Estimation chain.

name: Principal normalizer, compensated high exponent, endpoint certificate, order of choices

why: Numerics.

name: Least quadratic nonresidue n(p)<=C(log p)^A; deterministic poly-time square roots
statement: Via BIMS weak-GRH theorem with eps=7/16 and Tonelli-Shanks.

name: Main theorem (11/12)
statement: Every finite-order Hecke L over K=Q(sqrt-3) has no zeros in Re s>11/12; hence every Dirichlet L incl. zeta.
why: Goal statement.

name: PNT in APs: |pi(x;q,a)-Li(x)/phi(q)| << x^{11/12} log x uniformly in q<=x, absolute effective constant

name: Sextic-twisted Mobius family A_u(D)=sum_n mu(n)nu(n)chi_n(u)W(N n/D)
statement: Embed the target Mobius sum A_1(D) into a family indexed by u in O through the sextic residue symbol chi_n(u)=(u/n)_6.

name: Sixth-power rows replicate the target: A_{p^6}(D)=A_1(D)+O(D/Y)

statement: M_W(s)=W^(s)/L^S_K(s,nu) is holomorphic on Re s>11/12, contradiction at a zero.

name: Arithmetic identities: gamma_2(n)^3=mu(n)alpha(n); gamma_1 gamma_2 = mu alpha G; gamma_1 gamma_{-1}=chi_n(-1)

statement: P_h(X)=sum_d mu(d)w_h(d)/N(d) T_h(X/N(d)^3); short d by Cauchy-Schwarz, long d reduces to E at smaller scale.
why: DR.

name: Transfer estimate (two Poisson summations with enlarged row range)
statement: Remaining mean square bounded by new E at (H',X')=(H/N(b)^3, X/N(b)^3); second Poisson returns Mobius coefficients to cubic Gauss coefficients.
why: HB95/GL enlarged-range trick; the Mobius<->cubic-Gauss round trip is C1.

name: Theta realization; reflection proposition; uniformity in the twist; theta bounds
statement: c_theta(nb^3)=3^{5/2}|b| conj(chi_n(lambda)^2) gamma_2(n) (Patterson Thm 8.1 via DR (5.7)); twisted theta = combination of translates; reflection with fixed ray class twists.

statement: Goldmakher-Louvel number-field version of Heath-Brown's quadratic large sieve.
why: Cited theorem (Lean: QuadraticSieve/ re-proves it).

name: Separating variables in smooth weights
statement: Mellin separation of smooth weights.
why: Routine.

name: Uniform exclusion of Landau-Siegel zeros: (1-beta)log q >= c
statement: Absolute c>0 for every real zero in (0,1) of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet L of conductor q>=3.
why: Goal statement.

statement: sum_{p<=X, chi(p)=1} log p/p << ell + delta(log X)^2/ell; hence primes with chi(p)=-1 carry mass >= log X - C ell - ... .

name: Interpolation on a projected integer box
statement: If A:C^4->C^3 is surjective with kernel spanned by a vector with Q-independent coordinates, then polynomials of separate degrees t_j with prod(t_j-3(N-1)+1)>(4N-3)^4 interpolate on A(E_N). Proof: dimension count, nearest-point argument for an integer polytope, Lagrange interpolation on a supporting face.
cited_or_new: new proof of a multiplicity-type estimate
why: Uniform rectangular multiplicity estimate; close to Philippon/Fischler; new elementary proof.

name: Rectangle corollary; torus-derivation interpretation
statement: Rows with alpha_j<=T_j (T_1=32H^{2/3}U, T_2=T_3=32H^{-1/3}U) span; equals a rectangular multiplicity estimate for derivations D_j on (C^x)^4.

name: Biquadratic auxiliary field K=Q(sqrt d, sqrt 2), points theta_n=n1+n2a+n3b+n4ab, map A=(theta, sigma theta, sigma tau theta)
statement: Adjoin sqrt2 so that, for inert p (chi(p)=-1), Frobenius is sigma or sigma tau (both among the three used conjugates), and A has rank 3 with Q-independent kernel.

statement: Retain a row iff it increases the K-span of lower-weight rows; then S_2/S_1 <= (C_0/c_0)/H: almost all degree sits in the Frobenius-relevant coordinate.

statement: a^p == -a, b^p == (2/p) b mod p, so theta^p == sigma(theta) or sigma tau(theta).

name: Divisibility Delta in p^{E_p}R, E_p=sum floor(alpha_1/p), via unitriangular row replacement
statement: Replace theta^{alpha_1} by theta^r(theta^p-g_p(theta))^k; the change is a combination of strictly lower-weight rows (weight drops by m(p-H)), so the determinant is unchanged while each replaced row is divisible by p^k.

statement: (1/4)log|N Delta| <= (M/2)log M + (S1+S2)(log N + ell/2 + log 8) vs >= S1(log U - C ell - ...) - CMU with log N = (3/4)log U; limit gives 1 <= 13/16+1/16=7/8.

why: Neither the goal nor L contains sextic-twisted Mobius families or theta coefficients attached to 1/L; the device makes the reciprocal of an L-function visible to an automorphic form (non-analytic). It is the entire analytic engine of both A and Q (Lean: Moments+Eisenstein+GaussSum+Descent+Inversion+Reflection+QuadraticSieve ~ 56% of the zeta DAG). Reused as a device by release family 029 (Hecke zero-free half-plane over cyclotomic fields containing mu_12).
