why: No source found connecting interpolation determinants / Frobenius congruences with Siegel zeros; the argument is short and decisive (1 <= 7/8). Weighted greedy ordering to concentrate degree in the Frobenius-active coordinate is not in Laurent/Philippon/Fischler.

name: Family bootstrap: measure every row against the hypothetical rightmost zero beta_* of the whole Hecke family, with saturated two-witness zero detector (replace…
why: Lets Q control Hecke-twist rows unconditionally.

name: Compensated probe: marked-minus-rescaled prime slots with asymmetric scales (11/12 -> 7/8)
why: Specific design not found elsewhere; drives the improvement to 7/8.

name: Sixth-power row replication / amplification: chi_n(p^6)=1_{p not | n} so the target recurs ~Y/log Y times in the family
why: Short and decisive in A.

name: Sextic-twist Mobius <-> cubic-theta duality
statement: Twist the Mobius sum of a Hecke character over Q(sqrt-3) by the sextic residue symbol chi_n(u) and average over u in a box longer than the column range. Poisson summation in u produces sextic Gauss sums gamma_{-1}(n), which combine with mu(n) through gamma_2(n)^3=mu(n)alpha(n) into cubic Gauss sums, i.e. Kubota-Patterson theta coefficients. The theta transformation turns the dual sums into quadratically twisted sums controlled by the quadratic large sieve, and a Heath-Brown-type recursion close…
why: No equivalent found (test 1, searches A-E); non-analytic; load-bearing. F5: the device is a change of representation, recasting the reciprocal of an L-function (Mobius sums) as theta-coefficient sums through a sextic Fourier duality. The N3 is provisional and fragile under the strict rule, because each ingredient is classical. It falls to N2 if DR's full text (or Heath-Brown/Patterson) contains the Mobius-family-to-theta step, even in the reverse direction, or if test 4 shows strong models prop…

name: Family bootstrap on beta_* with saturated two-witness zero detector
statement: Suppose the supremum beta_* of zero real parts over the whole primitive Hecke family exceeds sigma_0. Measure every Poisson row against Z^{C(beta_*)}. Rows with zeros above the floor yield simultaneous large inverse and plain Dirichlet polynomials (saturated witnesses), which moment bounds count. This replaces DR's GRH.
why: Refined zero detector plus a standard supremum bootstrap; partly analytic; shown unnecessary at 11/12 by A.

name: Compensated probe (marked-minus-rescaled prime slots, asymmetric scales)
statement: At each slot prime p, replace the probe by conj(eta(p)) I_{eta;p}(X,Y,Zq_p) - q_p^{-3/2} I_eta(X/q_p,Y/q_p,Z), composed over K disjoint slots; X=Z^{17/48}, Y=Z^{23/48}; this cancels the scalar prime Euler contribution, leaving sextic-character prime factors, and moves C(s) from s-2/3 to s-11/16.
why: Improves an exponent inside the C1 framework with a mollifier-like local device; chain depth 3 (needs C1, C2).

name: Sixth-power row replication / amplification
statement: chi_n(p^6)=1_{p not | n}, so A_{p^6}(D)=A_1(D)+O(D/Y) for ~Y/log Y primes; the family mean square bounds the target.
why: Standard amplification, trivial once C1 is in place.

name: Strengthened recursive families (canonical E(H,X,F), marked inverse moment, plain fourth moment)
statement: Mean squares are run over a family carrying an extra squarefree label f with chi_n(f)^4 (A) or prime-slot marks (Q); two Poisson transforms per step contract (H,X) with H/X fixed.
why: Templated strengthening of the induction hypothesis (add a parameter / carry a tracked quantity): capped at N2.

name: Weighted Frobenius interpolation determinant for Landau-Siegel zeros
statement: In K=Q(sqrt d, sqrt2), form the determinant of monomial rows theta^{a1}(sigma theta)^{a2}(sigma tau theta)^{a3} over a box of points, rows chosen greedily in the weight order a1+H(a2+a3). For inert p>H, theta^p == sigma(theta) or sigma tau(theta) mod p, so a unitriangular row replacement shows p^{sum floor(a1/p)} | Delta. A Siegel zero makes inert primes carry mass ~log U, while the archimedean bound only allows (3/4)log U.
why: The divisibility device is a close variant of Dobrowolski/Cantor-Straus. Under the strict rule, a known mechanism imported from Lehmer's problem is transfer plus a new bridge, and the weighted ordering is a variant. Upgrade to N3 (F3) if an expert judges the weighted greedy determinant with Frobenius-to-conjugate replacement materially different from Cantor-Straus, or if test 4 shows it is not proposed even when Cantor-Straus is in context.

name: Interpolation on a projected integer box (uniform rectangular multiplicity estimate)
statement: Surjective evaluation on A(E_N) for polynomials of separate degrees t_j with prod(t_j-3(N-1)+1)>(4N-3)^4, uniform in A; proof by nearest-point argument.
why: A uniform zero estimate with a new elementary proof; close to Philippon/Fischler.

name: Thm main: H10 over Q is undecidable
statement: No algorithm decides, for f in Z[X_1..X_n] with n part of the input, whether f has a zero in Q^n.
why: Goal, not a device.

name: Diophantine model of integer arithmetic
statement: Diophantine subset of some Q^k representing Z with Diophantine graphs of + and x.
why: Cornelissen-Zahidi 2000.

name: recursively enumerable / Diophantine relation
statement: Standard r.e. and Diophantine relations on positive integers.
why: Textbook.

name: Finite rational tests: Herbrand-style ground-instance tests decided by the H10(Q) oracle
statement: For nonconstant f, an effective sequence of finite tests, each a finite conjunction of ground instances of the Skolemized theory T+{f(a)=0}+Phi, translated into finitely many rational-solvability queries; f has an integer zero iff every test succeeds. Run integer search and test-failure search in parallel.
why: Scaffold = Herbrand/Gilmore/compactness (N0 transfer from logic/automated reasoning). Using it to get H10(Z) <=_T H10(Q) without a Diophantine model: no precedent found in quick search (Yuyama's notes, snippet only, say the only known undecidability method goes through Diophantine models).

name: F=Q(sqrt2), d=75-53sqrt2 (norm 7), E: y^2=x^3-d^2x and its conjugate E^sigma
statement: Quadratic twists of y^2=x^3-x by d and d^sigma over F; at split primes r with (7/r)=-1 the reductions of E and E^sigma have opposite Frobenius traces.
why: Choice of a rank-one curve over a quadratic field is the Poonen/Shlapentokh rank-stability pattern.

name: Prop ell:rank: rank E(F)=1, mE(F)=ZP
statement: Two-isogeny descent over the PID Z[sqrt2]: |im alpha|=8 (torsion classes 1,-1,d,-d plus alpha(Q)), im alpha'={1}, so rank 1.
why: Hand descent; checked arithmetic of Q and sign patterns.

name: Elliptic point data T_a and coordinate functions x_0..y_2
statement: For a in R: T_0=O, T_1=P, T_{a+a'}=T_a+T_{a'}, T_a in mE(F_R), a!=0 => T_a finite with xy!=0; coordinates written as (x0+x1 sqrt2)/x2 etc. with ring-valued functions.
why: An additive homomorphism R -> E(F_R) is the Diophantine-model idea of Poonen 2002/Cornelissen-Zahidi applied to an abstract ring.

name: Index map eta: R -> *Z with T~_a = eta(a)P
statement: Transfer of mE(F)=ZP; eta injective, additive, eta(1)=1, NOT multiplicative.
why: Index of a point = Poonen 2002/Cornelissen-Zahidi indices, transferred to a nonstandard model.

name: Formal parameter z=-x/y, formal logarithm ell and truncation ell_K
statement: Standard formal group logarithm, truncated at degree K.
why: Textbook.

name: Prop ell:formal: valuation of index ratios and truncated-log approximation
statement: For p outside S_E, v(z(nP)/z(n'P))=v_p(n/n'); if p>K+1 and v_p(n/n')>=0, ell_K(z(nP))/ell_K(z(n'P)) = n/n' mod p^K; same for E^sigma.
why: Paper names Poonen 2002 Lemmas 9, 11 as precedent (05-elliptic.tex:110-118).

name: Lemma red:local-comparison (paired conjugate-curve test)
statement: If at a (possibly nonstandard) prime q there are h, j_0 independent of a with (i) ell_K-ratio of T_{ha},T_h congruent to a mod q^K and (ii) z(T^sigma_{(h-4)a})/z(T^sigma_{j0}) divisible by q^K, then every a~ is q-integral and a~ = eta(a) mod q^K.
why: Close to Poonen 2002 Lemma 11 (formal group approximating a square by a coordinate quotient); the conjugate-curve integrality trick is new as far as checked.

name: Thm hei:height (five-point height estimate); contact forms L_b, contact primes, contact radical M_S(s)
statement: There are five points C in P^1(Q) (incl. infinity), finite S and H,c>0 with h(s) <= H M_S(s)^c, where M_S(s) is the product of primes q not in S at which some contact order v_q(L_b(u,v))-min(v_q u,v_q v) is odd.
cited_or_new: new statement; method follows von Kaenel
why: Close variant of von Kaenel 2013 Prop 9.9 (Q-virtual GL2-type schemes, polynomial in radical) applied to the disc-210 Shimura curve; the odd-contact radical (only odd contact ramifies) is Beckmann/Darmon-Granville style.

name: Cor hei:enlarge-exceptions
statement: Enlarging S changes H but not c.
why: Immediate.

name: Cor pri:integer-coverage (ordinary contact representations)
statement: For every K, A in Z, Y_0, integers u1,u2,v (u3=Av-u1-u2) such that the 13 numbers v, L_b(u_i,v) are each +-k r with k in a fixed finite K and r>Y_0 a prime split in F, good for E and E^sigma, with local witnesses h, j_0 at both places.
why: GTZ application; the design (13 forms, two places, two curves) is new.

name: Recursive theory T with the representation axiom; branch ideals p+-; 'formal for this localization'
statement: Ring axioms (domain, char 0, sqrt2 not in Frac R), point axioms, and for every ordinary K: every A in R is u1/v+u2/v+u3/v where each contact value is eps k r with R/rR a field, sqrt2 = +-B_r mod r, and at each branch nonzero h, j_0 (independent of a) satisfying ring-language versions of tests (i),(ii) for all a in R.
why: No neighbour found for a substructure-robust forall-exists axiom that bounds heights of all ring elements through contact radicals.

name: Lemma red:standard-model: T is recursive and Z (T_a=aP) is a model
statement: Integer model via I14; constants hardcoded; existence suffices (non-uniform constants).
why: Routine verification.

name: Prop par:pole-parity: a positive existential Phi true on Z forcing even pole orders outside S_1
statement: Phi(b) holds for all b in Z; if Phi(b) and q not in S_1 then v_q(b)<0 implies v_q(b) even.
why: Close relative of Demeyer-Van Geel 2006 existential odd-valuation predicates and Cornelissen-Zahidi 2007 predicates; new is the all-primes one-sided pole restriction via a pair of twists.

name: Skolemized ground-term constraints (a)-(d)
statement: Rational variable per ground term; ring-operation, functionality, ground universal instances, and Phi on every term value; DNF and sum of squares turn each finite part into finitely many H10(Q) queries.
why: Herbrand 1930; Gilmore 1960; Davis-Putnam 1960 (the SAT/automated-reasoning analogue).

name: Lemma red:compactness: success of all tests gives R in *Q modelling T with root a and Phi on R
statement: Elementary diagram + ground constraints are finitely satisfiable, so compactness gives an elementary extension with an embedded term ring.
why: Textbook model theory.

name: Lemma red:coarsening: odd valuation selects a tested branch
statement: Quotient value group by convex subgroup J generated by negative values on R; Phi makes all J-values even, so odd v_q(r) is positive mod J; the coarsened place centres on exactly one of p+-.
why: Valuation coarsening standard; combination specific.

name: Prop red:index-congruence: a~ = eta(a) mod q^K at every contact prime q of every slope
statement: Combines I20 and I11.
why: Composition of I11 and I20.

name: Prop red:finite-test-success: uniform height bound h(A~) << B for all A in R and canonical-height squeeze
statement: delta=f(eta(a)) is a single ambient integer with |delta| <= C B^D; every contact prime of every slope divides delta to order K>=cD, so M_K^K | delta and h(slope) <= H|delta|^{c/K} << B; hence h(A~) << B for every A in R; applied to x(T_{a_j}) and canonical height 2 h^(P) eta^2 + O(1) this forces B bounded, eta(a_j) standard, a_j integers.
why: Canonical-height quadratic growth vs linear bound is classical (Silverman; also GFPV 2025, family 242), but the 'one error integer delta controls the height of the whole ring through contact radicals' squeeze has no neighbour found.

name: Proof of Thm main (parallel search + DPRM)
statement: Parallel search decides H10(Z); contradiction with DPRM.
why: Standard.

name: Curve family E_l: y^2=x(x-l)(x+3l) and formula Phi(b) (U=b(1-dt^2)/(1+dt^2), H'=b'(b'-U^2), points on E_e and E_{eH'} with x in b'Q^{x2})
statement: Phi(b): b=0 or exist m, m_d, t, e with the auxiliary values such that both E_e and E_{eH'} have a rational point with x in b'Q^{x2}.
why: pi/3-congruent-number family (Mokrani 2020; Wei-Guo 2022) supplies the curves; the two-twist parity trick is new.

name: Lemma par:soundness (odd pole => contradiction)
statement: If v_q(b)<0 odd, v_q(H')=3k so e and eH' have opposite parity; on the twist with even valuation every x has even valuation, contradicting x in b'Q^2.
why: Elementary.

name: Multiplier lists M, D_m and choice of t by weak approximation

why: Routine.

why: Local computation.

name: Monsky/Redei matrices K, N=K+D_s, reciprocity identity K+K^t=ss^t+D_s
statement: 2-Selmer matrices for the family.
why: Monsky appendix to Heath-Brown 1994; Wei-Guo 2022 Sec. 4.

statement: Under ker K=<1,1_B>, lambda not in im K.
why: Standard descent with chosen kernel targets.

name: Lemma par:global-point: rank 1, Sha[2]=0, (beta,1) realized by a rational point

why: Invocation (provenance: model-produced).

statement: Auxiliary primes q_0 (type (1,1)) and I (type (0,0)); K^#=K+lambda a^t, projection T=Id-1_B a^t, deleted matrix M_0=[[A,C],[C^t,0]] nonsingular; J-diagonal toggles via multilinear determinant; realize symbols by CRT+Dirichlet.

statement: No elliptic points, area 8, Riemann-Hurwitz forces r=5, g(X*)=0; each label's branch value is Galois-fixed hence rational.
why: Tabulated.

statement: Symplectic rep rho(g)x = x gbar, psi=Trd(Delta x ybar); fibres over a common base point geometrically isogenous; moduli map nonconstant.
why: Textbook (Deligne; Guitart-Molina).

statement: Splitting field K_0 of bounded degree unramified outside S and primes dividing M; fibres have good reduction outside S.

statement: R_l(g)=beta(g) mu~_g o g = r_l + r_l; odd, de Rham, HT weights 0,1; r_2 modular via OddRegularFontaineMazurAtTwo Thm 1.1.

statement: Single algebraic trace from reduction; Chebotarev.
why: Standard.

statement: Tame of exponent <= 2 at large primes of T; uniform upper ramification cut at fixed small primes.
why: Standard.

statement: J_1(N) ~ A x D_0 over L', Javanpeykar height of J_1(N) <= C N^12, Zarhin trick, Gaudron-Remond isogeny bound with dimension 8 g_0, Bost lower bound.

name: Lemma pri:pattern (prime patterns)
statement: Fixed finite K: for every A and B, the 13 forms equal +-k r with primes r>B, r=1 mod 8, r=3 mod 7, split in F, good for E,E^sigma, gcd(d1,d2)|4, r not dividing d1 d2.

statement: Selberg lambda^2 on squares.

statement: Oracle reduction + Davis 1973 normal forms.

statement: E/Q with E(Q)[2]!=0 and s_2(E) in {0,1}: ord_{s=1}L = rank = s_2 and Sha finite (any reduction at 2).

statement: If on arbitrarily large cubes h_x=h_0 prod (q*)^{lambda_q(x)} every nonzero vertex has nonzero central value with D(h_x)<=B, then L(E^{(h_0)},1)!=0 with D(h_0)<=B+C_E.

statement: Uniform denominator without loss in |G|.

statement: Poitou-Tate length bookkeeping.

statement: Adjoin fresh primary primes activated by nonzero linear forms so that one or two binary symbols equal 1 at every nonzero address; networks act as finite-difference operators whose coefficients are grounded-Laplacian minors.

why: Converts purely local congruence data at infinitely many (nonstandard) primes into one archimedean bound on the whole ring; that is exactly what a Diophantine model cannot give under Mazur's conjecture. The 'same delta for every A' observation (02-reduction.tex:810-814) is tiny but nowhere in the goal; the representation axiom is a gadget built only to make it work. Quick searches (abc-conditional H10(Q); height comparisons; Turing-reduction strategies) found no precedent: GFPV 2025 needs heigh…

why: It is the strategic move that makes Mazur's conjecture irrelevant: no Diophantine set or model is produced (07-consequences.tex:105-107). Snippet of Yuyama's notes: the only known method for undecidability goes through a Diophantine model.

name: Pole-parity existential formula Phi via a pair of twists of y^2=x(x-l)(x+3l)
why: New positive-existential predicate with an all-primes one-sided restriction.

name: Five-point odd-contact height estimate (Shimura curve disc 210 + von Kaenel)
why: Unconditional abc-type bound for an orbifold P^1 with five half-points; precisely tuned to parity.

why: Embeds one twist into a (Z/2)^b family of determinants; Chevalley-Warning gives a nonzero vertex congruent to the base mod 2^M; bounds transfer with no loss in b.

name: Contact-radical height squeeze (representation axiom + single error integer delta + canonical-height squeeze)
statement: Every element A of the tested ring is u1/v+u2/v+u3/v with all 13 contact values equal to +-k r for tested elements r; at every contact prime the root coordinates agree with their elliptic indices mod q^K, so M_K(slope)^K divides the one integer delta=f(eta(a)); the five-point estimate then gives h(A)<<B for all A in R; quadratic canonical height of eta(a_j)P forces B=O(1).
why: No neighbour found in the searches listed. Ingredients are classical, and the same release (242) uses the canonical-height half, so discoverability may be moderate. Holds as a candidate only; informal list, since no Lean exists (excluded from the shortlist for that reason, not on merit).

name: Finite-test (Herbrand + compactness) Turing reduction using negative H10(Q) answers
statement: f has an integer zero iff every finite set of ground instances of the Skolemized T+f(a)=0+Phi is satisfiable in Q; failure is detected with the oracle.
why: Under the strict rule, importing Herbrand/compactness refutation search is transfer. The bridge (using it to sidestep Mazur's obstruction for H10(Q)) is recorded as a NEW bridge in bridge_novelty, not as a jump.

statement: j0=d2, h=0 mod d1, h=4 mod d2 r^K; test (ii) on E^sigma gives eta(ha)=4 eta(a) mod q^K, which makes the truncated-log ratio on E equal eta(a) mod q^K without multiplicativity.

statement: For a closed word with singleton prime set U, the deletion-damaged centred word expectation is at most 1_lit-consistent * b_L * E[R |Delta G|], where Delta G = sum_{H subset U} (-1)^{|U|-|H|} G_H runs over 'hybrid' residue configurations (singletons in H overwritten by their forced residues). If |U| > L^{1/4} and Delta G != 0, expanding G = prod_w (1 - I_w) shows that some single hybrid contains positive witnesses whose prime supports cover U. A minimal cover yields T = L^{1/12} witnesses with …
why: This is the trace's 'turning point' and the most original-looking device in Part I. But the problem it solves is stated verbatim in HR21 section 5. The principle that only deletion terms covering every singleton survive is the content of Pilatte Lemma 9.2 together with the rank argument of Prop. 9.1, and both are in L. 007's contribution is to replace the truncated sieve, with its coefficient and remainder bounds, by an exact discrete-derivative identity used only for existence, plus a minimal-…

name: Two-band weighted divisor graph: uncentred heavily weighted core primes plus vertex-normalised centre primes with non-mean-zero centring theta = beta_Z^2
statement: Edge kernel g_d(x,y) = w_d(x)w_d(y) A^{omega_C(d)} 1_{d_C | x} prod_{p|d, p in Z}(1_{p|x} - theta/p). The core band C (weight A = e^{2 kappa}, uncentred) supplies size and cutoff savings; the centre band Z (weight 1) supplies cancellation. With vertex weight W(x) = prod_a beta_a^{-omega_a(x)} and closed-walk products normalised by W at each departure, a centre prime on a single good edge has total multiplier theta(1-theta/p) on its lit residue and -theta beta_Z^{nu_p(a)}/p elsewhere. The choice…
why: This is the strongest candidate in the family. It is insight-coded in the trace, passes test 2, and is load-bearing for the qualitative theorem. No arithmetic precedent was found. Two things stop it at N2. (a) theta = beta_Z^2 is the standard 'centre by the expectation under the operative measure' rule, applied once vertex normalisation has been chosen. The trace shows beta^2/p centring already present in the single-band design taken from Pilatte, so the matching is not where the step lies. (b)…

name: Finite residue comparison via Braverman's bounded independence, with the Alon-Goldreich-Mansour exact-independence correction
statement: Every event given by a depth-at-most-20, size-at-most-exp(L^6) circuit in residue-equality tests modulo primes up to e^L has the same probability, up to e^{-L^{10}}, under a uniform origin in any interval of length at least exp(L^A/2) as under the independent product law. Proof: encode residues by B = L^15 jittered dyadic bits; bound t-wise bit marginals by CRT; correct to exact t-wise uniformity by a Fourier/AGM step; apply Braverman (Corollary 2).
why: A known theorem (Braverman) and a known correction (AGM) are imported into a role that HR21 filled with the Kubilius model. By the codebook, cross-field transfer is N0, however large the field distance. The first application of bounded-independence fooling of AC0 to analytic number theory that we found is recorded as a new bridge, not as a eureka step.

name: Fixed-scale order of limits (graph fixed at B, X -> infinity first, then B -> infinity) with finite-prime stability of uniform non-pretentiousness
statement: Since uniform non-pretentiousness has no rate, all graph parameters are fixed at an auxiliary scale B. The analytic centring error is o(1/B) as X -> infinity, against B^{-1-c*/2} from the graph; then B -> infinity.
why: Conceptually important to the qualitative theorem, but a standard device.

name: First-visit tree organisation of closed walks with the exact weighted-subtree identity
statement: Walks are organised by their first-visit tree. Sum_Q u_a(Q) = S_a(T) = sum_v (1 - beta_a^{s(v)}), proved by a branching-percolation probability argument, cancels the background normalisation exponential exactly.
why: A standard encoding plus an elementary identity, tuned to C2's weights.

name: Conditional cylinder sieve: truncated inclusion-exclusion applied after conditioning, with centre residues left unconditioned
statement: Vertex-deletion conditions are expanded by a finite-cylinder truncation of the intersection poset (Rota chain expansion) after conditioning on fixed coordinates, so that centre-prime residues stay unconditioned and signed averages can be taken before absolute values.
why: An adapted construction with a precedent the paper names. Its new feature (conditioning before truncation, centre coordinates free) is the Part II counterpart of C1's purpose.

name: J disjoint centred prime supplies with whole-tuple nonbacktracking matrix and spectral passage
statement: Steps carry one prime from each of J supplies of reciprocal mass ~W, giving W^J mass against an operator cost (C sqrt W)^J. H_{d,d'} = 1_{d != d'} A_{d'} forbids repeating a whole tuple consecutively. J ~ log log X gives a power-of-log saving.
why: Retrieved framework, moved to ordinary averages

name: Padding divisors: uncentred squarefree q from primes not 1 mod 5, weight 4^{omega(q)}, normalised by sqrt(w), w = 5^{omega_Q}, for anti-concentration in short …
statement: An independent padding factor q makes the distribution of log(dq) spread at scale eta = e^{-J} (characteristic-function decay via PNT mod 5), so that each of the O(L/eta) short multiplicative intervals carries mass with a 1/L edge normalisation. The forest code counts repetition patterns uniformly over padding values, so padding weights are summed afterwards in one residue environment.
why: A constructed auxiliary object with no named precedent, but it implements a standard smoothing principle. It is also the Part I sibling of C2's two-role design, and that sibling weakens C2.

name: Random-prime rank estimate over R for lit-consistency congruences
statement: If B in M_r(Z) is nonsingular over R and primes are drawn from a measure with max atom alpha, then the probability that B x = f(x) mod the primes is small. This gives a saving for words with many independent lit-consistency pairs without invertibility modulo the summed primes.
why: Adapted from HR21 sections 6-7 to the present coefficients

name: Single narrow core band in place of layered core bands (second insight step)
statement: One narrow upper band of core primes replaces several layered core bands
why: Constructed simplification inside C2. Graded only because the PLAN makes every insight step a candidate.

name: Mixed-difference / common-hybrid witness cover (Part II, PV9)
against: Nearest neighbours: Pilatte 2026 Lemmas 11.6, 13.1, 13.6 (witnesses, active primes) and HR21's singleton cancellation. The 'pairwise changes' variant it improves on was probably closer to them. The identity E[(1_{Z=a} - 1/p)F(Z)] = (1/p)E[F(a) - F(Z)] is elementary, and mixed differences are standard (Gowers-type / inclusion-exclusion). Triggered by an explicitly stated requirement one sentence e…
why: The summarizer calls it the 'combinatorial turning point', and the model writes it in VERBATIM: the idea is visibly the model's. No reference is invoked at L164-171, and the paper gives no attribution for the mixed-difference / hybrid mechanism itself; it attributes only the downstream active-prime and triangular steps to Pilatte. It is non-analytic. Hybrids (configurations overwritten at a subset H of singleton coordinates) and the existence-only algebraic expansion of prod(1 - I_w) appear now…

name: Two-band weighted divisor graph with non-mean-zero centering theta = beta_Z^2 matched to endpoint normalization (Part I, PV4)
against: Weights A^{omega(d)} and centering at beta^2/p were already present in the single-band version (L66-68), modelled on Pilatte, so the split is one design step from a retrieved template. Driven by stated local problems (C12, C13), so conflict-driven refinement rather than a hidden leap. Its pay-off needs the first-visit tree and the conditional cylinder sieve (chain depth 2), whose novelty is low.
why: Coded as an insight backtrack: a viable single-band design is replaced by a structural re-design, with no reference invoked. The paper stresses that the center factor 'is not itself mean zero under uniform residues' and cancels only through the closed-walk normalization. This departs from the mean-zero centered factors of HR21 and Pilatte. Decoupling savings (core) from cancellation (center) is what lets a qualitative result work with no rate in the non-pretentiousness hypothesis.

name: Bounded-independence (Braverman AC0) bridge for comparing finite integer intervals with independent residues (Part II, PV8)
against: Transfer of a known theorem is not a eureka step by the project's codebook. A known route exists: Linial-Nisan's approximate inclusion-exclusion links Brun-type sieves and bounded independence (the paper sets out the lineage). The paper needs an extra correction to EXACT bounded independence (Alon-Goldreich-Mansour) that is not visible in the trace.
why: Large field distance (TCS pseudorandomness -> multiplicative number theory). It is invoked right after a stated obstruction, so the retrieval is targeted. The encoding of deletion predicates as constant-depth circuits is problem-specific.

name: Fixed-scale order of limits (graph at fixed B, X -> infinity, then B -> infinity) (Part I, PV5)
against: A routine order-of-limits device; well known in analysis and in MRT-type arguments.
why: It is the conceptual key to a qualitative every-scale result under a rate-free hypothesis, and it inverts the entropy-decrement failure (C4).

name: stratum smoothness over V
statement: X and every irreducible component of every nonempty intersection of components of E, restricted to f^{-1}(V), are smooth over V=Y\Supp D.

name: Section construction (Prop 1.3)
statement: If 0!=s in H^0(X,mL_X), then kappa(Y,L_Y)>=0; if kappa(Y,L_Y)=0 and s|_{X_y}=0 for some y in V, there is 0!=tau in H^0(Y,aL_Y) with tau(y)=0.

name: negative-fiber branch
statement: If kappa(F,L_F)=-inf then kappa(X,L_X)=-inf: a nonzero section of mL_X restricts nonzero to very general fibers (open nonvanishing locus dominates), and adjunction L_X|_F=L_F.

name: injectivity of restriction when kappa(Y,L_Y)=0
statement: h^0(Y,aL_Y)<=1; choose y outside all zero divisors; then H^0(X,mL_X)->H^0(F,mL_F) injective for all m, so kappa(X)<=kappa(F).

name: reduction through the base log Iitaka fibration
statement: Positive base dimension reduced to Kodaira-zero base via log Iitaka fibration q:Y'->T and restriction to H=(q f')^{-1}(t).

name: Logarithmic Hodge input (Prop 3.1)
statement: From s, a cyclic root cover gives a pure VHS V on Y° and a nonzero u:O(-L_Y)->Gr_F^d V whose Higgs iterates have regular coefficients in the ORIGINAL log cotangent lattice Omega^1_{Y'}(log D') on every higher model, also for homogeneous tensor replacements.

name: Extension of a weight projection (Lemma 3.2)
statement: For semistable g:Z->Delta with horizontal boundary, R^j g_* Omega^i(log(V_0+H)) is locally free with weight subbundles whose quotients are Hodge-graded canonical extensions.

name: Zero test in the original source frame (Lemma 3.3)
statement: If s vanishes on f^{-1}(y), y in V, then after blowing up y and ramification of order e (m|e), coefficients of u in the pulled-back ORIGINAL O_Y(-L_Y) frame vanish to order >= e/m (ae/m for degree-a replacements).

name: Marked-period construction (Prop 4.1)
statement: From u:L->F^pV build a homogeneous tensor replacement u_*:L^a->E_0=F^{p*}A, a quotient B->S on which A descends with irreducible connected representation through an adjoint group G, an algebraic compact-flag section j_u ('marks') determined by [u_*]; full Lie period + j_u generically immersive; nef lines H, H_u with K_S+D_0+cH_u big and K_S+b_0H big.

name: Homogeneous replacement with fewest factors
statement: Choose the replacement with irreducible connected representation and minimal number of retained rational simple factors.

name: Period quotient and descent / Generic Lie stabilizer
statement: Hodge-generic rational Lie automorphisms preserving F are trivial; an algebraic quotient remembering full integral Lie period and marks exists and A descends.

name: log-log metric bigness (Lemma 4.8)
statement: Semipositive metric with log-log growth near SNC boundary computes c_1 and volumes on the compactification.

name: Initial adjoint bigness
statement: K_S+D_0+cH_u is big for large c (curvature of the period differential subbundle, Campana-Paun).

name: Boundary drop (Prop 5.3)
statement: For every component D_i of D_0 (nonidentity local monodromy on g): nu(H|_{D_i}) < nu(H); if nu(H)=0 then D_0 is empty.

name: Section estimate
statement: A+tH-eT big for large t if nu(H|_{T_i})<nu(H)=r>0.

name: Adjoint bigness (Prop 5.5)
statement: If dim S>0 then K_S+bH is big for large b.

name: Higgs tails (Prop 5.6)
statement: For a line l in h^*E_0 inducing the same compact marks, the nef line P from iterated Higgs images satisfies nu(P+h^*H)=nu(P).

name: Degree-one roots
statement: Lie-theoretic lemma on graded ideals and highest graded pieces.

name: Connection dimension
statement: Zariski closure of a horizontal leaf germ with Zariski-dense image has dim >= dim U + dim H.

name: Orbit rank
statement: Local orbit filling for joint flag maps / projective line sections of flat representations.

name: Relative Iitaka diagram
statement: Y->W->S with Kodaira-zero geometric generic fiber of x and dim W - dim S = k.

name: Extraction of source valuations
statement: Model change of W_1 so that source divisorial valuations of omega are visible.

name: Rank-one base (exact section comparison)
statement: L_W=K_W+T_W ~ K_W+B_W+M_W big over S with H^0(W,lL_W) = H^0(Y_0,l(K+D)) in divisible degrees.

name: Removal of a period twist (Prop 7.2) + Nef subtraction (Lemma 7.3)
statement: If L big on generic h-fiber, L-h^*K_S pseudoeffective, K_S+bH big, and nef P upstairs with nu(P+H~)=nu(P), Q pi^*L >=_pe P, then L is big. Lemma: A+tP-bH big for large t when nu(P+H)=nu(P).

name: Orbifold transfer
statement: P_W pseudoeffective, pi^*P_W >=_pe P; determinants of Higgs maps give O(D_i^G - a r_i L_W) -> (Omega^1(W,B_W))^{i r_i}.

name: Uniform pseudoeffective threshold
statement: L_W pseudoeffective and Q pi^*L_W >=_pe P.

name: Relative pseudoeffectivity
statement: L_W - h^*K_S >=_pe 0.

name: SmoothProjectiveVariety, ReducedSNCBoundary, IsLogPluriform, sections, HasImageDimensionAtLeast, kodaira
statement: Scheme-theoretic encodings of smooth projective C-varieties, reduced SNC boundaries, log pluriforms via function-field Kaehler differentials, and Iitaka dimension via algebraically independent ratios.

name: StratumSmoothFibration, FiberModel, VeryGenerally, ComplexPoint
statement: Encodings of hypotheses and very-general fibers.

name: exists_open_nonzero_fiber_pluriform
statement: A nonzero log pluriform on X restricts to a nonzero log pluriform on every fiber model over a nonempty Zariski open U in D.complement.

name: chart specialization machinery (LogarithmicSpecialization, FiberChartSpecialization, NumeratorChart, exists_global_specialization)
statement: Local standard-smooth charts, logarithmic numerators, and gluing of fiber specializations of pluriforms.

name: exact_canonical_adjunction / based_relative_canonical_naturality
statement: Determinant of an exact sequence of free modules splits (adjunction K_X|_F = K_F for smooth f).

name: normal_root_zero_test; original_fiber_zero_ramified_root_factor; Descent.original_coefficient_in_point_ideal_of_fiber_zero; Blowup charts
statement: Algebraic core of R08: if t^e | s and r^m = s in Frac(R) with R integrally closed, then r = t^{e/m} c; fiber vanishing puts coefficients in the point ideal; blowup chart divisibility.

name: ReverseInequalityStatement, LogarithmicSubadditivityStatement, LogarithmicAdditivityStatement, MainTheoremStatement, SectionConstructionStatement
statement: Full theorem statements written as Props; never proved.

name: inf-multiplicity orbifold base B(f,Delta) and invariant kappa(f|Delta)
statement: m(f,Delta;D)=min over source primes E over D of ord_E(f^*D) m_Delta(E); B(f,Delta)=sum (1-1/m)D; kappa(f|Delta)=inf over equivalent models of kappa(Y',K+B(f',Delta')).

name: Rank-one comparison (exact comparison for Kodaira-zero fibers)
statement: For g:(X,Delta)->W with Kodaira-zero general fiber, a root of the generator spans a Hodge line M and orders define T with B(g,Delta)<=T<=1 and H^0(X,m(K_X+Delta)) = H^0(W,m(K_W+T+M)) in divisible degrees.

name: root-character eigenspace is one-dimensional
statement: The tautological form spans the root-character part of F^dH^d of the cyclic cover.

name: Adjoint-positivity input
statement: For an extreme Hodge line L (rank-one highest step of a complex summand of a real-polarized integral VHS) on class-C B: after modification tau^*L = p^*P with p:B'->S connected fibres, S smooth projective, P nef, and K_S+aP big for some a>0.

name: Curvature and numerical dimension; restriction to a boundary component
statement: nu of the parabolic highest line = generic rank of the line map; on a boundary component the limiting line lies in a unique weight grade of the limiting MHS.

name: Strict loss of rank at the marked boundary
statement: For every component D_i with nonidentity (incl. finite) local monodromy on the retained adjoint system: nu(P|_{D_i}) < nu(P). Proof: Ax-Schanuel decomposition G=HxQ along line-map fibers, Andre normality, then cases (infinite monodromy / finite inertia).

name: boundary subtraction by section counting
statement: If A+D big and nu(J|_{E_i})<nu(J) for all components, then A+tJ big for large t.

name: The projective period quotient
statement: After modification p:B'->S, S smooth projective, tau^*L=p^*P, retained adjoint variation descends with generically immersive full period map.

name: Adjoint addition (interpolation principle)
statement: If K_W+T+M big on h-fibers, M=p^*P, P nef, K_S+a_0P big: kappa(W,K_W+T+M) >= dim(W/Y)+kappa(Y,K_Y+C). Proof: general-type addition for D+cM+eta p^*A (c<1, semiample pullback absorbed in boundary), weak positivity section of D+aM-lambda p^*A, and D+M=(1-theta)E_+ + theta E_-.

name: Effectivity after a big base twist
statement: K_{W/S}+T+p^*H has a nonzero section for every big H on S if the general p-fiber has a relative log pluricanonical section.

name: Log-general-type addition in class C
statement: If K_F+T_F big on very general fibers, C <= B(h,T), T=1 on primes over codim>=2: kappa(V,K_V+T) >= dim F + kappa(Y,K_Y+C).

name: Minimal root cover of a reduced log-Kodaira-zero pair
statement: For reduced SNC D with kappa(K_J+D)=0 the minimal root cover has one-dimensional entire top log-form space (fails for rational D: 2/5 sum of 5 points example).

name: Log subadditivity (Cor 6.2), ordinary char-0 (Cor 6.3), core dimension and core tower (Cor 6.4-6.5)
statement: Consequences of the main theorem; Cor 6.2 is the 'Foundation' input to REV.

name: Projective adjoint positivity (Thm 1.2)
statement: Rationally polarized integral pure VHS on U subset Y whose ENTIRE highest Hodge step is a line; if tau^*M ~ cJ (extended highest line) then after modification M ~ p^*L, p:Y->S connected fibres, L nef, K_S+jL big for j>>0 (M~0 if S is a point).

name: Rationally minimal variation
statement: Unique smallest rational subvariation whose filtration contains the highest line.

name: Rank and a tangential limit (tangential rank principle) + nilpotent tangential convergence
statement: If holomorphic maps f(u,.) converge as u->0 and the limiting tangential rank equals the interior rank, the nearby image lies in the limiting image; nilpotent-orbit version.

name: Boundary and ramification rank loss
statement: nu(J)=r>0; for E a component with nonzero monodromy logarithm, or fixed pointwise by a nonidentity element of the finite quotient group: nu(J|_E) < r.

name: Parabolic canonical bundle formula
statement: For Kodaira-zero geometric generic fibre: K ~ g^*(K_Y+B+M)+R with B klt effective, M nef with Hodge realization via the least-index root cover.

name: Canonical root cover has p_g = 1
statement: For kappa(C)=0 and least b with H^0(bK_C)!=0, the b-th root cover has geometric genus one, so its top form is the entire highest line of a rational VHS.

name: Nonvanishing on fibres of the period projection
statement: If kappa(Z)>=0 and K_Y+B+M big on q-fibres, M=p^*L, then the generic p-fibre has kappa>=0 (product map Y->S x Z, cotangent map h_s^*omega_Z -> omega_{W_s}).

name: Effectivity from weak positivity
statement: K_{Y/S}+B+p^*P Q-effective for P big when generic fibre has kappa>=0.

name: Interpolation D ~ lambda E_1 + (1-lambda) E_2
statement: lambda=(1-v)/(j-v), A_S = vL + lambda/(1-lambda) H ample, E_2 = K_Y+B+p^*A_S klt after Bertini; Hashizume gives kappa(E_2) >= d + kappa(Z).

name: Integral tensor replacement + transverse-loop criterion; Thom-form boundary drop (alternative proofs)
statement: Two further proofs of the boundary estimate: faithful monodromy on the moving line, transverse loops on which the line is constant; curvature/Thom-form concentration.

name: birational variation Var(f) (whole geometric generic fibre)
statement: Var(f) = min trdeg_C L over algebraically closed C subset L subset Omega such that F is birational to a base extension of an L-variety.

name: Parameter field T_0 and kbar(U) = d + dim T_0
statement: Absolute Iitaka map combined with Y; family of images g(W_z) parameterized by T_0 with C(T_0) in C(Y); contraction of a log pluriform controls the differential.

name: Analytic birational constancy criterion over a curve; poles of lifted vector fields have positive asymptotic fixed order
statement: A smooth projective family over a curve whose (minimal root cover) top Hodge line is flat is birationally constant; proof minimizes an L^{2/m} integral with fixed leading coefficient (DHP extension, Paun-Takayama Bergman weights) to show lifted vector fields have poles only of positive fixed order, contracted on a big adjoint model.

name: Marked models; constant cocycle; unramified at moving divisors; descent of the whole fiber
statement: Recover a finite normalization V' of the relative Iitaka base; finite splitting cocycle made constant; multiplicity-one component at moving divisors forces unramifiedness; purity + finite etale descent define F over b.

name: Dimension retained by interpolation (Sec. 8)
statement: Nef contribution pulled back from an adjoint-positive base replaces the Hodge line; interpolation retains the second Iitaka-base dimension.

name: threshold discriminant B_{X'} and moduli rational b-line bundle M
statement: t_P = inf a(E;Y',Delta')/ord_E(f'^*P); B=sum(1-t_P)P; M = mu^*L - K - B on every Kahler model.

name: Threshold trace equals volume extension: ord^Hodge(tau) = t_P - 1
statement: The canonical Hodge extension of the local root volume equals the moduli line on every smooth Kahler model.

name: Root eigenline and deepest residue
statement: With coefficient-one horizontal components, iterated residue identifies the root eigenline with the volume line of a deepest stratum.

name: Product family on an auxiliary compact base (spreading)
statement: Proper surjection r:P->S with a marked klt family whose fibers are realized as finite product covers (MWWWZ) over a dense open, via Douady components and proper constructibility.

name: Changing the polarization (real -> rational)
statement: A flat real automorphism of the integral local system turns a real polarization into a rational one without changing integral monodromy.

name: Descent of semiampleness through Stein factorization and norms; unit extension lemma
statement: Semiampleness descends along proper surjections; isomorphism of line bundles extends across boundary under two-sided log bounds.

name: Adjoint positivity of the entire highest Hodge line on the full-period quotient, via strict rank loss on boundary and ramification divisors
statement: Y smooth projective, V a rationally polarized integral pure VHS on a dense open U whose entire highest Hodge step is a line, M in Pic(Y)_Q with tau*M ~_Q c J (extended highest line) on an alteration. Then after modification there is p:Y->S with connected fibres onto the (normalised) full period image and a nef L with M ~_Q p*L and K_S + jL big for j >> 0. Mechanism: Brunebarbe-Cadorel gives K_S + D big; rational minimality (BFMT transcendental part) + Andre normality + a tangential rank princip…
why: No statement found in any field giving adjoint bigness K_S + jL of a possibly non-big Hodge line on the full period image with boundary and ramification absorbed; BFMT and Ambro give stronger conclusions only under the generic-effectiveness hypothesis that the Iitaka kappa(F)=0 case violates. Every ingredient is named prior art (BC, BBT, BFMT, Andre, Bakker-Tsimerman Ax-Schanuel, CKS, Siu-type volume subtraction): the candidate is their problem-specific coupling, not a transfer. Downgrade risks…

name: Adjoint-addition interpolation (general-type addition with an ample twist + one weak-positivity section with a negative twist, combined to coefficient one on M)
statement: Sections of D_W + cM + eta p*A (general-type addition, c<1) times a fixed section of D_W + aM - lambda p*A (weak positivity over a big base twist), positive rational combination cancels the ample terms and gives coefficient one on M; needs neither abundance of L nor a limit of Kodaira dimensions.
why: Short exact-section combination following Viehweg/Campana (named by the paper). Novel only in that it avoids abundance of L and limits of Kodaira dimensions.

name: Analytic birational-constancy criterion: flat entire top Hodge line (finite character) of a kappa=0, h^0(K)=1 family over a curve => birational constancy after…
statement: pi: P -> C smooth projective with very general fibre D, kappa(D)=0, h^0(K_D)=1, top Hodge bundle a flat line with finite character => generic fibre birational to a constant variety after a finite extension (equivariantly for a finite group). Proof: lift a base vector field; control its poles along the zero divisor of the top form by L^{2/m} minimisation / DHP extension / Paun-Takayama Bergman metrics; poles are fixed divisors of a small ample perturbation of the canonical system; contract them …
why: Named close neighbour (Cao-Guenancia-Paun 2023) with the same flat-direct-image => triviality mechanism; the extension to non-minimal kappa=0 fibres by contracting pole divisors is a real but variant step. Not N3: no evidence it is far from CGP23 + DHP + BCHM.

name: Marked periods, Higgs-tail nef line and numerical removal of the period twist (REV)
statement: When the chosen highest vector need not span its Hodge space, add Pluecker 'marks' on compact flag factors so the marked period map is generically immersive; build a Higgs-tail nef line P with nu(P+H)=nu(P); remove the period twist numerically (Siu / nef Morse).
why: Variant of C1 plus Viehweg-Zuo Higgs constructions.

name: Section construction with retained zero in the original frame + zero test (REV)
statement: Uniform-in-y construction of sections whose zero is retained in the original source frame, giving injectivity of restriction to a very general fibre when kappa(Y,L_Y)=0; algebraic core: (r/tau^{e/m})^m = s/tau^e regular in a normal ring.
why: Popa-Schnell is the named neighbour; the algebra is standard. Its algebraic core is the only non-trivial piece of the family with Lean (RootFactor.lean, Descent.lean, Blowup.lean), but OFF the comparator DAG.

name: Tangential rank principle (limit of holomorphic maps with full limiting tangential rank stays in the limiting image)
statement: If the limiting tangential rank of a family of holomorphic maps approaching a divisor equals the interior rank, the nearby image lies in the limiting image.
why: Elementary analytic lemma; content belongs to C1.

name: Log-general-type addition in Fujiki class C via an auxiliary projective stable family
statement: Kovacs-Patakfalvi's projective log-general-type-fibre addition transported to class C by constructing an auxiliary projective family and descending relative sections.
why: Setting extension of KP.

name: Exact rank-one comparison: least-index root cover makes M the ENTIRE highest Hodge line (p_g = 1), with source-order boundary T
statement: H^0(X, m(K_X+Delta)) = H^0(W, m(K_W+T+M)) in divisible degrees with B(g,Delta) <= T <= 1, M the parabolic extension of the top line of the minimal root cover.
why: Exact source-order bookkeeping on top of BFMT's construction; the paper identifies its cyclic extension with BFMT's.

name: Kaehler b-semiampleness by product covers on an auxiliary compact base (BSA)
statement: Transfer of BFMT's algebraic b-semiampleness (effective SNC boundary, coefficients in [0,1]) to compact log-smooth Kaehler fibrations using MWWWZ-type product covers and a real->rational polarization change.
why: Kaehler extension of BFMT by transfer of a known covering construction.

name: O04+O06 / P01+P04 / R14+R16: adjoint positivity of the highest Hodge line (K_S+jL big on the full-period quotient S, M=p^*L at original level), via strict rank…
why: It is the single new input that turns the classical reduction (relative Iitaka fibration + canonical bundle formula + Viehweg weak positivity + KP/Hashizume addition) into a full proof of C_{n,m}; Birkar (2009) identifies the kappa(F)=0 case as exactly the obstruction. L contains: M nef (Kawamata/Ambro/FG), M b-nef and abundant only after generically finite base change (Ambro 2005, which breaks K_W and effectivity), K_S+D big on period images (BC), algebraicity (BBT). None states that the nef l…

name: O09 / P09: adjoint-addition interpolation D+M = (1-theta)E_+ + theta E_- (general-type addition with semiample pullback cM+eta p^*A absorbed into the boundary,…
why: Short exact-section device that needs neither abundance of P nor limits of Kodaira dimensions; used in ORB, ORD, VAR Sec. 8.

name: V03: analytic birational constancy criterion (flat top Hodge line of the minimal root cover over a curve => birationally constant family), via L^{2/m}-minimiza…
why: Works for Kodaira-zero fibres without good minimal models, which is exactly where Kawamata/Viehweg-Zuo isotriviality arguments need extra hypotheses; essential for whole-fiber variation.

name: R09+R17+R24: marked periods (compact-factor flag marks), Higgs-tail nef line P with nu(P+H)=nu(P), and numerical removal of the period twist
why: Handles a highest vector that does not span its Hodge space, which the whole-line versions cannot; converts positivity on S into actual base sections.

name: R02+R08: section construction with retained zero in the original frame (uniform in y over the original open base)
why: Gives injectivity of restriction to one very general fibre for every degree when kappa(Y,L_Y)=0, the decisive case of Popa's additivity; first assertion is the log Popa-Schnell base-nonvanishing conjecture under stratum smoothness. Its algebraic core is the only non-trivial piece of this family present in Lean (RootFactor.lean).

name: Shafarevich conjecture on holomorphic convexity; holomorphic hull
statement: Universal cover of every smooth connected projective complex variety is holomorphically convex; hull K^_V = {v: |g(v)| <= sup_K |g| for all g in O(V)}; convexity = all hulls compact.
why: Textbook SCV notion and the posed problem.

name: infinite Nori string
statement: Connected curve whose normalized components have finite pi_1-image but whose union has infinite image; a closed infinite Nori string cannot lie in a holomorphically convex space.
why: Classical obstruction (Lasell-Ramachandran, Katzarkov-Ramachandran, Coltoiu-Joita).

name: meridian
statement: Boundary of a small disk transverse to a divisor.
why: Standard.

name: special (Campana)
statement: No line bundle L with nonzero L -> Omega^p and kappa(M,L)=p; used only to conclude the surface is not special via OpenAIAbelianity2026 Cor. 1.4.
why: Cited definition; corollary-only use of a model-produced result.

name: semialgebraic subset
statement: Finite Boolean combination of real polynomial (in)equalities in affine charts; surface's universal cover is not biholomorphic to a semialgebraic open subset by OpenAISemialgebraicCovers2026 Cor. 8.1.
why: Standard; corollary-only use of a model-produced result.

name: Thm main (surface)
statement: There is a smooth connected projective surface X containing a connected nodal curve Z_0 with smooth rational components such that im(pi_1(Z_0)->pi_1(X)) is infinite; a component above Z_0 in X~ is closed, noncompact, a locally finite union of compact rational curves; hulls of its points are noncompact; X~ is not holomorphically convex.
why: Headline.

name: Lemma rational-hull (compact-curve obstruction, rational case)
statement: If Z subset X compact connected nodal with smooth rational components and infinite pi_1 image, every component W of its preimage in X~ is closed, noncompact, locally finite union of compact rational curves, holomorphic functions constant on W, hull of any point noncompact.
why: Paper names the precedent explicitly.

name: free pro-2 group F_d, weighted Magnus expansion, valuation nu
statement: g_i -> 1+U_i in A=F_2<<U_1..U_d>>, deg U_i=w_i; nu(g)=least degree of g-1; faithfulness and cofinality re-proved.
why: Textbook (Magnus, Lazard, Vinberg).

name: degree rules nu(gh)>=min, nu([g,h])>=nu(g)+nu(h), nu(g^{2^e})>=2^e nu(g)
statement: As stated.
why: Standard.

name: Lemma substitution
statement: If nu(alpha(g_i)g_i^{-1}) >= w_i + a then (alpha - id)(A_{>=n}) subset A_{>=n+a}; degree-raising operators may be substituted for Magnus variables.
why: Routine filtered-algebra substitution; folklore in pro-p/Magnus theory.

name: Frattini quotient; Frattini basis criterion; Hopfian property
statement: Elements spanning G/closure(G^2[G,G]) topologically generate; d elements of F_d with Frattini-basis images are a free basis.
why: Textbook (Burnside basis theorem, Hopficity of f.g. profinite groups).

name: Lemma weighted infinitude criterion (weighted Golod-Shafarevich)
statement: If nu(r_lambda) >= v_lambda, finitely many v below any bound, relator series converges and 1 - sum t^{w_i} + sum t^{v_lambda} < 0 for some 0<t<1, the pro-2 quotient is infinite.
why: Ershov 2011 Thm 2.1/Cor 2.2 states it; re-proved for the infinite-relator convention.

name: witness family: Eisenstein curve E, q, f induced by [4], parameter curve B, markings A_s (48 points)
statement: E=C/(Z+Z omega), omega^3=1; q:E->P^1 sign quotient; f induced by [4]; B=P^1 minus q(E[2]) cup q(ker(1-omega)) (5 points); A_s={z: f(z)=omega_bar^j s, j=0,1,2}.
why: Specific genus-zero marked family with torus lift; BK/EF use genus>=2 families; no equivalent found in quick search.

name: Lemma family (5 excluded points; 48 points as etale multisection; 24 collisions at s_*)
statement: As stated.
why: Routine verification on the witness.

name: torus group F=pi_1(T,0) free on x,y,a_0,a_1,a_2,c_0,c_1 with weights 1,1,1,1,1,2,2; Gamma=pi_1(B) free rank 4
statement: As stated; surface relation [x,y]c_0c_1c_2=1 gives nu_F(c_2)>=2.
why: Choice of weighted basis; routine once S13 fixed.

name: H=(Z/4)^2, K=ker(F->H) (rank 97), T^(4), S=P^1 minus A_{s0}, Pi=pi_1(S) (rank 47), p:K->Pi
statement: Multiplication-by-4 cover and sign quotient relate the small torus group F to the actual sphere group Pi; 'Keeping this connection based ... is essential'.
why: Lifting a sphere family to an elliptic (isogeny) cover to control monodromy is a known move (Kummer/Legendre style), here used based.

name: corrected based monodromy phi_m = iota^{eps(m)} H_1; 'pure'
statement: Endpoint of an iota-equivariant isotopy fixing 0, corrected by the sign so each puncture is fixed.
why: Standard point-pushing monodromy with a sign correction.

name: Prop based-monodromy
statement: phi_m form a homomorphism Gamma->Aut(F), pure, commute with iota_*, preserve K, p o phi_m|_K = beta_m o p (actual based sphere monodromy); p:K->Pi surjective.
why: Covering-space bookkeeping.

name: Lemma degree-one (three invariant double covers Y_j^2 = q(z) - omega_bar^j s)
statement: Every phi_m and iota_* act trivially on V=F/{nu_F>=2}: the two handle characters and three characters chi_j of explicit double covers with global basepoint lifts form a basis of V* and are monodromy- and sign-invariant.
why: Explicit invariant characters via double covers branched at puncture pairs; idea (monodromy acting trivially on H_1 mod 2 => unipotent on pro-2 completion) is standard in pro-l monodromy.

name: Prop monodromy-raising
statement: For every m in Gamma, phi_m - id raises weighted degree by >=1 on the completed Magnus algebra of F^.
why: Pro-2 unipotence of monodromy; known shape (Johnson/weight filtration), new specific verification for weight-2 boundaries.

name: core collapse: L free pro-2 on a_{h,j} (48), Phi:F -> L x| H, x->T_1, y->T_2, a_j->a_{0,j}, c_0,c_1->1
statement: Collapsing the lifted core kills its pi_1; Phi|_K is the collapse map followed by completion.
why: Van Kampen collapse; the semidirect-product substitution is a natural device.

name: pinched involution sigma(a_{h,j}) = a_{b_j-h,j}^{-1}, b_j mod 2H != 0
statement: As stated.
why: Computation.

name: Lemma pinched-sphere
statement: Pi_pair (kill 24 pair boundaries) free rank 24 with completion L/<<sigma(g)g^{-1}>>; any sigma-trivial quotient lambda:L->R gives theta:Pi->R dense with theta p = lambda Phi|_K; equalizer condition on K implies theta beta_m = theta on all of Pi.
why: Diagram chase; the key design choice is comparing on K before pinching.

name: Lemma finite-geometric-monodromy
statement: Action of Gamma on markings and sign factors through a finite 2-group (in H^3 x| Z/2); gamma_* has nontrivial sign, gamma_*^2 fixes markings and acts trivially on Pi_pair.
why: Half-twist/full-twist local computation.

name: shift-adapted basis u_{il,j} = delta_{T1}^i delta_{T2}^l (a_{0,j}), weights i+l+1; Lemma shift-basis
statement: u_{il,j} form a free pro-2 basis of L (Frattini images are the monomial basis xi^i eta^l of F_2[H]=F_2[xi,eta]/(xi^4,eta^4)); T_1-id, T_2-id, sigma-id each raise degree by >=1.
why: Basis adapted to a unipotent group action via iterated differences = Jennings/Lazard-type basis of the permutation module F_2[H]; close to known filtrations.

name: cyclic endpoint estimate: T^4=id and nu(w_i)>=d+i (i<=3) imply nu(w_4)>=d+4
statement: Proved via formal triangular automorphism T'(z_i)=z_{i+1}z_i, (T')^4-id=(T'-id)^4 in char 2, and the observation that T'^3(z_0) contains z_3 once as first letter.
why: Short char-2 binomial trick.

name: Prop involution: 24 relators r_g = sigma(g)g^{-1} impose sigma=id with cost tG(t); P=(1+t)G, G(t)=3t(1+t)(1+t^2)^2
statement: Frattini differential d = u + u^2 d/du + v^2 d/dv on R=F_2[u,v]/(u^4,v^4) satisfies d^2=0 and R = C (+) dC with C=span{u^a v^b: a in {0,2}}; lifting a basis of C to elements g gives 24 relators of degree w_g+1 whose normal closure is exactly the sigma-coinvariant kernel.
why: Self-described reusable mechanism; acyclic Frattini complex trick not found in quick search; nearest precedent Koch-Venkov (sigma-inverted relators lie deeper) found later.

name: Lemma transfer (nu_F >= n => L-component nu_L >= n)
statement: Represent L x| H on A_L; substitute degree-raising operators.
why: Direct application of S10.

name: deep monodromy relators Phi(phi_m(k_i)k_i^{-1}), m in M_N (basis of D_N/D_{N+1}, |M_N|<=4^N), cost 97 sum_{N>=J} 4^N t^{N+1}
statement: Counting monodromies by Magnus depth avoids estimating the rank of Gamma_J.
why: Depth-counting of relators is in the spirit of GS/Golod; application to monodromy invariance is specific.

name: Lemma deep-invariance
statement: f_K o phi_m = f_K for all m in D_J; hence Pi -> Q_0 is invariant under actual monodromy of Gamma_J.
why: Closed-subgroup argument.

name: t=49/200; J; M=<gamma_*^2>Gamma_J; B',C'; U subset P^1 x B'; pi_1(U)=Pi x| M; rho_0
statement: As stated.
why: Standard base change bookkeeping.

name: Y -> C' by blowing up section collisions; D=Y\U SNC; distinguished fiber D_* = main sphere + 24 tails
statement: As stated, with an explicit local induction for SNC.
why: Standard.

name: Lemma distinguished-meridians
statement: Every meridian of a component of D_* has trivial image under rho_0.
why: Local computation.

name: boundary power relators mu~_i^{2^e} with b t^{2^e} < 1/100
statement: High powers of the remaining boundary meridians.
why: Golod's method, named.

name: Prop infinite-quotient
statement: Q infinite; rho dense on every punctured fiber; component meridians of D finite order, of D_* trivial. Margin: G(49/200)>257/250, total < -1/125.

name: Lemma finite local detection and descent
statement: Given rho:pi_1(Y\D)->Q dense profinite with finite-order meridians, there is a finite quotient P_f injective on every local boundary image; the corresponding cover extends to smooth projective X->Y with SNC boundary and rho_X:pi_1(X)->Q with rho_X i_* = rho pi_*.
why: Standard 'choose a finite quotient faithful on local groups' device (orbifold uniformization / Kato-Namba / BK-EF style).

name: Lemma rational-special-fiber
statement: Resolution can be chosen so Z=h^{-1}(c_*)_red has smooth rational components and ordinary crossings.
why: Local models + Riemann-Hurwitz.

name: Lemma infinite-special-image (with deformation-retract neighbourhood via Lojasiewicz triangulation)
statement: Some component Z_0 of Z has infinite image in pi_1(X).
why: Standard regular-neighbourhood argument.

name: large fundamental group
statement: For every positive-dimensional closed irreducible Z, im(pi_1(Z^nu)->pi_1(X)) infinite.
why: Kollar's definition.

name: Thm main (fourfold)
statement: There exist a smooth connected projective fourfold X and a simple abelian surface A subset X with X of large pi_1 and im(pi_1(A)->pi_1(X)) = Z; X~ has no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvariety and is not Stein.
why: Headline.

name: Prop large-reduction (simple abelian surface with Z image => large-pi_1 fourfold with non-Stein cover)
statement: Given A subset S' with im(pi_1 A) = Z, X = complete intersection of c=d+2 general sections of I_F (x) L^m in W=S' x B (B abelian 6-fold, F=A x {0}) is smooth, pi_1(X)=pi_1(S') x pi_1(B), fibers over B have <=3 points off F, X large, X~ not Stein.
why: Lefschetz/Bertini/incidence count are standard; the 'add an abelian 6-fold to make everything else large' trick is new-looking but elementary.

name: Lemma red:compact-criterion
statement: X~ has no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvariety iff X has large pi_1.
why: Known equivalence (Kollar).

name: Lemma red:interpolation
statement: H^0(I_F (x) L^m) -> (+) L^m|_{p_i} surjective for large m uniformly in l distinct points off F.
why: Standard.

name: non-Stein obstruction: A_K = C^2/K, K=Z^3, A_K ~ T^3 x R, H_3 = Z, Andreotti-Frankel
statement: A component of the preimage of A in X~ is the closed submanifold C^2/K with nonzero H_3, impossible in a Stein manifold (Andreotti-Frankel); simplicity of A prevents compact curves in it.
why: Elementary given Andreotti-Frankel; closest precedents: toroidal (Cousin) groups C^2/Z^3 as non-Stein noncompact Lie groups, and Nori-string obstruction (compact components). New as an obstruction to the large-pi_1 Shafarevich conjecture in quick search.

name: reading framework: graphs with charts (D_v,d_v), readings [p]_v of paths of length <=N, axioms (P1)-(P3), 'closes on reading', groupoid Q
statement: (P1) prefixes/reverses/edge bijections; (P2) prefix-change compatibility for paths of length <= N/2; (P3) uniform Gromov hyperbolicity of all chart components.
why: A developing-map/Cartan-Hadamard frame in combinatorial dress.

name: Lemma local path criterion
statement: There is N_0 depending only on the hyperbolicity constant such that if readings satisfy (P1)-(P3) with N>=N_0 and e is a single-edge loop at v with [e]_v != d_v, then e is nontrivial in Q.
why: Variant of Gromov's Cartan-Hadamard / local-to-global theorem (Gromov 1987; Delzant-Gromov; Coulon; DGO).

name: ladder of width h; Lemma narrowing (width <=1000H => width <=H)
statement: Ladders compare readings; composition adds widths; narrowing via quadrangle slimness.
why: Fellow-traveller narrowing for local geodesics; standard in hyperbolic geometry.

name: guide (k-local geodesic in charts)
statement: Path each of whose subpaths of length <= k reads as a geodesic in the chart at its initial vertex.
why: Renaming of k-local geodesic.

name: Lemma extension (continue a guide by one edge, width <=50H)
statement: Repair by minimizing sum of chart distances between chosen nearby vertices at marks spaced in [L,2L].
why: Minimization repair is a careful variant of the local-geodesic-is-quasigeodesic argument.

name: synchronous comparison of geodesics with width 10(h+Delta)
statement: As stated.
why: Standard fellow-travelling.

name: six real algebraic slopes (4 red |lambda|<0.01, 2 blue |lambda|>4) with Galois group S_6; genus-two C with simple Jac (Zarhin)
statement: Weak approximation + Frobenius cycle types (6),(5,1),(2,1,1,1,1) give S_6; Zarhin gives End(Jac C)=Z.
why: Standard (Zarhin; Dedekind/Frobenius).

name: arrangement D: z-family (six slope hyperplanes z_2=lambda_i z_1, couplings z_1=+-c) and w-family; ball |z|^2+|w|^2<a; sigma(z,w)=(w,-z); 0.85<c/sqrt(a)<0.9
statement: Coupling hyperplanes meet exactly the four red slopes; z- and w-couplings disjoint (2c^2>a); sigma order 4 integral unitary.
why: No arrangement with 'coupling' hyperplanes identifying red meridians found in quick search.

name: Prop arrangement-local (exact local arrangements in deep congruence quotients)
statement: For W,R_0 there is torsion-free sigma-normalized principal congruence Gamma_0 with: every W-ball sees distinct labels isometric to a subarrangement of D; injectivity radius > R_0; exactly D near o.
why: Gram-matrix finiteness + congruence separation; standard in Stover-Toledo / Deraux style arguments.

name: Stover-Toledo virtual cyclic ramified covers
statement: Compact simplest-type congruence ball quotient, divisor with disjoint smooth totally geodesic components: a finite cover admits a degree-d cyclic cover branched over its preimage.
why: Cited, invoked as black box (C5).

name: global sign characters chi_z, chi_w with chi_w = sigma^* chi_z
statement: Sum of eight Stover-Toledo characters per family; equivariance by passing to sigma-invariant covers.
why: Routine.

name: filling rule (blow up centers, branch exceptional divisor iff k odd), smooth (Z/2)^2 cover V -> M^, distinguished fiber F_*=C x C, normal bundle pr1*L (+) pr2*…
statement: As stated.
why: Standard branched-cover filling of arrangements (Hirzebruch-type).

name: ordinary resolution near F_*: blow up F_*, quotient by s^2, blow up the two fixed curves, quotient by residual involution; glue with [V/<s>] to get orbifold S
statement: As stated.
why: Standard local linearization/blowup.

name: Abel map Sym^2 C = Bl_pt Jac(C); rational section [tau(p), i tau(q)]; f:Y->S; Prop orbifold-surface
statement: Y iterated point blowup of A=Jac(C) mapping into the ordinary locus over o.
why: Classical genus-two geometry.

name: dihedral labels q_z: pi_1(U_T) -> D_inf (red meridians -> r, blue -> b), modified over the red disk by coupling square roots (1 -+ z_1/c)^{1/2}; translation la…
statement: Defined chart-by-chart on finite models; need not define a representation of the global orbifold group.
why: Local (non-global) D_inf labels compatible on buffered overlaps; nothing equivalent found in quick search.

name: Lemma mod:extension
statement: l_z, l_w extend across the blowups and branched fillings of every finite model.
why: Local meridian computation.

name: sum label l = l_z + l_w (s-invariant); Lemma mod:central (order-4 lift of s commuting with deck group; descent to coarse quotient)
statement: As stated; 'central model' vs 'individual model'.
why: Equivariant-cover descent is standard; using the sum only near o is a design choice.

name: Lemma buffer-bound
statement: Nonzero z-translation on a loop over B(x,R) forces dist(x,L_z) <= B_1(R).
why: Compactness/hyperbolic-geometry estimate.

name: Prop kernel-compatibility (buffered agreement of individual kernels; sum kernel = intersection far from o)
statement: As stated.
why: Key compatibility; specific to this design.

name: graphs G_T(u): vertices = points of the covering, edges = paths with projected diameter < u; central quotient graph
statement: 'A word of arbitrary length in loops supported in one fixed bounded region can be one edge.'
why: Equivalent in effect to coning off bounded regions (electrification, Farb 1998; coned-off Cayley graphs).

name: Prop model-hyperbolicity
statement: Uniform u, delta such that every component of every G_T(u) and G_cen(u) is delta-hyperbolic, also after omitting analytic subsets.
why: Quasi-isometry to a hyperbolic cone over the ideal arrangement complement.

name: Lemma bounded-core
statement: Vertices over a bounded radial region have bounded graph diameter.
why: Direct.

name: arrangement-preserving collar near the sphere at infinity; metric d_K=|1-<xi,eta>|^{1/2}; ideal metric d_I via projected path diameter
statement: As stated, with transversality from arithmetic nondegeneracy.
why: d_K is the Koranyi-type (Carnot) gauge; collar standard.

name: Lemma mod:cone (hyperbolic cone over any bounded metric space)
statement: Graph C(I) with vertical edges and horizontal edges at height t when d_I <= e^{-t} is hyperbolic with absolute constant; distance formula t+t'-2j(+3).
why: Bonk-Schramm hyperbolic cone / Groves-Manning combinatorial horoball.

name: Thm orbifold-cyclic
statement: For sufficiently deep arithmetic level, im(f_*:pi_1(Y)->pi_1(S)) = Z.
why: Assembly.

name: Lemma app:surface-comparison
statement: Images of generators of pi_1(Y) equal images of loops in C x {q_0} subset V, representable near F_* in the sign-covered arrangement complement.
why: Normal push-off.

name: Lemma app:cyclic-upper (coupling relations k h_i = 1 identify the red meridians)
statement: Image of pi_1(C x {q_0}) in pi_1(V), hence of pi_1(Y) in pi_1(S), is cyclic (quotient of D_inf even part).
why: Short local computation once F14 is given.

name: graph G on the ordinary open set O; central charts (dist < J to Gamma o) vs individual charts (hyperplanes meeting B(x,K)); constants R=(2N+100)(u+1), J, K
statement: As stated.
why: Bookkeeping.

name: Lemma app:chart-axioms
statement: The readings satisfy (P1)-(P3).
why: Case analysis.

name: Lemma app:orbifold-meridians
statement: pi_1(U)->pi_1(T) surjective with kernel normally generated by transverse-disk boundaries (m-th powers of meridians).
why: Standard orbifold van Kampen.

name: Lemma app:true-relations
statement: A loop of edges of G nullhomotopic in S is trivial in P(G).
why: Subdivision + local closure; correctness-critical.

name: infinite order: the pushed loop e has nonzero sum label; every power e^n is a single edge with distinct read endpoints
statement: Hence every nonzero power of e is nontrivial in pi_1(S).
why: Payoff of F26; one step once F08 and F26 are in place.

name: Lemma ambient-realization (relative Godeaux-Serre)
statement: Smooth effective proper DM stack T with projective coarse space, Y -> T in ordinary locus => smooth projective fivefold S containing Y with pi_1(S) = pi_1(T).
why: Godeaux-Serre/Totaro method with a containment constraint plus Ehresmann deformation trick.

name: Lemma ambient-blowdown
statement: Given Y_1 subset S with (-1)-curve E and blowdown b:Y_1->Y_0, there are S_0 superset Y_0 and theta:pi_1(S)=pi_1(S_0) compatible with b_*.
why: Atiyah-flop-type contraction with an explicit polarization; classical local model, new global packaging.

name: Thm cyclic-embedding
statement: Simple abelian surface A subset S' smooth projective with im(pi_1 A -> pi_1 S') = Z.
why: Assembly.

name: Proof of Thm main (fourfold)
statement: Apply F03 to F41.
why: Assembly.

name: Fourfold witness: coupled red/blue pencil arrangement whose coupling hyperplanes collapse the genus-two surface group to the even part of D_inf, read by local …
why: Nothing in the goal or in L mentions arrangements, dihedral labels or coupling hyperplanes; the object is invented to make im(pi_1 A) exactly Z. It is simultaneously the source of the relations (cyclic upper bound) and of the local covers (infinite lower bound); all of sections 4-6 depend on it. The labels are deliberately NOT a global representation: a global one is impossible because some power of the generator must die in every bounded-rank linear representation (EKPR).

name: Surface witness: genus-zero 48-marked family from [4] on the Eisenstein curve, controlled through its torus lift so monodromy is pro-2 degree-raising
why: Makes the Bogomolov-Katzarkov route work in genus zero with a provable infinite quotient; BK's infinitude stayed conditional and Eyssidieux-Funar showed most BK candidates ARE holomorphically convex. Not a subterm of the goal.

name: Economical involution presentation: 24 relators sigma(g)g^{-1} of degree w_g+1 impose sigma-coinvariance with cost tG(t), P=(1+t)G, via the acyclic Frattini di…
why: Self-described reusable mechanism; it is exactly what produces the GS margin (1-G(t)<0 at t<1/4); without it the relations of the pinched sphere would exhaust the generator budget. The d^2=0 acyclicity computation is not in L.

name: Local path criterion with projected-diameter edges: detect infinite order from charts alone, every power of a short loop being one edge
why: Proves infinite order with no global representation and no finite quotients: the only conceivable kind of argument, since EKPR forces non-linearity. The diameter-not-length edge convention is the trick that makes Z^2 translation covers hyperbolic and powers single edges.

name: Abelian-surface reduction: simple A with pi_1-image Z gives C^2/Z^3 ~ T^3 x R in X~ (H_3 != 0, non-Stein), while adding a large abelian factor makes X large
why: Clean new obstruction to the large-pi_1 form: no compact subvarieties, yet a closed non-Stein submanifold. Separates the geometry (step 1) from the group theory (everything else).

name: Fourfold witness: coupled red/blue pencil arrangement with local dihedral translation labels
statement: Two 6-slope pencils in B^4 (z- and w-families; 4 red slopes |lambda|<0.01, 2 blue |lambda|>4) plus coupling hyperplanes z_1=+-c, w_1=+-c (0.85<c/sqrt a<0.9) meeting only the red slopes, symmetric under sigma(z,w)=(w,-z), embedded exactly in deep congruence ball quotients. Coupling relations k h_i=1 force the image of the genus-two surface group to lie in the even part <rb> of D_inf = <r,b>; chart-local labels q_z: red->r, blue->b, modified over the red disk by (1-+z_1/c)^{1/2}, give integer tra…
why: No equivalent object found in searches A-D (see test1.searches); it is not a subterm of the goal or of L; it is load-bearing for the entire fourfold. F3 (auxiliary construction): the arrangement plus its chart-local labels exist only to drive the proof. The N3 grade is provisional; it would fall to N2 if test 4 shows that the frame (pencil + D_inf + 'collapse red meridians') is readily proposed, or if an expert identifies coupling-type arrangements in the ball-quotient literature.

name: Surface witness: genus-zero 48-marked Eisenstein family controlled through its torus lift (degree-raising pro-2 monodromy)
statement: Spheres with markings f^{-1}(omega_bar^j s), where f is induced by [4] on E=C/Z[omega]; at s_*=q(e_0) the 48 markings collide in 24 pairs. Monodromy is computed on the 7-generator torus group F (weights 1,1,1,1,1,2,2), where three explicit double covers Y_j^2=q(z)-omega_bar^j s show it is trivial in degree one and hence degree-raising on the pro-2 Magnus algebra. The comparison with the actual 47-generator sphere group goes through the surjection p:K->Pi and the core-collapsed L.
why: No equivalent object found in searches A-D, and it passes tests 2-3. Confidence is lower than C1 because the paper names BK's passage as its architecture and the degree-raising principle is known; the witness is a careful instantiation of a named programme. It falls to N2 if test 4 arm R (BK route plus 'use a pro-2 GS quotient') yields isogeny-lifted genus-0 families readily.

name: Economical involution presentation: 24 relators sigma(g)g^{-1} imposing sigma-coinvariance at cost tG(t), via the acyclic Frattini differential and the shift-a…
statement: On L free pro-2 with basis u_{il,j}=delta_{T1}^i delta_{T2}^l(a_{0,j}) (weights i+l+1), choose g lifting a basis of C=span{u^a v^b: a in {0,2}} in F_2[u,v]/(u^4,v^4); the relators r_g=sigma(g)g^{-1} have degree w_g+1, their normal closure equals the sigma-coinvariant kernel, and P(t)=(1+t)G(t) with G=3t(1+t)(1+t^2)^2, leaving 1-G(t)<0 just below t=1/4.
why: Mechanism precedented by Koch-Venkov's sigma-group refinement of GS (sigma-inverted relators lie one level deeper), with a Jennings-type basis; the implementation (acyclic Frattini differential, P=(1+t)G) is new but is a variant. Downgraded from the analyst's weak N3.

name: Local path criterion with projected-diameter edges (representation-free infinite-order detection)
statement: If readings of paths of length <= N in charts satisfy prefix/reverse compatibility, prefix-change compatibility and uniform delta-hyperbolicity, with N >= N_0(delta), then a single-edge loop that does not close on reading is nontrivial modulo short closing loops. Edges are paths of projected diameter < u, so every power of a short loop is one edge, and Z^2 translation covers become hyperbolic.
why: Variant of Gromov/Delzant-Gromov Cartan-Hadamard, with named viewpoint in the paper; diameter edges are electrification. Strategically important (it is the representation-free argument EKPR forces), but not new machinery.

name: Abelian-surface reduction and the C^2/Z^3 non-Stein obstruction
statement: A simple abelian surface A in S' with pi_1-image Z yields, by a general complete intersection in S' x B (B an abelian 6-fold), a fourfold with large pi_1 whose universal cover contains C^2/Z^3 ~ T^3 x R (H_3=Z), which is not Stein by Andreotti-Frankel; simplicity of A excludes compact curves.
why: No exact precedent found, but it is a short combination of Andreotti-Frankel, toroidal groups and the Nori-string pattern, and it is borderline analytic. Its value is strategic (it reduces the large-pi_1 problem to a single group-theoretic image).

name: Finite local detection and descent
statement: Choose a finite quotient of a dense profinite image that is injective on every local boundary group; the associated cover compactifies to a smooth projective X with rho_X factoring.
why: Self-described 'reusable mechanism', but a standard device; serves as a negative control.

name: Ambient realization and ambient blowdown (relative Godeaux-Serre + Atiyah-type contraction with explicit polarization)
statement: Replace an orbifold by a smooth projective fivefold containing a given surface with the same pi_1; realize a point blowdown of an embedded surface in a new smooth projective ambient variety preserving pi_1 and the surface homomorphism.
why: Named classical constructions adapted with routine global care.

name: The hypersurface H and algebra A=P/(H)
statement: P=C[p,s,u,F,J], x=s^2+u^3+p^2F, H=x^2F-(1+2sx)J-p^2J^2-pu, A=P/(H). In localized coordinates (x,y,z,u) over C[p,p^-1] it reads H=p^-2(xy-z(z+1))-pu (I02).
why: Counterexample objects to a 70-year-old problem in char 0 do not exist in L (Gupta's char-p families do not lift; Dubouloz-Ghosh 2025 give only 'potential' counterexamples). The example is tiny (one quintic-ish polynomial in 5 variables) yet occurs nowhere in the goal-as-posed or L, matching the Cook-Reckhow profile. Risk: the design may be templated (El Kahoui-Ouali residual coordinate + Asanuma-type twist p^3u=xy-z(z+1) of a non-line), which would cap it at N2.

name: x,y,z and xy-z(z+1)=p^2(H+pu)
statement: y=s+x(x-u^3), z=sx+p^2J; identity xy-z(z+1)=p^2(H+pu). Over C[p,p^-1], (x,y,z,u) are coordinates with inverse s=y-x(x-u^3), F=p^-2(x-s^2-u^3), J=p^-2(z-sx).
why: Given H, a computation; conceptually it is the design key of I01, already credited there.

name: Lemma con:domain (A integral, dim 4, A[p^-1]=Laurent poly ring)
statement: A is a domain of dimension 4, p!=0 in A, A[p^-1]=C[p,p^-1,x,y,z].
why: Routine UFD/transcendence-degree argument. Lean proves it differently (L03).

name: Locally nilpotent derivation Delta=-p^2 d/du and exponential shift Phi=exp(w Delta)
statement: Delta fixes p,x,y,z, Delta u=-p^2; its values on s,F,J lie in P so Delta is an LND of P with Delta H=p^3, Delta^2H=0; Phi(H)=H+p^3w, A[w]=T:=P[w]/(H+p^3w).
why: Explicitly the El Kahoui-Ouali method.

name: Determinant-one change (L,M) in (F,J) and B=C[p,s,u,M]
why: Explicit coordinate change; existence is guaranteed by the residual-coordinate property built into I01.

name: Root L*=pu-p^2C mod p^3 and fifth coordinate e0 with certificate p^3e0-(L-L*)=(p^2Q1(L)-1)(H(L)+p^3w)
statement: C=Q(0), Q1=(Q-C)/L, L*=pu-p^2C, h=u-pQ-p^3F^3-p^2w, e0=-w-pF^3-Q1h; then p^3 e=L-L* in T and T=B[e]=C[p,s,u,M,e].
why: Explicit inverse for a case covered by cited theorems (Edo-Venereau Thm 7, Maubach Thm 4.5, El Kahoui-Ouali Thm 1.1).

name: Prop stabilization: A[w] = C^[5]
statement: There is a C-algebra isomorphism A[w]=C^[5]; explicit generators Phi^-1(p,s,u,M,e0).
