why: Known theorem applied to I01; novelty lies in I01 being residual.

name: Cor stable-coordinate: H is a coordinate of P[w] but not of P (SCC fails in ambient dim 5)
statement: Via Dutta-Lahiri Thm 3.4 and Thm main.
why: Immediate from main theorem + cited theorem.

name: S=C[p,x,y,z,u]/(xy-z(z+1)-p^3u), R=S/pS=C[x,y,z,u]/(xy-z(z+1))
statement: Auxiliary subalgebra S of A with S[p^-1]=A[p^-1]; R is the smooth quadric threefold (SL2/T) times A^1_u.
why: A Danielewski/Asanuma-type hypersurface over a known quadric; abbreviation once I01 is fixed.

name: Lemma deg:valuation (S->A injective, ord_p DVR valuation, divisibility)
statement: S embeds in A with same localization; R smooth domain; ord_p from S_{pS} with ord_p(b)>=i iff b in p^iS.
why: Routine.

name: valuation degree deg h=-ord_p(h), filtration F_dA, gr A, initial form in(h), graded injection gr A -> R[tau,tau^-1]
statement: deg is a degree function; gr A injects into R[tau^±] via [h]_d -> (p^d h mod p) tau^-d.
why: Standard construction.

name: s_R, f, g and center I=(f,g) in R
statement: s_R=y-x(x-u^3), f=x-s_R^2-u^3, g=z-s_R x, I=(f,g).
why: Defined by reduction of p^2F, p^2J; abbreviation.

name: Prop graded: gr A = G = R[tau, I/tau^2] = P/(H_top), smooth domain; exact-weight representatives
statement: With weights (p,s,u,F,J)=(-1,0,0,2,2), every h in A has a representative of max weight exactly deg h, G=P/(H_top), H_top=x^2F-(1+2sx)J-p^2J^2; G is an affine modification of R[tau] (Kaliman-Zaidenberg) and smooth.
why: The technique is standard; the specific identification G=R[tau,I/tau^2] (an affine modification with smooth total space) is a nontrivial computation specific to this example.

name: Locally nilpotent derivation (LND); homogeneous derivation of degree shift j
statement: D is LND if every element is killed by some iterate; homogeneous of shift j if it maps degree d to d+j.
why: Textbook.

name: Lemma induced-lnd: LND of A induces nonzero homogeneous LND D_0 of G, invariants pass to initial forms
statement: j=max over generators of deg(Dh_i)-deg h_i; D_0([h]_d)=[Dh]_{d+j}.
why: Standard (re-proved for Z-filtrations).

name: Prop positive-invariant: if A=C^[4], G has a nonzero homogeneous LND with a nonzero homogeneous invariant of positive degree
statement: Some coordinate q_r has positive degree (F_0A is proper since deg F=2); D=d/dq_i kills q_r.
why: Paper names its own precedent (Gupta's Derksen-invariant strategy).

name: Remark: Delta descends to G but moves R (u -> -tau^2)
statement: Coefficient preservation can fail; motivates lifting via line bundle rather than via R.
why: Remark.

name: Determinant ring R~=C[a,d,b,c,u]/(ac-bd-1) with x=ab, y=dc, z=db
statement: SL2 (with u adjoined) mapping to the quadric R; the standard torus bundle SL2 -> SL2/T.
why: Standard object; its use here is I20.

name: v=a^2(x-u^3)-d^2=a^3b-a^2u^3-d^2
statement: Single generator of I R~; fiber weight 2, valuation degree 0.
why: Determined by the example and the bundle; not a free choice.

name: Prop principalization: Spec R~ -> Spec R is a G_m-torsor (line bundle minus zero section), I R~=(v), G~=G⊗_R R~=R~[tau,V]/(tau^2V-v)
statement: Charts D(z+1), D(z); certificate f=C1 v, g=b^2 v, v=alpha f+beta g with alpha C1+beta b^2=1; two commuting gradings (valuation degree, fiber weight).
why: Change-of-representation step: pull back along a known torsor so that the center becomes principal. Close neighbours: Cox-ring/torsor tricks, Danielewski-variety arguments on SL2. Could be N3 if discoverability is low; graded N2 provisionally.

name: Prop linearization: Pic(A^1 x X)=Pic(X) for smooth affine X; unique normalized linear lift of any G_a-action to a line bundle
statement: Picard invariance via Weil divisors; uniqueness via C[t]*=C*; cocycle; induced LND preserves fiber weights.
why: Known results re-proved.

name: Prop homogeneous-lift: D_0 lifts to an LND D~ of G~ of fiber weight 0 and the same valuation shift j
statement: Conjugating by the degree-scaling sigma_lambda, uniqueness of normalized lifts forces homogeneity.
why: Short consequence of I21 uniqueness.

name: Lemma lnd-order: nu_delta additive, kernel factorially closed, delta(h) not in hT
statement: Order nu_delta(h)=max{n: delta^n h != 0}; nu(fg)=nu(f)+nu(g).
why: Textbook (Freudenburg, Algebraic Theory of LNDs, Prop 1.9).

name: Homogeneous pieces of G~: G~_e = tau^-e R~ (e<0), V^l R~ (e=2l), tau V^{l+1} R~ (e=2l+1)
statement: Exact description of each valuation-degree component.
why: Routine computation once I20 is in place. Lean: ModificationGrading.piece_negative/even/odd.

name: Prop extracted-lnd: if A=C^[4], R~ has a nonzero LND E of fiber-weight shift q<=0 with E^2(v)=0
statement: Positive-degree invariant divisible by V forces D~V=0; Case 1 D~tau=0: E=tau^j D~|R~, E(v)=0, q=0. Case 2: j=2l+1 odd, D~(r)=tau V^{l+1}E(r), q=-2(l+1), LND order shows E LND and E^2(v)=0.
why: New lemma, but assembled from standard LND-order and degree-piece bookkeeping; analytic once I20/I24 are given (pivot distance 1). Strengthening via a sign condition q<=0 is the key extra tracked quantity (Remark red:sign-essential).

name: Remark red:sign-essential: E_+ (b->a, c->d) has shift +2, E_+(v)=a^4, E_+^2(v)=0
statement: Shows the sign condition is necessary.
why: Example.

name: Lemma Mason-Stothers (abc for polynomials)
statement: max deg <= r(XYZ)-1 for coprime X+Y=Z not all constant.
why: Classical; in Mathlib.

name: Lemma rig:one-variable: LND of F[t] has delta(t) in F
why: Classical. Lean: LND.polynomial_dX_constant.

name: Auxiliary grading on R~: weights (a,d,b,c,u)=(0,3,-3,0,2)
statement: Z-grading commuting with fiber weight, under which N=d^2+a^2u^3 is homogeneous of degree 6 while a^3b has degree -3.
why: Choosing a grading making a target piece top-degree is a standard move in LND rigidity proofs; the specific vector is found by solving linear constraints (relation homogeneous, N homogeneous, a^3b lower). Low search cost once the strategy is fixed.

name: Highest auxiliary component E'=E_lambda
statement: E'=greatest nonzero shift component; still LND, same fiber shift.
why: Standard (Lean GradedLND.highest).

name: Orbit polynomials a(q),d(q),u(q)=exp(qE')(.) and N(q)=N+qE'(N); nonsquare of -u^3 in K=C(a,d,b)(u)
statement: d(q)^2+a(q)^2u(q)^3=N(q) of degree <=1; pairwise coprime; abc gives D_u=0, D_d=D_a; leading coefficients give (delta/alpha)^2=-u^3 in K, impossible; hence E' fixes a,d,u.
why: Paper names Finston-Maubach precedent; the nonsquare twist is a small variant.

name: h=cE'(b)-bE'(c); R~∩Q=C0=C[a,d,u]; fiber weight e-2<0 contradiction
statement: ah=E'(b), dh=E'(c); h in C0 has nonnegative weight but weight e-2<0.
why: Short computation.

name: Prop rigidity: no nonzero LND E of R~ with fiber shift e<=0 and E^2(v)=0
statement: Combines I29-I32. (Argument actually works for e<=1.)
why: New rigidity statement for a specific ring, proved by a known method (highest component + abc).

name: Theorem main (A integral dim 4, A[w]=C^[5], A not C^[4])
statement: Assembly: I03, I07; contradiction chain I16 -> I22 -> I25 -> I33.
why: Target.

name: Cor affine-fibrations: p:Spec A->A^1 and (p,H):A^5->A^2 are smooth A^3-fibrations, not Zariski-locally trivial (Dolgachev-Weisfeiler fails)
statement: Residual coordinate gives fibers; Jacobian gives smoothness; local triviality + Bass-Connell-Wright + Suslin would give A=C^[4] or H a coordinate.
why: Corollary via cited theorems.

name: residual coordinate; one-stably a coordinate; A^3-fibration; Stable Coordinate Conjecture; fiber weight; normalization of a lift; Pic
statement: Background vocabulary.
why: Literature definitions.

name: The witness polynomial H = x^2F-(1+2sx)J-p^2J^2-pu, x=s^2+u^3+p^2F
why: Resolves a problem open since the 1940s-70s in char 0; none of the many candidate families (Koras-Russell, Asanuma-Gupta, Venereau, Dubouloz-Ghosh 2025 'potential counterexamples') worked. Tiny object (one polynomial in 5 variables), not a subterm of the posed problem or L - the Cook-Reckhow profile. Must satisfy two antagonistic constraints simultaneously: residual coordinate over C[p] (so the cylinder is trivial) and a degeneration whose principalized center v=a^3b-a^2u^3-d^2 carries the nons…

name: Principalizing the center by pulling back along the SL2 -> SL2/T torus bundle, giving G~=R~[tau,V]/(tau^2V-v)
why: Converts the question 'does G carry a homogeneous LND with positive-degree invariant?' into an explicit single-relation ring where degree pieces are explicit (I24); non-analytic relative to the goal. The lift must work even though D_0 does not preserve R (Remark I17) - the paper explicitly flags this obstacle. Large drop in difficulty: after this step, extraction is bookkeeping.

name: Extraction lemma: polynomiality => nonzero LND E of R~ with fiber shift q<=0 and E^2(v)=0
why: New statement; the sign constraint q<=0 is exactly what rigidity needs (Remark I26 shows it is essential). Case 2 (tau moving) uses an LND-order count to get E^2(v)=0 and odd shift j - not obvious.

name: Weighted rigidity: auxiliary grading (0,3,-3,0,2), orbit identity d(q)^2+a(q)^2u(q)^3=N(q) of degree <=1, Mason-Stothers + nonsquare -u^3
why: The auxiliary weight vector isolating N=d^2+a^2u^3 from a^3b is a specific find; non-analytic. Combining abc with a nonsquare argument in the original fraction field is a small new twist (paper's own remark).

name: Positive-degree invariant obstruction from polynomiality
why: Neat replacement of the Derksen invariant by a single positive-degree coordinate.

name: The witness polynomial H (and the fourfold A = P/(H))
statement: P = C[p,s,u,F,J], x = s^2+u^3+p^2F, H = x^2F - (1+2sx)J - p^2J^2 - pu, A = P/(H). Design: over C[p^{+-1}], H = p^{-2}(xy - z(z+1)) - pu is a coordinate; mod p, H is linear in F,J with unimodular coefficients (x0^2, -(1+2s x0)), so H is a residual coordinate over C[p]; A contains S = C[p,x,y,z,u]/(xy - z(z+1) - p^3u) (Danielewski-type twist of (SL2/T quadric) x A^1) and A = S[f/p^2, g/p^2] is an affine modification along the non-principal divisor V(f,g) = A^2_{s,u} of R = S/pS, whose pullback to…
why: No near-equivalent witness found in any field; the char-0 problem was listed as open by human experts in July 2026 and by Ghosh (April 2026). The strategy is not new (Asanuma's ring, Gupta's 'tempting' affine-fibration route, El Kahoui-Ouali stabilization are all in L), so the eureka content is the specific design that makes non-polynomiality PROVABLE: the Danielewski twist of the SL2/T quadric plus a non-principal A^2 centre whose Cox/torsor pullback is a single v carrying the -u^3 nonsquare. …

name: Principalizing the centre through the SL2 -> SL2/T torus bundle and lifting the additive action
statement: Spec R~ -> Spec R (R~ = C[a,d,b,c,u]/(ac-bd-1)) is a G_m-torsor in which I R~ = (v), v = a^3b - a^2u^3 - d^2, so G~ = G (x)_R R~ = R~[tau,V]/(tau^2V - v); every homogeneous LND of G lifts uniquely (normalized, fibre-linear) to a homogeneous LND of G~ of fibre weight 0.
why: Its form is precedented: principalize on the Cox torsor and lift the action there (Arzhantsev-Gaifullin 2010, ADHL book); Brion (in L) covers the lift. It is N2 rather than N1 because the object it acts on (gr A of a new witness) and the homogeneity bookkeeping are specific. It would be F5 if it were N3. Borderline N1.

name: Extraction lemma: polynomiality gives an LND E of R~ with fibre shift q <= 0 and E^2(v) = 0
statement: If A = C^[4], the positive-degree invariant is divisible by V, so D~V = 0; Case 1 (D~tau = 0): E = tau^j D~|R~, E(v) = 0, q = 0; Case 2: j odd, D~(r) = tau V^{l+1} E(r), q = -2(l+1) < 0, and LND-order counting gives E^2(v) = 0.
why: A new statement for a new ring, assembled from textbook LND-order facts once C2 is in place. Tracking the sign of the fibre shift is the key extra datum (Remark I26 shows it is necessary). The 'templated strengthening' cap concerns induction hypotheses and does not apply directly, but the content is bookkeeping. Sibling 049 reuses it.

name: Weighted rigidity: auxiliary grading (0,3,-3,0,2) + Mason-Stothers + nonsquare -u^3
statement: No nonzero LND E of R~ with fibre shift <= 0 has E^2(v) = 0: the highest auxiliary component E' satisfies (E')^2(d^2 + a^2u^3) = 0; orbit polynomials obey d(q)^2 + a(q)^2u(q)^3 = N(q) of degree <= 1; abc plus the nonsquareness of -u^3 in C(a,d,b)(u) force E' to fix a, d, u; then h = cE'(b) - bE'(c) in C[a,d,u] has weight e - 2 < 0, a contradiction.
why: The paper names its own precedent, which is in L. The new elements are the weight vector (fixed by linear constraints) and keeping leading coefficients in Frac(R~) for the nonsquare. That is a small variant. 049 shows the step depends on the witness's exponents rather than being a free-standing device.

name: Positive-degree invariant obstruction
statement: If A = C^[4], some coordinate has positive valuation degree (since deg F = 2), and d/dq_i for another coordinate kills it; the induced homogeneous LND of G = gr A has a nonzero homogeneous invariant of positive degree.
why: Downgraded from the analyst's N2: it specializes Gupta's Derksen-invariant method, which the paper names and which is in L. Borderline N2 only because of the Z-filtration care noted in the paper and the Lean's non-homogeneous variant.

name: Exact graded identification gr A = G = R[tau, I/tau^2] = P/(H_top)
statement: With weights (p,s,u,F,J) = (-1,0,0,2,2), each h in A has a representative of top weight exactly deg h; G = P/(H_top), with H_top = x^2F - (1+2sx)J - p^2J^2, is a smooth affine modification of R[tau] (Kaliman-Zaidenberg).
why: Downgraded from the analyst's N2. Computing gr of a hypersurface by its top-weight form is standard; the identification with R[tau, I/tau^2] is a computation once H is fixed, and Lean does it by a routine Rees argument. Borderline N2 if one credits the exactness check.

name: Kakeya maximal conjecture in R^3 (Thm 1.1)
statement: For every eps>0 there is C_eps with ||K_delta f||_{L^3(S^2)} <= C_eps delta^{-eps} ||f||_{L^3(R^3)} for all 0<delta<1, f in L^3.
why: Goal statement, not a device.

name: Shading / density-sensitive union estimate (eq. intro-density)
statement: Shading Y(T) subset T with |Y(T)|>=lambda|T|; target |union Y(T)| >~ delta^eps lambda^3 sum|T| uniformly in lambda.
why: Standard; WZ2025 Thm 1.2 remark states the needed lambda^3 explicitly.

name: Indexed weighted model (indices i=(omega_i, M_i=(b_i,u_i), S_i), events, full-time planks counting complete traces)
statement: Weighted lines with time-bin shadings; repeated traces allowed; plank membership requires the entire trace; n, I, k=I/n, m=I/|E|.
why: Book-keeping variant of weighted shaded tube families.

name: Exponent notation A <=exp B, slow diagonal / fixed tests convention
statement: Compare quantities by limsup log(A/B)/log N; all errors subpower; finite test lists then slow diagonal.
why: Standard.

name: Uniform temporal profile F (deficit profile of shading across log-scales)
statement: Nondecreasing 1-Lipschitz F:[0,1]->[0,1], F(0)=0, with |S_i cap I| = N^{kappa - F(kappa)+o(1)} uniformly over occupied blocks of N^kappa bins.
why: Close variant of branching functions / Lipschitz multiscale profiles (Keleti-Shmerkin, Orponen-Shmerkin eps-linear decompositions, Shmerkin-Wang) applied to the time shading of each tube.

name: Temporal cost Pi_F with smoothed discount D(q,e) and plank parameter Delta_A (two-parameter deformation)
statement: P_{p,q}(e)=p e - (1/eta) int_{1/2-eta}^{1/2} min(q, r e) dr; Pi_F(t)=int_0^t P_{p,q}(F'); Delta_A = sup_B n_B/(a^{d-1-A} b^{1+A}), d=2-q.
why: No neighbour found for a profile-dependent temporal cost; but deforming an induction-on-scales statement by extra parameters matches WZ's two-parameter assertions D(sigma,omega)/E(sigma,omega) and the 'add a parameter' template (cap N2).

name: Critical exponent h(p,z) (Def 2.3) and existence lemma
statement: h(p,z)= least A in [0,d-1] with m <=exp N^{A+Pi_F(1)} Delta_A for all uniform-profile sequences; valid at A=d-1 by Cauchy-Schwarz + slope-separated pair counting; h(p,-1)=0.
why: Worst-case-exponent / induction-on-scales paradigm of Wang-Zahl (beta), Keleti-Shmerkin, Ren-Wang.

name: Finite cleaning (Lemma 2.5) and conditional-probability pigeonholing
statement: Delete cells with retained mass < theta_0 of original; total loss <= L theta_0 mu(Omega); simultaneous pigeonholing of conditional probabilities.
why: Standard dyadic pigeonholing/cleaning.

name: Regularization and inherited branching (Lemma 2.6)
statement: Every sequence has an extensive refinement with a uniform profile; restrictions only increase branching deficits G(t)-G(s)>=F(t)-F(s), with total increase <= loss exponent.
why: Standard multiscale regularization (cf. uniform sets/ branching numbers).

name: Cost properties (Lemma 2.8): additivity, lsc, Lipschitz under restriction, rescaling; d/dp Pi = F(1), d/dz formula
statement: Pi_F additive, zero on flat intervals, lsc under uniform convergence, 0<=Pi_G-Pi_F<=pe; filling occupied blocks gives F^fill.
why: Elementary consequences of the definition.

name: Critical parameter point via BV approximate differentiability (Lemma 2.9)
statement: g=h-z is separately monotone, hence BV and (upgraded by monotonicity) totally differentiable a.e.; if h(p,0)>0 on an interval there is (p,z) with h>0, h_z>0, h_p<=0, h_z<=1.
why: No Kakeya precedent found for differentiating the critical exponent in auxiliary parameters; nearest are envelope-theorem arguments in optimization (Danskin; Milgrom-Segal) - a transfer risk.

name: Hybrid equality sequences and compactness (Lemma 2.10)
statement: For h_0<h there is sharp H in (h_0,h] and a sequence attaining equality; equality is stable under extensive refinement; limits as h_0->h give exact critical equalities.
why: Variant of WZ/Ren-Wang extremal configurations; the hybrid two-exponent trick is a small variant.

name: Kakeya set estimate (GWZ Thm 1.1) as input
statement: If Delta_max(T)<=delta^{-eta}, lambda>=delta^{eta}, then |union Y(T)| >= delta^eps sum|T|.
why: Cited theorem (Guth-Wang-Zahl streamlined; equivalent in strength to WZ2025).

name: Weighted convex clustering + weighted set estimate in a line chart (Lemmas 3.2-3.3)
statement: Weighted, repeated-index version of GWZ via random sampling with Chernoff bounds over a delta^{-C} net of boxes; full-time plank bound implies weighted convex clustering.
why: Standard weighted-to-unweighted sampling reduction.

name: Quantitative planar Furstenberg estimate (Ren-Wang Thm 4.1, Wang-Wu shaded form) and weighted corollary
statement: Planar Furstenberg (s,t) estimate in dual shaded-tube form, weighted.
why: Cited.

name: Endpoint multilinear Kakeya (BCT/Guth) and cube-count corollary
statement: Trilinear Kakeya with endpoint; cube counts on small caps.
why: Cited.

name: Derivative capture (Lemma 4.1): p- and z-derivatives of h select saturated packet shapes; every equality has deficit <= v=-h_p
statement: At the differentiability point, perturbing (p,z) along (pdot,zdot) yields saturated assignments with limiting shape parameters determined by h_p,h_z.
why: Same as M1-11; envelope-theorem logic applied to a worst-case exponent.

name: Local bound and isotropic scale cut (Prop 4.1 in Sec 'local')
statement: Active mass in a plank of widths a<=b<=K over a K-block is <=exp T=m N^{-Pi(kappa)} K^{-H} a^{d-1-H} b^{1+H}; conversely saturated packets rescale to new equalities with explicit cut profile G.
why: Standard consequence of a worst-case exponent (WZ 'sticky/rescaling' step).

name: Slack and cap mass; common short-block plane (planiness via multilinear Kakeya)
statement: N^{H+(p-2)alpha} <=exp k^2 m/n; tubes through a point in a cap of radius 1/L have mass <= m L^{-H} N^{-Pi}; on short blocks the rich directions lie within O(K^{-1}) of one plane.
why: KLT planiness / Guth Cor 1.4; paper names it.

name: Plate Nikodym bound (L^2, 1xKxK plates, log K loss)
statement: ||N_K f||_2^2 <~ (1+log K)||f||_2^2 for maximal averages over 1xKxK plates.
why: Classical (Cordoba 1977 type; plate maximal functions).

name: Planar-prefix extension and positive flat delay (Lemmas 4.5-4.6)
statement: Furstenberg density inside plates + plate Nikodym bound force full temporal branching on an initial interval [0,tau], tau>0, of every equality profile.
why: Composite of known tools (planiness + Furstenberg + plate maximal); the 'flat delay' statement is new but its proof is a routine combination.

name: Saturated plates on a flat scale; anisotropic normalization; positive-deficit equality (graininess analogue)
statement: On flat scales the weighted set theorem captures saturated plates; anisotropic rescaling of aligned plates rules out arbitrarily small total deficit.
why: Variant of KLT graininess and WZ/GWZ multiscale rescaling of grains/planks.

name: Canonical equality profile F(kappa)=beta(kappa-tau)_+ via minimum delay and inner/outer cuts (Prop 5.4)
statement: Among equalities with deficit v, the least initial delay tau_*>0 is attained by a profile that is flat then linear; complementary inner (anisotropic) and outer (isotropic) cuts force the first-passage locations.
why: Self-similar/linear extremal profile is the stickiness paradigm (WZ sticky reduction; Keleti-Shmerkin / Orponen-Shmerkin eps-linear pieces). Minimum-delay selection is a new variant; same device in sibling 079.

name: Stationary data: four matrix forms X,Y,U,V in moving packet frames, widths at rates (k_X,k_Y,k_U,k_V)=(0,tau,l,1)
statement: Packets have time interval and normal parameter theta; X=M_1+theta M_2, Y=M_2, U=u_1+theta u_2, V=u_2; change of frame acts by the shear matrices [[1,dt],[0,1]] . [[X,Y],[U,V]] . [[1,0],[dtheta,1]].
why: Line-parameter coordinates and 'time change adds velocity to position' are classical (Bourgain 1999 / Katz-Tao slices); the normal-frame shear is a new variant.

name: Angular Frostman bound and conditional X estimate
statement: Direction nonconcentration with exponent gamma>0 and conditional normal-position estimate on stationary packets.
why: Routine consequences.

name: Two-parameter coordinate-entropy function H(c,a) with ordered conditional rates j_G, gap-kernel differentiation and entropy demand
statement: H(c,a)=lim H_N(e_c,Q(c,a))/log N on domain U; H(c,a)>=H(c,0)+d a; d_c H >= s_0 l + sum_G (w-k_G) j_G; demand M - w(g-d) >= tau+B_* in stripe limits.
why: Paper names Hochman-Shmerkin local entropy averages as related (PLAN: self-named precedent caps at N2); 2-parameter (scale, offset) entropy function is the analogue of sibling 079's C1 (graded N3/0.3 there).

name: Projection constraints from two frames: ordinary/pinned pair laws on one index, pair information on the refinement gap, robust planar projection, product-slope…
statement: a_1>=y_1, u_1>=v_1, v_1>0 => y_1>=min(1,s_0+v_1), a_1<1 => u_1<=(a_1-s_0)_+ (tied case analogous); proved by comparing the actual same-index joint law with the product of conditional marginals (positive mutual information needed) plus Ren-Wang projections and a product-slope (dt*dtheta) pinning bootstrap.
why: Pinning adapted from SW/OSW (named); the joint-vs-product mutual-information comparison is a standard entropy device.

name: Vanishing at the maximal endpoint (five-case closure)
statement: There are p>2 arbitrarily close to 2 with h(p,0)=0; proved by five case comparisons (Table) of stripe-averaged entropy demand against projection constraints.
why: Arithmetic closure.

name: Maximal reduction: h(p,0)=0 => ||K_delta f||_3 <= C delta^{-(p-2)/3-kappa}||f||_3
statement: Discrete estimate |A| >= c N^{-xi} n N max(N^{-1},lambda)^{p+1}, then indicator estimate and passage to L^3 retaining the density power.
why: Standard (Bourgain/Wolff/Tao).

name: Nikodym maximal estimates (R^3 and constant-curvature 3-manifolds) and local curved Kakeya (Bourgain condition)
statement: Via transfers of Gao-Liu-Xi.
why: Cited transfers.

name: Every Kakeya set in R^4 has Hausdorff dimension 4 (Thm 1.1)
statement: If K subset R^4 contains a unit segment in every direction (no measurability/compactness), dim_H K=4.
why: Goal.

name: Exact problems (versions 1 and 2), worlds, incidence selections, tempered data, observations p_s
statement: Sequences of weighted trajectory laws y(t)=y_0+tV in R^j, hidden coordinate w (quadratic in v1, affine in v2), native polynomial P_*; incidence events; polynomially bounded data.
why: Book-keeping model.

name: Cap class C(d), d<1 (density exponent below one per hidden bin + angular cap)
statement: f(L)-f(r)<=d(L-r) and joint (p_L,[V]) density <= n(L) N_0^{-Su}.
why: Hidden-coordinate density with exponent < 1 is a Frostman-type nonconcentration hypothesis; variant.

name: Charts, true packets, known atlases: quadratic test small along whole line pieces in a moving box, with mass floor m_c/q >= n(r) J_c
statement: Chart = time interval I of length q=N_0^{-h}, affine centre y_c, matrix D_c, test P of degree <=2 in (t,y,w) with |P|<=K a_r, |P_w|>=B/K on selected incidences; true if mass per time >= density x Jacobian.
why: No exact neighbour found; close relatives: Guth-Zahl tubes near low-degree hypersurfaces / polynomial Wolff axioms, HRZ multiscale polynomial Wolff, WZ convex grains, Wu regulus strips; Guth's outline suggests replacing convex sets by low-complexity semialgebraic sets in higher dimensions.

name: Minimum horizon H(E) (time cost infimum of true terminal systems); initial bound H(E)<=L
statement: H(E)= inf h for which a true terminal system with interval length N_0^{-h} exists; every homogeneous problem has H<=L via weighted planks.
why: Worst-case exponent paradigm (WZ) applied to the chart functional; the functional itself rides on M2-04.

name: Reduction to a bad weighted problem: dim_H K<4 => exists tempered version-2 problem in C(d), d<1, with H(E)>0
statement: Outer-measure finite selection of witnesses at one scale (Hausdorff covers with time fraction ck^{-2}), smoothing, densities g(1,0)>=sigma, g(0,0)<=0 (via R^3 weighted plank estimate on projected y-lines), g<=r+2-2u; endpoint maximization selects (r_0,u_0).
why: Standard Hausdorff-to-single-scale reduction plus 3D input; the encoding into charts is M2-04.

name: Algebraic analytic norm comparison (Bernstein-Remez for algebraic sheets) and polynomial cost of continuation
statement: For holomorphic algebraic sheets of degree <=D, sup norms on a real ball and a complex polydisc are polynomially comparable; continuation along broken paths costs polynomially.
why: Roytwarf-Yomdin Bernstein classes (named).

name: Two-color matching (comparison principle for scalar sheets with list sizes N^{d}, d<1)
statement: No sequence of two lists of C^{J+1} functions of size N^{d+o(1)} with a sampled incidence law where values agree to N^{-1} but some derivative of order <=D differs by >=K^{-1}; proof by alternating fresh conditional samples (paths) and endpoint-map Jacobian volume.
why: Paper names Christ's method of refinements as the analogue (PLAN cap N2).

name: Terminal time extension
statement: A true terminal system of cost h yields a known atlas of cost h-e with remaining length <= Ce.
why: Application of M2-08.

name: Critical paths: extremal (d_*, k, narrowness ell), linear relative profiles, composition of horizons, excluded improvements
statement: Optimize least cap dimension d_* with positive horizon, then maximal horizon rate k in (0,1], then minimal narrowness ell; maximizing sequences have linear profiles and nested true systems.
why: WZ-style worst-case exponent with lexicographic refinement; the same device appears in siblings 074-M1 and 079 C2.

name: Prepared tangent data, candidate conversion and original-law recovery of finite lists
statement: Local improvement candidates on substantial residuals become actual known atlases in original N_0 units with recoverable finite label lists.
why: Plumbing.

name: Scalar-normal first jet, higher-jet polynomial fitting, planar dot-product alternative (WZ sticky Thm 5.2 restatement)
statement: Conditional scalar estimates give polynomial fits along individual lines; planar input from Wang-Zahl sticky paper.
why: Cited WZ planar theorem (N0) + routine fitting.

name: Isotropic improvement (ell=0): velocity graph, polynomial qualification, conservativity of interpolated field (switched lines -> potential)
statement: Separated velocities determine an approximate polynomial field; multilinear Kakeya (Carbery-Valdimarsson determinant form) and interpolation combine line fits; switching lines makes the field approximately conservative, yielding a potential.
why: Polynomial-field fitting from directional data + multilinear Kakeya is in the polynomial-method tradition (Guth-Zahl, Bourgain-Guth); the conservativity-by-switching step is a variant of hairbrush/switching arguments.

name: Weighted full-time plank estimate (from sibling M1 'Lemma 2.3' = M1-14)
statement: Weighted, repeated-index R^3 set estimate under a full-time plank cap with long marks.
why: Thin weighted wrapper of GWZ Thm 1.1; locator 'Lemma 2.3' does not match M1's compiled numbering (Lemma 3.3).

name: Seven-direction tensor tests, restoration of an approximate real conic, and Degree restoration (Prop 6.x)
statement: For 7 directions with every triple independent: quadrics through them form <=1-dim space; T->(T(p_i,p_i,.)) injective on cubics; if they lie on a conic q, three-copy kernels at ranks 3,4,5 are q.(R^3)*, R q^2, {0}. The surviving cubic/quartic terms of the potential are re-expressed through the hidden coordinate w on retained trajectories, giving a quadratic chart test with gain h^{e_2}.
why: No neighbour found for absorbing degree-3/4 terms along a conic of directions into the hidden coordinate; classical apolarity covers only the kernel lemma.

name: Retained-edge planar rigidity: graph BSG with retained original edges + Orponen-de Saxce-Shmerkin multiplicative convolution => flat generated coefficients, pa…
statement: A BSG argument that keeps a substantial set of original incidence edges; ODS Fourier decay of multiplicative convolutions gives coefficients with small interval probabilities; affine-skew row fit.
why: BSG (SSV-style path version) and ODS are N0 imports; retaining original edges is a small variant. Bridge additive combinatorics -> Kakeya is a known route (Bourgain 1999, Katz-Tao).

name: Scalar mesh projection theorem; wide-interval improvement
statement: Projection to the scalar model at finite meshes gives full-time graphs; wide projected intervals give a time improvement by comparison.
why: Projection-to-lower-dimensional-model is standard strategy; implementation new.

name: Reduction to the horizontal model Y'=-Z+tv (Heisenberg/SL2-type horizontal lines), boxes H x H^2
statement: If projected intervals are narrow, planar rigidity forces Z=p+tv, Y=q_0-tp+O(N^{-e_0}) with k=ell; natural boxes horizontal size H, transverse H^2; hidden sheets nearly affine.
why: Horizontal/SL2 lines are the known Katz-Zahl/Katz-Wu-Zahl/Fassler-Orponen enemy; Korányi H x H^2 boxes are standard Heisenberg geometry.

name: Critical-rate improvement at 2k=1 (three-leg switch) and parameter bootstrap / return to wide intervals for 2k!=1
statement: At 2k=1, an affine primitive of x' plus three successive trajectory changes fill 3D base volume and force one heavy intercept bin; for 2k<1 a parameter bootstrap reaches width h_s^2, then wide intervals.
why: Switching/alternating-path arguments in the Heisenberg model are close to Christ refinements and Katz-Zahl/Fassler-Orponen SL2 arguments; new instance.

name: Exclusion of unbounded optimized narrowness (full-time localization, relative density cancellation, scalar projection)
statement: If ell=infinity, two nested chart labels localize trajectories over the whole normalized interval; normalization shifts cancel in relative densities; scalar projection yields atlases of time cost -> 0, contradicting k>0.
why: Composite of the paper's own tools.

name: Consequences: general direction-set bound, 4D Nikodym dimension on constant-curvature manifolds, fixed-chart curved Kakeya, rank-one quadratic curved Kakeya in…
statement: Transfers via Keleti-Mathe, Gao-Liu-Xi, Nadjimzadah.
why: Cited transfers.

id: M2-15 Degree restoration through the hi…
why: Handles the conic/quadric configuration of broad directions, i.e. the Guth-Zahl quadric obstruction, inside the isotropic branch; without it the improved test has degree 3-4 and is not an admissible chart. Non-analytic: nothing like 'absorb cubic and quartic potential terms along a conic of directions into the hidden coordinate' occurs in the goal or in L. Load-bearing for the ell=0 branch and (in its scalar version) for the zero-horizon scalar model that supplies projections to the other branc…

This is what converts Wang-Zahl's lambda^{K(eps)} into lambda^3: the cost Pi_F records how the shading deficit is spread over scales. Derivatives h_p, h_z identify the extremal deficit (v=-h_p) and the thin width rate (w), giving the stationary parameters used in the closure. No Kakeya/Furstenberg precedent found for differentiating a worst-case exponent in auxiliary parameters.

id: M2-04 + M2-05 Quadratic charts / true p…
why: Central new extension object: degree-2 tests held small along whole line pieces in moving boxes, nested across scales, measured by a time cost. Not in goal or L.

Replaces incidence counting by conditional entropy rates of four matrix coordinates with different refinement speeds; the shear X'=X+dt U+dtheta Y+dt dtheta V is the engine of the closure. Analogue of sibling 079's C1 (graded N3/0.3).
Turns density exponent d<1 into rigidity of scalar sheets; used in every regime.

name: Quadratic charts / true packets / known atlases with the horizon functional H(E)
statement: A chart is a time interval I (length q=N_0^{-h}), an affine moving box (y_c, D_c), and a degree-<=2 polynomial test P(t,y,w) with |P|<=K a_r along every assigned whole line piece, |P_w|>=B/K on selected incidences; it is true if its incidence mass per unit time is at least the hidden-bin density n(r) times its spatial Jacobian. The horizon H(E) is the least time cost of a true terminal system. A Hausdorff counterexample yields a problem with H(E)>0 in a class where hidden densities grow with ex…
why: Passes tests 1-3 as far as checked: no equivalent object found in any field searched; non-analytic; carries all of M2. Downgrade pressure: (i) Guth's published remark points to semialgebraic grains in higher dimension, so the idea may be one step from L; (ii) the horizon is a WZ-template worst-case exponent; (iii) M2 is unverified (14k lines, jump 3.059 -> 4). Not Lean-formalized: goes on the informal list only.

name: Deformed critical inequality: temporal deficit profile F, profile-dependent cost Pi_F with smoothed discount D(q,e), plank exponent A, critical exponent h(p,z)
statement: m <=exp N^{A+Pi_F(1)} Delta_A with Pi_F(t)=int_0^t [p F' - (1/eta) int min(q, r F') dr]; h(p,z)=least valid A; h(p,0)=0 for p->2 gives the maximal theorem with lambda^3.
why: Templated strengthening of an induction-on-scales statement ('add a parameter' + 'carry an extra tracked quantity'); PLAN caps it at N2. The temporal-cost integrand is a new design choice inside the template.

name: Derivative capture: a.e. total differentiability of the critical exponent (BV + monotonicity) and selection of extremal deficit and plank shape by h_p, h_z
statement: h-z is separately monotone, hence BV, hence totally differentiable a.e. (AFP Thm 3.83 upgraded by a monotone sandwich). At a point with h>0, h_z>0, every equality has deficit <= v=-h_p, and perturbations along (pdot,zdot) give saturated assignments whose shape parameters are fixed by h_p, h_z (w=h_z+l D_q).
why: Under the STRICT rule, importing the envelope-theorem principle is transfer; the Kakeya-specific execution (BV upgrade, saturated-shape selection) is a variant. Recorded as a new bridge (BV/envelope -> induction on scales). Would be N3/F2 only if an expert judged the shape-selection step non-envelope.

name: Degree restoration through the hidden coordinate (seven-direction tensor kernels; conic case)
statement: When the broad directions (1,v_i) lie near a conic q=0, three-copy tests leave the kernels q.(R^3)* (rank 3) and R q^2 (rank 4). The surviving cubic and quartic terms of the potential are re-expressed through the hidden coordinate w on retained trajectories, restoring a quadratic chart test with gain h^{e_2}.
why: Fails or only borderline-passes test 3 as a terminal repair, and is plausibly forced by the paper's own degree-2 chart choice (low pivot distance). Clever F5-type re-representation, but graded N2.

name: Two-parameter coordinate-entropy function H(c,a) in moving frames, with two-frame projection constraints (shear, product-slope pinning, pair information)
statement: Four coordinates X,Y,U,V refine at speeds (0,tau,l,1); H(c,a) with H(c,a)>=H(c,0)+d a and d_c H >= s_0 l + sum (w-k_G) j_G; frame change [[1,dt],[0,1]] M [[1,0],[dtheta,1]] gives projections constrained by Ren-Wang; the tied case needs the product slope dt*dtheta (pinning adapted from SW/OSW); same-index dependence handled by joint-vs-product mutual information.
why: Self-named precedents (HS, SW/OSW) cap at N2 under PLAN.

name: Canonical profile F=beta(kappa-tau)_+ via minimum delay and complementary inner/outer cuts; flat delay tau>0
statement: Among equalities with deficit v the least initial delay is positive and attained by a flat-then-linear profile that reproduces itself under outer cuts (stationarity).
why: Self-similar extremal profile = stickiness paradigm; minimum-delay selection is a variant.

name: Two-color matching comparison principle for scalar algebraic sheets (lists of size N^{d}, d<1)
statement: Two lists of N^{d+o(1)} smooth functions cannot agree in value to N^{-1} on a sampled incidence law while some derivative of order <=D stays separated; alternating fresh conditional samples give a polynomial endpoint map with nonzero Jacobian whose image is too large.
why: Self-named precedent; cap N2.

name: Horizontal (Heisenberg/SL2-type) model Y'=-Z+tv and the three-leg switch at the critical rate 2k=1
statement: Narrow projected intervals force Z=p+tv, Y=q_0-tp+O(N^{-e_0}) with natural boxes H x H^2; at 2k=1 three successive changes of trajectory fill 3D base volume and force one heavy intercept bin; for 2k<1 a parameter bootstrap reaches width h^2.
why: Known enemy model; switching argument is a variant.

name: Isotropic improvement: polynomial velocity field from line fits, conservativity by switching lines (potential)
statement: Separated velocities determine an approximate polynomial field; multilinear Kakeya (determinant form) and interpolation combine line fits; switching between lines makes the field approximately conservative, producing a potential.
why: Composite of known polynomial-method and switching tools.

name: L log L Orlicz class
statement: L log L(T) = {f : int |f| log(2+|f|) dmu < infinity}, mu normalized Lebesgue measure on T = R/2piZ.
why: Textbook Zygmund class.

name: Fourier coefficients and symmetric partial sums S_N f
statement: hat f(k) = int f e^{-ikx} dmu, S_N f = sum_{|k|<=N} hat f(k) e^{ikx}.
why: Textbook.

name: Thm main: a.e. convergence in L log L (thm:main)
statement: For every complex f in L log L(T) there is a null set N_f with S_N f(x) -> f(x) for x outside N_f, along the full sequence N = 0,1,2,...
why: Headline claim; graded via its machinery.

name: Uncentred interval maximal function M rho and good set G_rho = {M rho <= e^{4h}}, h = log log d
statement: M rho(x) = sup over arcs I containing x of the average of rho on I; G_rho = {M rho <= e^{4h}}; weak (1,1) gives |G_rho^c| <= C e^{-4h} = C (log d)^{-4}.
why: Maximal function is N0; restricting to its sublevel set at height (log d)^4 is a parameter choice of a known good-set strategy (Lie 2013).

name: Thm good-set: truncated integral estimate (thm:good-set)
statement: Absolute C, d_*: if d >= d_*, rho >= 0 periodic, int rho = 1, rho <= e^d a.e., then int over G_rho of sup_N |S_N rho| <= C d.
why: A good-set L1 estimate for one height layer is a known reduction template (Lie 2013 Prop 3.1); the novelty is the endpoint quantification (loss exactly d, exceptional set (log d)^{-4}), which is the whole difficulty but not a new concept.

name: Prop bounded inputs: a.e. convergence for bounded f (prop:fourier-bounded)
statement: Every bounded complex periodic function has a.e. convergence of S_N f along the full sequence; proof via Fejer means P_l, Thm good-set with d_l = d_* + log(2B/m_l), Markov.
why: Statement is classical (a special case of Carleson-Hunt). The proof route is new only in that it goes through Thm good-set.

name: Doubly exponential height layers f_j and d_j = 2^{j+1} + log^- m_j
statement: f = f_bd + sum_j f_j, f_j = f 1{e^{2^j} <= |f| < e^{2^{j+1}}}; four nonnegative parts q_j with mass m_j, rho_j = q_j/m_j <= e^{d_j}; sum m_j d_j < infinity iff int |f| log|f| < infinity (plus an entropy term).
why: Standard dyadic-in-log layer decomposition; the doubly exponential spacing is what makes (log d_j)^{-4} summable.

name: Cor weak-L1 maximal bound with Luxemburg norm (cor:fourier-weak-l1)
statement: Phi(t) = t log(2+t), ||f||_Phi Luxemburg; sup_lambda lambda mu{S* f > lambda} <= C ||f||_Phi for all f in L log L(T; C).
why: Direct application of Stein's 1961 continuity principle to the a.e.-finite maximal function.

name: Signed span [D] of a finite list
statement: [D] = { sum_{v in D} eps_v v : eps_v in {-1,0,1} }.
why: Standard.

name: Two laws: uniform output law U versus true input law P (dP = rho/m_top dU)
statement: U follows a uniformly chosen output point (fair bits); P is weighted by the current input; noisy labels are observations of the input point; processing choices depend only on spatial and membership state.
why: A change-of-measure / duality framing; the specific coupling of the two laws through a Fisher-information identity is new, but the device of weighting by the density is classical.

name: Compression parameters h, T, w, L, m_*
statement: h = log log d, T = floor(d h^{-5}), w = (log d)^{1/4}, L = d exp(w), m_* = floor(exp(w^3)).
why: Parameter choices.

name: Lemma entropy compression (lemma:compression)
statement: q strictly positive pmf on Z with q(x)/q(0) = int chi_{gx} d omega, -log q(0) <= D0 d; finite S with log|nS| <= D0 d h^{P0} log d for n <= d^2; d/h^2 <= E <= D0 d and -log E_lambda H_q(X_1+..+X_T - X'_1-..-X'_T) <= E for every prob lambda on S. Then there are x0 in S and S' subset S with log|S| - log|S'| <= C(D0) d^2/(E h^2) and, for EVERY probability v on S', int exp(-L sum_x v(x)(1 - Re chi_{g(x-x0)})) d omega >= e^{-CE}.
why: Passes a quick no-near-equivalent check: its conclusion (one centre and one omega-region good for all weights on S') and its hypothesis (uniform bound on noisy 2T-fold sums) do not match Chang/Lee/Bloom/Kelley-Meka statements. Risk: a judge may call it an entropy variant of Chang's lemma (N2).

name: Lemma noisy sum with prescribed marginals (entropy-foundations:variational)
statement: There is an exchangeable law of X^T with uniform marginals on S and Gamma in TS-TS such that D(X^T || U_S^T) + I(X^T; Z) + E c(Gamma) <= E, Z = sum X_i + Gamma; proved by finite Gibbs variational duality (dual: sup over multipliers a of sum E a - log max_z sum e^{sum a(x_i)} H_q(z - sum x_i)).
why: Close neighbour named by the paper (Lee 2017 entropy maximization).

name: Noisy-sum entropy cost C_p(X^s, Gamma) = D(X^s||p^s) + I(X^s; Z) + E c(Gamma)
statement: Cost of a correlated letter vector with an error Gamma relative to a product law p; nonnegative, convex in the joint law.
why: A conjunction of standard quantities (relative entropy, mutual information, expected cost); new as a packaged potential. Borderline N1/N2.

name: Lemma projection and conditioning rules (entropy-foundations:cost-rules)
statement: (i) dropping letters and keeping the error does not increase C_p; (ii) conditioning on finite J costs at most H(J); (iii) conditioning on a prefix is free and the comparison product can be changed to nu^k.
why: Direct chain-rule consequences.

name: Lemma selection of a conditional marginal (entropy-foundations:exchangeable)
statement: Conditioning the exchangeable law on a random prefix of length in [T/4, T/2] gives a marginal nu with log|S| - H(nu) <= CE/T, cost <= CE, and m_*-blocks within TV C m_* sqrt(E)/T of nu^{m_*}.
why: Pinning lemma is a close known neighbour (not cited by the paper).

name: Context W, refinement, and the functionals G_s(W), I_r(W), K_m(W; r)
statement: Context = finite variable jointly distributed with X ~ nu; G_s = H(sum of s iid letters | contexts); I_r = inf over couplings of r H(X|W) - H(X^r | sum, W^r); K_m(W; r) = noisy block cost with error Gamma.
why: Built from entropic-sumset vocabulary; new functionals but close to known quantities.

name: Lemma monotonicities and uniform entropy bounds (entropy-foundations:context-bounds)
statement: G_s nondecreasing in s, nonincreasing under refinement, <= D_* = C(D0) d for s <= m_*; I_r nonnegative, nondecreasing in r, nonincreasing under refinement, <= D_* for r <= T0.
why: Routine.

name: Lemma lifting block sums and refining contexts (entropy-foundations:block-cost)
statement: K_m unchanged if block sums are replaced by full iid m-letter rows; K_m nonincreasing under refinement.
why: Routine coupling lemma.

name: Lemma low-end noisy cost via thinning (entropy-foundations:thinning)
statement: For m <= m_*, 2mr <= T0, r <= T e^{-w^2}/2: K_m(W; r) <= CE, by tagging blocks with the common submeasure min(mu, Q), weighted acceptance B/(2r), and filling with R = (Q - eta)/delta.
why: Coupling bookkeeping.

name: Lemma gluing two couplings (entropy-refinement:gluing)
statement: Observing (sum of m letters, other contexts) refines W to W' with G_1(W)-G_1(W') = G_m(W)-G_{m-1}(W) and I_r(W)-I_r(W') >= K_m(W;r) - K_{m-1}(W;r); partial (Bernoulli-marked) observations scale both.
why: Elementary but well-aimed inequality; a judge would likely see it as a variant of entropy-increment arguments.

name: Prop finite refinement search with two visit orders (entropy-refinement:search)
statement: There is a finite refinement W and index j with G_1(empty) - G_1(W) <= C D_*^2/(E h^2) and K_{m_{j,1}}(W; r_j) <= K_{m_{j,0}}(W; r_j) + E. Proof: macroblocks ascending, subblocks descending, indices ascending, with skip rules p > c0/alpha0 + delta0 and P > c1/alpha1 + delta1; two telescopes (endpoint telescope for skips, exact-cost telescope for completed targets).
why: Weak N3: a hard-to-find combinatorial schedule that buys the h^{-2} saving the endpoint needs; nearest neighbours are generic increment/pigeonhole schedules. Could be graded N2 (it is a scheduling device inside a templated increment argument).

name: Freezing contexts and extracting one phase region (completion of lemma:compression)
statement: Freeze a context stack, compare with independent law p x q, find an atom z_* with Q_Z(z_*) >= q(0) e^{-CE}, write it as int prod |E chi_{gX}| d omega, restrict to R = {sum(1-|phi_i|^2) <= C_R E}, pick a coordinate and centre x0 by Markov, prune to S' of mass >= 1/2.
why: Standard extraction.

name: Thermal forms A = sum lambda_s (1 - Re chi_s), form order, q_A, F(A), K_A, Delta_A, B_A(r) (Definition Thermal forms)
statement: q_A(u) = Fourier coefficients of e^{-A}; F(A) = -log q_A(0) (free energy); K_A = e^{F-A} probability density; Delta_A(u) = ||1 - chi_u||_{L2(K_A)}; B_A(r) = {u : Delta_A(u) <= r}.
why: Transfer of XY-model Gibbs densities plus a Bohr-type metric; new packaging, close neighbours in stat mech and additive combinatorics (Bohr sets).

name: Lemma thermal positivity and monotonicity (lemma:thermal-monotonicity)
statement: q_A is a nonnegative even pmf; Cov_{K_A}(Re chi_u, Re chi_v) >= 0; hence coefficients increase and Delta_A decreases in form order, Delta_A is subadditive, F is increasing with decreasing increments; envelope bound for products of shifted thermal weights.
why: Cross-field transfer from statistical mechanics (Griffiths-Ginibre inequalities); re-proved for this one-site case.

name: Thermal labels Z = Y + theta, theta ~ K_A; label updates A+ = A + S_p + D_i; spatial forms S_p = R_p^2 (1 - Re chi_1)
statement: A noisy observation of the input point with XY-Gibbs noise; on each success the form is tightened by a spatial term at the current interval and a metric term D_i = lambda B; label errors independent given Y; choices never inspect sampled labels.
why: An auxiliary random variable built only to transfer frequency information into information-theoretic currency; no near neighbour found in the Carleson literature (quick search). Risk: noisy-channel/Gaussian-smoothing devices are common in information theory (e.g. de Bruijn identity, stochastic localization), so a judge may see transfer (N2).

name: Global label Fisher sum: sum over live jumping pieces of U(p) alpha_e J_p <= C d, with J_p = int |D|^2/M
statement: M_pm, M, D are the label-weighted child masses; the Fisher sum is bounded by the total information budget d + log h + E B_mem + O(d) via the chain rule and 'squared bias <= 2 x relative entropy to a fair bit'.
why: Known mechanism (entropy chain rule over a dyadic filtration, cf. Friedgut-style entropy proofs, martingale square function), new application.

name: Separated spectrum -> compression problem: high integers, separated collections avoiding B_A(r_sep) + {|j| <= sigma R_p}, snapping to gZ, polarizing v_x, sumse…
statement: Verifies the hypotheses of I12 for the label-weighted child moments: sumset size via a positive Riesz-type product over a dissociated subset (|Lambda| <= C d/beta^2) and the moment cap E_T(nu) <= D0 d via thermal envelope bounds.
why: Transfer of Chang/Lee dissociated-spectrum argument; the label side information is the only adaptation.

name: Gap potential F(A) - log|B_A(r)| with tracked radius r = r_sep/4 + eta x (number of additions)
statement: Starts at 0, bounded below by a numerical constant, increases by <= C2 t at a regular success, decreases by >= k_b/2 at a cheap success; telescoping gives sum_cheap k_b <= 2 C2 sum_regular t + C.
why: A non-obvious monovariant mixing two currencies (free energy and packing entropy) whose drop at cheap updates is exactly what is needed; no near-equivalent found. Risk: increment-potential arguments are a standard template (N2).

name: Lemma spectral update (lemma:spectral-update)
statement: Under count/form caps, a request at level b yields t in [d/h^2, D0 d], t >= eps k_b, a metric form D_i = lambda B with flat free-energy increment, and an input-only success set; either (i) regular test with success probability >= beta/2 and E_T(nu) >= t/4, or (ii) cheap deterministic update with t = eps k_b and uniform nu; log|S'| >= 0.8 k_b; gap potential bounds as in I29.
why: The regular/cheap dichotomy with an iterated compression (t shrinks by 4 each round) and a flat-increment selection is specific to this proof; components are N0-N2 but the update as a whole has no near neighbour found.

name: Prop regular evidence (prop:thermal-evidence)
statement: With N_h = ceil(h^{120}) fresh evidence clones per regular success, the observable event {some clone Z' with A(Z'-Z) <= 4 s_d and |sum nu(x) v_x(Z') chi_{gx}(V)| >= beta/4} has reference probability <= e^{-t/8}, while under the true law it occurs at every regular success except with probability o(h^{-20}).
why: Standard hypothesis-testing logic with a specific device (evidence clones).

name: Prop modulated delayed Haar estimate (prop:dyadic)
statement: For d >= d0, interval I with |I| in [1/2,1], rho <= e^d, mean <= 2, F_{j+1}-measurable multipliers |eps_j| <= 1 shared by all modulations, stopping time tau(x) = first j with E_{p_j(x)} rho > e^{4h}: int over I of max_{|u| <= Q} |sum_{j < tau} E_{p_j}[rho chi_u r_{j+1}] eps_j r_{j+2}| dx/|I| <= C d, uniformly in I, rho, J, Q, multipliers.
why: The lemma itself is a strong eureka candidate: a model-operator estimate whose statement encodes the right endpoint (L1 bound Cd per layer, stopping at (log d)^4) and whose proof is wholly new. As a statement it is a 'dyadic version of the conjecture', which a judge could call analytic (N2).

name: Finite procedure: live/static pieces, epochs, plateaus (normalization alpha, reset if m > 2 alpha), transfer rules (m < e^{-d}, Q > R0 d, n >= C0 h), membershi…
statement: A deterministic stopping/splitting procedure on the dyadic tree that partitions rho into plateau pieces whose normalized contributions sum exactly to the transform.
why: A stopping-tree decomposition (classical template: CZ / Carleson-measure stopping times, Lacey-Thiele tree selection) with new splitting rules.

name: Prop live budgets (prop:live-budgets)
statement: (i) per-branch sum k_b + sum t + sum relative metric costs <= Cd, n <= Ch; (ii) ||B_mem||_{L2(P)} + ||X_*||_{L2(P)} <= Ch, P(transfer) <= C h^{-10}; (iii) sum_live U(p_e) alpha_e <= Ch and kill sums <= 1; (iv) global label Fisher sum <= Cd (I27); (v) spatial bit relative entropies O(d), O(h) if stopped at the cutoff.
why: Many budgets, each by a standard probabilistic tool; the inductive caps (form cap, count cap) are an IH strengthening by tracked quantities (templated).

name: Reference law Q (fair membership coins) and score supermartingale S with factor exp((t/16) 1{success and evidence}) / (1 + e^{-t/16})
statement: Change of measure: P(S > R e^d) <= e^{-d}; combined with R <= exp(d + log h + B_mem) excludes Q > 1000 d outside probability O(h^{-10}).
why: Standard change-of-measure.

name: Prop capture on a plateau (prop:capture) incl. trimmed masks, polynomial products Q_z, edge charges, snapshots, activation
statement: Cumulative list D with appends at jumping post states; non-bad high u is within poly(1+|D|, d_1, 1/b)/|p| of [D]; E|D|_final <= C d_1 b^{-C}; bad-edge charges O(d) (one scalar level) and poly(h)(h + log d) (all main levels); snapshots of <= ceil(e^{k_{b/2}}) main or exp(C(d_1 + log 1/b)) scalar representatives with expected count poly(D_max, d_1, 1/b); non-bad high jumps before activation lie in one block of <= H_b depths.
why: Riesz-product entropy increment (Lee 2017) + windowed likelihood charging; strong but templated.

name: Lemma predictable signs (lemma:paths-sign)
statement: For fair signs r_{i+1} and F_i-measurable c_i: outside probability e^{-t}, sum c_i r_{i+1} <= (theta/2) sum c_i^2 + t/theta for every prefix.
why: Textbook.

name: Prop scalar plateau paths (prop:scalar-path) with potential psi(x) = b^{1/2}((|x|^2+b^2)^{3/4} - b^{3/2})
statement: Masked delayed transform on any contiguous interval is <= C b^{1/4}(1 + K_e + t) outside probability C e^{-t}.
why: Bellman-function technique (Burkholder; Nazarov-Treil-Volberg) with a new specific potential.

name: Lemma energy drift and innovations (lemma:paths-innovation)
statement: G_pre = G + g + r U_p; |a - vD|^2 <= M g_z; |U_p|^2 <= C max(G_pm)(J + g); (int|a|)^2 <= C(GJ + g); forward budgets E sum g <= C, E sum J <= Cd, E sum xi <= 2.
why: Routine.

name: Lemma delayed norm estimate on a run with absolute Fisher coefficient (lemma:paths-run-norm)
statement: On an outer-valid run, outside probability C e^{-t}, int |W_P(z)| dz <= C sum J_p + C lambda^{-1}(1 + sum xi + sum e') + C lambda t, lambda = b^{1/2}; proof via two-step blocks and concavity of the norm of X_0 = (W, f, lambda M).
why: Likely N2: a Bellman-function-style concavity estimate; the augmentation of the state by lambda M to get an absolute Fisher coefficient is clever but templated (add a tracked coordinate).

name: Prop vector estimates on inner-valid intervals with Fisher checkpoints (prop:vector-path) and Lemma simultaneous representatives / random dyadic list caps (lem…
statement: Predictable origins (run starts + checkpoints whenever accumulated J reaches 1) with expected number <= P(d, 1/b0); every inner-valid interval I satisfies int|sum a_p eps r| <= C sum_I J + C b^{-1/2}(1 + K_e + E_{e,b}) + C b^{1/2} t; parameters t_b, H_b chosen simultaneously over all representatives and all dyadic caps with E t_b <= C k_{b/4} + C log(Cd/b).
why: Bookkeeping.

name: Assembly of Prop dyadic: plateau reduction, exact decoding c_A(n) = 1 - Delta_A(n)^2/2 >= 1/2, scalar prefix, static families, rare transfers
statement: sup_u |T_e^u| is bounded by a frequency-independent majorant (eq 09-live-majorant); main levels cost O(d/h) per live plateau, times total live weight O(h) gives O(d); static families cost C U(q) m (1 + h + log^- m)(d + 2 + log^- m); transfers controlled by P(transfer) <= C h^{-10} and ||X_*||_2 <= Ch.
why: Summation bookkeeping; the key 'O(d/h) per plateau x O(h) weight' split is the design choice of I33/I27.

name: Haar profiles h, g, finite shift S_{a,s,J}, kernel kappa(u) = int g(v) h(v-u) dv, K_J(t) = int_{2^{-J}}^1 kappa(t/r) dr/r^2, c = int_0^1 kappa = -1/8
statement: Translation and scale averaging of the delayed Haar shift is convolution with K_J; kappa is odd, Lipschitz, supported in [-1,1]; c = -1/8 agrees with Hytonen's Haar-shift kernel evaluation.
why: Transfer of Petermichl-Hytonen dyadic representation.

name: Hilbert transform to Fourier projections: H_delta -> H in L2, Pi_{>=0} = (I + iH + P0)/2, S_N rho = chi_{-N} Pi(rho chi_N) - chi_{N+1} Pi(rho chi_{-(N+1)}), su…
statement: Standard reduction of the Carleson maximal operator to maximally modulated Hilbert transforms, with symbol identity int sin(2 pi k t) cot(pi t) dt = 1.
why: Textbook.

This is the device that converts frequency selection into information-theoretic currency: a new random variable Z = Y + theta, never present in the goal or in L, whose Fisher information along output paths is globally bounded by O(d) via the entropy chain rule, while decoding int chi_n a^s = c_A(n) c^{s+n} recovers each modulation. It is the literal analogue of an extension variable: tiny to state, absent from the problem, and it makes the 'separate costs for information and for choosing freque…

Not a subterm of the goal; its conclusion is uniform over all weights on the retained subset (one centre, one omega-region), which is what lets the spectral update choose the weight afterwards. The cardinality loss d^2/(E h^2) is exactly calibrated to the endpoint. The two-visit-order search buys an O(h^{-2}) entropy cost for the block-length jump, which the endpoint needs. Lean isolates the search as an abstract reusable Arena (Compress/Search.lean:16-325).

id: I29 + I30: gap potential F(A) - log|B_A…
why: A monovariant that mixes free energy with packing entropy of a Bohr-type ball. Cheap deterministic updates lower it by k_b/2 and regular ones raise it by at most C t, so cheap updates are charged to regular ones, whose total is bounded by likelihood evidence. This closes the per-branch budget sum k_b + t <= Cd and the count n <= Ch. No near-equivalent was found.

id: I32: Prop modulated delayed Haar estima…
why: A dyadic model of the Carleson operator at the exact L log L endpoint: stopped at (log d)^4, L1 bound Cd, uniform in depth and frequencies, with delayed multipliers. It is the right intermediate target and carries all the difficulty; DAG-wise everything flows through it (Lean: GridBound).

id: I40: delayed vector norm estimate with …
why: The b-independent coefficient on the Fisher sum is what allows Fisher charges to be summed once globally while representative-choice costs carry the logarithmic factors in a separate tail.

name: Thermal noisy labels of the input point (Z = Y + theta, theta ~ K_A = e^{F(A)-A}, A a ferromagnetic cosine form, updated adaptively)
statement: Attach to the input point Y a label Z = Y + theta mod 1 whose error law has density K_A proportional to exp(-sum_s lambda_s(1 - cos 2 pi s y)). Spectra and transforms are read through the label: G^u = int |E[a chi_u(Y) K_A(z-Y)]|^2 / E[a K_A(z-Y)] dz measures how much the label reveals the phase chi_u(Y). Each successful spectral update adds a spatial form S_p and a metric form D_i to A, so the noise concentrates (in the error variable) on a smooth Bohr set of the discovered frequencies. Integr…
why: The closest analogue of an extension variable in this family: a new random variable, tiny to state, absent from goal and L, which is what lets frequency selection be paid for in information. Downgrade risks: (i) a judge may read it as a randomised form of Bohr-set localisation (Bourgain/Sanders), i.e. a cross-field transfer with a stochastic twist (N2); (ii) noise-channel smoothing is generic information theory. It pays off only together with C2 (information accounting), C3 (compression) and C5…

name: Two-law accounting and the global label Fisher sum (information charged under the true input law, paid back along uniform output paths)
statement: With dP = (rho/m_top) dU, the sum over live jumping pieces of U(p) alpha_e J_p, with J_p = int |D|^2/M, is at most Cd. Information about labels and memberships is counted under P, whose relative entropy to U is at most d because rho <= e^d, and converted into L1 bounds along uniformly sampled output paths.
why: The mechanism (entropy chain rule over a dyadic filtration, information counted under the density law) is standard. The budget d is the L log L hypothesis read as relative entropy, which is what calibrates the method to the endpoint and makes Test 2 fail. Its novelty is inherited from C1 and from the conversion to uniform-output bounds, which is bookkeeping (Sec. 9).

name: Entropy compression lemma (one centre and one phase region valid for every weight on a large retained subset)
statement: If for every law lambda on a finite S the 2T-fold symmetric noisy sum has E_lambda H_q(X_1+...+X_T - X'_1-...-X'_T) >= e^{-E}, then there are x_0 in S and S' in S with log|S|-log|S'| <= C d^2/(E h^2) such that for every probability v on S', int exp(-L sum_x v(x)(1 - cos 2 pi g(x-x_0) theta)) d omega >= e^{-CE}.
why: A member of the Chang/Lee/inverse-Littlewood-Offord family. The paper names Lee 2017 as the related method, which caps it at N2 under the PLAN rule. The distinctive features (conclusion uniform over all weights so that the spectral update can choose the weight afterwards; loss calibrated to the endpoint) are real, but they are a strengthening of a known statement type, not a new concept. Upgrade to N3 only if Test 4 (P-C3, arm B) shows that models given Chang + Lee do not produce the uniform-in…

name: Finite refinement search with two visit orders (block-length increase at O(h^{-2}) entropy cost)
statement: A finite sequence of context refinements reaching an index j with K_{m_{j,1}}(W; r_j) <= K_{m_{j,0}}(W; r_j) + E while losing at most C D_*^2/(E h^2) one-letter entropy. Updates are 'offers' from block observations; because the width p_j need not shrink under refinement, indices are visited in two orders with a stopping rule comparing the entry upper g-value with the current lower one.
why: A clever scheduling device inside a templated telescoping/increment argument. It buys the h^{-2} saving the endpoint needs, so it is load-bearing for L log L as opposed to L log L log log L. Once the obstruction is identified it is the natural fix, and the paper itself motivates it that way. Potential-driven increment search is a template, so N2. It would be F4 if upgraded.

name: Gap potential F(A) - log|B_A(r)| with a tracked radius
statement: With F(A) = -log int e^{-A} and B_A(r) = {u : Delta_A(u) <= r}, the gap F(A) - log|B_A(r)| starts at 0, stays >= -C (summability of q_A), rises by at most C t at a regular success and falls by at least k_b/2 at a cheap success, with r growing by eta at each main addition.
why: A neat monovariant, but read through the Bohr-set lens it is the uncertainty-principle slack of a smooth Bohr set, tracked as density-increment arguments track Bohr-set size and rank. Its novelty is derivative of C1. It would be F4 if upgraded.

name: Spectral update with the regular/cheap dichotomy (iterated compression, flat free-energy range, input-only success set)
statement: From a request (e^{k_b} separated high label-weighted frequencies), iterate compression with t shrinking by 4 per round to obtain either a regular test (success probability >= beta/2, E_T(nu) >= t/4) or a cheap deterministic update; choose the metric coefficient lambda on a flat interval of free energy among ~e^{h/4}/log h adjacent ranges.
why: Load-bearing and intricate, but assembled from standard templates (increment dichotomy, regular-radius pigeonhole, Chang/Lee transfer). Not graded N3 separately: its non-template content is C1 + C3 + C5.

name: Prop modulated delayed Haar estimate (finite dyadic model at the L log L endpoint)
statement: For rho <= e^d of mean <= 2 on a dyadic tree, with stopping when the average exceeds e^{4h}, the maximally (trigonometrically) modulated delayed Haar multiplier sum_j E_{p_j}[rho chi_u r_{j+1}] eps_j r_{j+2} has L1 norm of its max over u bounded by Cd, uniformly in depth and number of frequencies.
why: As a statement it is the natural dyadic target, close to known maximally modulated Haar models and to Lie's good-set template, and analytic relative to goal + L. Its proof (Secs 3-9) is where the novelty lives, and that is credited to C1-C6. Downgraded from the analyst's provisional N3.

name: Endpoint reduction: Thm good-set with doubly exponential height layers
statement: int over {M rho <= e^{4h}} of sup_N |S_N rho| <= C d for mass-one rho <= e^d; layers e^{2^j} <= |f| < e^{2^{j+1}}, Borel-Cantelli on the exceptional sets (summable (log d_j)^{-4}).
why: The paper-named reduction template with endpoint parameters. Borderline N1/N2; graded N1 because it is a parameterisation of the known strategy.

name: Finite splitting procedure, live/static plateaus and live budgets (inductive caps on form, count, charge, radius)
statement: A stopping-tree decomposition of the input by spectral tests and membership splits, with per-branch invariants (A, n, Q, r, gap) carried by induction; budgets: sum k_b + sum t <= Cd, n <= Ch, membership surprisal O(h) in L2, plateau weight O(h), transfer O(h^{-10}).
why: The induction carries extra tracked quantities (form, count, charge, radius, gap potential): the 'carry an extra tracked quantity' template, so capped at N2 by the templated-strengthening rule.

name: Capture on a plateau: signed-span frequency lists, edge charges, snapshots refreshed by relative entropy
statement: Cumulative signed-span lists via Riesz-product entropy increments; likelihood-window edge charges; snapshots of representatives refreshed when mass measures change enough; one miss block before activation.
why: Strong but templated (Riesz-product entropy increment plus likelihood charging).

name: Path estimates: scalar Bellman-type potential psi and delayed vector norm estimate with absolute Fisher coefficient
statement: Maximal inequalities along output paths; the label-valued delayed estimate charges Fisher information with a b-independent coefficient by adding the coordinate lambda M to the state.
why: Bellman-function technique. Augmenting the state with lambda M is the templated 'track an extra quantity' move, so capped at N2. The Lean uses a different potential, which shows that the specific psi is not essential.

name: Half-wave propagator U, Bessel potential J^alpha, local smoothing norm
statement: Uf(x,t)=(2pi)^-3 int e^{i(x.xi+t|xi|)} fhat; J^alpha=(1-Delta)^{alpha/2}; estimate ||Uf||_{L^3(R^3x[1,2])} <= C_eps ||J^eps f||_3.
why: Standard (Sogge 1991; Peral/Miyachi).

name: Theorem 1.1 Critical local smoothing (L^3, every eps>0)
statement: For every eps>0, ||Uf||_{L^3(R^3x[1,2])} <= C_eps ||J^eps f||_{L^3(R^3)}.
why: The statement is the conjecture itself; its novelty is as a theorem, not as an item.

name: Fixed polynomial setup; negligible error; upper exponent Gamma (eq fw-upper-exponent)
statement: Structural constants, polynomial bounds and bounded number of operations fixed before s->0; Gamma = sup over setups and admissible sequences of limsup log B_s / log(1/s).
why: Critical/worst-case exponent formulation is standard in induction-on-scales (e.g. Guth's survey exponent beta for Wang-Zahl Kakeya, GWZ induction on scales); here formalised with explicit limit ordering. Close neighbours exist.

name: Uniform bound within a fixed setup
statement: Gamma real => B_s <= s^{-Gamma-eps} uniformly on families admissible in one setup.
why: Definitional.

name: Disjoint row restrictions and copies (energy accounting)
statement: Bessel-type inequality for V^*P_jV; copies only give N||g||^2.
why: Standard Hilbert space.

name: Extraction from finitely many classes (q-subadditive functional; l^3 sum of Hilbert norms)
statement: F(sum g_j)^{1/q}<=sum F(g_j)^{1/q} => some class has F(g_j)>=N^-q F(sum); applies to sum w^{-1/2}||A g||^3.
why: Standard dyadic pigeonholing.

name: Extrema of bounded exponent data (lexicographic minimisation in closure)
statement: Successive extrema on compact (or boundedly-minimised closed) slices are attained.
why: Compactness.

name: Strict improvement in a closure
statement: No data with z_n->z_0 and limsup c_n < c_0 = min on slice.
why: Closedness.

name: Pullback of a strict exponent contradiction
statement: Constructions with exponent Gamma+tau-r_m, r_m->0, in setups S_m are impossible.
why: Definitional.

name: Capacity tails / uniform integrability of normalised scores i_s
statement: P{P(X|Y)<e^-u/N}<=e^-u; normalised scores uniformly integrable.
why: Standard (AEP-type tail bound).

name: Stability under restriction (likelihood ratio bounds)
statement: Conditioning on E with P(E)>=s^alpha changes scores by <= alpha+tau outside 2s^tau.
why: Standard.

name: Negligible information and positive restrictions
statement: Pointwise information density tails; I_Q <= (I_P+log2)/q_0.
why: Standard.

name: Classical and hybrid cylinder states (base flow (X,B,Y)->(B+TX,Y+TX^2); hybrid normal fiber evolves by Schrodinger e^{-itHp^2/2sigma}; Gaussian analysis V_l)
statement: Classical cylinder: exact index (N,D) moving D_T=D+TN. Hybrid: normal fiber in L^2(R_D;H) with coherent-state analysis at widths d_l=(H/l)^{1/2}, q_l=(Hl)^{1/2}.
why: Cones locally look like parabolic cylinders (Bourgain-Demeter cone decoupling via cylinder; GWZ intermediate scales); Gaussian coherent-state wave packets are classical. The mixed classical-base/quantum-normal model is a new packaging.

name: Cylinder tests with polynomial normal shear and weight w=r^{3+eta} f^{1-eta}; kappa-regularity
statement: Heisenberg base box (|X-x|<=r,|B_T-b|<=lr,|Y_T-y-2x(B_T-b)|<=lr^2) and normal velocity/position windows after subtracting the shear alpha X+beta(T)X^2+K(Y_T-2XB_T); mu(Q)<=kappa w(Q).
why: Frostman / Katz-Tao convex-set nonconcentration and Wolff-type packet regularity are close neighbours; the specific sheared tests and eta-weight are new variants.

name: Assignments and normalised cubic functional B_s = s^{-1/2}/(e sqrt kappa) sum m^{3/2} w^{-1/2}
statement: Fractional assignments of final row mass to tests; cubic readout normalised by energy and regularity.
why: Reformulation of L^3 norm as l^{3/2} sum of packet masses (standard Wolff/GWZ style).

name: Polynomial cylinder setup
statement: Polynomial bounds on e/kappa, H, supports, densities.
why: Instance of P03.

name: Symmetries and Gaussian localization; repeated-cut regularity
statement: Invariance under translations, boosts, dilations, common shear; hybrid frame transfer negligible outside |N'-N|<=s^-eps d, |D'-D-tN|<=s^-eps q.
why: Standard Gaussian wave packet / Schur test.

name: Polynomial test reduction and sublevel estimate vol{|Q|<=rho||Q||}<=C rho^{2^-d}
statement: Only polynomially bounded tests matter; quadratic-polynomial sublevel bound.
why: Standard (Carbery-Christ-Wright type).

name: Theorem 2.4 Cylinder exponent bound Gamma_cl, Gamma_hyb <= eta/2
statement: Both cylinder exponents are at most eta/2.
why: New intermediate estimate; its novelty is carried by the items it uses.

name: One-time bound mu(Q)<=s^-o(1) kappa w(Q) l^{1+eta/2}; Gamma finite
statement: Single descendant test mass bound; gives B_s<=s^{-1+eta/4}.
why: Routine.

name: Extremal exponent data (p,d): m/(kappa w)=s^{p}, sum m = e s^{-d}, Gamma=d+(1-p)/2; minimal p in closure
statement: Dyadic binning gives homogeneous extremizers; choose smallest p; weight count sum w <= (e/kappa)s^{-(p+d)}.
why: Homogeneous pigeonholing of masses and 'worst-case' extremal choice are standard (Wang-Zahl, Guth); minimal-p selection inside the extremal slice is a variant.

name: Regularity peeling (coherent decomposition into subpower levels)
statement: Dyadic thresholds b; each level O(b)-regular, heavy tests of mass ~bw, total weight <= z/b.
why: Greedy dyadic peeling is standard (e.g. Wolff, Bourgain).

name: Saturation of a preserving split: b=kappa s^{pa}, z=e s^{-da}
statement: Any exponent-preserving split at depth a has regularity and energy exponents forced to the linear benchmarks.
why: Analogous to 'sticky/self-similar at all scales' consequences of extremality (Wang-Zahl stickiness; branching-function linearity in Orponen-Shmerkin). Variant.

name: Benchmarks l_i=s^i, E_i=e s^{-di}, kappa_i=kappa s^{pi}
why: Abbreviation.

name: Documented gate (row projection + synthesis with retained rows partitioned among tests)
why: Bookkeeping.

name: Matched-chain construction (common widths, read mass, width ratio and shear compatibility (M))
statement: On any finite mesh, masks can be inserted so documented tests have common widths, mass >= s^o(1)E_i, and successive shears satisfy (M).
why: New technical construction; analogous to compatible multiscale structure in sticky Kakeya. Variant.

name: Two-shear intersection (I) and partner count
statement: mu(Q- cap Q~-) <= s^-o(1) delta^-C kappa w /M where M = size of shear difference.
why: Sublevel/transversality counting; variant of standard incidence counting.

name: Group extraction
statement: Partition rows into groups with bounded reachability; extract near-extremal groups realising Gamma,p with relative weight count.
why: Pigeonholing variant.

name: Bottom Planck floor (Pl): H/(s f_1^2)=s^o(1) if Gamma_hyb>Gamma_cl
statement: Strictly nonclassical hybrid extremizers sit at the uncertainty scale at every depth.
why: Uncertainty-scale saturation is natural; classical comparison via phase lattice is a variant.

name: Shear costs R_2=(r^2/f)(|beta|+s|K|), R_1=(r/f)|alpha+2beta x-2Kb|; lexicographic minimal costs c=c_2, then c_1
statement: Exponents of growth of the curvature and linear shear of terminal tests, minimised in closure among extremizers.
why: New device (borderline N3): a second-level extremal choice of a geometric 'cost' among extremizers. Neighbours: minimal-delay / canonical profile in 074 (same release); Wang-Zahl multi-parameter extremal choices.

name: Finite costs and compact (Lipschitz) width profiles u(i), n(i), b_t(i)=n-tu; inequalities (A),(B)
statement: Arzela-Ascoli limits of width exponents; telescoped shear comparisons.
why: Branching-function / Lipschitz profile technique (Orponen-Shmerkin, Shmerkin) is a close neighbour.

name: Shape constraints: b_2(i)>=c(i-1), equality when c!=1; linear analogue
statement: Minimality of the cost forces the normal-minus-twice-angular width exponent to be the line c(i-1).
why: Same family as P30; minimal-cost-forces-linear-profile mirrors 'canonical temporal profile' of 074.

name: Affine extremal configurations (F): u=J(1-i), b_2=q(i-1) or b_1=c_1(i-1)
statement: Blow-up at a common differentiability point gives affine profiles while preserving extremality and minimal costs.
why: Rademacher + rescaling to tangent profile; standard in branching-function arguments (eps-linear intervals).

name: Rarity transport (Sp): P^j(U)<=s^-o(1) P^i(S)^{2/3}
statement: Power-rare predecessor events stay power-rare at later laws (via tail exponent + Holder).
why: Energy-to-probability transfer specific to this model; variant of 'measure of a rare set of tubes' arguments.

name: Measurable completion events and causal restrictions (Borel/analytic versions)
statement: Analytic projections of Borel path relations are universally measurable; inner/outer Borel versions.
why: Standard descriptive set theory (Lusin/Souslin).

name: Forward flattening of scores
statement: Restrict to subpower classes so prescribed log-probability scores have deterministic limits.
why: AEP-style flattening; standard in multiscale entropy (Hochman).

name: Transfer of conditional profiles
statement: Bidirectional subpower lists transfer conditional scores between laws.
why: Routine.

name: Time prediction (time choice score >= d(j-i))
why: Variant.

name: Recoverable phase names: score >= log(E_i/(kappa_i w)), equality under prediction
why: Variant.

name: Wave-envelope estimate (GWZ Thm 1.3) with Hilbert-valued and weighted extensions
statement: ||F||_4^4 <~ L^eps sum_R sum_tau sum_U |U|^-1 (int_U sum ||F_theta||^2)^2; Hilbert-valued via Gaussian randomisation.
why: Cited theorem; Hilbert extension by standard Gaussian randomisation.

name: Kinetic estimate for parabolic rays (kin)
statement: delta^-1 sum_{t,D} mu{Q_z(t) in D}^2 <~ delta^-eps kappa E under R^3-regularity of ray measure.
why: Direct corollary of GWZ via wave packets (known route: square function/wave envelope -> Kakeya-type collision estimates).

name: Scalar-channel estimate (SC)
statement: sum m^2/f^{1-eta} <= tau^-eta s^-o(1) b_0 e for 1-D normal channel, classical and Schrodinger.
why: 1-D collision counting / L^4 Strichartz-type bound; routine.

name: Memory bound for documented labels (mem) and prediction version
statement: P{X in label's list of delta^-R cells of width delta^L} <= delta^{(1-d+2Gamma+eta(L-1)-R)/2}.
why: New combination; variant.

name: Memory when both costs vanish
why: Special case of P43.

name: Exclusion of a strictly nonclassical zero-cost hybrid case
statement: Hybrid minimisers with Gamma_hyb>Gamma_cl cannot have c_2=c_1=0 (uses GWZ kinetic/crossing estimates).
why: Variant; GWZ used as black box.

name: Discretized planar Furstenberg estimate (RW), probabilistic form
statement: |union P_l|_Delta >= Delta^{-F(a,b)+omega}, F=a+min{1,b,(a+b)/2}, for Frostman probability measures.
why: Ren-Wang Thm 4.1; F(a,b) matches min(s+t,(3s+t)/2,s+1).

name: Likelihood and list comparisons (LP)
why: Standard.

name: Conditional planar incidence bootstrap (cond)->(inc)
statement: Conditional entropy-score version of Furstenberg: i(Q_1|D) >= a+min{1,a+g}.
why: Entropy/score version of a cited incidence theorem; known route (Hochman-style entropy versions of projection theorems).

name: Nested boosted names C(a) and lemma 'Geometric and probabilistic bounds for the boosted names'
statement: C(a)=(x_c,n_c,T_1^(a),position^(a)); profile D(a) Lipschitz with D(1)<=p+d; angular score >=(3-p)v; time score >=dzh.
why: Prototype of canonical names.

name: Exclusion of classical zero costs
statement: Classical extremizer with Gamma>eta/2 cannot have both costs zero; proves D'(a)>=1+3d contradicting D(1)<=p+d=1+3d-2Gamma (uses Ramsey).
why: One-variable version of the entropy-growth contradiction; shares architecture with 074.

name: Curvature displays (quadratic equality / pure linear / strict) and templates l(a,v), w(a,v)
statement: Which rounded shear coefficients R_a,k_a,bar k are recorded and at what precision.
why: Part of P52.

name: Canonical name C(a,v): finite record of time bin, rounded shear frame, derivative cell L, base cells [X]_v,[B]_{a+v},[Y-2[X]B]_{a+2v}, residual normal phase
statement: Finite phase-space record at time depth a and horizontal resolution v, retaining the changing shear frame.
why: Paper names Hochman-Shmerkin local entropy averages as precedent; same-release 074 uses coordinate entropy in two frames. Novel content: the recorded moving shear frame. Candidate F1 if upgraded.

name: Refinement and comparison of canonical names
statement: Finer names determine coarser to bounded lists; Lipschitz dependence.
why: Routine.
