name: Canonical entropy excess E(a,v)=H(a,v)-D_0-(p+d)a-W(a,v) >= 0 with endpoint equality / label prediction
statement: Nonnegative entropy excess on the (a,v) domain, vanishing at boundary points v=u(a) / (1,0) / (D,u(D)).
why: No near-equivalent found in quick search: an entropy-excess function on a 2-parameter (depth, resolution) domain with zero boundary trace and nonnegativity, driven to contradiction by transport inequalities. Neighbours (Shmerkin/Orponen branching functions; Hochman entropy porosity; 074 canonical profile) are 1-parameter or same-release.

name: Angular trace m(a,v) and time stationarity (ang),(ng)
statement: Almost-everywhere linear angular score and stationarity.
why: Lebesgue differentiation of Lipschitz profiles.

name: Mixed coefficient trace nu
why: Routine differentiation.

name: Memory consequences (mr): m >= (k_0+2Gamma+eta(L_raw-1))/L_raw
statement: Angular rate lower bound from P43.
why: Variant.

name: Admissible side variables Z (coarse/exact, quadratic/linear) and common phase
statement: Conditioning variables for conditionally independent replicas; measurable common phase F(Z).
why: Conditionally independent copies are standard (entropic sumset, Tao); choice of side is new.

name: Conditional angular dimension (time mark surprise d) and Angular separation (line avoidance)
statement: Conditional marks xi=(theta,r) have time-surprise d and avoid affine lines by a power.
why: Variant.

name: Replica information budgets (vb),(fib) and stationary conditional walks (leg)
statement: Negligible information between replicas' marks and common phase; resampling legs with explicit increments.
why: Conditional resampling (Markov chain/walk on fibres) is a known entropy technique; specific legs new.

name: Score calculus: pathwise score limits, monotone diagonal trace, prefixes with future conditioning, changes of law
statement: Distributional limits of scores with chain rule and Lipschitz increments.
why: Routine.

name: Conditional projection rule
statement: Entropy form of a discretised projection theorem under negligible information budget.
why: Entropy version of Bourgain/Shmerkin-Wang projection theorems: known route.

name: Finite radial exclusion; Radial dichotomy; parent-centred directions; low-exponent pin estimate; pin-product alternatives
statement: Dichotomy e_* in {0} or >= d for radial line concentration; product slope f=(theta_j-theta_i)(r_j-r_i) score >= dp.
why: Radial projection bootstrap of Shmerkin-Wang (SW2025 Sec 5.4) and Orponen-Shmerkin-Wang is the named neighbour in the sibling paper 074.

name: Admissible interior tangent data; radial spreading; crossing
statement: Tangent experiment with common root C_*, side Z, phase F, replicas with marks; hypotheses 'radial spreading' and 'crossing'.
why: Variant.

name: Differential cost (time-rate) and width-rate
statement: d_a H >= d + min(1,c)(w+x) + |1-c|(pi or G); d_v H bounds.
why: Variant.

name: Angular/commutator modes; projection amplification x>=min(1,d+M)
why: Projection-theorem consequence.

name: Basic phase rates, many-leg vertical rate, mark-motion comparison, orientation rates, two time innovations, horizontal width, binary time estimate
statement: Rate inequalities (modes),(Gq),(H-walk),(trans),(cross-q),(mix-q),(double),(e-q),(bin).
why: Variants; many case-specific computations.

name: Admissible local actions (surplus): (d_a - k d_v)E >= 2Gamma
statement: For freezing k=0 or motion speeds k, the entropy excess decreases backwards at rate >= 2Gamma.
why: Together with P54 forms the potential/monovariant; individually an algebraic consequence of P65-P67.

name: Fixed-width line estimate
why: Variant.

name: Stationary equality boundary (radial spreading at q=c_2=1,J=0)
Strict affine boundary: d_a H(a,v_0) >= 2+3d
Finite off-gap motion and off-gap path contradiction
statement: Path in (t,v) domain on which E decreases at rate >=Gamma while staying in the domain of valid inequalities contradicts E>=0, E=0 on boundary.
why: Characteristic-path / comparison argument for first-order differential inequalities is classical; part of the P54 package.

name: Proof of Theorem 2.4 (case analysis over c, J, q, d)
statement: Covers equality curvature, pure linear, strict curvature cases.
why: Assembly.

name: Round experiment (classical rays (B+tA,Y+t|A|^2) and wave with Schrodinger-type evolution in null coordinates; plateau analysis)
why: Null-coordinate (paraboloid/Schrodinger) form of the cone wave is standard (Lorentz/light-cone coordinates).

name: Round regularity: round tests and null-hyperquadric tests F=c+du+alpha.x+beta z+k(uz-|x|^2), discriminant 1, weight r^4 f^{1-eta}
why: Frostman/Wolff-type regularity with conformally invariant hyperquadric tests; hyperquadric family is a new choice (light cones / null planes are its degenerations).

name: Packet locality, enlarged tests, single-time estimate, composition of free gaps, saturation at inserted cuts (CE)
statement: Round analogues of P17, P20, P23.
why: Analogues of cylinder lemmas.

name: Thin endings reduce to cylinders (conformal flattening of null hyperquadric; overlap; conformal wave transport; capacity allocation; weight comparison; classic…
statement: Saturated round experiments with thin terminal shape have Gamma <= cylinder exponents.
why: Change of representation via conformal chart (F5-type). Neighbours: Lorentz rescaling (Ou-Wang, GLMX), cone-to-cylinder at small angular scale (Bourgain-Demeter). Variant.

name: Theorem 8.1 Round-cone bound Gamma_cl,round, Gamma_wav,round <= 100 eta
why: Assembly.

name: Angular uncertainty at saturated wave cut (round-Pl); spatial readout; plane-slab estimates
statement: r_j/d_{l_j}=s^o(1), u(a)=(1-a)/2; plane-slab caps.

name: Round phase name C(a,v) (grid) and profiles D(a,v), J(a,v,w); wave excess E(a,v)=D-4v-(p+d)a >= 0, E(a,u(a))=0
statement: Round analogue of P52/P54.
why: Same as P54.

name: Outgoing entropy (round-out): o_T >= 4d + min(1-d, m/2) via four transverse pins, Gram-Schmidt, projective directions and finite Ramsey colouring
why: Pinning/projection bootstrap of Shmerkin-Wang/OSW type; Ramsey colouring of triples to fix projection directions is a new gadget (borderline N3, F3).

name: Two-direction descent lemma
statement: Locally Lipschitz E>=0 with zero trace on v=t/2 cannot satisfy E_t+E_v/2<=-c where m<=q and E_t<=-c where m>=q (m monotone in t).
why: Elementary comparison/characteristics argument.

name: Annular estimate ||W_H g||_{L^3} <= C_delta H^-delta ||g||_3; null coordinates; uniform packet localisation; volume of physical predecessors; input regularity …
statement: Physical L^3 estimate per frequency annulus from Theorem 8.1 via L^infty-amplitude pieces and synthesis int|v|^3 <~ H^{-1/2} sum m^{3/2}.
why: Standard amplitude/level-set decomposition and wave-packet synthesis.

name: Proof of Theorem 1.1 (Littlewood-Paley summation)
why: Standard.

name: Corollary 9.6 full range 2<p<infty, alpha>max{0,1-3/p}
statement: Interpolation of L^3 with L^2 and L^infty kernel bound.
why: Standard interpolation.

name: Maximal half-wave and a.e. convergence (p>=3, s>1-2/p)
why: Established implication.

name: Maximal Bochner-Riesz bounds and a.e. summation (3<=p<infty, delta>1-3/p); strict nonmaximal BR range; sphere extension r>3; Kakeya maximal L^3
why: Established implication chain LS => BR => restriction => Kakeya.

id: P54 + P68 + P72 (round: P86 + P88): ent…
why: Turns the whole positive-cost case into a first-order differential-inequality problem for one scalar function: E>=0, E=0 on a boundary curve, and (d_a - k d_v)E >= 2Gamma along admissible directions; a characteristic path then forces E<0. Non-analytic: neither the canonical name nor its excess occurs in the goal or in L; the goal is an L^3 inequality. Load-bearing: every positive-cost configuration in Thm 2.4 and the whole round wave case of Thm 8.1 close through it (06:1083-1276; 08:1433-1471)…
Minimising the shear cost among extremizers is a non-obvious second-order extremal choice that pins the geometry (b_2(i)=c(i-1)). Load-bearing for everything after Sec 2.
Changes representation of thin round packets into a parabolic-cylinder model where GWZ (2+1) applies; keeps a 1-D Schrodinger evolution when the normal coordinate stays quantum.
Single inequality that closes the round case; Ramsey colouring to coherently choose projection planes is an unusual gadget.
Avoids any positive phase-space density for masked quantum evolutions; makes 'power-rare predecessor' a transferable notion.

name: Entropy-excess potential with zero boundary trace and transport inequalities
statement: E(a,v)=H(a,v)-D_0-(p+d)a-W(a,v) >= 0 on a 2-parameter (time-depth, resolution) domain, with E=0 at label-recoverable boundary points; admissible local actions give (d_a - k d_v)E >= 2Gamma; following a characteristic path backward from the boundary forces E<0. Round analogue: E=D-4v-(p+d)a, E_t+E_v/2<=-2Gamma or E_t<=-2Gamma, contradicted by the descent lemma.
why: Passes tests 1-3 as far as checked: no human 2-parameter analogue found, non-analytic, load-bearing. Downgrade pressure: (i) the 1-parameter core is standard branching-function/entropy-growth technique; (ii) the same mechanism appears in three sibling model papers of the same release, so this is a cluster-level device (one day after 074); (iii) the transport/descent step itself is elementary. Correctness of the whole package is unverified. Would fall to N2 if an expert identifies the 2-paramete…

name: Lexicographic extremal reduction: minimal mass exponent p, then minimal shear costs c, c1, forcing linear benchmarks and affine width profiles
statement: Among extremizers of the cylinder functional choose minimal p; any exponent-preserving split has kappa_a=kappa s^{pa}, E_a=e s^{-da}; then minimise curvature cost c (and c1); minimality forces b_2(i)=c(i-1); blow up at a differentiability point to affine profiles.
why: Worst-case-exponent paradigm (Wang-Zahl) plus eps-linear profile technique (Orponen-Shmerkin) are close neighbours; the shear-cost lexicographic layer is a variant, not a new concept.

name: Canonical name C(a,v): finite phase-space record with recorded moving shear frame
statement: Records time bin t_a, rounded shear coefficients (R_a,k_a,bar k), derivative cell L, base cells [X]_v,[B]_{a+v},[Y-2[X]B]_{a+2v}, residual normal velocity/position after subtracting the recorded shear.
why: PLAN rule: a precedent the paper names itself caps at N2 (Hochman-Shmerkin). Would be F1 if upgraded.

name: Hybrid classical/quantum cylinder model and thin-shape reduction by conformal flattening of null hyperquadrics
statement: Thin round packets near a null hyperquadric are mapped by a rational conformal chart (Bateman/Kelvin covariance of Box) to a parabolic-cylinder model; if the normal coordinate is below the uncertainty scale it keeps a 1-D Schrodinger evolution (hybrid model), else classical.
why: Variant of Lorentz/conformal rescaling plus cone-to-cylinder reduction (F5-type, but capped at N2).

name: Outgoing entropy bound via four transverse pins, Gram-Schmidt reveal order, projective directions and finite Ramsey colouring
statement: o_T >= 4d + min(1-d, m/2): four transverse pins give 4d; projecting onto 2-planes pi_ij with directions g_ij coloured by Ramsey on triples sharpens two time contributions when m>0.
why: Pinning bootstraps are known (SW/OSW); Ramsey colouring is a minor gadget.

name: Rarity transport (Sp): energy-to-probability bridge for masked (quantum) evolutions
statement: If all predecessors of a later row event U lie in S, then P^j(U) <= s^-o(1) P^i(S)^{2/3}.
why: Variant; short derivation from the extremal setup.

name: d_p(n,D): least universal coordinate dimension
statement: d_p(n,D) = least d such that every n-point subset of any L_p space has images in l_p^d and a scale s>0 with s||xi-xj|| <= ||yi-yj|| <= D s ||xi-xj||. Maps unrestricted (nonlinear).

name: Exact discretization (Ball): n points of L_p embed isometrically in l_p^{n choose 2}
statement: Every n-point subset of real L_p, 1<=p<inf, embeds isometrically into l_p^{binom n 2}. Proof: normalized pairwise p-th power vectors q(t)/s(t) lie in a compact set K on the simplex hyperplane; barycenter in conv(K); Caratheodory gives <=N atoms; y_i = ((S theta_a)^{1/p} z_i^(a))_a.

name: normalized gradients V
statement: V = {((z_i - z_j)/delta_e)_{e=ij} : z in R^n} subset R^E, delta_e = ||x_i-x_j||_p. Any family of normalized gradients gives scalar labels, i.e. coordinates of one map.

name: Weighted moment criterion (minimax reduction + Maurey sampling)
statement: If for every strictly positive probability lambda on pairs there is a random F in V with ||F||_inf<=K a.s. and sum_e lambda_e |E|F_e|^p - b| <= eta b (b,K uniform in lambda), then the points embed into l_p^d with distortion ((1+3eta)/(1-3eta))^{1/p}, d <= C max{1, K^{2p}/(eta^2 b^2)} log(2n).

name: Electrical-flow localization || |Q| ||_{2->2} <= 2 log n (GGNS)
statement: For a connected graph with positive conductances, the Euclidean projection Q onto im(C^{1/2}B) (transfer-current matrix) satisfies || |Q| ||_{2->2} <= 2 log n. Proof: heat-kernel integral representation of Q, entropy dissipation int I(h_s) ds = log(1/mu_v), log-mean Cauchy-Schwarz.

name: Weighted projection with controlled row sums (fixed-point reweighting)
statement: For every strictly positive probability lambda on E there is sigma >= lambda/2 such that the l2(sigma)-orthogonal projection P onto V has max_e sum_f |P_ef| <= H = 4 log(2n). Proof: sum_e sigma_e R_e(sigma)^2 <= (2 log n)^2 from I05; Brouwer fixed point of Phi_e(sigma) = u_e + (1-sum u) lambda_e with u_e = sigma_e R_e^2 / (2(2 log n)^2).

name: Retraction minimax substitute for the Brouwer reweighting
statement: There is P in the convex set {P : P A = A, P = A B} with all row sums <= 4 log|V| and, simultaneously, finitely many weighted Hilbert-valued energy bounds sum_e lam_e ||(P x_j)_e||^2 <= 4. Proof: each test w gives the weighted projection at sigma=(lam+w)/2; convex separation (weighted_error_to_uniform) upgrades averaged to uniform bounds.

name: Homogeneous increments: power-law intensity nu on (0,inf) x {1..m}, v_e(r,t) = r g_e(t)
statement: d nu(r,t) = p r^{-p-1} dr on each copy t; g_e(t) = (x_i(t)-x_j(t))/delta_e; then nu(|v_e|>a) = a^{-p} for every edge e (identical magnitude law for all pairs, since sum_t |g_e(t)|^p = 1).

name: signed Poisson sampling
statement: W = sum_{j<=N} eps_j h(omega_j), N ~ Poisson(M), omega_j ~ nu/M on a finite-mass region, eps_j uniform signs; independent on disjoint regions.

name: Signed Poisson formulas (cf, mgf, variance)
statement: E e^{itS} = exp(int (cos(th)-1) d nu); E e^{tS} = exp(int (cosh(th)-1) d nu); E S = 0, E S^2 = int h^2 d nu.

name: Common heavy-tailed marginal Y (p<2): Poisson sum of v against nu, all Y_e identically p-stable-like
statement: Y in V a.s.; E e^{i theta Y_e} = exp(p int (cos(theta u)-1) u^{-p-1} du), independent of e; tail c_p a^{-p} <= P(|Y_e|>a) <= C_p a^{-p} (a>=1).

name: Clip-and-project for p<2: F = P[Y]_T with critical capped moment b = E min(|Y_e|, T/H)^p ~ log(T/H)
statement: E|Y_e - F_e| <= C_p H T^{1-p}; sum sigma_e E|F_e|^2 <= C_p T^{2-p}; with a = T/H the Lipschitz part and quadratic tail each cost C_p H^{2-p} (additive), while b >= c_p log a. Choose T = exp(A H^{2-p}): relative error <= eta, K = HT, log K = O((log n)^{2-p}).

name: Ramp of overlapping dyadic truncations u = sum_{k<l} (v_{<=2^{k+l}} - v_{<=2^k}) (p>2)
statement: u_e = m_l(|v_e|) v_e where the multiplicity on dyadic bins is 1,2,...,l,...,2,1. Its p-energy b = p log2 (l^p + 2 sum_{j<l} j^p) ~ l^{p+1}, identical for all edges; L2 norm O_p(1); sup <= 2^{2l}.

name: Ramp projection error ||Z-u||_{L_p(rho)}^p <= C_p H^{p-2}(l+1)
statement: A_k = (P-I)v_{<=2^k} = -(P-I)v_{>2^k} in L2; Z-u = sum_{k=l}^{2l-1} A_k - sum_{k<l} A_k; split at 2^k ~ tau/16H, sup bound for small k, L2 bound + Chebyshev for large k; integrate tail. Then relative error ||Z-u||_p / b^{1/p} <= C_p H^gamma / l; choose l = ceil(L H^gamma).

name: Nearly additive Poisson moments: int|h|^q <= E|S|^q <= (1+eps) int|h|^q + C (int h^2)^{q/2}
statement: Rosenthal-type inequality with leading coefficient 1+eps (needed for distortion close to 1); proved for symmetric independent sums via scalar inequality (|a+b|^q+|a-b|^q)/2 <= |a|^q + (1+eps')|b|^q + C|a|^{q-2}b^2, then Poissonized by binomial approximation.

name: Bounded random gradient for p>2: W = signed Poisson sum of Z = Pu, F = W 1{max_e|W_e|<=K}, K = 8J log(2n), J = C H 2^{2l}
statement: Exponential moment bound P(|W_e|>Jz) <= 2e^{C0-z}; discarding the whole vector on the bad event keeps F in V; truncation error C_p J^p n^{-3} = o(1); log K = O((log n)^{1-2/p}).

name: Weighted-moment contract table (b, K per range)
statement: p<2: b = E min{|Y_e|,T/H}^p, K = HT; p>2: b = p log2(l^p + 2 sum j^p), K = 8J log(2n); all independent of the points and pair weights.

name: Packing lower bound d_p(n,D) >= log n / log(1+2D)
statement: Equilateral set e_1..e_n in l_p^n; distortion-D image is 1-separated in a D-ball; volume comparison n <= (1+2D)^d.

name: p-parallelogram defect sign / disjointness criterion
statement: Delta_p(a,b) = |a+b|^p + |a-b|^p - 2|a|^p - 2|b|^p is zero iff ab=0, else has sign of p-2; hence ||u+v||^p+||u-v||^p = 2||u||^p+2||v||^p iff disjoint supports (p != 2).

name: Antipodal row-and-column grid configuration X_k forces d >= k^2 for exact embeddings
statement: X_k = {0} U {+-r_i} U {+-c_j} in l_p^{k^2}; an isometry fixes antipodes (strict convexity), rows have pairwise disjoint image supports, columns too, every row meets every column (defect 2^p-4 != 0), so d >= k^2; n>=9, k = floor((n-1)/4).

name: Hoeffding-type bounded-sum estimate (re-proved, weaker constants)
dyadicRamp / bandPart / tailPart / cutPart, paretoVectorLaw, projectedRampLaw, convolutionPower, globalCut, clip
statement: Lean encodings of I13, I08, I16; the Poisson sum of the paper is replaced by an m-fold convolution power of a probability law (pick a coordinate uniformly, Pareto(p) radius on (1,inf), apply ramp, project by P, symmetrize).

name: Log-limit corollaries
statement: 0<gamma(p)<1 implies log d_p(n,D)/log n -> 0 for D>1 and -> 2 for D=1.

name: doubling metric space
statement: A metric space is doubling if every ball is covered by a fixed number of balls of half the radius.

name: Ramp of overlapping dyadic truncations for p>2 (with its error estimate I14)
statement: u = sum_{k<l} (v_{<=2^{k+l}} - v_{<=2^k}), i.e. u_e = m_l(|v_e|) v_e with multiplicities 1,2,...,l,...,2,1 on the dyadic magnitude bins. Energy b = p log2 (l^p + 2 sum_{j<l} j^p) ~ l^{p+1}, the same at every edge; projection error ||Pu - u||_p^p <= C_p H^{p-2}(l+1). With l = ceil(L H^{1-2/p}) the relative error is <= C H^gamma / l and log K = O((log n)^{1-2/p}). A single window (or a constant-height rectangle) has energy/error ~ w/H^{p-2}, which only gives log K ~ (log n)^{p-2}, subpolynomial o…
why: Non-analytic (test 2) and load-bearing (test 3, ~48% of the core) but test 1 fails at mechanism level. The ramp is ell times the de la Vallee Poussin-minus-Fejer window, transplanted from partial sums to magnitude truncations, and its gain is the standard spread-a-cutoff-over-scales effect (capacity log-cutoff; discrete Poincare extremal). Under the strict rule (a known device imported from another field is transfer) and given an estimated pivot distance of 1, it is a skilful adaptation, not a …

name: Clip-and-project with critical-moment amplification (p<2)
statement: Y in V with a common p-stable-like marginal; F = P[Y]_T. The additive error is O(H^{2-p}) at cap a = T/H, while the common capped moment b = E min(|Y|,a)^p >= c_p log a diverges logarithmically; T = exp(A H^{2-p}) gives relative error <= eta and log K = O((log n)^{2-p}).
why: Built from the standard p<2 toolkit (stable + truncation + Maurey), which 094 itself attributes to Indyk/Schechtman. The critical-exponent log-divergence is classical. The new coupling with the projection is a variant, not a new concept. Pivot distance about 1.

name: Reweighted projection onto normalized gradients with all l_inf row sums <= H = O(log n) (Brouwer reweighting in the paper; minimax over retractions in Lean)
statement: For every strictly positive probability lambda on pairs there is sigma >= lambda/2 such that the l2(sigma)-orthogonal projection P onto V has max_e sum_f |P_ef| <= 4 log(2n). Average bound sum sigma_e R_e^2 <= (2 log n)^2 from GGNS, upgraded to a max bound by a Brouwer fixed point of Phi_e(sigma) = u_e + (1 - sum u) lambda_e. The Lean replaces Brouwer by convex separation over the convex set of retractions {P: PA=A, P=AB}.
why: The average-to-uniform reweighting is Lewis/Talagrand-style change of density (in the home field and in L) and also Raecke/Goranci-style reweighted electrical routing. The Lean's minimax-over-retractions is an elementary variant. The import of electrical-flow localization into metric dimension reduction is a NEW BRIDGE (see bridge_novelty), measured separately and not a jump.

name: Weighted moment criterion (minimax reduction + Maurey sampling, b and K uniform in lambda)
statement: If for every strictly positive lambda there is a random F in V with ||F||_inf <= K and sum_e lambda_e |E|F_e|^p - b| <= eta b (b, K uniform), then the points embed in l_p^d with distortion ((1+3eta)/(1-3eta))^{1/p} and d <= C max{1, K^{2p}/(eta b)^2} log(2n).
why: A conjunction of standard tools with a named antecedent (Eskenazis); the relative-error/minimax packaging is a routine strengthening.

name: Antipodal row-and-column grid obstruction for exact embeddings, all p != 2
statement: X_k = {0} U {+-r_i} U {+-c_j} in l_p^{k^2}: any isometric image has disjointly supported rows and columns (Lamperti), each row meets each column, so d >= k^2; k = floor((n-1)/4).
why: Extension of Ball's quadratic sharpness to p>2 via Lamperti's classical criterion; elementary incidence counting; not load-bearing for the main bound.

name: Nearly additive Poisson moments with leading constant 1+eps
statement: int|h|^q <= E|S|^q <= (1+eps) int|h|^q + C_{q,eps} (int h^2)^{q/2} for signed Poisson sums, q>2.
why: A mild sharpening of Rosenthal-type bounds, needed only to reach distortion near 1.

name: Electrical-flow localization || |Q| ||_{2->2} <= 2 log n
statement: As in GGNS Thm 1.3.
why: Cited and re-proved; it exists in L. Its existence is itself model-produced (provenance flag).

name: I13 (+I14): ramp of overlapping dyadic truncations for p>2
why: Tiny definition (a sum of l band-truncations) that is nowhere in the goal or L, and changes the bookkeeping qualitatively: p-energy ~ l^{p+1} (superadditivity of t^p over overlapping windows) while the projection error only grows like H^{p-2} l. Without it a single truncation gives energy ~ l and no gain, so no subpolynomial bound for p>2. Lean: ramp_sum_bounded_law dominates 28% of the whole DAG; the p>2 branch is ~48% of the mathematical core (71/149 core DAG decls).

name: I12: critical-moment amplification for p<2 (clip a p-stable vector at T, project back, use b = E min(|Y|,T/H)^p ~ log(T/H), T = exp(A H^{2-p}))
why: Exploits the logarithmic divergence of the p-th moment of a p-stable law exactly at the critical exponent: the additive error O(H^{2-p}) is fixed, b grows like log T, so relative error -> 0 at cost K = exp(O((log n)^{2-p})). Not in goal or L. The same 'grow the common moment to absorb an additive error' principle (paper.tex:287-293) is the shared engine of both ranges.

name: I05+I06 (+Lean I07): truncate-then-correct via an O(log n) l_inf-bounded, l2(sigma)-contractive reweighted projection onto the gradient space
why: The structural insight that the gradient space of the complete graph (weights 1/delta_e) is O(log n)-complemented in l_inf uniformly over metrics, with simultaneous l2(sigma) contraction, so coordinatewise clipping/truncation can be undone. This is the cross-field bridge (electrical flows / spectral graph theory -> metric embeddings) on which both ranges rest; dominated share 0.25 in Lean.

name: I04: weighted moment criterion (uniform b, K over all test probabilities)
why: Clean reduction of a simultaneous (all pairs) moment-matching problem to one weighted test at a time; it is what lets the projection depend on lambda.

name: I20: antipodal row-and-column grid obstruction, all p != 2
why: Gives Theta(n^2) for exact embeddings for every p != 2 including even integers p > 2, with an elementary incidence argument.

name: Latent alphabet gadget: the separation concept (nonlinear K-equivariant observable stable under a noise law that every high-restriction-rank linear family dete…
statement: For every p*>0 there is r* such that for all large l there are V >= K=F_2^l, C:V->K and a law mu with C(x+k)=C(x)+k, Pr[C(x+a)!=C(x)]<=p*, and every G<=V* with dim(G|_K)>=r* detects a~mu with probability >=1/8. Plugged into the BKS/KMS rank-one test P -> P + a l^T, it gives completeness 1-eps while high-rank Fourier mass is damped by >=1/8.
why: The concept is non-analytic and load-bearing, but its strategy has a named-in-trace neighbour (Khot-Moshkovitz real-code noise test, invoked at L250 just before adoption) and an explicit programme in L (BKS Sec. 1.6). The trace analyst's 'no retrieval' for PV4 is overridden: L250-251 shows a retrieval trigger. The statement is close to a specification of what the KMS machinery needs; the hard content is its realisability (C2). Upgrade to N3 only if Test 4 shows the concept itself is rarely prop…

name: Explicit quadratic latent gadget: char-2 block C_blk(x,y)=y+Q(x), Q=(x2x3,x1x3,x1x2) on F_{2^d}^3, update spaces U_A on F-lines, all-isomorphism concatenation …
statement: Block: U_A={(a,Q(a)+w): a in A, w in D_A} makes the quadratic term cancel, so a uniform nonzero update changes the output with probability exactly 1-theta, theta=1/(q^2+q+1); a lifted character dies on U_A iff A=Fz and z.g(z)=sqrt(z1z2z3). Concatenating through every (A,J) gives p_t=(1-q^-3)(1-theta)^t while a full lift survives to a leaf with probability >=1/2.
why: No neighbour in searches for nonlinear decoders, quadratic codes, Cremona/APN maps or the 2-to-2 literature. In the trace it appears in one sentence without retrieval, right after a failed retrieval, as in 287. Its requirements were specified in advance by the model's own lessons, so a directed Arm A may hit often; the decisive arm is B. A same-day model-produced sibling (2-to-1 paper) shares the recursive-quadratic-tree architecture, so the architecture may be a house style of the producing mo…

name: Generic character spaces: <=3r alignments z.g(z)=sqrt(z1z2z3) for every binary-linear g, proved by independence of square-root monomials and specialization; ab…
statement: For fixed r, a uniform binary r-subspace of F^3 is generic with probability ->1 as d->inf.
why: A tailored definition with a textbook proof; its value is entirely inherited from C2.

name: Harmonic rank potential with fresh orientations: E[H_{r_j}-H_{r_{j+1}}] <= 4 theta per level, made valid under adaptivity by uniform isomorphisms J
statement: Rank loss probability <= 3r theta per level, so H_r drops by <= 3theta in expectation; depth s = H_{r0}/(8theta) keeps extinction probability <=1/2.
why: An F4-type potential, but a standard one; not graded N3.

name: Spectral comparison: latent-noise eigenvalue Lambda_g <= 7/8 on restriction rank >= r*, forcing low-rank Fourier mass and hence positive acceptance of the ordi…
statement: Matrix-test acceptance >= 0.99 implies E_{U,T} Pr[F_U(M,T)=F_U(M+al^T,T)] >= 0.9*2^{-r*} for uniform a in K.
why: Routine bridge.

name: Exact reduced keys + translation-orbit folding (projected table and pullback share a key)
statement: Tables are identified by support plus induced affine map; constant K-translates fold.
why: Paper's own precedent remarks.

name: Row-fibre advice: abundance of good row advice by erasure; short answer sets; transfer of a chosen witness to sparse projections
statement: A fixed positive fraction of (U,A,T,AM) admit column equations and a target certifying agreement; the certificate transfers to O.
why: Self-detected repair in the trace, but the machinery is KMS17/KS13; at most N2 for the erasure step.

name: Parameter architecture: beta=k^{-2/3}, clean singleton coordinates, Dinur-Steurer repetition fixed before the latent alphabet
statement: k beta^2 -> 0 and k beta -> inf; agreement <= exp(-c k^{1/3}).
why: Known technique.

name: Converse: NP-hardness at the BasicSDP threshold for all CSPs => UGC (dummy labels + KV gap + Rao repetition)
statement: A (1-eps, 1-eta) UG gap with fixed eta and eps->0 yields UGC by projection-game repetition.
why: Known route.

name: Inverse shortcode theorem (equality soundness for degree-two shortcode) derived from Grassmann expansion
statement: Retention eta => agreement with Mz+u on a bounded slice.
why: Imported.

name: Raghavendra transfer to the BasicSDP threshold (the posed problem)
statement: UGC => NP-hardness beyond alpha_Gamma for every finite Max-CSP.
why: Imported.

name: Amplification / stability-gap target: honest loss -> 0 while dishonest loss stays constant under repeated noise; rank-one (not Gaussian) linearity
statement: Specification of the needed test.
why: Sharpened target.

name: Latent alphabet gadget (concept): shift-equivariant nonlinear decoder C: V -> K with a noise law mu that rarely changes C but is detected with probability >= 1…
why: No precedent is named by the paper; the paper's own framing ('keeps the established degree-two inverse theorem and changes the noise using a nonlinear map') presents it as the new idea. Non-analytic: V, C, mu do not occur in the UG statement or in the cited theorems. Load-bearing: it is the only source of near-perfect completeness; without it the KMS/BKS route gives completeness 1/2. Reached after ~34% of the summary and many failures in a long-open problem (BKS18 Sec. 1.6 only suggests higher-…

name: Quadratic gadget construction: Q(x)=(x2x3,x1x3,x1x2) on F_{2^d}^3 with update spaces U_A; 'generic' spaces (<= 3r alignments with sqrt(z1z2z3)) proved via inde…
why: Appears with no retrieved antecedent (CLP / Lovett just rejected); no lesson predicts the specific map or the square-root-monomial genericity argument. Highly specific and small: a three-coordinate quadratic map, a counting definition and a potential - in the spirit of Cook's extension variables (tiny but hard to find). Load-bearing for EC1, which is load-bearing for the theorem.

name: Row-fibre abundance via union randomisation (erasure argument), goodness averaged over questions.
why: Triggered by a self-detected gap, stated twice VERBATIM.

name: Exact identification of tables by reduced keys (shared affine tables) + folding by K-translates.
why: Replaces approximate consistency (DKKMS/MZ) for a stated reason (errors concentrating on small slices).

name: Sparse projection beta = k^{-2/3} with clean coordinates; Dinur-Steurer repetition fixed before the latent alphabet.
Converse 'assertion => UGC' via a dummy-label baseline.
why: Strategically decisive: fixes the answer and architecture in the first 4% of the text.

name: strictly forward / substochastic matrix; paired edge operation
statement: A matrix on V is strictly forward if each nonzero entry goes to a strictly later time; substochastic if nonnegative with row sums <=1; a paired edge operation returns the endpoint plus an inverse port.

name: Configuration reduction (lem:model-reduction)
statement: A poly-time logspace randomized machine yields, uniformly in logspace, a polynomial-size V0, strictly forward substochastic S with bounded port degrees and paired ports, reward e, start x0, with p0=(I-S)^{-1}e in [0,1] and p0(x0)=acceptance probability.

name: Size convention B, stage count L=O(B), radix-D0 copy identifiers, rate grid b_k=2^{-Hk}
statement: B a power of two ~ log(n+2); stage-l vertex = base word plus l radix-D0 copy digits (affine-injective IDs); rates on geometric grid; prime field size 2^{O(B)}.

name: Rank channel and frame (\emph{frame})
statement: Channel A=(a0,F) uniform in F_P^{H x h0} conditioned on F (last h0-1 columns) linearly independent; identifier y retained at rate b_k iff all coords of A(1,y,..,y^{h0-1})^T lie in [0,L_k).
cited_or_new: new instance of k-wise-independent polynomial hashing

name: Rank-channel estimates (lem:env-ranks)
statement: Marginal retention ~ rate; pairwise conditional bound; Chebyshev lower tail for counts; affine-substitution invariance of the joint law.

name: Correction identity D=C-E+EC, I-D=(I+E)(I-C) (reward transfer)
statement: For a nonnegative correction E, D=C-E+EC satisfies I-D=(I+E)(I-C), so W=(I-C)p becomes (I+E)W=(I-D)p: transition mass moved into reward.
cited_or_new: new use of a classical preconditioning identity

name: Fixed-multiplier correction recurrence E_i=fQ((C+E_{i-1}C)/f)g with cutoff Q
statement: Q nondecreasing Lipschitz with (t-theta2)_+ <= Q(t) <= (t-theta1)_+, eighth root Lipschitz; E_i iterates the monotone map from 0.

name: Fixed point and factorial truncation (lem:hier-fixed-point)
statement: Unique strictly-forward fixed point E_*; (E_*-E_k)/f <= e^{1/theta1}(L_Q/theta1)^k/k!, uniformly in V, so a fixed k_* iterations suffice.

name: Pilot detectors U_i(y) (column overload test via rank_J of row-gated sampled scores) and multiplier g = gamma(max U_r)
statement: U_i(y)=E[rank_J{phi(G_i(x,y)/f)R_i(x): X_f(x)=1} | Y_f(y)=1]; many large entries in column y => U_i(y)>=19/20; U_i(y)>1/4 => many medium entries; positive multiplier => at most R_*/f large entries.

name: Residual bounds and unsigned-term domination (lem:hier-residual)
statement: D>=0, strictly forward, substochastic, D<=K_* f, D<=eps_good f on fully corrected columns, and D>=c_dom(C+E+EC).

name: Copy step C^+(x_i,y_j)=r_i(x)D(x,y)s_j(D(x,y)/f) on V x {0..D0-1}; one-stage density and active-count reduction (prop:hier-copy-step)
statement: Routing fractions spread large residual entries over D0 copies; C^+ <= f/2^H, |A(C^+)| <= 2|A(C)|, intertwining C^+P^r=P^rD.

name: Reward identity and shallow target (prop:hier-reward-target)
statement: C_lP_l^c=P_l^c-B_l(I-S); W_l=B_l e in [0,1]; W_{l+1}(x_i)=r_i(x)(W_l+E_lW_l)(x); 0<=p0(x)-W_l(all-primary copy)<=|V0|2^{-(H-1)l}; L=O(B) stages suffice.

name: Stochastic atoms: dense bins B_a, correction tables F with incoming gate T_y, detector score tables S_i; normalization by exact preparatory conditional mean
statement: Sample-dependent row-bounded tables whose conditional means on retention slices equal matrix entries (dense atom identity, correction atom identity).

name: Dense atom identity; correction atom identity; support margins; port contract; assembly comparisons; fine product bounds
statement: Exact conditional-mean identities and bounded supports/ports for the atoms; Lipschitz assembly comparisons with incoming gates.

name: Common default + exception list representation (\emph{default}); rank Lipschitz bound
statement: Arrays represented by finitely many exceptions and one common default; rk_k is 1-Lipschitz in sup norm.

name: Uniform affine spectral gap for SL_H(Z) x| Z^H on finite transitive sets (lem:env-affine)
statement: Lazy walk on elementary generators has spectral gap bounded below uniformly on every finite transitive G_H-set.

name: Conditional averaging (lem:env-gap) and validated walk variants (lem:env-variants)
statement: A rational Markov operator on each retention slice with ||K^d-Pi||_{L_s} <= C 2^{-cd} uniformly; each walk word expands into O(d)-bit variants, each a measure-preserving bijection on the full environment, exactly one passes the slice/wrap test at visited identifiers.

name: Task tuples, statistical budgets M, raw sample terms (direct, product, projection, reward) with importance factors
statement: Each task (input matrix, stage, rates, roles, suffixes) has budget M; sample terms use earlier estimates; true sample means equal targets (lem:est-true-means).

name: Homogeneous loss L(H,H')=|H-H'|^s/(H+H')^{s-1} and root discrepancy metric; scale/domain comparison; cost of releasing a source
statement: Loss comparable to |H^{1/s}-H'^{1/s}|^s, contracts under mixtures; source-domain change u->f costs (f/u)^{...} paid by child precision.

name: Additive schedule: average budget differences T_{b,m}-T_{b,m-1} by conditional walks of length l(M-m), grouped by dyadic slack (lem:est-paths, lem:est-mean-pre…
statement: Means telescope to the budget-m_j term; differences have norm 2^{-p+C0 d} so a walk of length O(d) suppresses noise to 2^{-p-K_n d}; immediate path descriptors take O(d) bits and children have budget <= M-d.

name: Row compression: default-plus-exceptions update with floors rho_j=2^{-c1 d_j}, capacity n_j=2^{c2 d_j}; first-overflow / stationary-reference charging; conditi…
statement: Compressing each prefix to a short exception list preserves row-function errors (prop:buf-error) and gives the exact-grouping error reserve (prop:est-clean).

name: Short fingerprints k(v)=tau(alpha P_v(r)+beta) (lem:fp-hash)
statement: O(log B) random bits give keys in {1..B} with pair collision O(1/B).

name: Budget-block salts with access rule; clean calculation; witness envelopes; escape charging; bucket aliasing; uniform block coupling; Theorem fp-estimators
statement: Comparing actual (hashed) calculation with a block-clean exact-equality calculation independent of the current salt yields the integrated moment bound (1/N)E sum X_f(v)/f |W_bar-W|^8 <= C^8 2^{-8p}.

name: Restoring (catalytic) equality test (lem:fp-catalytic)
statement: With a shared B-bit vector of arbitrary contents, four excursions (flip, xor-read, flip, xor-read) xor 1[k(v)=k(w)] into a result bit and restore the vector.

name: Exact digit streams from approximation residues; gate evaluation from regenerated addresses; elementary ops, multiplication by minimum-index bands, reciprocal,…
statement: Every numerical recipe at slack d answers digit queries with suspended storage O(d)+c(t-j).

name: Cursor, table tuple, restoring test, quantity query, terminal motion, excursion, paired motion (\emph{...}); regenerable record (def:ctrl-record); raw allowanc…
statement: Interfaces in which only one vertex address (the cursor) is kept; callers keep regenerable records only.

name: Inverse contour (lem:ctrl-tour), capped incoming ports, incoming score rank
statement: Contour of the tree of a deterministic terminal program enumerates predecessors (incoming ports) without a second address.

name: Allowance potential Phi(w,t)=Aw+Dt, Psi=t+a'w; allowance w=K1(1+M)-(K0+s0)d; Realization theorem (thm:ctrl-realization)
statement: Each suspended frame costs A(w_i-w_{i+1})+D(t_i-t_{i+1}); telescoping along the active call chain gives total O(M_top+t)=O(B) space, with Psi nonincreasing bounding all clocks.

name: Conditioning on one start (lem:final-majority)
statement: From the integrated 8th-moment bound, E[|W_bar(z)-W(z)|^8 | X_f(z)=1] <= N f/pi_f C^8 2^{-8p}; with p a large multiple of B the cost N is paid; median over enumerated conditional environments.

name: Fixed inverse-polynomial accuracy (thm:fixed-precision); main theorem; PromiseBPL=PromiseL; variable precision by padding (thm:probability); certified acceptin…
statement: Deterministic logspace poly-time transducer outputs p_M(x) within (n+2)^{-d}; hence L=RL=BPL etc.

name: Effective compiler with explicit bounds (thm:effective-simulation); total resource-capped interpreter
statement: A terminating compiler maps (M,a,b) to a deterministic logspace decider and explicit numerical bounds by specializing one fixed deterministic library.

name: Correction-and-copy hierarchy (shallow exact reward target)
statement: Stagewise: choose g by sampled column detectors, E=k_* iterations of E<-fQ((C+EC)/f)g, D=C-E+EC so I-D=(I+E)(I-C) (mass moved to reward), split large residual entries over D0 copies; max entry /2^H, active vertices x<=2; W_{l+1}=r(W_l+E_lW_l); after L=O(log n) stages 0<=p0(x)-W_L(primary)<=|V0|2^{-(H-1)L}.
why: No neighbour found for the whole construction across numerical linear algebra, Markov chains and space-bounded derandomization; it is non-analytic and load-bearing in Lean. Downgrade risks: it is a combination of individually known moves, and by itself it does not break the log^2 barrier (depth-L recursion). Grade is conditional on the proof being correct (comparator build pending).

name: Slack-telescoped multilevel estimator in one shared O(log n)-bit environment
statement: At budget M, sum over m of conditional-walk averages (walk length l(M-m)) of T_{b,m}-T_{b,m-1}; means telescope, differences have norm 2^{-p+C0 d} so O(d)-length walks suppress noise to 2^{-p-K_n d}; descriptors O(d) bits, children at budget <= M-d; integrated (all-vertex, retention-weighted) L_s errors; the final factor N is paid by p=Theta(log n).
why: The telescoping-differences principle is MLMC (an existing concept from numerical probability, so its import is transfer), and CDST23 already varies precision across recursion levels for the same purpose. The concrete space-accounting coupling is new, but under the strict rule it is a close variant. Upgrade to N3 only if test 4 shows hard discoverability given MLMC and CDST23 in L.

name: Allowance potential Phi(w,t)=Aw+Dt with stack telescoping
statement: Frame cost A(w_i-w_{i+1})+D(t_i-t_{i+1}) telescopes to Phi(top)=O(log n); Psi=t+a'w nonincreasing bounds clocks.
why: Routine potential argument downstream of C2.

name: Sampled column detectors and gated corrections
statement: U_i(y)=E[rank_J of row-gated scores over retained rows | Y_f(y)=1]; overloaded columns are not corrected and are split by copies.
why: Sampling-based overload detection is standard; part of the C1 cluster.

name: Block-clean coupling for adaptive short fingerprints
statement: Salts per budget block with access rule; compare with an exact-equality clean calculation independent of the current salt; charge escapes and collisions.
why: Standard coupling; not on the Lean path, so ineligible for the Lean shortlist anyway.

name: Validated walk variants (walks specified before conditioned endpoints are known)
statement: Each affine walk word expands to O(d)-bit wrap-guessing variants, each a measure-preserving bijection; exactly one passes tests at visited identifiers.
why: Engineering variant of known expander-walk sampling.

name: Factorial truncation of the correction fixed point
statement: (E_*-E_k)/f <= e^{1/theta1}(L_Q/theta1)^k/k! uniformly in V.
why: Routine estimate once I07 is defined; load-bearing but not hard to find.

name: Default-plus-exceptions row compression with first-overflow charging
statement: Compressed prefixes keep row-function errors within budget.
why: Standard sparsification idea with bespoke analysis.

name: Catalytic restoring equality test
statement: Flip/xor-read/flip/xor-read on a shared B-bit vector computes 1[k(v)=k(w)] and restores the vector.
why: Transfer from catalytic computing, acknowledged by the paper.

name: Uniform affine spectral gap (property (T)) / Lean Fourier torus gap
statement: Lazy walk on SL_H(Z) x| Z^H generators has uniform gap on finite transitive sets.
why: Cross-field transfer (group theory / expanders).

name: I06+I07+I09+I11+I12: correction-and-copy hierarchy (shallow exact target)
why: Turns an arbitrary poly-length substochastic computation into O(log n) stages where each stage cuts max entry by 2^H at the price of at most doubling active vertices; the row-sum potential |A|*maxentry decays as 2^{-(H-1)l}. Nothing like W_l appears in the goal or in L. It gives the approximation without any gap promise. Lean residual/factorial carry ~35% of the whole proof DAG downstream.

name: I20 (+I17,I19): budget-difference telescoping averaged by slack-proportional expander walks in one shared O(log n)-bit environment
why: This is the step that pays O(slack) instead of O(log n) per recursion level: children at budget m<=M-d, walk/descriptor length O(d), noise 2^{-p-K_n d}. Combined with integrated (all-vertex) error norms, then one factor N paid at the end. MLMC-type telescoping is not known in the derandomization-of-space literature as far as quick searches show.

name: I28 allowance potential Phi=Aw+Dt with stack telescoping
why: Makes the O(log n) space bound exact and uniform; nonincreasing Psi bounds numeric clocks.

name: I09 sampled column detectors U_i and gated corrections
why: Needed for bounded incoming degree and active-count control.

name: I23 block-clean coupling for adaptive fingerprints
why: Handles adaptively chosen endpoints vs. hash salts.

name: restriction order A>=B, tensor semiring S, full direct sum, legs
statement: Tensors over C modulo mutual restriction form a commutative semiring under full direct sum and tensor product; restriction = independent linear substitution on each leg; m denotes the unit tensor of size m.
why: Classical Strassen semiring of tensors.

name: tensor rank R, leg flattening
statement: R(A)=least m with m>=A; flattening ranks are restriction-monotone, additive, multiplicative.
why: Classical.

name: matrix multiplication tensor T_n and exact-rank exponent nu
statement: T_n=sum x_ij y_jk z_ki; nu=inf_n log_n R(T_n); 2<=nu<=3.
why: Classical (nu equals omega).

name: tensor character (spectral point)
statement: Additive, multiplicative, restriction-monotone lambda:S->R_{>=0}, lambda(1)=1.
why: Strassen 1988 spectral points; Lean structure Character (L01).

name: Detecting characters (special case of Strassen's spectral theorem)
statement: If k<d^nu there is a character with lambda(T_d)>=k.
why: Statement is Strassen's duality theorem; only the proof route (I22) differs.

name: oriented dot products B_X(m),B_Y(m),B_Z(m) and dot-product exponents p_X,p_Y,p_Z
statement: B_X(m)=x sum_i y_i z_i; for every character lambda(B_X(m))=m^{p_X} with p_X in [0,1] (multiplicativity + monotonicity).
why: Renaming of <1,1,m> evaluated at a spectral point.

name: lambda(T_m)=m^{p_X+p_Y+p_Z}
statement: T_m is isomorphic to B_X(m)B_Y(m)B_Z(m); T_m>=m gives p_X+p_Y+p_Z>=1; t=(p_X+p_Y+p_Z)/3.
why: Classical factorization of matrix multiplication tensors.

name: elementary degeneration A ~> B (integer weights, keep minimal total weight)
statement: After fixed substitutions give each variable an integer weight (possibly negative) times eps^w; retain minimal-weight terms.
why: Classical.

name: Interpolation: A~>B implies lambda(A)>=lambda(B)
statement: Bini interpolation applied to characters: lambda(B)^j<=(jL+1)lambda(A)^j.
why: Classical.

name: Finite separation: A^{oplus 5M} ~> oplus_h (A_h tensor B_X(M))
statement: If A=sum_{h<=M} A_h shares the X-leg while Y- and Z-sectors are disjoint and matched, then 5M copies of A degenerate to the full direct sum of the A_h, each with its own copy of X and an extra M-dimensional dot product B_X(M). Proof: L=5M Fourier copies with phases zeta^{2rg}, zeta^{r(u-h)}, zeta^{r(-v-h)} force u-v+2(g-h)=0; weights g^2, hu-h^2, -hv give total weight (g-h)^2, so the weight-zero part has g=h and u=v.
why: Lossless separation of a shared leg with a gain factor; replaces lossy Salem-Spencer zeroing-out. Same device as the family's own Sept-24 GROUP lemma (J03; model-produced precedent).

name: Shared-leg entropy inequality lambda(T) >= e^{p_X H(q)} prod_i lambda(T_i)^{q_i}
statement: For T=sum T_i with a common X-space and matched disjoint Y/Z-sectors, for every character and every probability vector q.
why: Method-of-types corollary of I10; closest neighbour is the entropy form of known spectral points. Graded jointly with I10 at novelty stage.

name: polynomial multiplication tensor C(a,b) and R(C(a,b))=a+b-1
statement: C(a,b)=sum x_i y_j z_{i+j}; rank a+b-1 by evaluation/interpolation; output flattening rank a+b-1.
why: Classical.

name: permuted characters lambda_pi and sum_pi p_X^{(pi)}=6t
statement: Each lambda_pi is a character; every exponent occurs twice.
why: Standard symmetrization.

name: symmetrized profile P(a,b)=(prod_{pi in S_3} lambda_pi(C(a,b)))^{1/(6t)}

Severi-dimension and fibre counts give codim >= T-k; transfer to C follows.
