Downgrade risks: (i) it is an assembly of N0 tools (FGvS, Beauville/AHH, CHT, Galazka), and a judge may score expert assembly as N2; (ii) reduction mod 2 to exploit per = det is a standard reflex. Not a templated induction strengthening, so no cap …

name: Smooth-form border bound bdc(G) >= (r-1)(d-1)/(4e) via IFT persistence of simple polar points, kernel lifts and multihomogeneous Bezout
statement: If a smooth nonzero form G of degree r in d variables is a coefficientwise limit of n x n affine determinants, then r(r-1)^{d-2} <= 2^{d-2} binom(2n-1,d-1), hence n >= (r-1)(d-1)/(4e).
why: Close variant of an LLM-assisted precedent in L that 108 cites as its base. The IFT persistence argument for finitely many simple polar points is a genuine simplification of the border step, but not a new concept.

name: Linear-size two-gate coefficient selector (count gates + signed 3x3 equality gadget)
statement: per_m(A(X)) = (-2)^{2k}((k-q)!)^4 G_D(X) for m >= 11k-2q and any complex D.
why: Assembly of classical gadgets (Friedland-Levy count gate, Valiant/DHMTW signed equality gadget) with routine weight tuning.

name: Lean-only Frobenius 'square-form' delta bound and transcendence-degree Severi substitute
statement: In char 2 write f = a^2 + x b^2 + y c^2 + xy d^2. Then delta(C) <= 5 dim K[x,y]/(a,b,c,d) + #{singular points with d != 0}, and curves in the spectral family with delta >= T have transcendence degree n with 18n + T <= 9(k+1)(k+2).
why: New elementary proof of a weaker form of a cited theorem, required by Mathlib's lack of Severi theory. Not a eureka step for the mathematics; noteworthy as autonomous formalization work.

name: Adjugate-generation lemma: degree-(k-1) forms vanishing on Z are constant combinations of adjugate entries (H^1(ker psi) = 0 via the commutator image)
statement: see name
why: Technical lemma inside C2; spectral-sheaf folklore flavour.

name: OR-AND-OR circuit and total gate count S_3(f)
statement: Depth-3 OR-AND-OR circuit, unbounded fan-in/fan-out, free input negations and constants, strictly layered; S_3(f) = minimum TOTAL number of AND and OR gates (bottom gates and output counted).
why: Textbook depth-3 circuit model; total-gate count is the standard size measure.

name: sign g of a predicate; correlation |E gH| with a CNF indicator H
statement: g = +1 on accepted inputs, -1 otherwise; correlation of g with H is |E_x g(x)H(x)| under uniform x.
why: Standard.

name: clause, CNF, scope, width, normalized clause
statement: Clause = OR of literals; CNF = AND of clauses; after removing tautologies a nonconstant clause has distinct variables; scope = its variable set, width = |scope|; violated on exactly one assignment to its scope; false clause has empty scope.
why: Standard.

name: C_b(V) and corr_b(G) = max over width-<=b CNF indicators J of |E GJ|
statement: C_b(V) = CNF indicators on {0,1}^V with clause widths <= b (no bound on clause count); corr_b(G) = max_{J in C_b(V)} |E_z G(z)J(z)|.
why: Abbreviation: correlation with a fixed function class.

name: p-random restriction (T, rho), restricted function G_{T,rho}, and the averaging identity E_x GH = E_{T,rho} E_z G_{T,rho}H_{T,rho}
statement: T keeps each coordinate independently w.p. p; rho uniform outside T; filling T uniformly gives a uniform point, eq. (restriction-expectation).
why: Hastad random restrictions.

name: cylinder (subcube) on the live set
statement: Prescribe a pattern on U subset T; indicator is a conjunction of unit clauses; measure 2^{-|U|}.
why: Subcube.

name: Lemma restriction (Restriction bound): clause-count-independent signed CNF expansion under p-restriction
statement: For H a width-<=k CNF on [d], 0<p<1, b>=1, theta = sum_{l=b+1}^k C(k,l)(2p/(1-p))^l < 1: there are W(H,T,rho) >= 0 with E W <= 1/(1-theta) and |E_z G(z)H_{T,rho}(z)| <= W corr_b(G) simultaneously for all real G on {0,1}^T. No dependence on the number of clauses.
why: Candidate. Quick lit check (Oct 2026): no statement found that expands a restricted width-k CNF into width-b CNF tests with expected coefficient mass <= 1/(1-theta) for ARBITRARY constant pk (b depending on pk). Neighbours: Hastad switching lemma (pk<1/5, DT depth), Razborov encoding proof, Segerlind-Buss-Impagliazzo small-restriction switching, Lovett-Wu-Zhang mild restrictions (first moment of useful terms), Gopalan-Meka-Reingold DNF sparsification. None gives this conclusion.

name: easy/hard at U; counts a_U (violated easy clauses) and c_U (violated fully-revealed clauses); q
statement: Index i easy at U iff |E_i cap (T minus U)| <= b; a_U = sum of v_i over easy i; c_U = sum over i with E_i cap (T minus U) empty; q = total violated count.
why: Part of I07; counting-of-violated-clauses normalisations have neighbours (PPZ isolation counting; Razborov encodings), but this specific easy/hard split is internal to I07.

name: K = conjunction of initially easy clauses after rho (width <= b CNF)
statement: K = 1[a_empty = 0]; K >= H_{T,rho}; first-order approximation of H.
why: Sub-conjunction of H.

name: violation paths P_j(T): sequences of successively hard clause indices with revealed sets U_h
statement: P = (i_1..i_j) with i_h hard at U_{h-1}, U_h = U_{h-1} cup (E_{i_h} cap T); each step reveals > b coords, so length <= |T|/(b+1); indices distinct; a_{U_h} >= c_{U_h} >= h on support.
why: Variant of canonical-decision-tree paths, but selection is "any hard violated clause" (all of them, summed), not the first one.

name: Telescoping partition-of-unity expansion: 1 = sum_i v_i/q, r_P = t_P - sum_i r_{Pi}, giving H_{T,rho} = K + K sum_j (-1)^j sum_{P in P_j} prod v / prod a_{U_h}…
statement: Distribute the unit excess K - H among violated hard clauses with weights v_i/q, replace q by the count a_{U_j} of easy violated clauses, and push the remainder to longer paths; finite alternating expansion.
why: Part of the I07 cluster; no neighbour found that writes a CNF as an alternating sum over violation paths with violated-count denominators.

name: Marker mixture: random order of a clauses and c markers; conjunction of clauses before first marker has expectation c/(c+w)
statement: Represents the rational weight c/(c+w) (w = # violated clauses in an indexed family) as a convex mixture of conjunctions of those clauses, so every term K prod v / prod a equals omega(P) E[J_P] with J_P in C_b(T).
why: Elementary random-ordering identity (classical), used here in a new role: realizing reciprocal-count weights as convex combinations of CNFs. The use is new, the identity is N0.

name: path weight omega(P) = prod 1/c_h; W_j, W(H,T,rho) = sum over compatible paths
statement: Compatible paths (all selected clauses simultaneously violable with rho) prescribe a pattern sigma_P on U_j; c_{U_h} is constant on the cylinder; omega(P) = prod 1/c_h; W = sum_j W_j.
why: Part of I07 cluster (bookkeeping).

name: Reweighting by a full assignment y (E W_j = E_{T,y}[sum over paths violated at y of 2^{|U_j|} prod 1/c_{U_h}(y)])
statement: Sample y uniform, set rho = y outside T; conditional on (T,rho) multiply by 2^{|U_j|} to undo the cylinder probability.
why: Standard reweighting.

name: Backward (reverse) path counting: injective reverse encoding from terminal set R_j, recursion F_s(R) = (1/|V_R|) sum_{i in V_R} sum_{D subset E_i,|D|>b} alpha^…
statement: With alpha = 2p/(1-p), pi(T) 2^{|U_j|} prod 1/c = pi(R_j) prod alpha^{|D_h|}/|V_{R_h}|; one-step weight <= theta; hence E W_j <= theta^j and E W <= 1/(1-theta).
why: Part of I07 cluster; the averaging-instead-of-multiplying device is what removes the clause count and permits arbitrary constant pk.

name: theta = sum_{l=b+1}^k C(k,l)(2p/(1-p))^l
statement: Poisson-like tail; <= sum_{l>b} Q^l/l! with Q = 2pk/(1-p).
why: Tail sum.

name: Lemma sparse-partition: every width-b CNF on m vars is a DISJOINT sum of <= 2^{eta m} width-b CNFs with <= M(b,eta) m clauses each
statement: For every b>=1, eta>0 there is M(b,eta) such that H = sum_{a<=q} H_a pointwise, q <= 2^{eta m}, H_a width <= b with <= Mm clauses, satisfying sets pairwise disjoint.
why: Re-proof of the disjoint sparsification lemma (known, cited); restated with clause count Mm instead of variable-occurrence bounds.

name: sunflower, core, petals
statement: Distinct sets with common pairwise intersection C (core); petals = sets minus C.
why: Erdos-Rado.

name: Lemma sunflower-bound (Erdos-Rado): > s!(r-1)^s distinct s-sets contain an r-sunflower
statement: Classical, with proof by induction on s.
why: Erdos-Rado 1960.

name: eligible sunflower at size i (r_i members, nonempty core); branching state = active antichain + separate unit-clause side condition; branch 0 inserts core C, b…
statement: F = F_0 + 1[C false] F_1 with disjoint supports.
why: IPZ branching with DHMTW side condition; keeping the side condition separate from the active family is a bookkeeping refinement.

name: occurrence bounds e_i, added-clause invariant (<= e_u + 1 per literal), insertion charging N_u <= (e_u+1)(2m + sum_{v<u} N_v), budgets D_i
statement: Bounds the number of steps per path linearly in m.
why: IPZ accounting.

name: leaf counting via per-size decision streams with few ones + binary entropy bound; threshold choice r_i = 2^{q_i}
statement: #leaves <= prod 2^{m F_i h_2(1/r_i)} <= 2^{eta m}.
why: Standard entropy counting as in IPZ01.

name: Definition language: data x (d bits), Hankel/Toeplitz hash seed u, monic modulus P of degree r = ceil(d^{2/3}), t ~ d^{1/6} coefficients beta_j in F_2[Z]/(P); …
statement: d = floor(n/5); r = ceil(d^{2/3}); t = largest even j with j^6 <= d; parameter bits are part of the input; evaluator never tests irreducibility.
why: Close variant of PSZ00 input-index construction + ABI86/IPZ01 polynomial families; parameters r, t tuned to the sqrt(d) live sets.

name: Hankel (Toeplitz) linear hash h_i(x) = sum_s u_{i+s-1} x_s
statement: Universal linear hash; only uniformity of h(w) for nonzero w is used.
why: Toeplitz hashing.

name: Prop polytime: L decided by one deterministic TM in time C(n+1)^a
statement: Integer parameter search, O(rd + t r^2) bit operations; no irreducibility test.
why: Routine algorithmics.

name: Prop good-slices: for fixed b, B and large n there is a setting of non-data bits whose slice g satisfies Pr_{T,rho}[|T| not in [m0/2, 2m0] or corr_b(g_{T,rho})…
statement: Probabilistic method over (u, beta): hash injective on the restricted cube w.p. >= 1 - 2^{m-r}; then signs t-wise independent; t-th moment + union over (C_m+1)^{Mm} sparse tests + sparse partition gives corr_b <= 2^{-m/8}; average over parameter choices.
why: Close variant of IPZ01's random-polynomial depth-3 (bounded bottom fan-in) argument, transplanted to restricted cubes.

name: h(w) uniform for every nonzero w (successive pivots), hence injectivity on a restricted m-cube except w.p. <= 2^{m-r}
statement: Union bound over 2^m - 1 differences.
why: Universal hashing.

name: limited independence from Lagrange interpolation: uniform beta in F^t gives t-wise independent unbiased signs on distinct hash values
statement: Evaluation map surjective for q <= t distinct nodes; lambda balanced.
why: Standard k-wise independence construction.

name: count of sparse tests <= 2^{Mm[1 + b log2(2m+1)]}
statement: Encoding of normalized clauses and lists of <= Mm clauses.
why: Counting.

name: t-th moment bound E Y^t <= t^t 2^{mt/2}, Markov, union bound
statement: Terms with a singleton point vanish; at most 2^{mt/2}(t/2)^t surviving descriptions.
why: Standard moment method for k-wise independent sums.

name: binomial tails of |T| and averaging to fix one parameter setting
statement: Pr[m<m0/2], Pr[m>2m0] <= 2^{-m0/16} each; averaging argument.
why: Chernoff-type.

name: Order of quantifiers and parameters: fix A, s = 3A, B = 64(s+1), p = B/sqrt d, k = ceil(3(s+1) sqrt d), Q = 4B[3(s+1)+1], then choose b = b(A) with sum_{l>b} Q…
statement: pk is a (large) constant depending on A; b is chosen after A so the restriction lemma applies; the slice is chosen after (b, B). "This is the only place where the desired circuit exponent affects the target width."
why: Strategic insight but arithmetically forced given I07 + I26; in Lean exists_final_parameter_width / exists_factorial_tail_width.

name: Correlation transfer to width k: |E g H| <= 2^{-m0/16} E[W_H 1_good] + Pr[not good] <= 6 2^{-m0/16} for every width-k CNF H, no independence needed
statement: Combine I07 (per H) with I26 (good event, uniform over all width-b tests).
why: Direct combination.

name: near-balance: constant-true CNF gives |E g| <= 6 2^{-m0/16}, so Pr[g=1] >= 1/4
why: Trivial instance of I33.

name: Circuit counting: <= S middle CNFs with <= S clauses; delete clauses wider than k (error S 2^{-k} each); gH = H for middle gates of an exact OR; sum over middl…
why: Standard.

name: Lemma field-existence: monic irreducible polynomial of every degree r over F_2
statement: Elementary construction of GF(2^r) and counting of lower-degree elements.
why: Textbook; Lean uses Mathlib GaloisField + primitive element instead (route difference).

name: slice: function of the data bits obtained by fixing the parameter bits
why: Subfunction under a restriction of non-data inputs.

name: Comparator definitions: Circuit3, gateCount = bottomCount + middleCount + 1, FiniteMultiTapeMachine, MultiTapeHaltsIn, runSteps
statement: Self-contained model of depth-3 circuits and multi-tape TMs on top of Mathlib Turing.Tape.
why: Formal renderings of standard models.

name: Multi-tape TM implementation of the evaluator (Tape*.lean, Machine*.lean, LanguageBit*.lean): ~1224 decls, ~7900 lines; machine constants C = 24000*3^8, a = 8
statement: Explicit compilation of hash, polynomial multiply/reduce, Horner loop, parser into a finite multi-tape machine with time bound.
why: Routine implementation (negative control for the load-bearing proxy).

name: Restriction lemma: clause-count-free expansion of a p-restricted width-k CNF into width-b CNF tests with E W <= 1/(1-theta), valid for ANY constant pk (b = b(p…
statement: For H width <= k on [d], b >= 1, theta = sum_{l=b+1}^k C(k,l)(2p/(1-p))^l < 1: exists W(H,T,rho) >= 0 with E W <= 1/(1-theta) and |E_z G H_{T,rho}| <= W corr_b(G) for all G simultaneously. Proof: H_{T,rho} = K + K sum_j (-1)^j sum_{paths} prod v_{i_h}/prod a_{U_h}; each term = omega(P) E[J_P] (marker mixture); count paths backwards from the terminal live set with weight 1/|V_R| averaging over eligible violated clauses.
why: No neighbour found in four searches over the switching-lemma family (Hastad, Razborov, Rossman, SBI, Lovett-Wu-Zhang, GMR, IMP12); the conclusion (clause-count-free L1 expansion into narrow CNFs at arbitrary constant pk) differs from all of them; non-analytic; the knockout shows it is the step that breaks the sqrt n ceiling. Not templated (the IH F_s(R) <= theta^s is incidental). Confidence held at 0.5 because the switching-lemma neighbourhood is dense and expert-heavy, zbMATH/MathOverflow were…

name: Marker mixture: c/(c+w) realised as a convex mixture of conjunctions of the indexed clauses (random order of clauses and c markers)
statement: Uniformly permute a clause objects and c markers; the conjunction of clauses before the first marker holds w.p. c/(c+w) at a point violating w of them. Applied independently per path step, K prod v/prod a = omega(P) E[J_P] with J_P in C_b(T).
why: Classical identity in a new role; graded as part of the C1 cluster. Standalone it is N1-N2.

name: Strategy/quantifier insight: choose b after A so pk may be any constant, with a slice whose restricted correlation exponent (1/8) does not depend on b
statement: Fix A; s = 3A, B = 64(s+1), k = ceil(3(s+1) sqrt d), Q = 4B[3(s+1)+1]; choose b with sum_{l>b} Q^l/l! <= 1/2; then choose the slice for (b, B).
why: Conceptual crux but arithmetically forced by C1 + C4; its novelty is inherited from C1.

name: Prop good-slices: a k-wise independent slice whose random restrictions have corr_b <= 2^{-|T|/8} simultaneously over all width-b CNFs
statement: For fixed b, B and large n, some parameter bits give Pr_{T,rho}[|T| out of [m0/2, 2m0] or corr_b(g_{T,rho}) > 2^{-|T|/8}] <= 4 2^{-m0/16}.
why: Close variant of IPZ01 Sec 1.2 transplanted to restricted cubes; the paper names the precedent.

name: The language: Hankel/Toeplitz hash + degree-<t polynomial over F_2[Z]/(P), with hash seed, modulus and coefficients as input bits
statement: d = floor(n/5), r = ceil(d^{2/3}), t ~ d^{1/6}; accept iff lambda(sum beta_j h(x)^j) = 0.
why: Downgraded from the analyst's N2: a conjunction of L concepts with the paper's own named precedent (PSZ00); parameter tuning only.

name: Disjoint sparse partition with linear clause count
statement: Width-b CNF on m vars = disjoint sum of <= 2^{eta m} width-b CNFs with <= M(b,eta) m clauses each.
why: Re-proof of the disjoint sparsification lemma; downgraded from the analyst's N1 because DHMTW14 already states the needed form up to the trivial occurrence-to-clause-count conversion.

name: I07 Lemma restriction, as the cluster I11 (telescoping violation-path expansion) + I12 (marker mixture keeping tests in C_b) + I15 (backward averaging count: 1…
why: It is the step that breaks the sqrt n barrier: it allows any constant pk (b chosen after A), while every switching-lemma statement in L needs pk below an absolute constant. Conclusion type (signed CNF mixture with L1 cost, clause-count free, tests stay CNFs) is not a subterm of the goal or of L; the paper itself contrasts it with Hastad. Load-bearing: 346/2046 Lean decls (16.9% of whole DAG, ~38% of the lower-bound half); nothing else lifts width. Pieces are tiny identities (1 = sum v_i/q; c/(c…

name: Strategy insight I32 + I26: choose b AFTER A so pk may be any constant, and make the slice pseudorandom so its correlation exponent (1/8) does not depend on b
why: Explains why parity/majority cannot work (their corr_b decays like 2^{-m/b}) and why a pseudorandom slice can. The quantifier order is the conceptual crux of omega(sqrt n).

name: I26 Prop good-slices (k-wise independent slices with small corr_b on almost every restriction)
why: Needed with exponent independent of b and simultaneously over all width-b tests; uses sparse partition on the restricted cube.

name: I12 marker mixture (c/(c+w) realised as a convex mixture of conjunctions)
why: Keeps every test a width-b CNF, which is what makes corr_b the right currency.

name: I17 disjoint sparse partition with linear clause count
why: Large Lean share (Sparse* defs ~22% frac_dag_dependents).

name: limit cycle (geometric, counted once)
statement: Image of a nonconstant periodic solution isolated among periodic orbits; counted once regardless of multiplicity/stability; center orbits are not limit cycles.

name: half-plane arc equation u=x^2/2, du/dy = phi_pm(u) - y, phi_pm(u)=F(+-sqrt(2u))
statement: On each half-plane, y is monotone in time; with u=x^2/2 every excursion is an arc of du/dy = phi(u) - y.

name: arc endpoint data: half-width r(h,t), relative midpoint M, v=M_r
statement: r=(y_> - y_<)/2, M=(y_>+y_<)/2 - phi(h) at base height h for the arc of peak t; v = dM/dr at fixed h.

name: Global arc coordinates (lem:arc-data)
statement: Each arc meets u=h transversally exactly twice; t->r(h,t) smooth increasing bijection (h,inf)->(0,inf); |M|<r, |v|<1, r^2>=2(t-h); dh/dt|_r>0.

name: characteristics, operator D = d_h - alpha d_r, hyperbolic angles theta=arctanh(M/r), L=arctanh(v); characteristic system
statement: Curves of fixed peak in the (h,r)-plane ('characteristics'); along them h'=-r sech^2 theta, theta'=k(h)-sinh(2theta)/r, L'=sinh(2theta)/r, k'=-r sech^2theta phi''(h).

name: Variation at fixed height and width (lem:variation)
statement: First variation of the midpoint under a profile variation psi: [(M+r)K(y_>)-(M-r)K(y_<)] dY = int K psi(u) dy with positive coefficient; strict profile comparison phi1(u)-phi1(h) > phi0(u)-phi0(h) for u>h implies M1>M0.

name: parabolic variation table at zero profile (1/3, 1/15, 1/105 coefficients)
statement: For the zero profile arc u=(w^2-y^2)/2, delta M(0,w) for psi = s, s^2/2, s^3/6 equals w^2/3, w^4/15, w^6/105 (and width derivatives).

name: Smooth scaling at zero width (lem:arc-scaling)
statement: M = k(h) r^2/3 + r^3 A, v = 2k(h) r/3 + r^2 B, t = h + r^2(1/2 + rC) with smooth remainders through r=0 (via signed auxiliary parameter rho).

name: Transverse extension to the axis (lem:axis-extension)
statement: For phi continuous at 0 with phi(0)=0 (derivatives may blow up), limiting endpoints a(t)<0<b(t) exist on an open ray of peaks; M(0,r) smooth, |M|<r, |M_r|<1; r-derivatives converge as h->0.

name: Periodic-orbit matching (prop:cycle-matching)
statement: Nonconstant periodic orbits <-> zeros of Delta(r)=M_+(0,r)-M_-(0,r) on one open interval; each orbit has one positive and one negative y-axis crossing; isolated orbits <-> isolated zeros (no hyperbolicity assumption).

name: quadratic reference profile q_{lambda,kappa}(u)=lambda u + kappa u^2/2; model midpoint H(lambda,kappa,r); P=H_lambda, Q=H_kappa, R=P_r, S=Q_r, G=PS-QR
statement: Midpoint data of the quadratic profile at base height 0 and width r, and its first parameter/width derivatives.

name: Reference functions j_kappa, Theta_kappa, L_kappa (fit:references)
statement: Quadratic arcs labelled by peak slope z: smooth reference system with j(0,z)=z, |j-z|<=|kappa| s^2/2, d_z j>0, d_z Theta>0, z->Theta(s,z) bijection onto R, d_z L>0.

name: reference slope field J_kappa(s,theta)
statement: J_kappa(s,theta)=j_kappa(s,z(kappa,s,theta)); (J_kappa)_theta>0.

name: Curvature comparison (lem:curvature-comparison)
statement: For actual profile phi and constant curvature kappa, E(s)=k(h(s))-J_kappa(s,theta(s)) satisfies E'+aE=-s(phi''(h)-kappa)sech^2 theta, z'=E/d_zTheta, E(s)=int_0^s exp(-int a) f; phi''>=kappa => E<=0, theta >= Theta_kappa(s,z(r)), L(r)>=L_kappa(r,z(r)) (strict if not identically equal).

name: midpoint fit slope lambda_*(r,M,kappa); conditional derivative v_hat, L_hat
statement: For given r, |M|<r, kappa: unique slope with H(lambda_*,kappa,r)=M; v_hat=H_r at the fit, L_hat=arctanh v_hat.

name: Positive conditional derivative (fit:conditional-derivative)
statement: d_kappa L_hat>0 and d_kappa v_hat = G/P > 0; hence G>0 for every model arc (quantitative first-order bound, no differentiation of improper integrals).

name: Properness of the conditional fit (fit:properness)
statement: L_hat(r,M,kappa) -> +-inf as kappa -> +-inf (monotone convergence + average-slope contradiction).

name: R,S>0 and width identity (fit:positive-derivatives)
statement: kappa P + lambda = (rH_r+H)/(r^2-H^2); kappa R = r(1-H_r^2)/(r^2-H^2)((L_mod)_r - 2H/(r^2-H^2)); R,S>0 everywhere.

name: Global quadratic fit (thm:quadratic-fit)
statement: For every r>0 and (M,v) with |M|<r, |v|<1 there is a unique (lambda,kappa) in R^2 with H=M, H_r=v; (lambda,kappa,r) -> (H,H_r,r) is a diffeomorphism R^2 x (0,inf) -> {|M|<r,|v|<1}; P,Q,R,S,G>0.

name: Transport of the fit (lem:fit-transport)
statement: Fitted parameters of an actual profile satisfy P lambda_r + Q kappa_r = 0, D kappa = -(R/G)(lambda - k(h)), D lambda - kappa = (S/G)(lambda - k(h)).

name: Model inequality (thm:model-inequality): (R/G)_r <= 0
statement: For all lambda, kappa in R, r>0: d/dr (R/G) <= 0 at fixed model parameters.

name: W = R S_r - S R_r, gamma, model transport operator calD = kappa d_lambda - alpha d_r
statement: (R/G)_r = -P W/G^2; calD W = (2gamma+3alpha_r)W + gamma_r G_r - gamma_rr G; W = 16 r^3/45 + O(r^4).

name: endpoint coordinates m=r-H, n=r+H, ell=dn/dm, w=ell_m/ell, Schwarzian calS of the endpoint correspondence n(m); weighted endpoint quantities X, Z, gamma; D_*, …
statement: calS = ell_mm/ell - 3/2 w^2 is the Schwarzian of m -> n(m); X=kappa P+d, Z=dP+3kappa Q, gamma as endpoint averages.

name: Endpoint algebra (model:endpoint-algebra)
statement: X_m Z_mm - Z_m X_mm = l^2(m+n)^2/(m^2n^2(1+l)^3) D_* = 3kappa^2/m_r^3 W; at a zero of W, gamma_rr - sigma0 gamma_r = m_r^2 l(m+n)^2/((1+l)m^2n^2) (w_*-w)/(m-n).

name: Riccati linearization, common projective label, Schwarzian formula, inverse-square bound (model:Riccati)
Signs at a possible zero of W (model:zero-sign), three cases
statement: If kappa>0 and W=0 then gamma_rr - sigma0 gamma_r > 0; cases m<=n; m>n & l>=1; m>n & 0<l<1 (polynomial certificates J(l,z), A, T, baseline factorization).

name: Small-width fit (lem:fit-small-width)
statement: kappa(h,r)=phi''(h)+2/7 phi'''(h) r^2+O(r^3), kappa_r = 4/7 phi''' r + O(r^2), lambda = k(h) - phi'''(h) r^4/35 + O(r^5), smooth remainders.

name: Strict third derivative (prop:third-derivative)
statement: phi'''>0 on (0,inf) => lambda(h,r) < k(h) and kappa_r(h,r) > 0 for all h,r>0 (reverse for phi'''<0).

name: Fitted slope intercept (prop:intercept)
statement: If ((k(u)-d)/u)'>0 for all u>0 then lambda - h kappa < d everywhere (reverse for <0).

name: Range of the fitted curvature (lem:fitted-curvature-range)
statement: min phi'' <= kappa(h,r) <= max phi'' over [h,t], strict if phi'' nonconstant.

name: Isolated-zero count for f' = b q, q nondecreasing (lem:isolated-zero-count)
statement: f' = b q with b>0 continuous, q nondecreasing => at most two isolated zeros (zero intervals allowed); positive derivative at every zero => at most one zero.

name: quintic profile split phi_pm = d0 u + b0 u^2 +- p(u), p = e u^{1/2}+c u^{3/2}+a u^{5/2} (a>=0), and the four sign cases of (e,c)
statement: Even coefficients give a common quadratic part, odd coefficients change sign; case 1 (e,c>=0) no cycles; case 2 (e>=0,c<0) p'''>0 -> <=2; case 3 (e<0,c>=0) p''>0 -> <=1; case 4 (e,c<0) u p''-p'>0 -> <=1.

name: Case 1: no periodic orbit when p>0 (integrating factor)
statement: If two positive arches share endpoints, w=u_+-u_- satisfies a linear ODE with positive forcing and w(A)=w(B)=0, contradiction.

name: Sharpness: F_eps = eps(4x - 20/3 x^3 + 8/5 x^5), first-order energy displacement Q(s,0) = -pi s^2(s^2-1)(s^2-4)
statement: Two simple zeros s=1,2 (Q_s = 6pi, -48pi) give two hyperbolic cycles for small eps>0.

name: Refutation of Hernandez Rosales' degree-5 four-cycle proposal (Odani Example 3)
statement: x'' + (1/10)(x^4-10x^2+5)x' + x = 0 rescales (x=sqrt5 u) to Odani's example with exactly two cycles; amplitude equation 2X^4-10X^2+5=0 has roots X^2=(5+-sqrt15)/2.

name: normalizations: F(0)=0 by translating y; reflection X=-x(-t) to make a>=0
statement: Reflection plus time reversal preserves geometric cycles and negates the x^5 coefficient.

name: limit cycle (geometric)
statement: Periodic orbit with an open neighbourhood containing no other periodic orbit; geometric images counted once.

name: logarithmic flag (free/dependent scales, exact log relations f_i = sum a_ij Z_j + b_i), height blocks, saturation
statement: Ordered scales Z_1>>...>>Z_m>>1 along an escaping sequence, f_i=log Z_i, h_i=e^{-Z_i}; dependent scales tied triangularly to later ones with bounded backgrounds; saturated if within each block dependent nodes precede free and log Z_first-free = o(log Z_last-dependent).

name: Finite saturation and preservation of free coordinates; stability under bounded backgrounds
statement: A finite set of large inputs admits a flag after linear change; logarithms of free scales can be inserted; finite saturation; promoting an ordinary coordinate t->0 keeps old free coordinates free.

name: Real and angular path estimates; good contours and buffered sides; background sensitivity; exceptional anchor constant; common safe columns
statement: Complex paths through far anchors along which the largest scale turns vertical first; nested contours with Re of scales positive and separated; control of anchor-dependent growth and simultaneous avoidance of pole lattices.

name: packet: tree of raw functions S^{j,+-}_alpha on bands, child exponent sets, transitions, growth/safe-column and antiholomorphic-source estimates, lateral deter…
statement: An actual analytic function plus two lateral trees of successive asymptotic expansions in e^{-a Z_j}, with domain, transition, error and growth estimates; supports iterated left-finite.

name: Separation (thm:separation)
statement: On a saturated flag, if all paired terminal coefficients vanish the actual function vanishes identically far in the regime; otherwise the first nonzero exponent lambda has equal lateral coefficients and exp(sum lambda_i Z_i) S^1 -> c_lambda(t).

name: Holomorphic proxies/Cauchy correction; propagation of coupled growth; source ratios; weighted maximum estimate; upgrade at preceding transition; one finite tra…
statement: Technical steps of the separation proof (dbar-corrections, weighted maximum principle removing N-dependent constants, induction from terminal level to root).

name: finite request; controlled family; differentiated primitive contract (Assumption); positive in series order / strict positive increment
statement: Uniformity bookkeeping for finitely many labels/derivative orders/budgets; packets whose negative-exponent coefficients vanish.

name: Packet calculus (thm:calculus)
statement: Packets closed under finite sums, products, independent derivatives, exponential monomials, regular analytic operations, unit inversion, and regular implicit solution in ordinary variables (with finite coherence jet order).

name: Elimination with a deferred floor (prop:elimination-recursion) + promotion, local inverse estimate, Taylor replay, common domains lemmas
statement: Induction on ordinary variables / order of a limiting zero, with an exact mode and two quantitative alternatives for a center field that need not vanish; constructs charts through anchors where the equations vanish while a free large input survives.

name: retestable for elimination
statement: Germ invariance of terminal formal coefficients under small perturbations of retained free inputs preserving flag relations and regimes.

name: Absolute isolated-zero finiteness (thm:absolute-zero)
statement: A finite real system with all coordinates (incl. coefficient parameters) variable has finitely many isolated solutions if every sequence of distinct solutions is either analytic at its limit or an anchored saturated flag regime of a retestable library; closure under derivatives, products, inverses, multipliers, specializations.

name: Primitive passage packets: additive (thm:additive-packets), one-rate regular/stable (thm:regular-packets), mixed two-clock (thm:mixed-packets)
statement: Scalar normal-form passage ODEs (actions with log corrections, endpoint layers, clocks L,W with ratio c=W/L comparable/0/inf) have outputs satisfying the packet + differentiated primitive + retestability conditions.

name: Simultaneous globally subanalytic preparation (thm:subdivision-preparation)
statement: Lion-Rolin preparation: on finitely many cells f_nu = c_nu(p)|x-a(p)|^{q_nu} U_nu(...) with strong units.

name: box induction: complete radius list, far domains -> monomial annuli Du = A tau^lambda u^m F(X); jet-order induction -> nozero / simple-root terminal boxes; one…
statement: Preparation of the scalar field D_0 z = R(p,x,z) on cells, uniform in coefficients, without blow-up desingularization.

name: Crossings of a boundary arc (lem:subdivision-crossing)
statement: A periodic orbit crosses a transverse arc at most once; a tangential nonsingular arc lies in one trajectory.

name: Finite passage templates (thm:finite-templates)
statement: For each d, finitely many identity pieces, charts and passage rules, integers N_d, E_d: apart from <=E_d orbits with tangential boundary arcs, every periodic orbit is a cyclic word of <= N_d passages/connectors from a finite alphabet.

name: Terminal reduction (thm:terminal-reduction) + diagonal primitives, tied endpoints, structural extensions, boundary corners
statement: Each terminal passage is one scalar transfer (ordinary/additive/one-rate/mixed) with regular argument graphs; independent arguments, exact residual-amplitude identities; analytic extension at bounded-clock corners.

name: admissible open data; positive-margin completeness; finite differential and algebraic closure; absolute zero property for this closure
statement: Open analytic systems with margins g_j>0 whose bounded positive-margin limits stay in the domain; closure under constants, coordinates, sums, products, derivatives, inverses of nonzero functions, specializations; every generated system has finitely many isolated real solutions.

name: Projection count (thm:projection-count)
statement: If F(p,x)=0 has full row rank on its zero set and the absolute zero property for its closure, fibers M_p have a uniform bound N on connected components (points if m=n). Proof: barrier rho = 1+|p|^2+|x|^2+sum g_j^{-2}, generic tilt via Sard/Fubini, induction on #parameters.

name: Matching systems (thm:matching-system): moving cuts, endpoint graph ties, cyclic rank, injection of hyperbolic cycles into fiber components
statement: Finitely many fixed open analytic systems per degree; every retained periodic orbit is represented; at a hyperbolic cycle full row rank (cyclic matrix kernel zero iff multiplier != 1); different hyperbolic cycles lie on different components (analytic continuation along a component stays in the cycle).

name: Graph and finite-jet lifting; cleared finite differential closure; recovery after graph enlargement
statement: Exact enlargements by regular graphs preserve isolated solutions; denominators cleared; a free flag input stays recoverable.

name: Hyperbolic realization of a finite cycle count by rotation (lem:counting-rotation)
statement: For finitely many limit cycles of V, V + mu(-Q,P) with small mu of one sign has at least as many hyperbolic cycles nearby (w' = div V w + |V|^2 > 0, psi(r)=a r^m).

name: final assembly: B_*(d) = T(d) + sum_w sum_I N_{w,I}; affine rescaling into the fixed square
statement: Any finite collection of limit cycles is moved into the square by z=a+Ru (degree preserved), rotated to hyperbolic cycles, and bounded by B_*(d).

name: Quadratic-fit coordinates for Lienard half-arcs (global fit + transport law)
statement: For the arc equation du/dy=phi(u)-y at base height h and half-width r, with endpoint data M (relative midpoint) and v=M_r, there is a unique quadratic profile lambda(u-h)+kappa(u-h)^2/2 whose arc has the same (M,M_r); the fitted parameters satisfy P lambda_r+Q kappa_r=0, D kappa=-(R/G)(lambda-k(h)), D lambda-kappa=(S/G)(lambda-k(h)), with D the characteristic derivative and k(h)=phi'(h).
why: The engine of the first proof of the degree-5 LMP case (open since 1977; CLZZ Aug 2026 still lists it open). No Lienard or limit-cycle source in searches fits a model profile to arc endpoint data. Cook-style: H and the fit are a few lines to state, are implicitly defined, and about half the Lean core hangs on them. Strong downgrade risk: the derivation of the transport law is the classical osculating-elements computation (10 lines) and the model family is suggested by the problem's even part, s…

name: Model inequality (R/G)_r <= 0 via the Schwarzian of the quadratic arc's endpoint correspondence
statement: For every model profile (lambda,kappa) and width r>0, d/dr (R/G) <= 0. Proof: W=RS_r-SR_r=16r^3/45+O(r^4)>0 near 0; at a first zero of W along model characteristics the sign of gamma_rr - sigma0 gamma_r is fixed by an endpoint determinant identity and the Schwarzian of the endpoint correspondence n(m) of a quadratic arc (via Riccati linearization), closed by three polynomial certificates.
why: Load-bearing and technically clever (reading the model arc as a projective correspondence between its endpoints), but the statement is posed by E1, the tools are textbook (Schwarzian of a solution ratio, chain rule, Riccati linearization, first-zero barrier, polynomial sign certificates) and Schwarzian-based cycle bounds are a known route (CGP 1996, cited by the paper itself). Upper N3 only if the endpoint-correspondence Schwarzian were judged independently discoverable-hard; no evidence for th…

name: Packets (trees of lateral asymptotic expansions on nested complex bands), separation theorem, packet calculus and absolute isolated-zero finiteness
statement: A packet records an analytic function together with two trees (lateral +/- determinations) of successive asymptotic expansions on nested complex bands over a saturated logarithmic flag, with domain/transition/error estimates. Separation: if both trees vanish the function vanishes (no simultaneous convergence in all small exponentials). With a differentiated implicit calculus and elimination induction this yields absolute isolated-zero finiteness: finitely many isolated solutions when coefficien…
why: If correct, 143a would settle the existential Hilbert 16 problem and packets would be the key analytic engine. But as a device a packet is a multi-scale, parametric extension of Ilyashenko's superexact series combined with Ecalle's lateral determinations, and the paper itself frames separation inside that quasianalytic tradition. Extending a named framework to more variables is a close variant (N2), even when the extension is very hard. The hardness here is in the proof, not in finding the obje…

name: Shape comparisons for general profiles: phi'''>0 => kappa_r>0 and lambda<k(h); ((phi'-d)/u)'>0 => lambda-h kappa<d
statement: As named; stated in the paper for general smooth profiles, but in Lean only for the quintic profile class phi(u)=F(sqrt(2u)) with a : Fin 6 -> R.
why: Barrier-argument consequences of E1+E2 under classical Lienard shape conditions. Potentially reusable for other Lienard-type F (paper says so), which makes them the natural downstream test bed for E1, but they are not jumps themselves.

name: Moving-cut matching systems + projection count: uniform boundedness reduced to absolute isolated-zero finiteness
statement: Represent a return by equations matching endpoints of finitely many local passages with moving cuts; within each regular chart, different hyperbolic cycles lie in different fiber components; a Khovanskii-type projection count bounds components uniformly once absolute finiteness holds for the differential/algebraic closure; Duff rotation makes isolated cycles hyperbolic.
why: Clean architecture, but each piece has a named precedent (cyclic systems, Khovanskii/Gabrielov/Wilkie uniform finiteness, Duff rotated fields). Leans N1 in substance; kept at N2 for the moving-cut variant.

name: E1 = Q11+Q19+Q20: quadratic-fit coordinates for Lienard half-arcs (global diffeomorphism (lambda,kappa,r) -> (H,H_r,r) and transport law D kappa = -(R/G)(lambd…

Odd-only methods (Rychkov) and slow-fast cyclicity (Li-Lu) did not reach the general quintic; the fit converts the comparison of two non-symmetric half-arcs into monotonicity of two scalar fitted quantities (kappa_+-kappa_-, intercepts) driven by phi''' and ((phi'-d)/u)' signs. Not a subterm of the goal or of L; H is defined implicitly through ODE solutions. Lean: H has 404 DAG depe…

The idea of reading the arc as a projective correspondence between its two endpoints and computing its Schwarzian explicitly is unusual. Not in goal or L.

It replaces simultaneous convergence in all small exponentials by a tree of expansions with weighted Cauchy corrections. Not in goal or L.

why: Stated for general profiles 'independently of the polynomial application' (introduction.tex:112-115), so reusable for other Lienard-type F; Lean kappa_width_pos dominated share 22%.

why: Clean architectural reduction that separates the analytic difficulty (absolute finiteness) from uniformity; stated as reusable for other classes (01-introduction.tex:229-235).

name: Indexed IFS Phi=(phi_i), phi_i(x)=r_i x+t_i, 0<|r_i|<1; self-similar measure mu_{Phi,p}
statement: mu = sum_i p_i (phi_i)_* mu; equivalently the law of lim phi_{I_1}...phi_{I_n}(0) with I_j iid ~ p. Repeated (indexed) maps allowed.
why: Hutchinson 1981.

name: Exact overlap (equality of complete affine maps for distinct same-length words)
statement: phi_u=phi_v for distinct words of equal positive length; equality includes signed slope and translation.
why: Standard (Simon 1996, Hochman 2014).

name: Random affine map G_n and random-walk entropy rate h_RW = lim H(G_n)/n = inf H(G_n)/n
statement: P(G_n=g)=sum_{w: phi_w=g} p_w; h=lim H(G_n)/n=inf_n H(G_n)/n by subadditivity; 0<=h<=H(p).
why: Garsia entropy / Varju survey Conjecture 3 uses exactly this quantity.

statement: Base-2 average log contraction.
why: Standard.

statement: dim_H nu = inf{dim_H E : E Borel, nu(E)>0}.
why: Standard.

name: Exact dimensionality of mu (Feng-Hu Theorem 2.8) and equality of the two measure-dimension conventions
statement: lim log mu(B(x,s))/log s = d for mu-a.e. x; d = dim_H mu.
cited_or_new: cited, not re-proved in paper; RE-PROVED in Lean
why: Feng-Hu 2009. Lean re-derives it via Hopf maximal inequality, Birkhoff/Maker averages and a maximal ball-ratio bound.

statement: See main_statement.

statement: Regroup into n-blocks with alphabet = distinct maps of G_n (same mu), SLLN for prefix probability and contraction, covering argument.
why: Folklore (Feng-Hu, Hochman); merging coincident maps into a new alphabet is standard.

statement: calH_s(X)=int_0^1 H(floor(X/s+u))du; Delta_s measures non-saturation between scales s and 2s.
why: Varju 2019 averaged entropy; Wang 2011 translation averaging.

name: Lemma 2.1 Entropy calculus (smoothing identity, affine invariance, integer-ratio concavity and convolution monotonicity, scale and grid comparisons)
statement: calH_s(X)=h(X+V_s)-log s; calH_s(aX+b)=calH_{s/|a|}(X); for t/s integer, G_{s,t} concave, in [0,log N], and G_{s,t}(X+Y)>=G_{s,t}(X).
why: Re-proof of cited lemmas (signed scaling added).

name: Lemma 2.2 Entropy and dimension: limsup max{calH_s,H_s^0}/log(1/s) <= d
statement: For exact-dimensional compactly supported nu.
why: Standard.

name: Lemma 2.3 Uniform nonsaturation: d<1 implies delta=inf_{v>0} Delta_v(mu)>0, for unequal signed ratios
statement: If Delta_{v_n}->0 then TV bound gives G_{v_n,Kv_n}->log K; stopped self-similarity transfers near-saturation to all smaller scales (loss C_*=log(1/a_*+2)+1), contradicting P11.
why: Named precedent (BV Lemma 13); the extension via a stopping time to unequal signed ratios is routine.

name: Lemma 2.4 Two-point gain: G_{s,t}(X+vJ)-G_{s,t}(X) >= Delta_v(X)-s/v-v/t
statement: Fair pair at distance v raises window entropy by Delta_v minus boundary losses; no integer-ratio needed.
why: Restatement of Varju's fair-pair comparison in the averaged-entropy calculus.

name: Pair capacity c_ell(nu): max total weight of fair two-point laws with separation in [2^-ell,2^{1-ell}) forming a submeasure of nu (an LP / fractional matching)
statement: c_ell(nu)=max sum_e w_e s.t. w_e>=0, (1/2) sum_{e ni x} w_e <= nu({x}).
why: Named predecessor (Varju Prop. 21); the LP/fractional-matching packaging is a natural formalization of 'mass in fair pairs at scale 2^-ell'. Candidate for N3 only jointly with P15.

name: Lemma 3.2 Finite-law pair bound: k(H(nu)-H^0_rho(nu)) <= log|kF| + C_k sum_{2^-ell<=2rho} c_ell(nu), C_k=60000k^4, independent of minimal separation
statement: Exact-minus-grid entropy of a finite law is bounded by the k-fold sumset growth plus pair capacity at all finer bands; separation-free.
why: Quick check found no precedent for a separation-free deficit-to-pair-capacity bound with a sumset term; the paper names Varju Prop. 21 only as a predecessor. Key non-obvious device: conditioning on the k-fold sum Y makes the refinement cost linear (not t log 1/t) in exceptional probabilities, so costs sum geometrically over all finer scales.

name: Randomized nested partitions rho_h=rho 4^-h with independently perturbed internal cuts (density <= 20/rho_h)
statement: Each parent of length in [rho_h/2,2rho_h] split into N in [2,8] pieces, cuts perturbed by +-rho_{h+1}/10; cuts independent of samples; separating depth J exists but is never bounded.
why: Randomized grids are standard; here an auxiliary gadget for P15.

statement: On the event that at most one coordinate deviates and the sum is near its mean, all child labels equal the mean's labels; the event B is Y-measurable so carries no binary-entropy cost; h_2(q)<=3sqrt q with q<=t^2.
why: Graded together with P15.

statement: Converts mean deviations into band capacities; geometric summation removes J.
why: Routine coupling/geometric series.

statement: Coding = iid types then independent uniform words within types; types fix the signed slope r(kappa).
why: Known disintegration (GSSY; SSS; Kaenmaki-Orponen).

statement: Finite random translation laws given the type environment.
why: Conditional laws of the standard disintegration.

statement: Under the dimension-loss hypothesis, conditional translation laws carry linear entropy invisible at scale 2^{-An}.
why: Close neighbours: Hochman's entropy of the full affine map (Thm 1.4), RV Appendix A, Barany-Verma Thm 3.5. The observation that types fix slope so translation entropy = conditional map entropy is a short step.

name: Digit-count sumset bound: |k D_b| <= (k+1)^{m^b}, hence log|kS| <= n m^b log(k+1)
statement: A k-fold sum of block translations is determined by digit counts; fixed types make this uniform in omega and sign-independent.
why: Trivial counting, but essential pairing with P15.

name: Proposition 4.2 Pair mass in finite scale bands: E[1_{E_n} sum_{ell=a_n}^{B_n} c_ell(nu_{omega,n})] >= c n with deterministic finite B_n (no growth bound)
statement: P15 + P22 + P23 with k chosen after b, eps; B_n = max band index among finitely many laws.

statement: Pathwise convolution identity.
why: Standard.

name: Window entropy g_j = G_{r/M, Mr}(tau_j) at target depth L (r=2^-L), with 0<=g_j<=2 log M and g_j nonincreasing in j
statement: A monotone sequence in the block index at each physical scale; its decrements are the per-window gains.
why: Window entropy of partial convolution products is a standard object in this literature.

name: Lemma 5.1 Conditional pair gain: E[g_j - g_{j+n} | F_{j+n}] >= (delta/2) c_{L-ceil(sigma_j)}(nu_{theta^j omega,n})
statement: Pairs from the window, rescaled to distance in [r,4r), each gain Delta_v(tau_{j+n})-5/M; averaging the unobserved future types restores D_{R_{j+n}}mu by Jensen (Delta convex), where nonsaturation gives delta.

name: Separated band selection: choose n_1<...<n_q successively with a_{n_i}-A'n_i-1 > B_{n_h} (h<i), candidate starts J_i (multiples of n_i), retention events A_{i,…
statement: Adaptive choice of block lengths after earlier (uncontrolled) band endpoints are known; every band contributes delta c T/(4D) while each physical scale's total drop is <= 2 log M; so q <= 8D log M/(delta c), contradiction.
why: No precedent found for a scale-free counting that pits q adaptively separated relative-depth bands against a telescoping bound at each physical scale. Pieces (telescoping, diagonal selection) are standard.

name: Lemma 5.2 Disjoint retained windows: at each target L, retained windows from all bands are pairwise disjoint, so total gain <= 2 log M
statement: x_j=L-ceil(sigma_j) is nonincreasing; a finer-band window ends before any coarser-band window starts.
why: Graded with P28.

name: Completion of proof: no dimension loss (d<1, d chi<h) is possible

why: Known.

Non-analytic: neither pair capacity nor the sumset-plus-capacity inequality is a subterm of the goal, of Mathlib, or of the bibliography. Non-obvious device: conditioning on the k-fold sum Y makes the per-level refinement en…

Removes the last need for effective separation: band endpoints B_n can be arbitrarily large because each n_i is chosen after the previous B_{n_h} are known, and a band's contribution delta c T/(4D) is independent of n_i. Monovariant: at each physical scale g_j is nonincreasing and retained windows from different bands are disjoint, so all gains share a 2 log M budget; q bands force q <= 8 D log M/(delta c). Not a subterm of the goal or L.

name: Finite-law pair bound with the sum-observation refinement (log-free, separation-free)
statement: For every k>=1 there is C_k (=60000k^4) such that every finitely supported nu on R and every rho>0 satisfy k(H(nu)-H^0_rho(nu)) <= log|kF| + C_k sum_{l: 2^-l <= 2rho} c_l(nu), F = supp nu, with C_k independent of the minimal gap of F. Key device (P17): after revealing Y = X_1+...+X_k, refining the cells costs at most 9k sum_i p_i, LINEAR in the exceptional probabilities (no binary-entropy/Fano cost for the event B, which is determined by Y); averaging random cuts gives cost <= C k^4 E|X-X'|/rho…
why: The only item for which no prior near-equivalent was found. The delta over L is sharp and checkable: Varju's Prop 21 (single-scale, doubling hypothesis, h/log(1/h) loss from Lemma 26) becomes a multiscale, log-free bound by observing the k-fold sum. That delta is exactly what the unbounded band endpoints B_n require, and it is the separation-free bridge that Baker / Barany-Kaenmaki make necessary. Against N3: it is a strengthening of a named predecessor in L by a single device; the sum observat…

name: Pair capacity c_l(nu)
statement: c_l(nu) = max sum_{e in E_l(F)} w_e subject to w_e >= 0 and (1/2) sum_{e contains x} w_e <= nu({x}), with E_l(F) the pairs at distance in [2^-l, 2^{1-l}); i.e. the largest total weight of fair two-point laws in band l forming a submeasure of nu.
why: A renaming, as an LP, of the maximal Bernoulli-decomposition mass in Varju's Prop 21 (in L), restricted to one dyadic band. Varju's proof literally minimises the residual, so 148's paper names this predecessor correctly. Not F1: it introduces no new variable beyond Varju's object. Reconciliation with f1_pair_capacity.json/.md (F1 agent, same day): it independently finds the same Varju Sec 4.2.3 identity, the fractional b-matching and sub-coupling forms, and that Kittle-Kogler 2026 replaced c_l …

name: Scale-free separated-band counting with adaptive block lengths and disjoint retained windows
statement: Choose n_1 < ... < n_q successively with a_{n_i} - A'n_i - 1 > B_{n_h} (h<i), using no growth bound on B_n. At each target depth L the retained windows from all bands are disjoint in block index, so their gains telescope to <= 2 log M (g_j is nonincreasing). Summing over L = 1..T, each band contributes delta c T/(4D), independent of n_i, so q <= 8 D log M/(delta c), a contradiction.
why: Telescoping of a monotone multiscale entropy and diagonal parameter choice are standard (Varju's Lemma 27 is the in-L template). The adaptive arrangement is a genuine but modest variant. Would be F4 if raised.

name: Map entropy retained by block types (types fix slopes, so translation entropy = conditional map entropy)
statement: E H(nu_{omega,n}) = H(G_{bn} | Omega_n) >= n(bh - m log(b+1)); E H^0_s(nu_{omega,n}) <= H^0_s(mu) + 1; under dimension loss E[1_{E_n}(H - H^0_{rho_n})(nu_{omega,n})] >= eps n.
why: This is where exact overlaps are absorbed with no arithmetic input. It is a short adaptation of named precedents: GSSY types plus Hochman's full-map entropy.

name: Uniform nonsaturation for signed unequal ratios
statement: If d<1 then delta = inf_{v>0} Delta_v(mu) > 0, for any signed, unequal ratios (stopped self-similarity).
why: A named precedent with a routine extension.

name: Conditional pair gain by Jensen over the unobserved future types
statement: E[g_j - g_{j+n} | F_{j+n}] >= (delta/2) c_{L - ceil(sigma_j)}(nu_{theta^j omega, n}).
why: Prop 20 composed with a standard Jensen-over-environment step (borderline N2).

name: Linear pair mass in a finite band with uncontrolled endpoint
statement: E[1_{E_n} sum_{l=a_n}^{B_n} c_l(nu_{omega,n})] >= c n with B_n finite but with no growth bound.
why: Assembly. Its novelty lives in C1. P23 is a trivial count whose role (sumset sub-linear in k) is the tensor-power-style amplification that C1 needs.

name: proper k-coloring; chromatic number chi(R^2)
statement: c: R^2 -> {1..k} with c(x)!=c(y) whenever |x-y|=1; chi(R^2) the least such k, no regularity.
why: Classical; it is the goal itself.

name: measurable chromatic number chi_m(R^2)
statement: Least k when each colour class must be Lebesgue measurable.
why: Falconer 1981.

name: weak measurable k-coloring (Def 1.1)
statement: Lebesgue measurable c with sum_i int_{B(0,R)} int_{S^1} 1_{A_i}(x)1_{A_i}(x+u) dsigma(u) dx = 0 for all R; i.e. monochromatic unit pairs form a dx dsigma-null set.
why: The almost-everywhere relaxation of a measurable proper colouring is the obvious relaxation; Falconer/Payne density-point arguments already work with a.e. statements. Naming and using it as the target of a transfer from arbitrary colourings is new. Not N3: it is a one-line weakening of an existing notion.

name: Transfer of colorability (Thm 1.2): proper k-coloring exists <=> weak measurable k-coloring exists, every k, ZFC
statement: Forward: Prop 4.2 (I25). Reverse: density points (I26) plus de Bruijn-Erdos compactness (I27).
why: No prior theorem identifies the unrestricted chromatic number of the plane with any measurable variant; Payne 2009 shows such identifications fail for translation-invariant subgraphs (rational unit displacements: chi=2, chi_m>=5). Shelah-Soifer 2003 show the ZFC vs ZF+DC+LM values could differ for related graphs. The transfer itself is the statement; its engine is I10.

name: No weak measurable five-coloring (Thm 1.3)
statement: There is no weak measurable 5-coloring of R^2.
why: As a statement it implies chi_m(R^2)>=6, which improves Falconer 1981 (no improvement found in searches). Its machinery is graded separately; named precedents: Falconer/Payne density points, Sokolov-Voronov 2025 interfaces and strips, Townsend 2005 annulus, Moser spindle.

name: Isbell/Hadwiger hexagonal 7-coloring (index-7 sublattice 2-omega)
statement: Voronoi hexagons, circumradius 2/5, coloured by cosets of (2-omega)(Z+Z omega).
why: Classical (Isbell 1950, Hadwiger 1961).

name: E = F(i) (F real algebraic numbers), K = algebraic unit rotations, D = dual of discrete E (Def 2.1)
statement: E as a discrete countable group; D = Pontryagin dual of E_disc (compact metrizable); action (ad)(z)=d(az); psi_z(d)=d(z).
why: Pontryagin dual of a countable dense subgroup of R^2 with the discrete topology: a quotient of the Bohr compactification of R^2. Standard objects; the specific choice of E = Q-bar (real-closed F) is what matters, and that choice is part of I10.

name: C = j(R^2), the ordinary continuous characters inside D
statement: j(xi)(z)=exp(i xi.z); Borel subgroup, not closed.
why: The canonical embedding of R^2-hat into the Bohr-type dual.

name: wild K-invariant law: nu(C)=0 (Def 2.2)
statement: A K-invariant Borel probability on D giving C measure zero.
why: A conjunction of invariance and a null condition; name only.

name: Rigidity of wild character laws (Thm 2.3): every K-invariant probability on D with nu(C)=0 is Haar
statement: nu wild => nu = m_D; equivalently all nonzero Fourier coefficients vanish.
why: Nearest neighbours: Crum 1956 (measurable positive-definite functions = continuous + a.e.-zero part; radial version continuous + c*delta_0) is a measurable-on-R^n statement; the paper's statement is on a discrete countable group with no measurability, which Crum does not cover. Measure rigidity for group actions on tori/solenoids (Furstenberg x2x3, Bourgain-Furman-Lindenstrauss-Mozes 2011, Benoist-Quint) concerns stiffness of stationary measures for lattices in SL_d(Z); here the acting group is…

name: Wild null events (Lemma 2.4): cosets of C null; difference law wild; L_a (continuous on a line) null
statement: Positive-mass coset has finite K-orbit; K divisible so finite images trivial; two nonparallel continuous lines give a character in C.
why: Elementary: divisible groups have no nontrivial finite quotients; orbit-counting of disjoint cosets.

name: Invariant-mean line integral I(h) on F/Z (eq 2.4)
statement: I(h)=m(sum_k h(t+k)) for an invariant mean m on the discrete group F/Z; agrees with Lebesgue integral on C_c; needs no measurability.
why: Invariant means on amenable discrete groups are classical; periodization against them is a routine device.

name: Vanishing line average (Lemma 2.5): I(phi(t) f_nu(at)) = 0 for wild nu
statement: No strongly continuous vectors (Bochner on R after extending the coefficient, then Fourier uniqueness on F-hat); weak integral V_phi is continuous hence zero.
why: Close in spirit to Wiener/Crum-type arguments that singular spectral parts have vanishing averages; the device of invariant-mean averaging along an algebraic line is a modest variant.

name: Moment-free equivariant location functional L(lambda) (Lemma 2.6)
statement: Unique minimizer of J(s)=int(sqrt(1+|s-t|^2)-sqrt(1+|t|^2))dlambda; Borel, translation- and O(2)-equivariant.
why: Variant of the moment-free spatial median (minimize E(|X-s|-|X|), Kemperman/Haldane); pseudo-Huber smoothing makes it strictly convex. Known trick.

name: Compact-tower approximation property (eq 2.10 / source-4)
statement: For bounded H on Y, finitely many H_r and bound B so that every rotation U_k H is within eps of sum b_r^k H_r with W-measurable coefficients.
why: Uniform version of a compact (finite-rank module) extension; standard in Furstenberg-Zimmer theory.

name: Relative singularity (Lemma 2.7) along a compact tower, by universal transfinite induction
statement: For an ergodic K-system with equivariant d: X->D of wild law, the difference law of two conditionally independent samples over every tower factor gives C measure zero. Proof: failure gives m equivariant coset centers (I14), phase lists encoded by elementary symmetric functions, compact approximation forces many index collisions; line average (I13) on the earlier factor forces few collisions; x_j = k_j + k_j' (sum of two algebraic unit vectors) links them.
why: Structure (induction over a Furstenberg-Zimmer tower, show a property survives compact extensions) is the standard template of Furstenberg's Szemeredi proof. The collision/phase-list counting inside the step is specific. The IH is strengthened to range over all systems (templated: 'strengthen to all substructures'), so the cap at N2 applies to the strengthening; the collision argument alone is a combinatorial estimate.

name: Phase-list encoding H(y) by elementary symmetric functions
statement: Unordered list of m phases encoded in C^m via Newton identities; continuous injection of T^m/S_m.
why: Standard (symmetric-function coordinates on unordered tuples).

name: Compact tower (Lemma 3.1)
statement: Countable-ordinal tower of compact extensions ending at a factor Y with X x_Y X ergodic; bounded fiber basis via invariant HS kernels.
why: Furstenberg-Zimmer structure theorem, re-proved for K.

name: Conditional multiple averages (Lemma 3.2) for power maps u -> u^{n_j} along every Folner sequence
statement: Over a relatively weak-mixing factor, averages of P(prod U_{u^{n_j}} v_j) decouple; vdC/Hilbert induction.
why: Relative weak mixing implies characteristic factor for multiple averages: Furstenberg 1977, adapted to power maps of an abelian group (surjective since K divisible).

name: Radial identities (Lemma 3.3): w(|A-B|) <= w(A)+w(B) for w=-log m, and Avg m(2r|Re u|) -> m(r)^2
statement: Uses |A-Bu^2|^2 = |-L+(A-B)u+Lu^2|^2 with L=sqrt(AB) in F (real-closedness), so two- and three-term multiple averages compare; m = |projected character|^2 is radial.
why: The algebraic identity among unit directions that converts multiple ergodic averages into a triangle-type inequality for -log of a radial coefficient was not found anywhere in a quick search. Against: once one has m radial and multiple-average decoupling, looking for polynomial identities in u with equal moduli is a natural move; it is a lemma inside I10 and arguably part of that candidate.

name: General position in a number field (Lemma 3.4)
statement: Cayley parametrization u(t)=(1+it)/(1-it); arbitrarily large S in K cap N with every d_0 elements a Q-basis.
why: Generic-position via nonvanishing polynomials over infinite field; textbook.

name: Addition under a cap (Lemma 3.5)
statement: If w(0)=0, subadditive in the difference sense, w(p_j)<=H, then any integer combination with l1-length M landing in [0,p) has w <= 4MH.
why: Elementary residue bookkeeping.

name: Syndetic-set / number-field endgame of Thm 2.3
statement: If m(r)>0 then {u: w(2r|Re u|)<=H} is syndetic in K; general-position bases and capped residues give m>=c on (0,2rc_0) cap F, contradicting the line average.
why: Assembly of I20-I22 with standard syndeticity; graded with I10.

name: Continuous vectors and positivity (Lemma 4.1): H_c = L^2 of a factor = spectral subspace on C; extends to a positive strongly continuous R^2 action
statement: For a measure-preserving action of the dense subgroup E, vectors with continuous orbits form L^2 of a factor; projection is conditional expectation (so positivity and sum-one survive).
why: Ingredients standard (SNAG spectral theorem, Bochner, Stone-Weierstrass, the fact that a closed Koopman-invariant subalgebra is L^2 of a factor). The packaging as 'the continuous factor of an action of a dense subgroup' resembles the classical extension of measurable/continuous actions (Mackey point realization) but is used here without point realization.

name: From proper to weak measurable colorings (Prop 4.2)
statement: Restrict to E, average over the amenable group E x| K to get an invariant law on proper labellings; project label indicators onto H_c; residual has Haar spectral measure by I10 so unit correlations survive; extend to all unit directions by continuity; sample a jointly measurable field and take least positive label.
why: The amenable averaging step is known (Bourgeat-Heinrich-Melotti-Robert 2015, Gwyn-Stavrianos 2020, Matolcsi-Ruzsa-Varga-Zsamboki fractional chromatic number); the novel part is retaining exact unit-distance exclusions while passing to ordinary measurable functions, which hinges on I10.

name: Density-point properness (Lemma 4.3)
statement: Full-density points of a weak class contain no unit pair.
why: Falconer/Payne density-point argument, adapted to product-a.e. exclusion.

name: de Bruijn-Erdos compactness
statement: A graph is k-colorable iff every finite subgraph is.
why: Classical.

name: typical point; typical circle sampling
statement: A point of density one in its own colour; (y,r) with y+re typical for a.e. e.
why: Density-one point; standard.

name: Circle traces W_x and maximal palette P_x(e) (Def 5.1)
statement: W_x = weak-* limits in L^inf(S;R^5) of circle samples (a_i(y_n+r_n e))_i with y_n->x, r_n->1 typical; P_x(e) = labels with positive weight at e in some trace (essential union).
why: Nearest neighbours: Young measures / weak-* limits of oscillating sequences (Tartar), tangent measures (Preiss), Falconer's density-point rotations, and the 'colour seen on the unit circle' arguments of Woodall/Townsend/Sokolov-Voronov for regular maps. None defines an angular, center-indexed set-valued palette from weak-* limits of unit-circle samples of an arbitrary measurable colouring. It is a natural 'blow-up' object once one wants circle information at every center, so a judge may grade i…

name: Palette transfer (Lemma 5.2): exclusion c(x+e+v) not in P_x(e) cup P_x(v); density; smooth transport P_z(f) cap P_x(s(f)) empty
statement: Strong L^1 convergence of the second factor against weak-* first factor; two-angle sum map change of variables.
why: Weak-strong pairing and change of variables are standard; the transported exclusion is the circle analogue of Falconer's rotation argument.

name: Sixty-degree exclusion P_x(f) cap P_x(Rf) = empty
statement: x+f = x+Rf+R^{-1}f.
why: The equilateral-triangle (Moser rhombus) relation; classical in unit-distance arguments.

name: binary center for {i+,i-}; alternating sign function s_x
statement: P_x meets the pair a.e.; selection alternates under rotation by pi/3.
why: Name for a conjunction.

name: Binary-center separation (Lemma 5.5): binary centers for one pair are delta_*-separated
statement: Two close binary centers force s_x invariant under six circle diffeomorphisms F_j near rotation by 0; bounded-distortion growth of a conull interval forces full measure, contradicting measure pi.
why: Named precedent: Sullivan/DKN bounded distortion for circle group actions; adaptation replaces minimality.

name: Palette cardinality (Prop 5.6): 1 <= |P_x(e)| <= 2 a.e., every center
statement: Three labels at a positive set of angles force infinitely many binary centers on x+S, contradicting I33.
why: Local, circle-sampled analogue of Falconer's chi_m>=5 argument; strengthened to 'at most two'.

name: Transition graph Gamma_x via limsup_{h->0} D_ij(B,h)/|h| > 0 (Def 6.1)
statement: ij is an edge at x if the area of i->j transitions under shift h near x is comparable to |h|.
why: An interface density: int|1_A(x+h)-1_A(x)|/|h| is the Bourgain-Brezis-Mironescu/Davila difference-quotient characterisation of perimeter; Gamma_x records where the pairwise 'interface measure' has positive upper density. Close variant of known BV/perimeter notions, applied without finite-perimeter assumptions.

name: Avoiding trace (Lemma 6.2): an edge ij of Gamma_x gives a trace avoiding i and j
statement: Circle-average of a_s - a_s(.+h) is o(sqrt|h|) in L^2 by |sigma-hat(xi)| <= C(1+|xi|)^{-1/2} and Plancherel; average over transition set (area >= c|h|) is o(1).
why: Fourier decay of circle measure and the Plancherel square-function estimate are classical (Stein); matching normalisation |h| to the decay exponent 1/2 is the new twist.

name: Strict state separation (Lemma 6.3)
statement: States at x representing complementary label groups; supports have no chordal-distance-one pair.
why: Direct consequence of I30.

name: Singleton-pair alternation impossible (Lemma 6.4)
statement: No state function alternating between {X} and a pair under R; uses gamma with cos gamma=5/6.
why: Moser-spindle-type angle (cos=5/6 is the spindle rotation) in circle form.

name: Local finiteness of cyclic centers (Thm 6.5)
statement: {x: Gamma_x contains a cycle} is closed and locally finite (triangle via binary separation; four-cycle via continuity of states; five-cycle similarly).
why: New statement, assembled from I33-I38.

name: Four-cycle state continuity (Lemma 6.6) and support-contact step ban (Lemma 6.7)
statement: x -> 1_{w_x=s} continuous into L^1(S) on the four-cycle locus; contacts ban angular steps.
why: Technical.

name: Disk averages p^eps and p_i(q)+p_i(z) <= 1 at unit distance (Lemma 7.2)
statement: Mollified colour probabilities; unit pairs cannot both exceed 1/2.
why: Mollification; the inequality is the averaged form of properness (as in Falconer and in fractional-chromatic arguments).

name: Thresholded renormalised vector q^eps into the 1-skeleton of the 4-simplex (complete graph K5) (eq 7.4)
statement: q_i = (p_i-alpha)_+ / sum_k (p_k-alpha)_+; off small disks at most two coordinates positive, so q^eps maps into the graph K5.
why: This is the nerve map of a cover of multiplicity <= 2 (partition of unity into the nerve), classical in dimension theory (Alexandroff/Lebesgue). Used on a colouring with arbitrary boundaries, it is a change of representation, but the device is textbook. Not N3.

name: Small holes and tree fillings (Lemma 7.4)
statement: Off core disks around cyclic centers, Gamma_z is a forest, so violation disks can be filled continuously through trees.
why: Tree contractibility is standard; the measure estimates (missing edges have o(eps) overlap) are new but routine.

name: Cover obstruction on a square (Lemma 7.5): no relatively open cover of multiplicity <=2 and mesh <=2
statement: Partition of unity into segments plus Brouwer.
why: Lebesgue covering theorem (covering dimension of the square is 2), 1911/Brouwer 1913.

name: Non-null core loops (Lemma 7.6)
statement: If every core loop were null, extend g_n over the disks and contradict I44.
why: Direct from I44.

name: Midpoint detection by a reduced circuit (Lemma 7.7)
statement: Free homotopy classes in a graph have cyclically reduced words; loops in a class meet every edge midpoint of the word.
why: Fundamental group of a graph is free; textbook.

name: Connected midpoint preimage crosses the annulus (Lemma 7.8)
statement: A component of g^{-1}(m) meets both boundary circles.
why: Standard planar separation argument.

name: A cycle of common exclusion continua (Prop 7.1) with straddling regions Delta(K)
statement: Compact connected K_j through a common x, with both endpoint labels absent from Delta(K_j) = {z: min|z-q|<1<max|z-q|}.
why: Named precedent for regular maps; new is producing the continua from measure data via topological extraction.

name: One-sided strip restrictions O(e), I(e) (Lemma 8.1)
statement: Signs of e.v_j decide which labels survive just outside/inside the unit circle about x.
why: Named precedent.

name: Five-cycle exclusion (Prop 8.2)
statement: Six-position words of diagonals mod 5: three steps can't sum to 0 or +-2 unless constant; six equal steps don't close.
why: Finite combinatorics; Lean proves by `decide` over Fin 5^6 = 15,625 tuples (Exclusion.lean:60-63).

name: Four-cycle exclusion via six-position words and projective ray geometry (Lemmas 8.3-8.4, Prop 8.5)
statement: Two antipodal pairs of split directions and a parity rule.
why: Finite geometric case analysis.

name: Triangle case: local binary rigidity, boundary is one R-orbit, alternating pi/3 sectors (Lemmas 8.6-8.7)
statement: Outsider state s in {X,Y} alternates in exactly six sectors of angle pi/3.
why: Named precedent (Townsend).

name: Polynomial three-label region (Lemma 8.8): v^2(3xi^2-v^2)^2 < l^3(1-l/4)(l-1)^2 implies only triangle labels near x+z
statement: Triple-angle identities; two directions summing to z lie in opposite-outsider sectors.
why: Elementary trigonometry.

name: Moser spindle placement z_g=((35+12i)/37)(g+(-290+149i)/250) and seven-point rational certificate (Lemma 8.9, Sec 8.6)
statement: All seven Moser vertices strictly inside the three-label region; checked by hand interval arithmetic with 4-decimal boxes (h=0.00011).
why: Moser spindle is classical; the placement is a small explicit certificate (7 points, 2 tables), not a search artefact.

name: Positive five-color badness (Cor 1.4)
statement: Every 5-colouring has invariant-mean monochromatic-unit-pair frequency >= delta = 1/|E(H)| for an existential finite non-5-colourable unit-distance graph H.
why: Direct from known finite-graph bounds; graph H is existential (not exhibited).

name: FullApprox c alpha t: global graph-valued approximant on closedBall 0 5 with small disk holes
statement: Lean reorganisation: angular contradictions are used to show all common-interface graphs are acyclic (commonInterface_graph_acyclic), so a global map into K5 exists (fullApprox_exists), then graph_map_small_mesh_impossible + no_large_positive_sequence contradict.
why: Contrapositive packaging of paper Sec 7-8; same content.

name: Rigidity of wild K-invariant laws on the dual of the discrete algebraic plane (Thm 2.3), with its proof engine
statement: E = Q-bar as a discrete group, D its compact dual, C the continuous characters j(R^2), K the algebraic unit rotations. Every K-invariant probability on D with nu(C)=0 is Haar; equivalently, a K-radial positive-definite function on E whose spectral measure ignores C has all nonzero coefficients 0.
why: No near-equivalent in any field found; Crum's theorem is the closest statement-level analogue but requires measurability on R^n, which is exactly what C1 removes; non-analytic and heavily load-bearing. Not transfer: no existing theorem is imported. Downgrade risks: an expert may know a rigidity theorem for rotation-invariant measures on duals of real-closed fields, or regard C1 as 'Crum on Q-bar' (N2). F5 because it re-represents unit-distance constraints of an arbitrary labelling as a spectral…

name: Forward transfer: arbitrary proper colouring -> weak measurable colouring via the continuous-translation factor (Prop 4.2 + Lemma 4.1 + Def 1.1)
statement: If R^2 has a proper k-colouring then it has a weak measurable k-colouring (any k, ZFC).
why: Same device as C1 seen at statement level (C1 is what makes it work). Counted once with C1 for family_D. The averaging and spectral-subspace parts alone would be N1-N2 (I24 'continuous factor' packaging is close to standard Koopman/factor facts).

name: Circle traces W_x and maximal palettes P_x(e) (Def 5.1) with palette transfer and cardinality <= 2
statement: At each center, weak-* limits of unit-circle colour samples near x define an angular set-valued palette; exclusions transport between palettes; almost every palette has <= 2 labels.
why: Natural blow-up/Young-measure object built on Falconer's density-point circle sampling; the specific definition is new but a close variant of an existing technique. Not N3.

name: Radial identity |A-Bu^2|^2 = |-L+(A-B)u+Lu^2|^2 giving w(|A-B|) <= w(A)+w(B) for w=-log m (Lemma 3.3)
statement: Multiple-average decoupling plus an equal-modulus polynomial identity in u (needs L=sqrt(AB) in the real-closed F) gives a triangle-type inequality for -log of the radial conditional coefficient.
why: Graded as a component of C1's device; it is the step that turns ergodic decoupling into arithmetic. Low confidence: small identity, plausibly found by a directed search for equal-modulus relations. Not counted separately for family_D.

name: Relative singularity along a compact tower (Lemma 2.7)
statement: Wildness of the conditional difference law survives every stage of a Furstenberg-Zimmer tower.
why: Templated strengthening ('strengthen to all substructures': IH ranges over all systems) caps at N2; the collision count inside is new but local.

name: Transition graph Gamma_x (|h|-normalised transition density) and avoiding traces via circle Fourier decay (Def 6.1, Lemma 6.2)
statement: ij is an edge at x when transitions i<->j under shift h have area >> |h| near x; then a circle trace avoids both i and j, because circle averages of a_s - a_s(.+h) are o(sqrt|h|).
why: Interface-density notion close to BV/perimeter difference quotients; matching the |h| normalisation to the circle decay exponent is new but routine.

name: Graph-valued thresholded disk averages + Lebesgue/Brouwer cover obstruction (eq 7.4, Lemmas 7.4-7.6)
statement: Map the colouring to the 1-skeleton of the simplex (K5); fill holes through trees; a square has no cover of multiplicity <= 2 and mesh <= 2.
why: Classical dimension theory transferred; the continuous K5-valued representation is the nerve map of the colour-threshold cover. Transfer, not a jump.

name: Weak measurable colouring (Def 1.1)
statement: Measurable colouring whose monochromatic unit pairs are dx dsigma-null.
why: Natural relaxation; its value comes from C1/C2.

name: Common exclusion continua with straddling regions Delta(K) and one-sided strips (Prop 7.1, Lemma 8.1)
statement: Compact connected K_j through a common point, both endpoint labels absent from Delta(K_j); strips just inside/outside the unit circle use only allowed labels.
why: Named precedents; new is producing continua from measure data.

name: Binary-center separation (Lemma 5.5) by Sullivan bounded distortion
statement: Two distinct binary centers for the same pair are delta_*-apart.
why: Adaptation of a named technique.

name: I10 (with I16, I20, I23): rigidity of wild K-invariant laws on the dual of the discrete algebraic plane
why: It is the entire reason an arbitrary (non-measurable) colouring can be converted to a measurable one. Before it, only symmetry could be extracted by averaging (Bourgeat et al., Gwyn-Stavrianos, Matolcsi et al.). Nothing in the goal (maps C -> Fin 5) or in L (Mathlib + bib) mentions duals of dense subgroups, wild laws or C-singular spectral parts: non-analytic. Load-bearing: residual_fourier dominated share 0.44 of the target DAG; ~0.40 of the non-background core. Payne 2009's rational-unit-grap…

name: I25 + I24 + I03: forward transfer (proper -> weak measurable) via the continuous-translation factor
why: First identification of chi(R^2) with an almost-everywhere measurable chromatic number; contrasts with Payne 2009 and Shelah-Soifer 2003 where such identifications fail or depend on axioms. The projection-is-conditional-expectation step (I24) is what keeps nonnegativity and sum-one; without it the spectral split would not produce colourings.

name: I29 circle traces and maximal palettes P_x(e)
why: A new defined object: center-indexed angular palettes from weak-* limits of unit-circle samples; every step of the 5-colour obstruction is phrased in it. Allows Falconer-type rotation arguments at every center with no regularity of colour boundaries, which is precisely what earlier map-type arguments (Woodall, Townsend, Sokolov-Voronov) lacked.

name: I20 radial identity |A-Bu^2|^2 = |-L+(A-B)u+Lu^2|^2 giving w(|A-B|) <= w(A)+w(B)
why: Converts multiple ergodic averages into a metric-type inequality on the radial coefficient; this is the step that makes the number-field endgame possible. Uses real-closedness essentially (L = sqrt(AB) in F).

name: I16 relative singularity along a compact tower (phase-collision step)
why: Original collision-count argument linking compact approximation and the line average.

name: homomorphism density t(H,G), edge density p(G), Sidorenko inequality
statement: t(H,G)=hom(H,G)/|V(G)|^{|V(H)|} (all maps, noninjective included); p(G)=2|E(G)|/|V(G)|^2; conjecture t(H,G)>=p(G)^{|E(H)|} for bipartite H with an edge.

name: Main theorem (counterexample)
statement: For the incidence graph H of the 22 triples on 13 points (35 vertices, 66 edges) there is a finite simple G with an edge and t(H,G)<p(G)^66.

name: The complex: 22 triples on I={0..12}, point pairs E, incidence graph H, corners
statement: Faces j in J (22 triples listed with opposite faces and a 3-bit label); E = point pairs inside faces (33); H=(I sqcup J, C) with C={(i,j): i in j}; a 'corner' is an incidence.

name: face-neighbor graph; bit labels; separation a_e
where: sections/complex.tex:128-134; bits column of Table tab:comp…
statement: Faces are adjacent if they share a pair; a_e = (1/3)#{bit positions where the two faces on e differ}.

name: Prop. complex: (1) each pair in exactly two faces, |E|=33, face graph connected; (2) six bit classes, each 11 faces covering 13 points with a growth order; (3)…
statement: Finite certificate (tables tab:complex, tab:complex-orders, degree/neighbor table eq:complex-colors).

name: discriminant sign of a symmetric form
statement: sign(Z)=chi(det of the induced nondegenerate form on V/rad Z).

name: signed half-rank layer kernel K_xi(Z) on S_D (D=2r), c_0=chi((-1)^r)
statement: K_xi(Z)=1{rank Z=r, sign Z=xi}/P(rank=r, sign=xi), a mean-one nonnegative kernel on pairs (point matrix X_i, center matrix Y_j) evaluated at X_i-Y_j.

name: Rank-layer limit (lem:rank-layer)
statement: For fixed even D>=D_0, as q->inf over odd primes, E prod_{(i,j) in B} K_{xi_ij}(X_i-Y_j) = E_eta prod_j prod_{e={i,k} subset j, both active}(1+c_0 eta_e xi_ij xi_kj)+o(1), uniformly in B and signs, eta_e independent uniform signs; same with Y_j-X_i.

name: parity form of the sign model; four-corner sets U_e
statement: E_eta prod(1+c_0 eta_e xi xi) = prod_{e: U_e subset B}(1+prod_{kappa in U_e} xi_kappa): each fully active pair tests the parity of its four incidence signs.

name: bipartite kernel density t_{I,J}(W), transpose, symmetric t(H,U)
statement: t_{I,J}(W)=E prod_{(i,j) in C} W(x_i,y_j) with independent samples; W^T swaps sides.

name: typed activation kernel W_q((a,x),(b,y)) = E_{S,xi|a,b} prod_{kappa in S} K_{xi_kappa}(x^kappa-y^kappa)
statement: Vertices carry a type (intended point/face) and one independent matrix coordinate per kappa in a coordinate set K; at each type pair an activation law picks which coordinates are used and with which signs.

name: phi_alpha, overlap moments A_ab(alpha,beta), zero-first-moment condition
