statement: phi_alpha=1{alpha subset S} prod_{kappa in alpha} xi_kappa; A_ab(alpha,beta)=E phi_alpha phi_beta; impose E phi_alpha=0 for all nonempty alpha, so disjoint nonempty pairs give zero.

name: coefficient C_A(a,b) = sum over all-nonempty pair labels alpha_e of prod over corners A_{a(i)b(j)}(alpha_e(i,j), alpha_f(i,j))
statement: Limiting nonconstant contribution at type assignment (a,b).

name: Coordinate expansion (lem:kernel-expansion)
statement: Under zero first moments, t_{I,J}(W_q)=1+sum_{a,b} prod pi prod nu C_A(a,b)+o(1); transpose analogous.

name: activation sets M_kappa=U_e cup U_f (7 coords), Gamma_kappa=U_e triangle U_f (6), and the two-branch base law with one negative corner sign sigma
statement: At corner kappa: w.p. 1/2 S=M_kappa with sign law 2^-7(1+sigma theta prod_Gamma xi), w.p. 1/2 S=Gamma_kappa with 2^-6(1-sigma theta prod_Gamma xi). First moments cancel (E phi_Gamma=0) while the overlap moment A(U_e,U_f)=sigma theta/2 survives; exactly one sigma=-1.

name: Support forcing (lem:kernel-support)
statement: At identity types the base-law coefficient has exactly one nonzero term, alpha_e=U_e, value -(theta/2)^66; proof via support identity cap_{kappa in U_g} M_kappa = U_g.

name: Pinning by vertex and pair scores (lem:pinning)
statement: If color refinement of a bipartite F is discrete within parts, there are vertex/pair scores s such that id is the unique maximizer of Q(f)=sum s_{f(u)}+sum_{edges} s_{f(u)f(v)} over all part-preserving maps (repetitions allowed). Round scores -||h_t||^2 + 2<h_t,.> give a sum-of-squares identity; lexicographic weighting L_0^{R-t}.

name: Gibbs priors pi_a ~ e^{rho s_a}, thinning lambda_ab=e^{rho(s_ab-s_max)}; choose rho large
statement: Thinning multiplies every all-nonempty term by prod lambda, so the type-sum is Z^{-1} sum C(a,b) e^{rho Q(a,b)}; identity dominates, giving t_0<0.

name: dilution by an inactive point type: t(W)=1+eps^13 t_0, t(W^T)=1+eps^22 t_1
statement: Inactive type * with probability 1-eps on the point side; the 13 vs 22 asymmetry makes the controlled negative term dominate the uncontrolled transpose term.

name: Negative symmetric kernel via crossed product V((x,y),(x',y'))=W(x,y')W(x',y)
statement: Symmetric, mean one, t(H,V)=t_{I,J}(W) t_{I,J}(W^T)<1; scale into [0,1].

name: Transfer to a finite simple host (lem:finite-host)
statement: Sampling n>(595+66 mu^66)/Delta labelled vertices gives E t(H,G_n)<=mu^66-Delta+595/n and convexity gives a realization with t(H,G)<p(G)^66.

name: Subspaces and symmetric matrices (Grassmann counts, signed rank layers, nullity tail)
statement: Gaussian binomials; P(rank k, sign xi)=(1/2+O(1/q))q^{-b(n-k)}; P(dim ker>=u)=O(q^{-b(u)}).

name: Split forms and maximal isotropic subspaces (N_r=prod(1+q^a))
statement: Nondegenerate 2r-form has an r-dim totally isotropic subspace iff det character is c_0; count of maximal isotropic subspaces.

name: Concentration of restriction signs
statement: For any family U of r-subspaces, the fraction with nonsingular restriction of sign xi is 1/2 +O(q^{-1/2}+|U|^{-1/2}) in L^1.

name: Complementary images at half rank
statement: B nonsingular, rank A=r in S_{2r}: rank(B-A)=r iff AB^{-1}A=A; then chi(det B)=c_0 xi_1 xi_2.

name: Local transverse approximation; center parametrization by maximal L-isotropic subspaces
statement: On transverse face triples, F_j=(16+O(1/q)) f_{xi1}(Q;L) -> 8 on matches (and 4 f -> 2 for two active incidences); L^1 error O(q^{-1/2}).

name: Joint determinant signs (asymptotic independence of the 33 pair signs)
statement: For D>=12 the law of (chi det(X_i-X_k))_e tends in TV to uniform on {+-1}^E; proof by Schur complement + quadratic Gauss sum rank bound.

name: Transverse limit
statement: Rank-layer identity on the event T of nonsingular point differences.

name: Lagrangian counting formulas; symplectic reduction; pair transitivity
statement: L_N=prod(q^j+1); containment probabilities; P(dim(A cap B)=h) ~ q^{-b(h)}.

name: Chart comparison: symmetric matrices as graph Lagrangians; rank defect = intersection dimension; unsigned kernel J
statement: Gamma_X={(x,Xx)} Lagrangian; dim(Gamma_X cap Gamma_Y)=D-rank(X-Y); signed weighted integrals bounded by unsigned Lagrangian ones.

name: Mass of ordered triple orbits (dimensional profile, cost C=(D+1)c+sum b(s_i)); individual orbit lower bound
statement: Every ordered symplectic orbit of a feasible profile has mass asymp q^{-C}; residual transverse orbits = congruence classes of nonsingular forms.

name: planted law nu and density ratio dnu/dmu = F_{123}
statement: Choose center Y, then three Lagrangians meeting Y in dimension r; the center integral equals nu(O)/mu(O) on each orbit.

name: lift-form parametrization, subspace cost, cyclic difference image, nullity cost
statement: Lagrangians meeting Y' in R are graphs of symmetric forms on R^circ; pair intersections = p_i + nullity of cyclic differences; image codimension b(dim V).

name: Gain exponents g (three active) and g_2(h)=b(floor(h/2)) (two active)
statement: Pointwise face factor O(q^g) with explicit maximum over finitely many parameter tuples.

name: Global profile cost via six bit-class exposure orders and a geometric mean
statement: P(profile)=O(q^{-C}) with C=(1/2)(sum_j C_j - sum_e (1-a_e) b(h_e)); each class exposed face by face along a spanning growth order, P(A)^6 <= prod_t P(A_t).

name: baseline beta_j, slack S_j, excess separation E; faces with <=2 active incidences have S_j>=h^2/24-h/12
statement: C - sum g_j = sum_j S_j + E; equality cases classified.

name: Coercivity Q >= (P^2+T^2+delta^2)/342
statement: Homogeneous quadratic part of the slack is coercive on the feasible cone.

name: Profiles not separated by the first cost: propagation through the face graph, then choose D
statement: Large pair dimension propagates to all pairs (connectivity), contradicting E<=33M via a pair with a_e>1/3; then D>M_*+44C_* forces u=c, v=0 and integer slack classification leaves c=0, h_e in {0,2}.

name: Strict span inequality sum_i k_i >= 2k (+1 if not direct)
statement: For subspaces on edges of a simple graph, local spans dominate twice the global span, strictly if not a direct sum.

name: Costs for residual profiles (nondirect O(q^{-D+1641}); direct O(q^{-(1/3)sum b(h_e)}))
statement: Counting pair spaces and containments; constant 618 = sum C(2 deg(i),2).

name: Vanishing singular contribution; proof of the rank-layer lemma
statement: For sufficiently large even D (and D>1641), the weighted contribution of configurations with some positive pair intersection is o(1).

name: Amplification and injective supersaturation (cor:amplification)
statement: (i) t(H,F)<c p(F)^66 for every c>0 via categorical powers; (ii) fixed deficit for injective copies at positive limiting density via blow-ups.

name: p-forcing; failure of the forcing conjecture (cor:forcing)
statement: Interpolate W_s=(1-s)W_0+sW_1 between the host's adjacency kernel (t(H)<p^66) and a rank-one perturbation p+delta ab (t(H)>p^66) to get a nonconstant graphon with t(K_2)=p, t(H)=p^66; sample to finite graphs with t(C_4)->limit>p^4.

name: Signed half-rank layer kernel and its limiting sign model (rank-layer limit)
statement: For D=2r large and q->inf, the nonnegative mean-one kernels K_xi(Z)=1{rank Z=r, sign Z=xi}/P(.) on symmetric D x D matrices over F_q satisfy E prod_{(i,j) in B} K_{xi_ij}(X_i - Y_j) -> E_eta prod_j prod_{e={i,k} subset j, both active}(1 + c_0 eta_e xi_ij xi_kj) with eta_e independent uniform signs; i.e. integrating out a face 'center' Y_j turns the three point-face incidences into an exact, non-perturbative product of pair-sign factors whose pair signs are the determinant characters of X_i - X_…
why: The N3 attaches to the representation change I08(+I25), not to the kernel object I07, which is N0 transfer (Huo-Wan class indicator in L). Function: a nonnegative pairwise kernel whose common-neighbour integrals reproduce, at full (non-perturbative) strength, a hypergraph-type pair-sign model with independent pair signs; this is what the hypergraph counterexamples have for free and what Lovasz's local theorem shows a graph counterexample must achieve far from the constant kernel. No neighbour f…

name: Two-branch activation law (M_kappa vs Gamma_kappa, opposite sign biases, one negative corner) with support forcing
statement: At each corner kappa, with prob 1/2 activate S=M_kappa=U_e cup U_f (7 coords) with sign bias +sigma theta on prod_Gamma xi, else S=Gamma_kappa=U_e triangle U_f (6 coords) with bias -sigma theta; all nonempty first moments vanish, the overlap moment A(U_e,U_f)=sigma theta/2 survives; support identity cap_{kappa in U_g} M_kappa = U_g leaves exactly one nonzero identity-type term, -(theta/2)^66, with exactly one sigma=-1.
why: Load-bearing and non-analytic, but its function (an odd global sign on a mod-2 closed structure, all first moments killed) is the hypergraph parity template of Conlon-Lee-Sidorenko transplanted onto C1's sign model, and mixture-with-opposite-biases is routine; support forcing is a short complex-specific check. Provisional N3 downgraded to N2. Would revert toward N3 only if P-C2 shows near-zero hit rate even with C1 given.

name: The witness H: Levi (vertex-face incidence) graph of a 13-vertex triangulated 2-sphere (35 vertices, 66 edges)
statement: 22 triples on 13 points; each of 33 pairs in exactly two faces; verified here: V-E+F=13-33+22=2 and every vertex link is a single cycle, so it is a triangulated 2-sphere (the paper never says so).
why: Levi graphs of triangle complexes are the established candidate class (K_{5,5}\C_10 = Moebius strip); the sphere triangulation is chosen to satisfy proof-generated constraints (pairs in two faces, bit classes, WL-discreteness, separation). Not reusable as a device.

name: Colour-refinement pinning with Gibbs tilting
statement: Discrete colour refinement yields vertex/pair scores making the identity the unique maximizer of a quadratic score over part-preserving maps; exponential priors e^{rho s} and thinning make the identity term dominate, so the averaged coefficient t_0<0.
why: Self-declared adaptation of WL; the sum-of-squares round score is a neat variant.

name: Singular-tail accounting: six bit-class exposure with geometric mean, separation surplus, coercivity, propagation, choice of D
statement: P(profile)=O(q^{-C}) via six spanning growth orders and P(A)^6<=prod P(A_t); slack identity C - sum g_j = sum S_j + E; large pair dimensions propagate through the face graph until the a_e>1/3 pair makes them too costly; D>1641 leaves residual integer cases killed by span counts.
why: Bespoke bookkeeping of standard fractional-cover and bootstrap patterns; large but not a new concept. It serves C1 (a proof device of the lemma, not a separate jump).

name: Typed activation kernel with one matrix coordinate per corner and zero-first-moment design
statement: Vertices carry a type and independent matrix coordinates; at each type pair an activation law picks coordinates and signs; vanishing first moments force every surviving term to have all-nonempty labels.
why: Standard graphon engineering wrapped around C1.

name: Dilution asymmetry eps^13 vs eps^22 and crossed-product symmetrization
statement: An inactive point type of mass 1-eps gives t(W)=1+eps^13 t_0 and t(W^T)=1+eps^22 t_1; the crossed product V((x,y),(x',y'))=W(x,y')W(x',y) is a symmetric kernel with t(H,V)=t(W)t(W^T)<mean^66.
why: Simple, load-bearing, standard ingredients.

name: I07+I08 (+I25): signed half-rank layer kernel K_xi on symmetric matrices over F_q and the rank-layer sign-model limit
why: Nothing like it occurs in the goal (which mentions only H and G) or in L. It is the mechanism that makes the counterexample possible: a common 'center' matrix at half rank forces complementary images (I25), so a face of three incidences becomes a multiplicative constraint on the determinant signs of the three point-pair differences, and the pair signs are asymptotically independent. In effect it simulates, inside an ordinary bipartite homomorphism density, the kind of 3-wise parity obstruction …

name: I15+I16 (+I12): two-branch activation law on M_kappa / Gamma_kappa with one negative corner sign; zero first moments; support forcing to a unique -(theta/2)^66…
why: A finite gadget, invented for this H, that cancels every nonconstant first sign moment yet keeps a signed overlap moment. Together with the support identity cap_{kappa in U_g} M_kappa = U_g it makes the identity-type coefficient a single, negative product. It is the sole source of negativity in the proof, and it is not in the goal or in L. The paper's own text has no precedent cue.

name: I03 (+I04/I05): the witness H, a 13-vertex triangulation of the 2-sphere (22 triangles) with a 3-bit face labelling whose six bit classes are spanning growth s…
why: Judged against the problem as originally posed (Sidorenko: all bipartite H), the witness is not a subterm. No prior literature proposes sphere-triangulation incidence graphs as candidates (the smallest previously open case discussed is K_{5,5} minus C_10). The paper's degree checks show it escapes every known positive criterion (not weakly norming, fails Coregliano's degree counts, minimum degree 3).

name: I17+I18: pinning by colour-refinement vertex/pair scores plus Gibbs priors and thinning
why: It turns WL-discreteness of H into a weighting under which the identity type assignment dominates all part-preserving maps, repetitions included. The sum-of-squares round score -||h(f(u))||^2+2<h(f(u)),h(u)> is a neat identity. Without it the negative identity term could be swamped.

name: I35+I36+I38: profile cost by six bit-class exposure orders with a geometric mean, the separation surplus E from a_e>1/3, and propagation of a large pair dimens…
why: This is the device that controls the singular tail, the main technical obstruction (the normalised kernels grow like a power of q). The bit labelling is designed so that every pair is internal to at most two of the six classes (a_e>=1/3), and the surplus from one strictly separated pair kills the 'common intersection' mode via propagation.

name: leave / terminal edge count F_n
statement: Run uniform triangle removal from K_n until triangle-free; the leave is the set of uncovered edges, F_n its size.
why: Design-theory term (leave of a partial triple system); process from BFL2015.

name: Main theorem: L2 convergence of F_n/n^{3/2} to 1/(2 sqrt 2)
statement: E[(F_n/n^{3/2} - 1/(2sqrt2))^2] -> 0; hence convergence in probability and of E F_n / n^{3/2}.
why: The statement (constant) was conjectured: joosKuehn2025 Conj 16.2; the theorem is new, the concept is not.

name: Fixed parameters eps=1/2000, r0=8000, L=100, B=50, H0=8001
statement: Numerical constants fixing the stopping density, link-cycle length, suffix length and suppression exponent.
why: Parameter choice.

name: Prefix trajectory p_i, stopping step i0, p, D=np^2, m=n^2p/2
statement: p_i = 1 - 1/n - 6i/n^2; i0 chosen so p = n^{-1/2+eps}+O(n^{-2}); D ~ n^{2eps} common neighbours per edge.
why: JK/BFL trajectory.

name: Rooted template (H,I), extension count X_{H,I,psi}, scaling S(H,I), same-root subtemplate, rooted density, balanced
statement: Rooted extension counts with scaling n^{v-|I|} p^{e}; balanced = every same-root subtemplate has rooted density <= that of (H,I).
why: Standard (Spencer counting extensions; JK templates).

name: Good prefix (degrees, codegrees, link-cycle counts up to length 8000, two rooted-extension upper bounds) with failure prob <= exp(-(log n)^{4/3})
statement: There is a prefix-measurable event G_n of probability 1-n^{-omega(1)} on which G_{i0} has (1+-n^{-c}) degrees and codegrees, (1+-n^{-c})D^j labelled j-cycles in every vertex link (3<=j<=8000), and polylog-factor extension upper bounds for all templates on <= 8001 vertices.
why: Cited black box in the paper (C5 invocation). Lean re-proves it by a different route (see L10-L14).

name: Triangle degree d_e and the linear triangle hypergraph T on E(G)
statement: Fix a good G; E=E(G), T=triangles as 3-subsets of E; d_e=(1+-n^{-c})D.
why: Standard.

name: Priority scan; edge "untouched before t"
statement: Independent uniform priorities U_T; scan in increasing order, accept a triangle iff all its edges remain.
why: Standard.

name: Priority representation
statement: The accepted-triangle sequence of the scan has the law of uniform sequential triangle removal from G.
why: Re-proved, standard.

name: Call (focus of one or two edges, threshold, parent); root/non-root calls; candidates; child call
statement: Root call: focus {e}, candidates all triangles at e. Non-root call: focus {f,g} subset T, threshold U_T, candidates all triangles meeting the focus except T; each candidate S has a unique focus edge e(S) and child call on S\{e(S)} at threshold U_S.
why: Close variant of the recursive random-rank oracle for greedy MIS/matching (Nguyen-Onak 2008; Yoshida-Yamamoto-Ito 2009) and of Spencer/Grable backward exploration, specialised to edge-pair foci.

name: Finite paired test with one jointly ordered candidate list and expose-all rule
statement: At a call: expose priorities of all candidates in fixed type order; scan those below threshold in priority order (one joint order across both focus edges); stop false at first true child, else true.
why: Engineering variant of the standard oracle; the paper flags joint ordering as essential.

name: Exact paired test
statement: The finite test terminates; a root call at (e,t) returns true iff e is untouched before t; a pair call returns true iff both focus edges are untouched before U_T.
why: Correctness of a greedy oracle; same induction as Nguyen-Onak style simulations.

name: Independent unfolding (fresh uniform priority at every occurrence in the tree of all possible calls); omitted-parent root variants
statement: Deterministic tree of all possible calls; an independent uniform variable per child occurrence serves as priority and threshold; distinct roots use disjoint trees.
why: Spencer's branching process realised on the graph's computation tree (cf. belief-propagation computation trees). Lean calls the resulting equations "cavity" equations.

name: Finite evaluation of unfoldings (factorial decay of decreasing paths)
statement: Almost surely every call at every threshold has a finite evaluation; P(decreasing path of length j) <= M^j/j!.
why: Penrose-Sudbury 2005 argument re-given.

name: q_e(t), q_{e,T}(t) (omitted-parent survival), I_{e,T}(t) = int_0^t q_{f,T} q_{g,T}
statement: Survival probabilities in the independent unfolding and the message integral.
why: Cavity/message quantities; Spencer f(c) analogue per edge type.

name: Product identities
statement: P(pair true at t) = q_{f,T} q_{g,T}; q_e = prod_{S ni e}(1 - I_{e,S}); q_{e,T} = prod_{S ni e, S != T}(1 - I_{e,S}); all C^1.
why: Exact cavity / belief-propagation recursion on a tree; Spencer1995 eq. for scalar case.

name: Scalar comparison q(t) = (1+2Dt)^{-1/2} (solves q' = -D q^3)
statement: Spencer's branching survival law (1+Qc)^{-1/Q} with Q=2, c=Dt.
why: Cited formula.

name: Log time s = (1/2)log(1+2Dt); z_e(s) = log(q_e/q)
statement: Change of variables making q = e^{-s}; z(0)=0.
why: Standard ODE normalization.

name: Edge-adjacency matrix A (A_ef=1 iff e!=f in a common triangle)
statement: Real symmetric matrix on E(G) with row sums 2d_e.
why: Adjacency matrix of the triangle-hypergraph 2-shadow on edges (standard construction).

name: Exact z-equation and linearized error ||z' + (A/D)z||_inf <= C(n^{-2a}+n^{-c}+log n/D) under bootstrap assumptions
statement: Differentiating the product identities; bootstrap ||z||_inf <= n^{-a}, I_{e,T} <= 1/2.
why: Routine linearization/bootstrap.

name: Link trace estimate tr((M_u/D)^r) = 1 + O(n^{-c*}) from link-cycle counts
statement: Closed walks of even length r=8000 in the vertex link: injective walks are labelled cycles; tree-supported and cycle-supported non-injective patterns are lower order.
why: Quantitative re-proof of a known method.

name: Star approximation ||M_u/D - 11^T/N_u||_2 = O(n^{-gamma})
statement: Leading eigenvalue ~1 and simple; other eigenvalues O(n^{-gamma}); eigenvector close to normalized all-ones.
why: Standard eigenvalue perturbation.

name: Star-average decomposition: P = sum_u 11^T/N_u (extended to E), R = A/D - P with ||R||_2 = O(n^{-gamma}), ||R||_inf = O(1)
statement: A is the sum of the extended link matrices M_u (two edges in a common triangle share a unique vertex); each edge lies in exactly two stars, so the l2 error does not grow with n.
why: Novel use; P = B^T N^{-1} B for the unsigned vertex-edge incidence B is classical (line-graph identity B^T B = 2I + A_line).

name: Vertex-space factorization P = UV, VU = Id + W and max-norm bound ||e^{-sP}||_inf <= 1+2s, ||e^{-sP}||_2 <= 1
statement: (Uy)_{uv} = y_u+y_v, (Vx)_u = average over star; e^{-sP} = Id - U int_0^s e^{-v(Id+W)} dv V; ||e^{-v(Id+W)}||_inf <= 1.
why: Push-through identity (UV)^j = U(VU)^{j-1}V is standard; its use to control an edge-space semigroup by a vertex random walk is the new move. Part of candidate E1.

name: Finite bounded-perturbation (Dyson) expansion with mixed norms: K terms in max norm, remainder in l2 and converted by sqrt(m)
statement: Iterate E(s) = E0(s) - int E0(s-v) R E(v) dv K times, K gamma > 2; terms are polylog in max norm; remainder <= n (Cn^{-gamma})^K (log n)^K/K! = o(1).
why: Cited expansion; mixed-norm remainder trick is standard in analysis (e.g. resolvent expansions in random-matrix local laws).

name: Uniform max-norm semigroup bound sup_{s<=log n} ||e^{-sA/D}||_inf <= C1 (1+log n)^J
statement: For every graph satisfying the degree, codegree and link-cycle conditions.
why: No neighbour found that controls a max-norm heat semigroup of a quasirandom edge-adjacency operator via star averaging; ingredients (trace method, line-graph identity, Dyson expansion) are individually known. Candidate E1.

name: Unfolded probabilities q_e, q_{e,T} = (1+o(1))q(t), I_{e,T} = O(log n / D) uniformly
statement: Bootstrap/continuity argument using I20 and I26.
why: Standard bootstrap once I26 is available.

name: Off-pattern product bound q_{f,T}q_{g,T}/(1-J_n)^2 <= 2q(t)^2
statement: Deleting at most two no-success factors from a pair call increases the product by at most (1-J_n)^{-2}.
why: Direct corollary.

name: Triangle type vs occurrence
statement: A member of T as opposed to its occurrences in an unfolding.
why: Plumbing.

name: k in {1,2} uniformly sampled oriented root edges, all roots executed at threshold 1; collision event C_k = some type exposed twice among all exposed lists
statement: Compares the finite tests (shared priorities) to independent unfoldings (disjoint trees).
why: Standard sampled-root second-moment experiment.

name: Coupling by exposed triangle types: |P(X^fin in H) - P(X^ind in H)| <= P_ind(C_k)
statement: Use U_T at the first exposure of each type and fresh variables afterwards; executions agree until a repeat.
why: First-repetition coupling, standard in local-limit arguments.

name: Formal graph Gamma of visited calls with label map lambda, formal vertices, birth calls, properties (i)-(iv)
statement: Each root adds a formal edge; each visited child glues a new vertex to its attachment edge; the only triangles of Gamma are gluing triangles.
why: Exploration-graph encodings are standard in local analyses (Spencer, Bohman triangle-free), but this gluing graph is tailored.

name: Ancestral call path; Gamma_{a,b}; extra-edge witness
statement: (a,b) distinct, nonadjacent in Gamma, labels adjacent in G, lambda injective on Gamma_{a,b}.
why: "Cycle in the explored neighbourhood" certificate; tailored form new.

name: Geometric witness for a collision: C_k produces an extra-edge witness; P(C_k) <= O(1/n) + P(witness exists)
statement: Case analysis on injectivity of lambda and on the latest vertex of a formal triangle.
why: Tree-likeness certificate; close in spirit to standard "explored ball is a tree unless a cycle is found" arguments.

name: Call forest paths, pattern (h, l1, l2, marks, focus choices), formal graph J, J^+ = J+ab; pattern count C 2^l
statement: v(J) = 2r+l, e(J) = r+2l.
why: Bookkeeping.

name: Embedding an extra edge: #emb(J^+ -> G) <= (2m)^r (2D)^l D^{-B}, via a last-L-births suffix template for long patterns
statement: Short patterns: whole J^+ is a template with all subtemplate scalings >=1, gain p. Long: template on the last L=100 born vertices with backward edges and ab has scaling D^L p < 1 and all completion scalings <= 1, so polylog many extensions; gain D^{-B} independent of path length.
why: Template counting is standard (JK, BFL); the suffix trick to get a length-independent gain is new but routine for experts.

name: Visitation weights b(t) = q(t)^2, C_D = 1+2D, mu = log(1+2D)/(2D)
statement: b is the off-pattern survival factor; mu its integral.
why: Definition.

name: Off-pattern event O_x: every off-pattern candidate at a required call below t_x has a false child, evaluated hypothetically
statement: Necessary for visiting all required calls; O_x independent across x given selected priorities.
why: New device; hypothetical evaluation of subtrees follows Lemma finite-evaluation.

name: Visiting an embedded pattern: P(all required calls visited) <= C_D^3 (2mu)^l / (h! l1! l2!)
statement: Decreasing priorities along each segment give 1/j!; each selected priority carries a factor 2b(u) from O_x; integrating gives mu^j/j!.
why: Decreasing-path 1/l! bounds are standard (Nguyen-Onak 2008; Penrose-Sudbury); weighting by off-pattern failure is the new twist.

name: Uniform collision bound P_ind(C_k) = O(D^{15-B} + n^{-1}) = o(D^{-1})
statement: Pattern count x embedding bound x root probability x visitation bound, summed: D^{-B} C_D^3 exp(24 D mu) = O(D^{15-B}).
why: Cluster I32-I40 delivers o(1/D) coupling error for adaptive paired queries with growing D; no neighbour found achieving sub-1/D local-approximation error in this setting. Candidate E2.

name: Moment identities: P(all k finite roots true | prefix) = E[(F_n/m)^k | prefix]; unfolded = ((1/m) sum_e q_e(1))^k
statement: Sampling roots with replacement turns survival probabilities into moments.
why: Standard.

name: Conditional L2: E[(Y_n-1)^2 | prefix] = o(1) uniformly on G_n; normalization a_n = mq(1)/n^{3/2} -> 1/(2sqrt2); removal of bad prefixes
statement: Y_n = F_n/(m q(1)); bad prefix contribution <= Cn P(G_n^c) = o(1).
why: Routine.

name: Scope remark: no claim for arbitrary starting graphs, general hypergraph removal, or fluctuations
statement: Scope limitation.
why: Not a mathematical item.

name: ExposureTree: a free monad of priority exposures with "fresh" (independent) and shared interpretations
statement: Inductive tree of exposure queries over keys K with values V; fresh interprets every exposure with an independent copy; product PMF gives the shared one.
why: Formalization device (free monad / decision tree); corresponds to Grable's adaptive exposure decision trees.

name: Discrete-grid priorities: priorities in Fin N, depth-bounded grid queries, grid->continuum error
statement: All probabilities are finite PMFs on Fin N; errors from ties and grid are shown to vanish as N -> infinity.
why: Formalization device.

name: Cavity operator, cavityDepth (Picard iteration) and cavityLimit in a space of bounded continuous functions
statement: cavityOperator H q e parent t = prod_{T in candidates}(1 - int_0^t prod q); cavityDepth k = k-fold iterate; Cauchy in BCF; limit = solution of the product identities.
why: Cavity method / belief propagation (statistical physics) plus Picard iteration: transfer. The Lean naming makes the import explicit.

name: Moving star average: movingStarMean/movingStarLift on a shrinking active edge set; movingResidualForcing; trajectorySeminorm; activeLinf/activeL2
statement: Time-dependent version of P = UV for a nested family of active edge sets, with seminorms along trajectories.
why: Moving (discrete-time, shrinking-support) variant of the paper's star-averaging device I23-I24.

name: movingStar_mixed_stability and moving_perturbation_mixed_norm_absorb
statement: Mixed l2/l_inf stability of x_{k+1} = x_k - a_k(P_k x_k + R_k x_k) + forcing on a nested active set.
why: Discrete-time analogue of I25-I26.

name: Self-contained prefix: centred codegree vector recurrence with star drift; edge-barrier improvement; degree/wheel/balanced-template tracking; rooted upper boun…
statement: For triangle removal from K_n up to density n^{-1/2+1/2000}: codegrees (1+-n^{-c}), degrees, link-cycle counts (via wheels as 2-balanced templates), polylog^{3*8001+2} rooted upper bounds, with failure <= exp(-(log n)^{4/3}). Proved from Freedman (re-proved) and the moving-star stability, without Joos-Kuhn.
why: Replaces the paper's only black box (JK, 87 pp.) with a triangle-specific proof in which codegree self-correction is a linear max-norm stability statement for the same star-averaged operator; no human neighbour found (BFL2015 needed triangular extensions; JK chains/branching families). Lean-only, no prose exposition; see novelty pass.

name: Freedman inequality for finite Markov histories (two-sided and maximal forms)
statement: P(sum of bounded martingale increments >= r and predictable variance <= V) <= exp(-r^2/(4(V+cr))).
why: Freedman 1975 (transfer from probability).

name: Rooted-count moment bound from intact-survival: E[X^q] <= U((2((q+1)k)+1)^k M)^q if P(F intact) <= U p^{|F|}
statement: Spencer-type extension-count moment bound transferred to the removal process.
why: Standard moment method.

name: Max-norm semigroup stability via star averaging (A/D = P + R, P = UV, VU = I + W, mixed-norm Dyson expansion)
why: Named by the paper as one of the two new continuation estimates (introduction.tex:130-133). The naive bound loses e^{O(D)} (stability.tex:100-103); this device is what makes the D -> infinity regime work. Not a subterm of the goal or of L; the decisive object P = sum of star averages appears nowhere in BFL/JK/Spencer. Reused in Lean (moving-star version) to give a self-contained prefix proof replacing JK: evidence of payoff beyond its own theorem.

name: o(1/D) collision bound: extra-edge witness + suffix-template D^{-B} gain + off-pattern-weighted visitation (2mu)^l/l!
why: Paper flags the sub-1/D precision as new and necessary for the second moment (introduction.tex:116-118; witnesses.tex:4-7). Lean canonical_collision_sum dominated share 0.317 (passes 20% proxy). Weighting each step of a visited path by the off-pattern failure factor b(t)=q(t)^2 converts D^l path counts into poly(D) total, a non-obvious quantitative move.

name: Lean-only self-contained prefix via moving-star codegree stability
why: Removes the paper's only black box (JK, 87 pp.) with ~7k lines of a triangle-specific proof; dominated share 0.269. BFL2015 needed carefully designed triangular extensions to pass the n^{7/4} barrier; the Lean route controls the whole codegree vector by a linear max-norm stability statement plus link spectral control from wheel counts.

name: Paired-focus finite test with one jointly ordered list and expose-all rule
why: Paper says joint ordering is "essential to the later visitation estimate"; full exposure makes collisions detectable.

name: Independent unfolding and exact product (cavity) identities
why: Load-bearing: all continuation probabilities live here.

name: Max-norm semigroup stability via star averaging
statement: If G has (1+-n^{-c}) degrees and codegrees and (1+-n^{-c})D^j labelled j-cycles in every link (j <= 8000), then sup_{0<=s<=log n} ||exp(-sA/D)||_inf <= C(1+log n)^J, where A is the edge-adjacency matrix of the triangle hypergraph. Mechanism: each link matrix is l2-close to its averaging projection; the sum P of star averages factors as UV with VU = I + W (W = neighbour random walk), so ||e^{-sP}||_inf <= 1+2s; the l2-small remainder R is handled by a K-term Dyson expansion whose remainder is co…
why: No near-equivalent found anywhere; non-analytic; knockout-essential and reused (Lean prefix) beyond its own proposition. Confidence is low because each step is one move from a classical tool; Test 4 may well show it is discoverable once l_inf stability is identified as the bottleneck.

name: o(1/D) collision bound for adaptive paired queries (extra-edge witness + suffix template + off-pattern-weighted visitation)
statement: P_ind(some triangle type exposed twice) = O(D^{15-B} + 1/n) = o(1/D): a repeat yields two visited ancestral call paths plus an extra G-edge; embeddings of such path unions are <= (2m)^r (2D)^l D^{-B}; visiting a prescribed embedded pattern has probability <= C_D^3 (2mu)^l/(h! l1! l2!) with mu = log(1+2D)/(2D).
why: Load-bearing and non-analytic, but each component has a close precedent (Nguyen-Onak/Penrose-Sudbury decreasing paths, Spencer/local-limit tree-likeness, JK extension bounds). The new content is quantitative (off-pattern weights, length-independent D^{-B}), which the codebook grades as a variant. Upgrade to N3 only if Test 4 shows models fail to reach sub-1/D precision.

name: Lean-only self-contained prefix via moving-star codegree stability
statement: For triangle removal from K_n up to density n^{-1/2+1/2000}, with probability >= 1 - exp(-(log n)^{4/3}): codegrees, degrees and link-cycle counts are (1 +- n^{-1/80000})-accurate and rooted extension counts are at most polylog^{3*8001+2} times scaling. The centred codegree vector x_k obeys x_{k+1} = x_k - a_k (P_k x_k + R_k x_k) + martingale forcing (moving star average P_k, link-spectral remainder R_k), and its max norm is kept below a barrier by mixed-norm stability; Freedman controls the fo…
why: As an item it is a variant of C1 inside the same family (templated reuse). Its real significance is as evidence for C1: the same device yields, within this release, a new proof of a BFL/JK-type prefix theorem for triangles that humans needed 40-90 pages and different machinery for. That is the downstream-speedup signature PLAN step 9 asks for, but it is produced by the same model on the same problem, so it is not a held-out test. Lean-only and without prose; the reconstruction is from signature…

name: Paired-focus recursive test with a single jointly ordered candidate list and expose-all rule
statement: Edge e survives to threshold t iff no triangle S at e with U_S < t has both other edges surviving to U_S; for a pair focus the two edges' candidates are scanned in one priority order and all candidate priorities are exposed.
why: Standard oracle with an engineering refinement (joint ordering, expose-all) that the paper needs for C2.

name: Independent unfolding with exact product (cavity) identities
statement: Give every occurrence in the tree of possible calls a fresh priority; then q_e = prod_{S ni e}(1 - int_0^t q_{f,S} q_{g,S}).
why: Transfer: Spencer's branching process, made exact per edge type (cavity equations).

name: Two-random-root moment experiment and first-repetition coupling
statement: P(k sampled roots survive | prefix) = E[(F_n/m)^k | prefix]; finite vs independent answers differ by at most P(repeat).
why: Standard.

name: Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity e(A), e(H,A)
statement: e(A)=lim d! l(A/a^N)/N^d; e(H,A) for an ideal of definition H.

name: reduction / minimal reduction of an ideal
statement: Q subset I with I^{n+1}=QI^n for n>>0; minimal if inclusion-minimal; e(Q,A)=e(I,A).

name: short complex
statement: finite free complex in degrees 0..d with finite-length homology and H_0 != 0.

name: Dutta multiplicity chi_infty(F)
statement: lim_n p^{-nd} sum (-1)^i l H_i(Phi^n F), Phi^n = Frobenius scalar extension.

name: additive length lambda on T_I with zero-stability and parameter hypotheses
statement: lambda: I-power-torsion C-modules -> [0,inf], additive, lambda(0)=0, direct sums and filtered colimits of length-zero modules killed by a common I^a have length 0; mu=lambda(C/I) in (0,inf); lambda(C/(z^a))=a^h mu; lambda H_i(z^a;C)=0 for i>0. C need not be Noetherian.

name: isomorphism modulo length zero (Serre quotient)
statement: map with length-zero kernel and cokernel; length-zero objects form a Serre subcategory.

name: filtered-complex nilpotence observation
statement: a filtration-preserving map that is zero on E_1 lowers homology filtration; a composite of (#steps) such maps is zero on homology (mod length zero).

name: Uniform complex estimate (Thm 2.1, thm:complex)
statement: Under I05, a finite free complex F in degrees 0..h, contractible off V(I), with alternating rank 0 and all differential entries in I^s satisfies lambda H_i(F)=0 (i>0) and lambda H_0(F) >= mu s^h (b_0 - (A_h/s) sum b_i), with A_h depending only on h (uniform in C, I, lambda, F).

name: Koszul acyclicity modulo length zero (lem:acyclicity)
statement: contractible off V(I) => H_i(F) killed by a fixed I-power, finite length, lambda H_i=0 for i>0 (via F (x) K_a ~ sum_T F[|T|]).

name: blowup Y=Proj(sum I^n), L=IO_Y=O_Y(1), exceptional divisor E, closed immersion Y->P^{h-1}_C
statement: Rees-algebra Proj; L invertible even for non-Noetherian C; E=Proj(gr_I C) -> P^{h-1}_{C/I}.

name: graded comparison on the exceptional divisor (lem:complex-graded-comparison)
statement: (C/I)[Z] -> gr_I C has length-zero kernel in each degree; H^v(P^{h-1}_{C/I},V(t)) -> H^v(E,V(t)) iso mod length zero; gr^t_I C ~ H^0(E,O(t)); lambda(C/I^M)=mu binom(M+h-1,h).

name: chi_lambda (hyperhomology Euler characteristic on Y)
statement: chi_lambda(D)=sum (-1)^k lambda H_k(Y,D) via finite Cech cover.

name: twisted complex G with G_i = L^{-is} (x) F_i = O_Y(-is)^{b_i}
statement: on the blowup, divide the i-th differential by z_j^s (entries in L^s); F_Y subset G with quotient layers O_E(l)^{b_i}, l=-is..-1.

name: twist maps vanish on hyperhomology (lem:complex-twist-maps)
statement: for D=F_Y(x)V or G(x)V: D(j+M)->D(j) is 0 on H for M>=M_D; hyperhomology I-power torsion of finite length.

name: Euler comparison chi_lambda(F_Y)=lambda H_0(F) and chi(F_Y (x) V)=rank(V) chi(F_Y) (lem:complex-euler-comparison)
statement: compare eventual images of the Koszul tower F/J_aF, the ordinary-power tower F/I^MF and the geometric tower RGamma(F_Y/L^M) modulo length zero; twist invariance from alternating rank 0; vector-bundle rank formula via a resolution by twists.

name: bundle with prescribed cohomological roots (supernatural bundle) over Z (lem:complex-root-bundle)
statement: for integers r_1>...>r_{h-1}, V=f_*O(-1-r_1,...,-1-r_n) for f:(P^1)^n -> P^n (multiplication of binary forms), rank (h-1)!; V(a) has cohomology in the single degree #{j: r_j>a}, Euler char prod(a-r_j), any base ring.

name: root positions r_j = round(s*rho_j), rho_j = roots of H'(x), H(x)=prod_{i=1}^h (x+i)
statement: Rolle: -(j+1)<rho_j<-j; for large s choose integers r_j with -(j+1)s<r_j<-js and |r_j - s rho_j|<=1. Interlacing forces cohomology of layers into the right degrees; the limiting positions make every layer sum s^{-h} sum_{l=-is}^{-1} prod(l-r_j) -> (H(0)-H(-i))/h = (h-1)! for all i=1..h.

name: positivity chi_lambda(G (x) V) = lambda H_0 >= 0
statement: with the root positions, E-layers of twists of D=G(x)V have cohomology forcing H_k(Y,D) to have length 0 for k != 0, so chi(D) = lambda H_0(Y,D) >= 0.

name: sum estimate and Riemann-sum error
statement: 0 <= (h-1)! lambda H_0(F) + mu sum_i (-1)^i b_i sum_{l=-is}^{-1} prod_j (l-r_j); layer sums = (h-1)! s^h + O(s^{h-1}); alternating rank identity gives the bound.

name: Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity e_HK(H,D)
statement: lim l(D/H^[q])/q^dim D (Monsky).

name: length inputs (thm:length-inputs)
statement: complete local domain D, perfect residue field: there are C and lambda with the stability axioms, lambda(C/(z^a))=a^h e((z),D), positive Koszul homology length 0, and lambda(C/HC)=e_HK(H,D) (char p) or <= e(H,D) (mixed char).

name: Faltings normalized length lambda_infty on Lambda-modules
statement: lambda_infty(M_n (x) Lambda)=p^{-nh} l_{A_n}(M_n) for finitely presented, inf over surjections for f.g., sup over f.g. submodules in general.

name: normalized length limits (lem:normalized-limit)
statement: zero-length stability under sums/colimits; sup over increasing unions; colimit with lengths -> 0 has length 0.

name: finite stages B_q = A' (x)_{A^{1/q}} D^{1/q} exhausting C = D_perf
statement: Cohen-Gabber normalization A=k[[t]] subset D generically separable; B_q injects into C via linear disjointness.

name: perfection conductor g^{1/q} C subset B_q (lem:perfection-conductor)
statement: trace-dual basis argument.

name: lambda_infty(C/HC)=e_HK(H,D); Koszul vanishing; e_HK((z))=e((z))
statement: stagewise q^{-h} l(D/H^[q]) up to O(1/q) error; Roberts' Frobenius homology theorem gives Koszul vanishing in the limit; Koszul Euler char = e.

name: finite-length module comparison lambda_infty(C (x) M)=lim q^{-h} l(Phi^n M) (lem:perfection-finite-length)
statement: same conductor argument for non-cyclic finite-length M.

name: mixed-char length algebra C=(D (x)_A A_infty)_perfd and its normalized length
statement: Bhatt-Scholze perfectoidization; CLMST Cor 4.0.4 (Koszul homology almost zero), Prop 4.0.10 (almost isos same length), Def 4.0.8/Cor 4.0.18 (e_perfd(H) <= e(H), equality for parameter ideals).

name: residue-field extension preserving e (lem:residue-extension)
statement: complete B -> B' flat, mB'=m_{B'}, residue field algebraic closure, e(B')=e(B); mixed case via unramified DVR tower V->V'.

name: flat-local reductions (lem:reduction)
statement: reduce to complete, R domain, dim R = dim S > 0, residue field of S algebraically closed (Nagata localization, prime filtration additivity).

name: perfect ideal
statement: pd_T(T/J)=grade J.

name: factorization R -> T -> S=T/J with perfect kernel and the complex F = P (x) K(x;T) (prop:setup)
statement: T=R(x)_A U from Cohen factorization of A->S (AFH); e(T)=e(R); J perfect of grade b; F has length h, F_0=T, contractible off t, entries in t, alternating rank 0; generic local rings complete intersections (regular in mixed char), each minimal prime over J on a unique component in mixed char.

name: Ma's Hilbert-Kunz identity e_HK(J+(x),T)=e((x),S) (lem:ma-hk)
statement: for perfect J with complete-intersection T_Q at minimal primes.

name: Lech in characteristic p (thm:positive-characteristic)
statement: apply I08 to F^(q) (x) D_perf on each component D=T/P with s=q-c; get e_HK(HD,D) >= e(D); HK associativity gives e_HK(H,T) >= e(T)=e(R); I33 gives e(S) >= e(R).

name: Dutta multiplicity >= e(R) for short complexes over complete char-p local domains (cor:dutta-domain) = IMW Conjecture 8.1 for complete char-p domains
statement: alg. closed residue field: apply I08 to C (x) Phi^n F with C=R_perf, s=q-c; general residue field: base change + prime filtration + Hochster-Huneke/BHM Frobenius homology growth for small components.

name: multiplicity can only increase when cutting by a dimension-lowering element of H (lem:mixed-quotient)
statement: f in H, dim A/(f)=t-1 => e(H,A) <= e(H,A/(f)).

name: asymptotic upper bound for e(L+(x^N),B) (lem:mixed-asymptotic)
statement: dim B/L<d => O(N^{d-1}); L=q prime with B_q regular => <= N^d e((x),B/q) + O(N^{d-1}); via prime avoidance chosen to generate qB_q.

name: deep finite extensions via roots of parameters and Heitmann's integral-extension Briancon-Skoda
statement: z_i = u_i^{1/q}; Heitmann/HeitmannMa Prop 2.8 puts b D inside (z)^{q-h} D for a finite normal domain D; rank r cancels: q^h e((z),D)=r e(B).

name: power rule lambda(C/(J,x^N)C)=N^d lambda(C/(J,x)C) via mapping cones
statement: Euler characteristic linear in each exponent using I09 for all cones.

name: prime-filtration upper bound and two-limit argument (N then q)
statement: lambda(C/(J,x^N)C)/r <= sum_j e(H_{j,N},B); N->inf gives a bound independent of D,C,lambda; combine with I08 lower bound, then q->inf; sum over components with coefficient 1 (generic regularity).

name: Lech in mixed characteristic (thm:mixed-characteristic)
statement: e(S) >= e(T) = e(R) when R has mixed characteristic.

name: finite free reduction with common coefficient field (lem:charzero-finite-free)
statement: R -> R'=L[[X]]/I L[[X]] -> S finite free, e(R')=e(R).

name: polynomial certificate of a strict counterexample (lem:charzero-certificate)
statement: finite system over Z[t] encoding algebra structures, freeness, locality, e(R)>=r via vanishing (u-r+1)-minors + reduction relation, e(S)<=e(S_0) via monic initial relations of gr S_0.

name: Artin approximation + specialization to an algebraically closed field of char p (lem:charzero-specialization)
Lech in residue characteristic zero (thm:charzero)
statement: contradiction with I34 via I42-I44.

name: Main theorem assembly (sec:assembly)
statement: reductions + three characteristic cases.

name: SeparableOrder: subring of D separable over Frac(A) used instead of Cohen-Gabber
statement: order A D K L = {x in D : x separable over K}; every x^{p^e} lies in it (purely inseparable exponent), so Frobenius-normalized limits can be computed over a generically separable order.

name: dutta_complete_charp: Dutta bound for ALL complete Noetherian local rings of char p (no domain hypothesis)
statement: IMW Conjecture 8.1 in characteristic p for every complete local ring, via prime filtration (cyclicDutta) exactly as in the paper's residue-extension step.

name: Roberts' Frobenius homology theorem (positive homology of Phi^n F is o(p^{nd}))
statement: proved via a conductor bound on finite separable stages rather than cited.
cited_or_new: cited in paper, re-proved in Lean

name: Uniform complex estimate (Thm 2.1): lambda H_0(F) >= mu s^h (b_0 - A_h sum b_i / s) via blowup twist + supernatural-bundle pairing
statement: C any commutative ring (not necessarily Noetherian), I=(z_1..z_h), lambda an additive length on I-power-torsion modules with zero-stability (direct sums/filtered colimits of length-zero modules killed by a common power of I), lambda(C/(z^a)) = a^h mu, positive Koszul homology of z^a of length 0. F finite free in degrees 0..h, contractible off V(I), alternating rank 0, differential entries in I^s. Then lambda H_0(F) >= mu s^h (b_0 - A_h sum_i b_i / s), A_h depending only on h. Proof: pass to the…
why: No equivalent statement exists anywhere found (its char-p consequence was an open conjecture, IMW2022 Conj 8.1, and Ma 2017 names it as the missing step). It is non-analytic as a mechanism, load-bearing for every leg (76.6% closure, ~85% of the core), and Lean-backed on the comparator chain. Confidence is low because every component is precedented: the bundle and positivity are Eisenbud-Schreyer (N0 transfer; I16 re-proved over Z), dividing by the exceptional divisor is a standard blowup move (…

name: Root tuning: r_j = round(s * rho_j), rho_j the critical points of H(x) = prod_{i=1}^h (x+i)
statement: Choose bundle roots so that each layer sum sum_{l=-is}^{-1} prod_j (l - r_j) ~ s^h int_{-i}^0 H'/h = (h-1)! s^h for every i = 1..h, with interlacing -(j+1)s < r_j < -js from Rolle.
why: Forced by the target identity once C3 and the ES pairing are in place; interlacing is the standard ES constraint. Expected high discovery rate (positive-control-like).

name: Blowup twist G_i = O_Y(-is)^{b_i} and local pairing positivity chi_lambda(G (x) V) >= 0 modulo length zero
statement: If F has entries in I^s, dividing the k-th differential by L^s on Y = Bl_I gives a complex G of type (0,s,..,hs); pairing with a supernatural bundle whose roots interlace gives hyperhomology concentrated in degree 0 modulo length zero, hence chi >= 0.
why: Each half is a standard move (blowup division; ES positivity). Their composition is the content of C1 and is graded there.

name: Non-Noetherian Euler comparison chi_lambda(F_Y) = lambda H_0(F) via stabilized images of truncation towers
statement: For F contractible off V(I), the hyperhomology Euler characteristic of the pullback to the blowup equals the alternating sum of lambda H_i(F), modulo length zero, with no Noetherian hypothesis.
why: Technical variant of a standard comparison.

name: Abstract stable additive length interface (TorsionLength + zero-stability + parameter hypotheses)
statement: Axiomatize an additive length on I-power-torsion modules with zero-stability and Koszul/parameter scaling so that one theorem covers module length, Faltings normalized length on D_perf, and CLMST perfectoid length.
why: Packaging of known properties of normalized length (analyst had N2; downgraded: no new idea, conjunction of L concepts).

name: Mixed-characteristic scheme: Heitmann depth in finite extensions of rank r, rank cancellation, prime-filtration upper bound, N-limit before q-limit
statement: Replace Frobenius by roots of parameters and Heitmann's integral-extension Briancon-Skoda (via HeitmannMa Prop 2.8) to make entries deep; normalize CLMST lengths by the extension rank; upper bound by a prime filtration with x^N, N -> infinity first.
why: Every move is standard mixed-char practice.

name: Char-0 one-sided polynomial certificate (minors + reduction relation for e(R) >= r; monic initial relations for e(S) <= e(S_0)) + Artin approximation
statement: Encode a strict counterexample by finitely many polynomial identities preserving only one-sided multiplicity bounds, then specialize to char p.
why: Named precedent (Ma Sec 5).

name: Lean route: SeparableOrder in place of Cohen-Gabber; Roberts' theorem re-proved via conductor bound
statement: Build the char-p normalized length over the subring of D separable over K; re-prove Roberts' Frobenius homology bound.
why: Standard workaround and a re-proof of a cited theorem.

name: I08: uniform complex estimate lambda H_0(F) >= mu s^h (b_0 - A_h sum b_i / s)

name: Incidence criterion
statement: Let ell be an odd prime, K a finite field of characteristic 2 containing a primitive ell-th root of unity, kappa = ell^2. Given an (ell+1)-regular finite set system (V,F) of incidence girth >= 12 and x_v in K^m with sum_V x_v x_v^T = -I_m, sum_{v in f} x_v x_v^T = 0 for every f, and 0 < m < |V| <= m*kappa, there are a finitely presented G with ell-torsion and a,b in K[G] with ab = 1 != ba.
why: The only item in the family with no neighbour found in any field and no retrieval trigger in the trace. Its content is a finite certificate that beats the sofic rank bound (t < m*kappa) by exploiting D = ell+1 = 0 in K. That is exactly why it cannot exist in characteristic 0 and why it forces nonsoficity. Against: every component is standard (averaging idempotents, glued finite groups, HNN character twists, augmentation specialization, DJ transfer). It emerged incrementally from the model's own…

name: Glued subgroup averages give a rectangular one-sided identity
statement: With P_v the averaging idempotent of K_v = F_ell^2 and the partition of K_v \ {1} by its ell+1 lines L_f: sum_{u in K_v} u = 1 + sum_{f ni v}(L^_f - 1). Hence U_{-,v} = -kappa x_v P_v and T_{v,-} = P_v x_v^T satisfy UT = I_m once the local Gram sums vanish and the total is -I_m.
why: Standard averaging device. The new use (subgroup averages weighted by rank-one Gram matrices) is the mechanism of C1 and is graded there.

name: Punctured polynomial pairing
statement: For q = 2^h, holes O in the lower set S_{(q-2)/2} of F_q^n, and x_v = (f_o(v))_{o in O} with f_o the degree-<=(q-2)/2 interpolant of the indicator of o on S: sum_{v in line} x_v x_v^T = 0 for every full affine line, and sum_{v notin O} x_v x_v^T = -I_m.
why: A retrieval-triggered transfer from coding theory, built on a classical line-sum fact. The punctured-hole trick is a new arrangement, not a new concept. It is graded N2 because the paper's named precedents (GL, DLZ) supply the decisive features (products and line restrictions).

statement: For large h there are holes O in S with 2N/D^2 <= |O| <= 7N/D^2 and a family of full affine lines avoiding O, D-regular on V = A \ O, with incidence girth >= 12.
why: Heavy but technique-standard (random slabs, LLL, trades, Linnik). It dominates proof length, not novelty, so it is a budget sink rather than a cut.

statement: Twist via HNN letters tau_v so that conjugates of eP_v become orthogonal character idempotents eQ_{alpha_v}. Pack t coordinates into m slots (t <= m*kappa), and detect b_mat*a_mat != 1 via J_0 Delta C = e(TU - P), which specializes to X^T X - I_t != 0 because rank X <= m < t.

name: Planar balance (Euler) embedding of the local groups
statement: If the incidence graph has girth >= 12, each F_ell^2 embeds in the glued group N. A minimal balanced planar diagram yields black degree >= 3, white degree >= 2 and faces of length >= 12, contradicting Euler's formula.
why: Standard small-cancellation counting, replacing an imported theorem (Haefliger). Insight-driven in the trace, but the origin is constructed from known counting, and the simplification ratio is about 1:1.

With m = 1 mod 4 the label counts balance exactly and all intersections are odd except S_{x_A} cap S_{x_A}.
