name: Group labels and traces (lem:labels)
statement: A monomial with nonidentity label has trace 0. A monomial with identity label is a polynomial in the S_g.
why: The grading of the crossed product, plus the vanishing of the conditional expectation onto the group-algebra-free part.

name: free sum s(k)=sum_g k(g) S_g
statement: A real-linear, F_n-equivariant map from finitely supported real functions on F_n to self-adjoint elements of M, with A_g s(k) A_g^* = s(lambda(g)k).
why: The analog of the free Gaussian functor field X(xi), realized by the free Bernoulli field S_g instead of semicirculars. It repackages known concepts.

name: Norm of a free sum (lem:free-sum), K=3*pi
statement: ||s(k)|| <= 3 pi ||k||_2. More generally, ||sum z_j|| <= 2 (sum ||z_j||_2^2)^{1/2} + max ||z_j|| for free, centered, self-adjoint z_j.
why: The Ricard-Xu / Voiculescu free Khintchine inequality (Haagerup-type), applied to the scalar self-adjoint case.

name: coefficient cocycle D (Fox derivative form)
statement: Given real finitely supported h_j, the unique cocycle D: F_n -> R^(F_n) with D_{x_j}=h_j and D_{gb}=D_g+lambda(g)D_b.
why: A 1-cocycle into the left regular representation, i.e. the Fox derivative. Named by the paper.

name: formal algebra P, evaluation ev_0, derivation delta (delta z=0, delta a_j = i sigma(h_j) a_j)
statement: On the universal *-algebra of n unitaries and one self-adjoint z, the *-derivation driven by the conjugated-log fields sigma(h_j).
why: A close variant of Voiculescu's cyclomorphy setting: trace-preserving derivations on algebraically free generators. The specific field is the free analog of the Gaussian cocycle deformation derivation (Peterson; Sinclair).

name: word derivative = cocycle value: delta a_g = i sigma(D_g) a_g, delta z_g = i[sigma(D_g), z_g]
statement: Because a_g sigma(k) a_g^* = sigma(lambda(g)k), the derivation acts on every group word through the cocycle value D_g.
why: The noncommutative analog of alpha_t(u_g)=omega(t b(g)) u_g for Gaussian cocycle deformations (Sinclair 2011; Peterson-Sinclair 2012), which the paper does not cite.

name: Universal initial trace identity (lem:flow-trace-identity)
statement: tau(ev_0(delta^r p))=0 for all p in P and r>=1. Proved by label preservation, plus a first-variation argument: conjugating S_g by exp(iuY_g), with Y_g in W*(S_b : b != g), preserves the joint law by freeness.
cited_or_new: new proof of a cyclomorphy-type criterion
why: Its content (tau composed with delta is 0, so the flow is trace preserving) is the cyclomorphy criterion. The first-variation-by-free-conjugation proof is a neat variant.

name: conjugation by a unitary of B preserves freeness from B
statement: If A is free from B and U is a unitary in B, then UAU^* is free from B, and the joint law with B is unchanged.
why: Folklore.

name: polynomial vector field V_j(X)=i H_j(X) X_j, H_j(X)=sum_g h_j(g) X_g S X_g^*
statement: The ODE dA_j/dt = i s_t(h_j) A_j, where s_t uses the time-t conjugates of the fixed S.
why: With h_j=delta_e it reduces to Popa's free malleable deformation A_j -> C^t A_j. For general h_j it is a time-ordered (free) version of the Gaussian cocycle deformation. Close neighbours exist.

name: Global solvability in a generated subalgebra (lem:flow-global-ode)
statement: The polynomial ODE has a unique global smooth solution in any C*-subalgebra E containing S, and the solution stays unitary.
why: Picard-Lindelof in Banach spaces.

name: Moment invariance (lem:flow-moments)
statement: tau(ev_t(p)) = tau(ev_0(p)) for all t, by a uniform factorial bound on iterated derivatives, real analyticity, and I16.
why: Standard analytic-continuation step in cyclomorphy-type exponentiation.

name: operator norm from moments
statement: ||b|| = lim tau((b^*b)^k)^{1/2k} in a faithful tracial vN algebra. So moment preservation gives an isometry.
why: Folklore.

name: Polynomial flow and displacement bounds (prop:flow)
statement: There is a one-parameter group beta_t of trace-preserving normal automorphisms of M fixing S, with ||beta_t(A_j)-A_j|| <= |t| K ||h_j||_2 and ||beta_t(A_w) - e^{itS} A_w|| <= |t| K ||D_w - delta_e||_2.
why: The leaning is N3. Its parts have close precedents: cyclomorphy (named), Popa's free malleable deformation and Sinclair / Peterson-Sinclair Gaussian cocycle deformations (not named). What appears new is the word-displacement bound in operator norm, inside M itself, with no ambient dilation.

name: Small coefficients with a prescribed word value (lem:small-cocycle)
statement: For n>=3 and eta>0 there are a word w and a finitely supported real h with h_1=h, h_j=0 for j>=2, ||h||_2<eta and ||D_w - delta_e||_2 < eta.
why: Weak N3. Posing the problem (generator values small in ell^2 while one word value approximates delta_e) is non-analytic and seems new. Once posed, the solution is textbook free probability: circular law and spectral cutoff. So the pivot is one step from L, and a judge may grade it N2.

name: free prefix words a=x_1, b_j=x_2^j x_3 x_2^{-j}, p_j=(a b_1)...(a b_j), w_m=p_m a, T_m=1+sum lambda(p_j)
statement: A word whose Fox derivative in x_1 is a sum of m+1 group elements that are free, apart from the identity term.
why: Routine engineering of free subgroups and Nielsen moves. The trick that D vanishes on the b_j (h_j=0 for j>=2) is small.

name: Free prefixes and the cocycle value (lem:cocycle-prefixes)
statement: p_1..p_m freely generate a free subgroup, and D_{w_m} = T_m h.
why: Nielsen transformations plus the Fox chain rule.

name: Q_m = T_m T_m^*, mu_m = spectral law of Q_m/m
statement: Spectral measure of the normalized prefix-sum operator.
why: Abbreviation.

name: Spectral limit of the prefix sums (lem:cocycle-spectrum)
statement: mu_m converges weakly to the free Poisson (Marchenko-Pastur, rate 1) law, which has no atom at 0.
why: Free central limit theorem: (1/sqrt m) times a sum of free Haar unitaries tends to a circular element c, and cc^* is free Poisson.

name: spectral cutoff inverse E_m, R_m=f_m(Q_m), h^(0)=T_m^* R_m delta_e
statement: A truncated pseudo-inverse gives ||h^(0)||^2 = tau(R_m) <= 1/(dm) and ||T_m h^(0) - delta_e||^2 = mu_m([0,d]).
why: Spectral-cutoff (regularized) least-squares inverse.

name: reality of h^(0) and finite truncation
statement: Complex conjugation J commutes with real functions of Q_m, so h^(0) is real. Approximate it by a finitely supported real h.
why: Routine.

name: completion of A
statement: C is a completion of A=(A_1..A_n) if (A,C) is a freely generating Haar tuple.
why: A renaming.

name: Approximating the extra generator in one step (prop:perturbation)
statement: For every eps>0 there are a trace-preserving automorphism alpha and a word w with ||alpha(A_j)-A_j||<eps and ||alpha(A)_w - C||<eps. The new completion is C' = C A_w^*. The proof sets alpha = gamma^{-1} o beta_1, where gamma is the Nielsen automorphism C -> C A_w.
why: It looks non-analytic and new: a norm-small automorphism of L(F_{n+1}) that makes a long word in the first n generators approximate the (n+1)-st. It turns the known non-uniformity of free/cocycle deformations on long words, usually used for rigidity, into a constructive absorption device. The risk is the unverified shlyakhtenko2026 precedent.

name: Nielsen automorphism gamma: A_j -> A_j, C -> C A_w
statement: The basis change c -> cw of F_{n+1} induces a trace-preserving automorphism, via I05.
why: Aut(F_{n+1}) acts on L(F_{n+1}).

name: tuple distance d_2 and word-polynomial Lipschitz constant L(F)
statement: ||F(U)-F(V)||_2 <= L(F) d_2(U,V), by telescoping.
why: Abbreviation of a telescoping bound.

name: adaptive error-budget iteration (F_{j,k}, eps_k, alpha_k, w_k, G_{j,k}, L_k, r_k; dense sequence y_j)
statement: At each stage, approximate y_1..y_k in the current tuple, choose eps_k, perturb, substitute the witness word, and only then fix the future budget r_k.
cited_or_new: new instance of a standard scheme
why: A standard diagonal Cauchy-limit construction with tracked budgets. The paper describes shlyakhtenko2026 as using 'a limiting generation argument', so the template has a named precedent.

name: the limit tuple is free Haar and generates M
statement: Norm convergence preserves the word traces. L^2-density of the word algebra plus the conditional expectation give W*(A^(inf))=M.
why: Routine.

name: Isomorphism of consecutive ranks (thm:rank-step)
statement: L(F_n) is isomorphic to L(F_{n+1}) for n>=3.
why: Results are not graded as machinery.

name: only the first n generators need to converge
statement: The completions C^(k) may fail to converge; the targets are approximated in L^2.
why: Commentary.

name: amplification Q^t and induced map Theta^t
statement: The normalized corner p(Q (x) B(l^2))p with trace t. Tracial isomorphisms amplify.
why: Murray-von Neumann.

name: L(F_2) is isomorphic to L(F_3) (thm:main)
statement: Compose N_3=N_4=N_5 and amplify by sqrt 2. Dykema gives N_3^{sqrt2}=N_2 and N_5^{sqrt2}=N_3.
why: Checked arithmetic: 1+(3-1)/2=2 and 1+(5-1)/2=3.

name: fundamental group F(Q)
statement: F(Q) = {t>0 : Q^t is isomorphic to Q}.
why: Murray-von Neumann.

name: all interpolated free group factors are isomorphic; fundamental group R_{>0} (cor:all-interpolated)
statement: Combine Thm main with Radulescu's dichotomy (including infinity) and the amplification formula.
why: C5 transfer.

name: free entropy dimensions depend on W*-generators (cor:entropy-dimensions)
statement: Transport semicircular tuples (for delta, delta_0) and group tuples (for delta^*, delta^star) from L(F_n) into L(F_2). Then each of the four dimensions takes every value n>=2.
why: Transport by distribution-preserving isomorphisms. N1-level argument.

name: transported tuples X^(n)=theta_n(S^(n)), Y^(n)=theta_n(G^(n)); G^(n)=(Re u_j, Im u_j)
statement: Self-adjoint generating tuples with prescribed entropy dimensions.
why: Standard tuples.

name: One-step absorption of a free generator
statement: For a freely generating Haar (n+1)-tuple (A,C), n>=3, and every eps>0, there are a trace-preserving automorphism alpha and a word w in F_n with max_j ||alpha(A_j)-A_j|| < eps and ||alpha(A)_w - C|| < eps.
why: Its form is precedented in L by a model-assisted preprint and in ergodic theory, and it is close to analytic in the goal. Its non-trivial content is inherited from I22+I23. The provisional N3 in paper.json is withdrawn.

name: Small cocycle with a prescribed word value
statement: For n>=3 and eta>0 there are a word w in F_n and a finitely supported real h with ||h||_2 < eta such that the Fox cocycle D with D_{x_1}=h, D_{x_j}=0 (j>=2) satisfies ||D_w - delta_e||_2 < eta.
why: The only item with no neighbour found and no retrieval trigger in the trace. It is where non-amenability enters: it fails for Z (Dirichlet kernel) and for property (T) groups. The eureka content lies in posing the problem: small generator values, a word value near delta_e, coupled to absorption. Solving it is textbook once posed, and Lean found a second elementary proof. If Test 4 is decided at pivot level (prop:flow given), expect N2. The N3 claim really attaches to the cluster C2+C4.

name: Cocycle-driven polynomial flow
statement: dA_j/dt = i s_t(h_j) A_j with s_t(k) = sum_g k(g) A_g(t) S A_g(t)^*, which generates trace-preserving automorphisms beta_t fixing S, with ||beta_1(A_j)-A_j|| <= 3pi||h_j|| and ||beta_1(A_w) - C A_w|| <= 3pi||D_w - delta_e||.
why: A free/internal analogue of known cocycle deformations. Neither Popa/IPP nor Sinclair/Peterson-Sinclair is cited by 287, but both are standard in the field.

name: Word derivative equals cocycle value (exact operator-norm word displacement)
statement: delta a_g = i sigma(D_g) a_g, hence ||beta_1(A_w) - C A_w|| <= 3pi ||D_w - delta_e|| exactly (no BCH error).
why: The expected noncommutative analogue. It matters as the coupling that makes C2 meaningful, so grade C2+C4 together for the cluster test.

name: S = Arg(C): bounded Borel logarithm as flow driver
statement: Replace the semicircular driver by S = arg(C), so e^{iS} = C and any flow fixing S fixes C. The discontinuity of the logarithm sidesteps the K_1 obstruction in C*_r(F_{n+1}).
why: Retrieval and transfer of IPP's deformation device. The insight backtrack it triggered has origin 'retrieved', not 'constructed'. The trace analyst's N2 and the paper analyst's N1 are overridden (alt N1 if the representational use is credited).

name: Adaptive error-budget iteration with L2 generation
statement: Iterate C1. Fix eps_k before the witness word w_k and the future budget r_k after it. The A^(k) converge in norm to a free Haar tuple whose word algebra is L2-dense, so it generates M via E_N.
why: A standard diagonal template whose same-problem-area precedent is in L. 287's own Lean proof swaps it for a Baire argument, so the explicit forward-budget ordering is dispensable. Borderline N2 only if that ordering is credited.

name: Nielsen correction (gamma: C -> C A_w, alpha = gamma^{-1} beta)
statement: Compose the flow with the inverse of the free-basis change c -> cw, so that beta(A_w) ~ C A_w becomes alpha(A_w) ~ C.
why: A known object used one step from its standard role.

name: Universal initial trace identity (first-variation proof of tau o delta = 0)
statement: tau(ev_0(delta^r p)) = 0 for all p in the free formal algebra and r >= 1. Analyticity then gives moment invariance.
why: A new proof of a known criterion.

name: Free sum s(k): l2_R(F_n) realised inside M through the free complement
statement: s(k) = sum_g k(g) A_g S A_g^*, with the S_g free, so l2 cocycle values become operators in M.
why: A repackaging of the free Bernoulli field. It has an F5 flavour but is not new.

name: Support-independent free-sum bound (K = 3 pi)
statement: ||sum_j z_j|| <= 2 (sum ||z_j||_2^2)^{1/2} + max ||z_j|| for free centred self-adjoint z_j.
why: Known inequality, re-proved.

name: commutant {S}', hyperinvariant subspace, transitive algebra
statement: {S}'={A: AS=SA}; a closed subspace is hyperinvariant if invariant under {S}'; an algebra is transitive if its only closed common invariant subspaces are 0 and H. S has no nontrivial hyperinvariant subspace iff {S}' is transitive.
why: Textbook (Radjavi-Rosenthal).

name: coordinate tails K_{>=h} in K=l^2(Z)
statement: K_{>=h} = closed span{e_j: j>=h}, with K_{-inf}=K, K_{+inf}=0.
why: Standard.

name: 2-adic base X=Z_2 with Haar measure, odometer theta x=x+1, H_0=L^2(X;K), scalar multipliers M_g
statement: Base = 2-adic integers, completed Haar probability, theta = +1 (the dyadic odometer); H_0 = L^2(X, mu; l^2(Z)).
why: Dyadic odometer is the standard rank-one ergodic system.

name: Theorem 1.1 (direct model): weights beta_j, contraction V, fiber lattices = tails, ||S^n|| <= exp(-10 floor((n+1)^2/4)), V commutes with S and moves tails back…
statement: Existence of the 2-adic fibered weighted shift S with the four listed properties.
why: Graded via its core device E1 (B16-B18).

name: Corollary 1.2: every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space carries a nonzero norm-quasinilpotent S with transitive, proper, strongly closed comm…
statement: Negative answer to the hyperinvariant-subspace problem (HSP), in the quasinilpotent case, plus a non-dense transitive algebra.
why: Goal statement.

name: Fields from scalar multipliers (decomposable operators)
statement: An operator on L^2(Y;K) commuting with all M_g is a measurable essentially bounded field A_y; projections give projection fields.
why: Decomposable operators / direct integrals: textbook.

name: Commutant algebra lemma: {T}' is a proper SOT-closed unital algebra for nonscalar T
statement: Elementary.
why: Textbook.

name: weighted space l^2(w), right translation R; log-convex/log-concave two-ended weights with quadratic log growth (QuadraticWeights)
statement: w positive decreasing; log w convex on j<=0, concave on j>=0; sum_{j!=0} w_j^{1/j}<inf; log w_n/n^2 -> -a, log w_{-n}/n^2 -> a with a>log 3.
why: Specialization of Domar-type weight conditions (Domar 1981 in L).

name: Lemma 2.1 weighted translation criterion: closed R-invariant subspaces of l^2(w) are exactly the tails; the fiber shift has invariant lattice {K_{>=h}}
statement: Unicellular (standard-subspaces-only) bilateral weighted shift under the quadratic two-ended hypothesis.
why: Known theorem class (Domar 1981; Nikolskii for unilateral); re-proved here for one weight class.

name: support separation: nonzero b,c with vanishing correlations sum_j b_j c_{j-r}=0 (r>=1) have max supp b <= min supp c
statement: Titchmarsh-type support theorem for weighted correlations.
why: Domar's method.

name: greatest convex minorant anchored at 0; contact indices
statement: Convex envelope of -log|b_n|; strict-curvature points are contact points.
why: Standard.

name: slope-matching / geometric-middle estimate with lambda in (log 3, a): C_lambda = 2/(e^lambda-1) < 1
statement: Choose two contact coefficients whose product dominates the correlation; the tails are o(M); contradiction 1 <= C_lambda + o(1).
why: Technical specialization of a known method.

name: residue maps T_m(x)=x mod 2^m with nesting and step formulas
statement: T_m(theta x)-T_m(x)=1 unless T_m(x)=N_m-1 (wrap).
why: Standard.

name: Lemma 3.1 ergodicity of the odometer
statement: theta is ergodic.
why: Classical.

name: Prop 3.2 fibers: every S_x bounded, norm e^{-c}, invariant lattice = tails; Prop 3.3 explicit power bound
statement: Verification that the designed weights satisfy B08 uniformly in x; ||S^n|| <= exp(-c floor((n+1)^2/4)).
why: Routine verification.

name: two-ended residue-corrected weights a_k^+(x)=c(k+1)+J_m+D T_m(x), a_k^-(x)=c(k+1)+J_m+D(N_m-1-T_m(x)) on blocks I_m=[8^{m-1},8^m), c=10, D=100
statement: Quadratic log-weights whose sub-leading residue corrections change by +D on the positive end and -D on the negative end when the base moves by theta (except at rare wraps).
why: See E1.

name: Lemma 4.1 two-ended drift: sum_{k<n} Delta a_k >= Dn - C(x), sum_{-q<=k<0} Delta a_k <= -Dq + C(x), C(x) finite a.e. (possibly non-integrable)
statement: Pointwise linear drift of the log-weights along theta in opposite directions at the two ends; Borel-Cantelli (paper) / x not an integer of Z_2 (Lean).
why: See E1.

name: backward intertwiner V: (Vf)(theta x)=V_x f(x), V_x e_j=b_j(x)e_{j-1}, with b solving b_{j+1}(x)beta_j(x)=b_j(x)beta_{j-1}(theta x) (closed form b~_j(x)=w_{j-1…
statement: A contraction commuting with S that maps the tail K_{>=h} at x densely onto K_{>=h-1} at theta x.
why: Provisional; the central eureka candidate E1.

name: fiber invariance identities (I-P_x)S_xP_x=0, (I-P_{theta x})V_xP_x=0 and measurable tail label s(x)
statement: M-invariant subspace = field of tails K_{>=s(x)}; s(theta x) <= s(x)-1 when finite, and s=-inf propagates.
why: Routine.

name: Lemma 5.1 strict descent on a probability space: s(theta x) <= s(x)-1 (finite), -inf propagates => s = +-inf a.e.
statement: No measurable integer-valued function strictly decreases along a measure-preserving map.
why: Classical recurrence fact restated.

name: transitivity of the unital algebra generated by S, V and all M_g
statement: Assembly.
why: Assembly of B09+B18+B20.

name: structure: L^2(X;K_{>=h}) are ordinary invariant subspaces; S not compact (fibers compact); multiplier algebra not maximal abelian (Arveson inapplicable); fini…
statement: Side results distinguishing the example from known positive theorems.
why: Corollary-level.

name: rotation factor R_theta, weighted rotation T_f=U f(V), affiliated invariant subspace / invariant projection (1-p)T_f p=0
statement: Standard hyperfinite II_1 factor and the operator class of Zhu-Fang-Shi.
why: Standard (ZFS 2017).

name: Theorem 1.1: for every irrational theta there is continuous f:T->[0,1], f^{-1}(0)={1}, int log f=-inf, with no nontrivial invariant projection of U f(V) in R_t…
statement: Negative answer to ZFS's question (Math. Scand. 120 (2017) p.264).
why: Goal.

name: Lemma 1.3 hyperinvariant projections lie in M (Dykema 2005 Prop 2.1)
statement: If T in M, the projection onto any hyperinvariant subspace is in M'' = M and T-invariant. So 'no invariant projection in M' => 'no hyperinvariant subspace'.
why: Known route (Dykema 2005; the Haagerup-Schultz programme).

name: Corollary 1.4: nonzero norm-quasinilpotent operator with transitive commutant on every separable infinite-dimensional H
statement: Second, independent proof of the HSP counterexample.
why: Goal.

name: Remark 1.5: contradicts Cho-Ko-Lee 2017 Corollary 2.8 (hyperinvariant assertion at mu=1)
statement: I+T has the same commutant as T, so the published hyperinvariant assertion fails.
why: Corollary of C04.

name: sampling kernels w_m^{(1)}, w_m^{(2)} and Lemma 2.1 scalar sampling estimates (Fejer kernel, BV discrepancy)
statement: Kernels forcing a small positive move without wrap; second-moment and two-power decorrelation estimates.
why: Standard Fourier/discrepancy estimates around an ad hoc kernel.

name: Lemma 2.2 nonzero finite convolution (compactness of Laurent-polynomial pairs)
statement: If A_0,B_0 >= delta then some (AB)_{-n}, 0<=n<=2K, is >= eps(K,D,delta).
why: Elementary.

name: Prop 2.3 parameters at a prescribed angle: divisible frequencies q_i with {q_i theta} realizing independent trial phases; spread condition; sampling sets N_{j,…
statement: Successive choice of block scales m_j,K_j,C_j,L_j and divisible frequencies; trial phases are chosen probabilistically then realized by characters of the fixed rotation.
why: Close in spirit to successive-approximation constructions in ergodic theory over rotations; technique-heavy, not a short cut.

name: Lemma 3.1 fields from scalar multipliers; tracial crossed-product representation, covariance A(sigma x)=S^{-1}A(x)S, trace formula
statement: Group-measure-space model of R_theta as fields.
why: Textbook.

name: Lemma 3.2 positive diagonal: a nontrivial invariant projection has 0<<p(x)e_0,e_0><1 a.e.
statement: Ergodicity + trace formula.
why: Elementary.

name: Lemma 3.3 compact-set transfer: identities pass to weak limits of endpoint measures with uniformly absolutely continuous marginals (Lusin)
statement: Weak-limit transfer of a.e. operator identities.
why: Standard measure theory.

name: measurable cost cocycle g_*(x)=sum_j C_j sum_{i in J_j} floor(u_i(x)+alpha_i), f_*=e^{-g_*}, and cocycle F_k, ratios R_{x,y}(k)
statement: Rare logarithmic drops: each term is the step cocycle 1_{[1-alpha_i,1)}(u_i) = alpha_i + {u_i} - {u_i+alpha_i}; finite a.e. but with divergent integral.
why: Assembled from classical step cocycles; see E3.

name: Lemma 3.4 rational graphs: invariance identity transfers from positive orbit pairs to translations by multiples of 1/q_A
statement: Sampling transfer via C08 and C11.
why: Technical transfer; part of the E2 machinery.

name: Lemma 4.1 product densities: L^2 norm of an infinite product density <= exp(C/2)
statement: Kakutani-type absolute continuity of product measures.
why: Kakutani.

name: ordered biased coupling P_j: shared mixed-radix digits, top/bottom components of widths a_s,b_s with probability rho_s(w)=kappa_s sqrt(w/m_s), tagged component…
statement: Pairs (x,y) with u_i(x)<=u_i(y), uniformly L^2 marginals, and quantitatively positive threshold-crossing probability after conditioning on either endpoint.
why: See E2.

name: Lemma 5.1 conditional convolution obstruction: exact vanishing of the full convolution + finite-window lower bound + endpoint-conditioned tail bounds => c*eps …
statement: Cauchy-Schwarz on probability x counting measure, conditioning one factor on x and the other on y, avoids any union bound over infinitely many exceptional events.
why: See E2.

name: Theorem 5.2 measurable obstruction with Lemmas 5.3 truncation bound and 5.4 tail attenuation
statement: T_*=U pi(f_*) has no nontrivial invariant projection in M.
why: Assembly of E2/E3.

name: Lemma 6.1 transport by an affiliated positive operator preserves invariance and trace
statement: Unbounded affiliated intertwiner H with HA=BH maps invariant projections of A to invariant projections of B of equal trace.
why: Named precedent (Mori).

name: smoothing and relocating drops; background cost g_0 diverging at 0; continuous weight g=g_*+1+b o sigma-b with non-integrable transfer b
statement: Continuous weight with one zero cohomologous (up to constant) to the measurable one.
why: Routine cohomological engineering.

name: Cor 6.2 T_f nonzero quasinilpotent (special case of ZFS Thm 2.3)
statement: Uniform ergodic averages of log max(f,e^{-M}).
why: Known.

name: Appendix A: product realization on T^N (rationally independent angles), ordered orbit-pair sampling Prop A.3, Brown measure delta_0 (Lean), atomic/diffuse pola…
statement: Second model with independent coordinates; used by Lean for the HyperinvariantSubspaces comparator.
why: Same E2 machinery on an easier base.

name: Backward intertwiner across fibers: two-ended opposite-drift weights over the odometer making a fiber-moving backward shift a bounded element of the commutant
why: It is the step that turns the HSP into a one-dimensional descent on a probability space; everything else is known (Domar fibers, decomposable operators, recurrence). Within one fiber the backward shift is unbounded (w_{j-1}/w_j -> inf); boundedness appears only by moving to the next fiber, with the sup-normalization L(x) finite a.e. but non-integrable C(x) -- a pointwise-finiteness trick. Syntactically tiny (opposite residue corrections +-D T_m), like Cook's extension variables, and invisible i…

name: Conditional convolution obstruction with endpoint-conditioned tail attenuation on ordered biased couplings (top/bottom/tagged components)
why: Conditioning one Cauchy-Schwarz factor on x and the other on y avoids a union bound over infinitely many exceptional events -- the paper names this as the key to controlling the infinite tail. Used twice (circle and product models); essential for the IP route and for the Lean HSP comparator via FiniteFactor.

name: Measurable cost cocycle of rare logarithmic drops at divisible frequencies realizing independent trial phases at a prescribed irrational angle
why: Makes the angle prescribable (no Diophantine condition), the main improvement over an exists-theta construction (ContinuousCircleWeight comparator). Determinant zero with finite a.e. cost.

name: Trace-preserving transport of invariant projections by an unbounded affiliated coboundary multiplier (measurable -> continuous weight)
why: Lets an unbounded, non-integrable transfer function move the obstruction while preserving trace.

name: Domar quadratic criterion + strict-descent lemma
why: Load-bearing (43% of direct-route DAG lines).

name: Backward intertwiner across odometer fibers: two-ended opposite-drift weights making a fiber-moving backward shift a bounded element of {S}' (B16 weights, B17 …
statement: Over the 2-adic odometer theta, choose log-weights a_j(x) of a bilateral shift with quadratic growth and sub-leading corrections that increase by D at the positive end and decrease by D at the negative end when x -> theta x (except at a.e.-finitely many wraps). Then b~_j(x)=w_{j-1}(theta x)/(e^c w_j(x)) tends to 0 at both ends, sup_j b~_j(x)=L(x) is finite a.e., and V (Vf)(theta x)=V_x f(x), V_x e_j=(b~_j(x)/L(x)) e_{j-1} is a contraction commuting with S that maps each fiber tail K_{>=h} dense…
why: No source in any searched field contains a bounded commuting operator that moves invariant tails backward between fibers of an ergodic base; single-fiber versions are impossible (unbounded), and the known II_1 route reaches the HSP only via the far heavier IP machinery. The device is tiny and invisible in the goal, and if correct it resolves a ~50-year-old problem in ~10 pages. Downgrade risks: (a) pivot is short once the II_1 commutant analogy is in mind (the same release produced IP first or …

name: Conditional convolution obstruction with endpoint-conditioned tail attenuation on ordered biased couplings (C15-C17)
statement: If all products A_v B_{-n-v} sum to zero, the finite-window coefficients are bounded below on an event of probability c, and each tail ratio is bounded by eta plus indicators of events with conditional probability <= delta given x (resp. y), then c eps <= (2K+1)(eta + 2 sqrt(delta)).
why: Components (prescribed-marginal couplings, Laurent compactness, conditioned Cauchy-Schwarz, Kakutani densities) are known; the obstruction is a long technical estimation chain tailored to one weight, not a short device with a large budget drop. Upgrade to N3 only if an expert judges the endpoint-conditioned attenuation genuinely new and reusable.

name: Rare-drop measurable cost cocycle at divisible frequencies realizing independent trial phases at a prescribed angle (C08, C12)
statement: g_*(x)=sum_j C_j sum_{i in J_j} floor({q_i x}+{q_i theta}) with q_i | q_{i+1}, {q_i theta} close to independently chosen trial phases.
why: Engineering of classical cocycles; the novelty is quantitative tuning.

name: Trace-preserving transport of invariant projections by an unbounded affiliated coboundary multiplier (C18, C19)
statement: H affiliated, injective, HA=BH on Dom H: closure of H(ran p cap Dom H) is a B-invariant projection in M with the same trace.
why: Named precedent.

name: Domar quadratic criterion (B09-B12) and strict-descent lemma (B20)
statement: Unicellularity of the fibers; no measurable integer function strictly decreases along a measure-preserving map.
why: Re-proof of a known theorem class; classical recurrence.

name: state / pure state
statement: Positive functional of norm one; pure = extreme point of the state space.
why: Textbook.

name: GNS representation and equivalence h~k of pure states
statement: h~k iff the GNS representations are unitarily equivalent.
why: Textbook.

name: tracial algebra
statement: Unital C*-algebra with a faithful tracial state, extended normally to B**.
why: Renaming of 'C*-algebra with faithful tracial state'.

name: property (U): every pure state of B has exactly one state extension to C
statement: Inclusion B in C such that each pure state of B has a unique state extension.
why: Established notion in the cited literature.

name: peaking sequence ((P_n) peaks to h)
statement: A decreasing sequence of projections peaks to h if h is the only state with h(P_n)=1 for all n.
why: Projection specialisation of AAP excising nets / closed projections; Tanaka2026 (model-produced) also uses projections q_n with tau(q_n)=2^-n excising a product state.

name: support projection r_h in B**
statement: Least projection of B** on which the normal extension of h is one; minimal when h is pure.
why: Textbook.

name: conditional expectation; faithful
statement: UCP map C->B fixing B, B-bimodular; faithful if E(a*a)=0 implies a=0.
why: Textbook.

name: reduced word in A and the stable unitary v
statement: a_0 v^e1 a_1 ... v^em a_m with E_1(a_t)=0 at (+,-) turns and E_2(a_t)=0 at (-,+) turns.
why: Ueda's HNN words.

name: centered element
statement: x in ker E.
why: Textbook.

name: continuous chain
statement: B_gamma = closure of union at limit ordinals.
why: AW04.

name: base algebra A_0 = CAR = (x) M_2 and p_n = e_11^{(x)n}
statement: UHF(2^infty) with product vector state peaked by p_n, tau(p_n)=2^-n.
why: Classical CAR algebra; same base as Tanaka2026.

name: active index / bridge iteration (X_beta)
statement: Continuous chain from A_0 adjoining at active j the bridge for (p_n),(q_n^j) with tau(q_n^j)=2^-n.
why: AW04-type chain with T16 as step.

name: A[T] = C*(A_0, v_j : j in T active)
statement: Subalgebra generated by A_0 and a subset of stable unitaries.
why: Abbreviation.

name: dependency sets I_j and dependency-closed T
statement: Countable I_j subset j with q_n^j in A[I_j]; T is closed if j in T implies I_j subset T.
why: As a definition it is a closure-under-a-function abbreviation; its value lies in T21.

name: schedule sigma: kappa x kappa -> kappa injective with sigma(beta,eta) >= beta, kappa = c^+
statement: Bookkeeping fixed before the construction; replaces diamond's guessing.
why: Folklore bookkeeping (e.g. Kunen-style iterations of length c^+).

name: unique extension of a pure state is pure
statement: If h pure on B has unique extension to C, the extension is pure.
why: Folklore.

name: equivalent pure states are unitarily conjugate; unique lifts of equivalent states are equivalent
statement: Kadison transitivity gives u in B with k = h o Ad(u*).
why: Classical. Lean re-proves Kadison self-adjoint transitivity.

name: peaking under restriction
statement: If (P_n) in B peaks to H on C, it peaks to H|B in B and H is the unique extension of H|B.
why: Elementary observation.

name: decreasing excision (AAP)
statement: Pure h admits a decreasing net of positive contractions x with h(x)=1, x -> r_h strongly, ||x(a-h(a))x|| -> 0.
why: AAP86.

name: projection excision
statement: A peaking sequence excises its state; ||P_n a P_t|| -> 0 when h(a)=0.
why: Specialisation of AAP86.

name: cross-excision (Akemann-Weaver Lemma 1)
statement: h not~ k: ||x_lambda a y_nu|| -> 0 on the product net.
why: AW04 Lemma 1.

name: trace-null supports
statement: No f.d. irreps + tracial tau => tau(r_h)=0 for every pure h.
why: Short folklore fact; key role but easy.

name: at most one trace-preserving expectation; it is faithful
statement: Uniqueness and faithfulness of trace-preserving conditional expectations.
why: Folklore.

name: peaking expectation onto D=C*(p_n)=C(N_0 u {infty})
statement: E(a)(n)=tau(d_n a d_n)/tau(d_n), E(a)(infty)=h(a) is a trace-preserving conditional expectation when traces strictly decrease to 0.
why: Atomic diagonal expectation is standard for c_0-type masas; the twist (value h(a) at infinity, continuity via excision, trace has no mass at infinity) is new but short.

name: (U) + faithful expectation + simple base => simple extension
statement: Simplicity is inherited without ideal analysis.
why: Short, folklore-level.

name: reduced HNN adjunction H(A) with stable unitary and expectation; uniqueness by reduced-word trace vanishing
statement: For trace-preserving theta:D_1->D_2 with expectations, there is a faithfully tracial H(A)=C*(A,v), v d v*=theta(d), E_A killing reduced words; unique up to iso.
why: Ueda's reduced HNN extension; re-proved with the needed expectations.

name: reduced amalgamated free product Z=F*_D G with E_D, E_F, traces
statement: Hilbert D-module free product; E_F kills a_0 b_1 ... b_m a_m words; trace faithful.
why: Standard reduced amalgamated free product. Lean builds it differently: a scalar l^2 Fock space over the atoms of D (AtomicTraceData), possible because D=C(N u infty) with no trace mass at infinity.

name: restriction: C*(A',v) = H(A') for D_1,D_2 subset A'
statement: HNN commutes with shrinking the base.
why: Routine.

name: reordering two adjunctions: H_k(H_j(O)) = H_j(H_k(O))
statement: Two HNN adjunctions with data in a common base O commute, fixing O, v_j, v_k.
why: Symmetric multi-letter HNN extension.

name: HNN commutes with inductive limits of bases
statement: R = closure of union of H(O_beta) is H(O).
why: Routine.

name: the selective bridge (HNN along two matched peaking sequences)
statement: A faithfully tracial, no f.d. irreps; (p_n^1),(p_n^2) peak to f_1 not~ f_2 with equal traces strictly decreasing to 0. The reduced HNN extension along theta(p_n^1)=p_n^2 gives (U) for ALL pure states of A, and h~ ~ k~ iff h~k or {[h],[k]}={[f_1],[f_2]}; H(A) faithfully tracial, simple if A is.
why: No equivalent in L or found elsewhere; it supplies what CF22 Sec. 8 asked for, in a form that works for nonseparable bases.

name: peak transfer through stable letters and the two-ended endpoint criterion
statement: ||dP_G|| <= ||E_D^F(d*d)||^{1/2}; a word decays under x..y if both endpoint expectations decay; matched endpoints are split as phi(a)1 + a^0 and the scalar term moves the peak through the letter, P_n^{l(b)} b = b P_n^{r(b)}, exposing a centered internal coefficient.
why: Inseparable from T16; graded with it.

name: (U) along a continuous chain; unique lifts of equivalent states equivalent
statement: Transfinite composition of (U).
why: AW04.

name: inequivalence persists at limits
statement: Inequivalent on a tail => inequivalent on the limit.
why: Routine.

name: base peak: A_0 separable simple, p_n peaks, tau(p_n)=2^-n; no f.d. irreps above A_0
statement: Properties of the CAR base.
why: Classical.

name: inherited iteration: A[T cap beta] is a bridge iteration for dependency-closed T
statement: Sub-iterations over closed index sets are again bridge iterations; A[T] simple, tracial, separable if T countable.
why: Forcing-iteration analogue; C*-proof routine given C13 and L03.

name: closed-subiteration theorem: A[S] subset X_delta has (U) for every dependency-closed S
statement: Postpone each omitted active step j past the retained ones: R_beta = H_j(O_beta) by P14 and L15, and the omitted pair stays inequivalent on O_beta by T16's no-other-join clause; then T16 gives (U) for A[S u j] subset A[S u (j+1)], and L17 composes.
why: Structural pattern exists in set theory (sub-iterations over adequate index sets are complete suborders) and AWW10 has the free-group special case; the C*-mechanism (reordering HNN adjunctions + no-other-join) is new.

name: countable determination
statement: Every pure h on X_delta has a countable dependency-closed S with h|A[S] pure and h its unique extension.
why: Pure-restriction half is AWW10; uniqueness half is T21.

name: state count: |delta| <= c => X_delta has <= c pure states
statement: Counting via countable determination.
why: Routine.

name: Kishimoto-Ozawa-Sakai homogeneity
statement: Pure states of a separable simple C*-algebra are automorphism-conjugate.
why: KOS03; Lean re-proves it by a quasicentral Krylov-row argument (dominated share 0.111).

name: q_n^j = gamma(p_n) via KOS on separable A[S], with tau(q_n^j)=2^-n from uniqueness of the trace on gamma(M_{2^n})
statement: A matched-trace peaking sequence for the target state, supported on a countable dependency-closed set.
cited_or_new: new here; close variant in model-produced Tanaka2026
why: Close variant exists in Tanaka2026 (model-produced).

name: ZFC recursion of length kappa=c^+ with a state-independent schedule
statement: Build X_beta by bridges scheduled by sigma; countable determination + regularity of c^+ catch every final pure state.
why: Standard bookkeeping once L22 and T16 exist.

name: moment-norm formula ||x|| = lim t((x*x)^r)^{1/2r} for faithful tracial t
statement: Faithful traces determine norms from moments.
why: Folklore.

name: atomic Fock-space model of the amalgamated free product
statement: Replaces Hilbert C*-modules by l^2 over reduced paths through the atoms of D.
why: Formalization device.

name: KOS re-proof via near-central rows (Krylov band averages)
statement: Quasicentral Cesaro averages of Krylov projection chains give near-central row isometries; with Kadison transitivity this yields same-class control and an intertwining limit automorphism.
why: Known theorem, known technique.

name: Selective bridge: reduced HNN extension along a partial isomorphism of two matched peaking-projection algebras
why: Replaces the global automorphism of AW04/FH17 crossed products (which needs separability via KOS and cannot give (U) for all pure states; CF22 Q8.2 is open) with a partial isomorphism of two copies of C(N u infty). The data are countable, so the step works over nonseparable bases. Gives (U) for ALL old pure states and exactly one join; CF22 Prop 8.3 shows this property is what a diamond-free construction needs. Small and non-obvious: matched trace values make theta trace-preserving; trace-null …

name: Closed-subiteration theorem: (U) from every dependency-closed sub-iteration by postponing omitted adjunctions
why: Converts the bridge's no-other-join clause into a global statement; this is the step that removes diamond (introduction.tex:104-105). No C*-algebraic precedent found; dominated share ~0.11.

name: Countable determination replacing diamond; schedule of length c^+
why: Bounds the pure states by c at every stage and supplies a separable determining subalgebra for KOS; highest substantive dominated share (0.153-0.156).

name: Peaking expectation E(a)(n)=tau(d_n a d_n)/tau(d_n), E(a)(infty)=h(a)
why: Makes the HNN data available from a peaking sequence alone; no formula of this form found.

name: Matched-trace peaking sequence q_n = gamma(p_n) via KOS on a separable determining subalgebra
why: Avoids needing gamma to preserve the trace: uniqueness of the trace on gamma(M_{2^n}).

name: Selective bridge: reduced HNN extension along matched peaking-projection algebras (T16 with I20, L09, L07)
statement: A faithfully tracial, no finite-dimensional irreps; (p_n^1),(p_n^2) peak to inequivalent f_1,f_2 with tau(p_n^1)=tau(p_n^2) strictly decreasing to 0. Adjoin v with v p_n^1 v* = p_n^2 as Ueda's reduced HNN extension over D_i = C*(p_n^i). Then every pure state of A has a unique state extension, and the extensions of h,k are equivalent iff h~k or {[h],[k]} = {[f_1],[f_2]}.
why: No construction in any searched source gives an extension that preserves unique extension for all pure states and joins exactly one prescribed pair. The crossed-product precedents (AW04, FH17) need a global automorphism and separability, and the global version of the property is open as CF22 Q8.2. Downgrade pressure: CF22 Sec. 8, which is in L, explicitly suggests a 'partial crossed product' amalgamation for the same goal. The ingredients (Ueda HNN, AAP excision, AW cross-excision, AWW free-pro…

name: Closed-subiteration theorem: (U) for A[S] in X_delta for every dependency-closed S (T21 with L20, I14)
statement: In a bridge iteration with countable dependency sets I_j, every dependency-closed S gives an inclusion A[S] in X_delta with property (U). Proof: postpone each omitted active step past the retained ones (reordering), keeping its pair inequivalent by the bridge's no-other-join clause, then apply the bridge.
why: Templated strengthening: (U) is proved for every closed substructure ('strengthen to all subsets/substructures'), and the induction carries an extra tracked invariant, so it is capped at N2. Close variants exist: the AWW10 special case, and the set-theoretic complete-sub-iteration pattern. The C*-mechanism (postponing adjunctions by HNN reordering while no-other-join keeps the pair apart) is new and is the step that removes diamond, so N3 is plausible if the cap is waived.

name: Countable determination and the c^+ schedule replacing diamond (L22, C23, T25, I15)
statement: Every pure state of X_delta is the unique extension of its pure restriction to a separable A[S] with S countable dependency-closed; hence at most c pure states when |delta| <= c, and a fixed injective schedule kappa x kappa -> kappa with kappa = c^+ treats every pure state.
why: Assembly of AWW10's restriction argument, C2 and standard bookkeeping. The idea is posed in CF22 Sec. 8.

name: Peaking expectation E(a)(n)=tau(d_n a d_n)/tau(d_n), E(a)(infty)=h(a) (L09)
statement: For a peaking sequence with traces strictly decreasing to 0, D=C*(p_n)=C(N u infty) and the displayed map is the trace-preserving conditional expectation onto D.
why: New formula; the only novelty is the value h(a) at infinity, and continuity follows from excision.

name: Matched-trace peaking sequence q_n = gamma(p_n) by KOS on a separable determining subalgebra (I25)
statement: gamma from KOS on A[S] carries g to the reference state on A[S]; q_n = gamma(p_n) peaks to g and tau(q_n) = 2^-n because gamma(M_{2^n}) is a unital matrix subalgebra.
why: Close variant in Tanaka2026 (model-produced). It would be N0 if Tanaka's device is confirmed equivalent from the PDF.

name: Reordering of two HNN adjunctions over a common base (P14)
statement: H_k(H_j(O)) = H_j(H_k(O)) fixing O, v_j, v_k, when both data lie in O.
why: Corollary of the multi-letter HNN or free-product associativity.

name: Trace-null supports: tau(r_h)=0 without finite-dimensional irreps (L07)
statement: If B has no finite-dimensional irreps, every tracial state vanishes on the support projection of every pure state.
why: Folklore; its role in C1 is what matters.

name: Lean-only re-proof of KOS homogeneity via near-central rows (I28)
statement: Kishimoto-Ozawa-Sakai homogeneity, proved with Krylov projection chains and Cesaro-averaged quasicentral rows.
why: Re-proof of a cited theorem.

name: faithful action
statement: An action is faithful when its kernel is trivial; stabilizers need not be trivial.
why: Textbook.

name: almost periodic homeomorphism
statement: f is almost periodic if the closure of {f^j} in Homeo(M) is compact.
why: Standard dynamics notion.

name: almost-periodic corollary
statement: For M as in Thm cor:lie, every almost periodic homeomorphism has an iterate f^m on a continuous R-flow.
cited_or_new: new proof of a conjectured consequence (Pardon Conj 1.4)
why: Immediate corollary: compact abelian Lie group, torus exponential.

name: Thm main (p-adic exclusion)
statement: Every jointly continuous Z_p-action on a connected Hausdorff second-countable n-manifold without boundary has nonzero kernel, hence factors through a finite quotient.
why: The statement itself is the classical p-adic formulation; novelty is in the proof.

name: Thm cor:lie (Hilbert-Smith)
statement: A locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected Hausdorff second-countable n-manifold without boundary is a Lie group.
cited_or_new: new (claimed resolution of a famous conjecture)
why: The conjecture statement.

name: test space
statement: Locally compact, finite-dimensional, separable metrizable space: a finite polyhedron, a space homeomorphic to one, an open subset of one, or finite products.
why: Conjunction of standard classes.

name: test categories T(X), T^0(X), P(X), P^0(X)
statement: T^0(X): smallest full replete triangulated subcategory of D^b(Sh_R(X)) containing Rf_* R_B for every continuous f from a compact finite polyhedron B; T(X): its closure under direct summands. P, P^0: same with semialgebraic f.
why: Close neighbours: Woolf's Witt groups of perfect and constructible complexes; Ranicki-Weiss local chain category generated by continuous simplices (paper names both). The variation (generated by proper images of arbitrary continuous maps, not constructible) is new but small.

name: Simplex generators and summands
statement: Closed simplices suffice as sources; every object of T is a summand of an object of T^0; summand closures are thick.
why: Standard skeletal filtration.

name: Duality and compact support on T
statement: Verdier duality restricts to a triangulated duality on T^0, T, P^0, P; biduality is invertible; objects and duals have compact support.
cited_or_new: new in this generality (proof via proper pushforward of simplex duality)
why: Direct consequence of standard Verdier duality (Kashiwara-Schapira) for proper maps; a known technique.

name: Direct images and open extension
statement: Allowed maps induce exact duality-compatible pushforwards Rg_! = Rg_* on T; open extension j_! is fully faithful.
why: Standard sheaf theory.

name: Symmetric cone
statement: The cone of a symmetric morphism u: L -> #L carries a neutral nonsingular symmetric form for the translated duality.
why: Balmer 2000 / Woolf 2008 Lemma 2.1 (delta = +-1 version re-proved).

name: Products with the interval
statement: External products B x A stay in T(I x X); the external duality comparison is an isomorphism and compatible with traces.
why: Standard Kunneth/duality.

name: Two endpoint forms
statement: There is a neutral form on (i_0)_*A + (i_1)_*A with diagonal parts c(i_0)_*alpha and -c(i_1)_*alpha.
why: Woolf 2008 Prop 3.11 transplanted.

name: Homotopy invariance of E_r = W_r(T)
statement: Homotopic maps of test spaces induce equal maps on E_r; contractible test spaces have point Witt groups.
why: Woolf's argument; the only new content is that it runs inside T.

name: Cutoff
statement: For K closed inside O open, every A in B^0(X) admits s: A' -> A with A' compactly supported in O and s invertible near K.
why: Ranicki-Weiss Lemma 4.14 / Cor 4.15 is the named precedent; the sheaf version via polyhedral neighbourhoods of f^{-1}K is routine.

name: Objects supported in an open set
statement: The essential image of j_!: B(U) -> B(X) is the objects with cohomology supported in a compact subset of U; thick and duality-stable.
why: Routine from cutoff.

name: Germ description of the Verdier quotient
statement: Hom in B(X)/B(U) equals colim over neighbourhoods N of X\U of Hom_{D(N)}(A|_N, B|_N).
cited_or_new: new proof of an expected statement
why: Standard style (Verdier quotient by objects supported in U = germs near the complement); proof routine given cutoff.

name: Witt localization (Balmer-Walter)
statement: Long exact sequence W_r(B(U)) -> W_r(B(X)) -> W_r(B(X)/B(U)) -> W_{r-1}(B(U)), natural in maps and in P -> T.
why: Balmer-Walter 2002 Thm 2.1, invoked.

name: Open cover gives a dense inclusion
statement: For X = U cup V, extension gives a fully faithful duality functor B(V)/B(U cap V) -> B(X)/B(U) with dense image.
why: Excision via germs; routine.

name: Dense doubling (cofinality with exponent 2)
statement: For a dense full duality-stable triangulated inclusion A in C, there is d: W(C) -> W(A) with i d = 2 and d i = 2.
why: Hornbostel-Schlichting Appendix A Thm A.2; the doubling D(q)=q+q+H(x[1]) is an explicit proof.

name: Point calculation
statement: E_r(pt)=F_r(pt)=Z (signature) for r = 0 mod 4, else 0.
why: Witt groups of R.

name: Finite diagram chases with exponents
statement: Five-lemma and square chase with explicit annihilating exponents q^3 and 4q.
why: Quantitative five lemma.

name: Bounded comparison F_r(S^j) -> E_r(S^j)
statement: Kernel and cokernel of the semialgebraic-to-continuous comparison on S^j are killed by 2^{e_j}, uniformly in r (e_j = 3(9^j-1)/4).
why: A Mayer-Vietoris induction comparing two homology theories, made integral; standard technique (comparison of homology theories on spheres), new application. Induction carries 'uniform in r' (templated).

name: Rational sphere calculation
statement: G_r(S^j) tensor Q = G_r(pt)_Q + G_{r-j}(pt)_Q for G = E or F; so E_d(S^d)_Q and F_d(S^d)_Q are one-dimensional (d odd).
why: Suspension iso for a homology theory.

name: Signature on a finite semialgebraic relation
statement: Semialgebraic objects are generically locally constant; local signature on a small ball respects any finite Witt relation; hence im F_d(S^d) in F_d(S^d)_Q is exactly Z u_F.
why: Generic local signature is a standard idea (Witt-space / constructible theory).

name: Fixed sphere lattice
statement: For odd d >= 3 there is L_d = 2^{e_d} with E_d(S^d)_Q = Q u_d and im E_d(S^d) in L_d^{-1} Z u_d.
why: If one accepts that E is a homology theory with coefficients W(R), this is E_d(S^d) = Z up to bounded 2-torsion: expected. The novelty is proving it for the non-constructible category T.

name: Action of degree
statement: A degree-s map f: S^d -> S^d acts as multiplication by s on E_d(S^d)_Q; same for pushed orientation forms of closed oriented triangulable d-manifolds.
why: Local-degree computation.

name: Contractible quotient is an integral isomorphism
statement: For d odd and U a nonempty contractible open subset, E_d(X) -> W_d(T(X)/T(U)) is an isomorphism over Z (both d = 1, 3 mod 4).
why: Two-line consequence of localization plus homotopy invariance; the choice of odd d is the design decision.

name: Invariant chart subset (Newman reduction)
statement: There is an open subgroup G = Z_p acting faithfully and orientation-preservingly on a connected invariant open subset O of a chart.
why: Pardon 2013 Section 4.1.

name: odd stabilization W = O x R^{d-n}, d odd > n
statement: Stabilize to an odd dimension d >= 3, with trivial action on the extra factor.
why: Stabilization by R^k is standard; the choice of an odd d is a small design decision.

name: Collapse and compactification
statement: c: S^d -> W^+ is continuous; the action extends to W^+ fixing infinity; orbit spaces are compact metrizable.
why: Routine.

name: Averaged degree-one test
statement: After shrinking G to an open subgroup H that moves points less than the pinch scale, the Haar average of a ball pinch P_{z,r}, normalized, descends to a: Y -> S^d with deg(aqc)=1.
why: Averaging maps/metrics over a compact group is classical (Bochner-Montgomery, Repovs-Scepin averaged metric, Palais). Applying it to a pinch to get an integral degree-one class on the orbit space is a small new twist.

name: Rational orbit pullback injectivity
statement: For a compact G-space E, Rr_* k = r_* k and Q -> r_*Q splits by Haar averaging; so Cech H^j(E/G;Q) -> H^j(E;Q) is injective.
why: Classical rational transfer (Borel, Bredon, Montgomery-Zippin).

name: Killing a rationally trivial map to an odd sphere
statement: For d odd >= 3, K compact metrizable, v: K -> S^d with v^* gamma = 0 rationally, some degree-s map D_s makes D_s v nullhomotopic.
why: Rationalization of odd spheres is K(Q,d) (Serre); DFW 2003 use the same telescope.

name: Finite quotient sheets
statement: For every k there is a nonempty open V in Y on which W/p^kG -> W/G is m = p^k disjoint sheets, with a locally constant multiplier beta: q^{-1}V -> mu_m, beta(gw) = zeta^{g} beta(w).
why: Elementary consequence of faithfulness and the subgroup classification of Z_p.

name: Extending a homotopy from a closed subset
statement: Homotopy extension for maps into S^d from closed subsets of compact metrizable spaces.
why: Borsuk homotopy extension for ANR targets.

name: Moving a test into a prescribed open set
statement: For any nonempty open V in Y \ {y_inf}, some D_s a is homotopic to h with h constant on Y \ V.
why: Combines a rational transfer with odd-sphere rationalization; each piece is standard, the combination on a wild orbit space with no dimension bound is new.

name: Source of a restricted test
statement: Over X \ {b}, the source of f = tqc is an oriented open subset of W and f is proper there, so duality is only ever used on manifolds and test spaces.
why: Observation.

name: orbit sheaf H and eigensheaves H_lambda
statement: H = q_* C_{W^+} (C = real plane), T = action of 1 in G, H_lambda = ker(T - M_lambda), H_D = sum over D, Lambda = mu_{p^infty}.
why: Isotypic decomposition of a smooth representation of a profinite abelian group.

name: Character coproducts
statement: Rq_*C = q_*C = direct sum of H_lambda; Rt_* commutes with these (infinite) sums for compact targets.
why: Standard soft-sheaf argument.

name: Real orthogonality
statement: Distinct character subsums are orthogonal for the pushed orientation form, so character projectors are self-adjoint.
why: Standard.

name: Character classes z_i(t)
statement: For a finite partition of Lambda and a compact test t with contractible neighbourhoods at b_t, z_i(t) in E_d(X) is the unique lift of [A_t, alpha_t] + [A_t, alpha_t(2e_i - id)] under the integral localization iso; e_i is the germ of the character projector near X \ U.
why: No near-equivalent found in a quick search. Neighbours: G-signature / isotypic Witt classes for finite groups (Atiyah-Singer, Neumann, equivariant Witt groups); Witt groups of sheaves (Woolf). Using the 'twice the summand' trick [A,a]+[A,a(2e-1)] plus localization to avoid splitting idempotents at the fixed point is new as far as checked.

name: Sum of character classes
statement: Sum_i z_i(t) = 2 [A_t, alpha_t] integrally, via an explicit isometry S = sum E_j P_j.
why: Elementary matrix identity.

name: Covariance of character classes
statement: g_* z_i(t) = z_i(g t) for maps g of compact tests.
why: Naturality.

name: Homotopy invariance of character classes
statement: Homotopic tests t_0, t_1: Y -> S^d have equal z_i, even though b_t moves; proved through the close-pair test space C_d in S^d x S^d.
why: The close-pair trick (subdivide the homotopy, test with pairs in C_d) is a neat device, but standard in spirit.

name: Equal parts for a concentrated test
statement: If h is constant off a finite-sheet region V, multiplication by beta is an isometry cycling the parts D_i = zeta^i D_0, so z_0(h) = ... = z_{m-1}(h).
why: The sheet-label multiplier twisting characters is the standard Fourier/induction picture for a cyclic cover; the transversal partition is the new touch.

name: Contradiction on the invariant chart
statement: No faithful orientation-preserving Z_p-action on a connected open subset of R^n: z̄_i(a) = (4/p^k) u_d, contradicting the lattice once p^k > 4 L_d.
why: Assembly.

name: Suspending the first product input (signs)
statement: Sign comparison (-1)^r for the external product under suspension.
why: Sign conventions.

name: equal-parts-in-a-fixed-lattice strategy
statement: Fix an integral lattice L_d^{-1} Z u_d first, then for every k produce p^k integral classes with equal rational images summing to 4 u_d; contradiction for p^k > 4 L_d.
why: Divisibility/counting contradictions are classical (Smith theory, transfers, Yang's dimension raising), but using Witt-group integrality of real-coefficient signatures to defeat the Haar-measure 'fractional degree' of a p-adic action is new as far as a quick search shows. Real coefficients are needed to split characters; Witt groups restore integrality that C-coefficient homology loses.

name: Integral character classes z_i(t)
statement: For a compact test t: Y -> X and a finite partition Lambda = D_0 u ... u D_{m-1} of the p-power roots of unity, z_i(t) in E_d(X) = W_d(T(X)) is the unique integral class with l_U(z_i) = [A_t, alpha_t] + [A_t, alpha_t(2e_i - 1)] in W_d(T(X)/T(U)), where e_i are the self-adjoint character projectors on the punctured target and l_U is the integral localization iso for a contractible U around b_t (d odd).
why: A close variant exists: isotypic signature classes for finite group actions (Atiyah-Singer, Gilmer, CSW), including the identity [b] + [b*sigma] = 2[b|V+] for an involution. 304's contribution is to make this work for a profinite group with infinite-dimensional character parts and a non-manifold orbit space. It does so by germ-localizing projectors on the punctured target, lifting integrally through a contractible quotient with d odd, and taking 2x the summand to avoid splitting idempotents. Th…

name: Equal parts in a fixed lattice (organising strategy; L_d fixed before k)
statement: A faithful Z_p action yields, for every k, p^k integral classes in E_d(S^d) whose rational images are equal and sum to 4u_d. Each is then (4/p^k)u_d, contradicting im E_d(S^d) in L_d^{-1}Z u_d once p^k > 4L_d, where L_d is fixed before k.
why: The counting is the classical (and, per the F1 agent, also the Izumi/Rokhlin K-theoretic) free-action signature divisibility (|G| equal isotypic parts of an integer), run with |G| = p^k growing against a lattice fixed beforehand. What is new is the coupling: signature integrality on a finite test polyhedron, reached from a wild orbit space by the averaged degree-one test (C4) and the move-test (C5). This is the first such bridge for Hilbert-Smith that our searches found, but bridge novelty plus…

name: Equal parts for a concentrated test (sheet multiplier beta)
statement: If h: Y -> S^d is constant off a region V where W/p^kG -> W/G has p^k labelled sheets, multiplication by a locally constant beta with beta(gx) = zeta beta(x) cyclically permutes the parts D_i = zeta^i D_0, so z_0(h) = ... = z_{m-1}(h).
why: Once the character classes and the finite sheets exist, the multiplier is the standard trivialisation of a character local system. N1 (borderline N2).

name: Averaged degree-one test a: Y -> S^d
statement: After shrinking G to a small open subgroup H, the Haar average of a ball pinch, normalised, descends to a: Y = W^+/G -> S^d with deg(aqc) = 1.
why: A one-step application of classical compact-group averaging. The idea of a degree-one map out of the wild orbit space is a neat use of it, with close neighbours in L.

name: Moving a multiple of the test into a prescribed open set
statement: For any nonempty open V in Y \ {y_inf}, some D_s a (deg D_s = s > 0) is homotopic to h constant off V.
why: A composition of named known techniques. The family analyst's N2 is lowered to N1, borderline N2, because DFW's telescope is cited and used identically.

name: Test categories T(X) generated by Rf_* of arbitrary continuous maps from compact polyhedra
statement: T(X) is the thick subcategory of D^b(Sh(X;R)) generated by Rf_* R_B for continuous f: B -> X with B a compact polyhedron (non-constructible in general). E_r(X) = W_r(T(X)). Verdier duality restricts to it, and E_r is homotopy invariant.
why: An adaptation of Woolf / Ranicki-Weiss that the paper names. It is technically necessary because the action forces non-constructible images.

name: Fixed sphere lattice via bounded 2-power comparison with the semialgebraic subcategory
statement: Comparison F_r(S^j) -> E_r(S^j) has kernel and cokernel killed by 2^{e_j}, uniformly in r, with e_j = 3(9^j - 1)/4. Hence im E_d(S^d) -> E_d(S^d)_Q lies in L_d^{-1} Z u_d with L_d = 2^{e_d}.
why: A uniform-exponent strengthening of a standard comparison (templated strengthening: uniform/quantitative version), so it is capped at N2 regardless. It is technically the crux for correctness, and the family analyst's gap 1 sits here.

name: Cutoff lemma and germ description of the Verdier quotient T(X)/T(U)
statement: Morphisms in T(X)/T(U) are germs near X \ U, realised by cutting off the finite polyhedral sources. This lets projectors defined on the punctured target act in the quotient.
why: A new proof of an expected statement in a new category, with named antecedents. N1, borderline N2.

name: Homotopy invariance of character classes via the close-pair space C_d
statement: z_i(t) depends only on the homotopy class of the test map, shown by pushing through a close-pair space C_d of pairs of nearby test maps.
why: An expected property with a technical device. The analyst's provisional N2 is lowered.

name: Integral character classes z_i(t) (localization-lifted 'twice the isotypic summand')
why: It is hard to anticipate an invariant that is (a) integral, (b) defined for each character part of a profinite action with infinite-dimensional stalks, and (c) homotopy-invariant in the test map even though the decomposition fails at the fixed point at infinity. The trick [A,a] + [A,a(2e-1)] avoids splitting idempotents, and odd d makes the localization lift integral. It is not a subterm of the goal or of L, and every step of the contradiction runs through it. Rational or C-coefficient homology…

name: Equal parts in a fixed lattice (fix L_d before k)
why: It reformulates the profinite 'Haar fractional degree' as p^k equal integral classes summing to 4, against a lattice fixed in advance. The order of quantifiers (L_d before k) is the crux. No precedent found for Hilbert-Smith.

name: Moving a positive multiple of the degree-one test into any open set of the orbit space
why: It works on orbit spaces with no dimension bound (the known theory says dim is n+2 or infinity), avoiding the classical obstacle. It bridges a global degree with local sheet symmetry.

name: Averaged degree-one test
why: It is the only use of small subgroups: an integral degree-one class on the wild orbit space, which is impossible for any finite group.

name: Bounded (2-power) comparison F -> E on spheres; T categories generated by arbitrary continuous images
why: It extends sheaf Witt homology integrally to non-constructible objects, which the action forces on us. Rational equivalence alone would lose the denominator bound.

name: globular set; parallel cells; s_i,t_i; d_j, boundary of d_j
statement: Cells in each dimension with source/target maps satisfying the globular identities; two cells are parallel if their immediate sources and targets agree; d_j is the representable j-globe; boundary of d_0 is empty.

name: globular sum shape / pasting scheme, height, tuple, Theta_0 with designated sums
statement: S = d_{h1} amalg_{d_{b1}} ... d_{hl}, b_a < h_a, h_{a+1}; height = max cell dimension; Theta_0 = shapes with globular maps; designated sums are these amalgamations.

name: Def 2.1 coherator convention (globular theory; Grothendieck coherator in the Ara-Henry convention)
statement: A globular theory is a category under Theta_0 with the same objects preserving designated sums. A Grothendieck coherator has a tower C_0=Theta_0 -> C_1 -> ... with colimit C, stage r+1 freely adjoining fillers d_j -> S of chosen parallel pairs d_{j-1} => S with j>0 and dim(S) <= j; and every such pair has a filler.

name: models A = Mod(C); endomorphism category E_G; free functor F; D_j, boundary D_j, I_j, J_j; sets I, J
statement: Models: presheaves on C taking designated sums to limits = globular sets with interpretations of each freely adjoined operation. E_G(S,T)=Set(G(T),G(S)); interpretations are functors C_r -> E_G under Theta_0. D_j=F(d_j), I_j: boundary D_j -> D_j, J_j: D_j -> D_{j+1} source inclusion.

name: I-cellular extension; cellular; finitely cellular
statement: Transfinite composite of pushouts of coproducts of I_j; cellular = map from initial model is such; finitely cellular includes I_0.

name: units e, e_p^q; compositions *_i; inverses w_i; homotopy ~; pi_0, pi_r(X;u,v), pi_r(X,x)
statement: Chosen operations from contractibility; alpha ~ beta iff one (r+1)-cell joins them; homotopy sets; based groups at iterated units.

name: Lemma 2.2 Division with specified boundaries (normalization operations U_h^k, c_h, d_h, K_gamma)
statement: Left/right multiplication by a fixed r-cell gamma at level i<r induces bijections between homotopy sets at a prescribed boundary and at the induced boundary (empty sets allowed).
cited_or_new: cited, re-proved with explicit boundary correction

name: Lemma 2.3 Change of boundary and vertex
statement: Endomorphism homotopy sets at any (r-1)-cell u biject with pi_r(X,x) for x its source/target vertex; arrows x->y give natural bijections.

name: Prop 2.4 Weak-equivalence test (exact-boundary criterion)
statement: f in W iff bijective on pi_0 and on all pi_r(X;u,v) iff for every boundary b and cell y of Y with boundary fb there is x with boundary exactly b and an (r+1)-cell fx -> y.

name: Lemma 2.5 Closure properties of W (2-out-of-3, retracts, filtered colimits, transfinite composites)
statement: W has 2-out-of-3, retract closure, closure under filtered colimits of arrows.

name: Def 2.6 contractible model (X -> 1 in W; equivalently nonempty with joining cells for all parallel pairs)
statement: X contractible iff X->1 in W iff every parallel pair has a joining cell iff X->1 lifts against all I_j.

name: Lemma 2.7 Lifting tests: W with RLP(J_j) => RLP(I_j); I-inj = W cap J-inj; every model is J-fibrant
statement: Approximate lift plus lifting its homotopy against J_j corrects to a strict lift.

name: Unit retraction D_{j+1} -> D_j of J_j and of its pushouts / transfinite composites
statement: The unit on the source cell retracts J_j; pushouts and transfinite composites inherit compatible retractions.

name: q-coskeletal model; A_q
statement: Every globular boundary of dimension j>q has exactly one filler.

name: Lemma 3.1 Cutoff reflector R_q (built in the free order of C; bijective on cells through q; R_k R_q = R_k)
statement: A_q -> A has a left adjoint R_q whose unit is bijective on cells of dimension <= q; constructed by keeping cells through q, putting a unique cell over each parallel pair above q, and interpreting generators in the original free order (generators of output <= q use the arity bound dim(S)<=j).

name: Lemma 3.2 Higher attachments preserve lower cells
statement: Relative cellular extensions using only I_j (or J_j) with j>k are bijective on cells through dimension k (in A and in A_q).
cited_or_new: new proof of a folklore fact

name: Recursive description [S_1..S_p], v(S), spine T_m(S) and Lemma 3.3 Finite spine
statement: T_0(S)=[v(S_1),...,v(S_p)], T_m(S)=[T_{m-1}(S_1),...]; T_m(S) has height <= m+1, contains all cells of S through dimension m, and T_m(S)->S is a finite composite of pushouts of source inclusions d_j->d_{j+1}, j>m.

name: Prop 3.4 Contractibility of free shapes F(S), F_q(S)
statement: For every nonempty finite globular-sum shape, F(S) and F_q(S) are contractible.

name: assertion E(q,n); 'upper' index; descending induction on n at fixed cutoff q
statement: E(q,n): for every cellular X in A_q and every a: D_n -> X, the pushout of J_n along a is a weak equivalence. Prove by descending induction on n with q fixed; upper J-cellular extensions are in W.

name: Lemma 3.5 Top-dimensional base case E(q,q)
statement: At the cutoff the J_q pushout is a weak equivalence: retraction + bijection below q + unique fillers above q.

name: Lemma 3.6 Upper-cell splitting and pushout
statement: An upper I-cellular weak equivalence i: U -> V with U cellular admits a retraction, and its pushouts along maps to cellular U' are in W.

name: tree diagram at depth n; K^lin (linear string on same vertices)
statement: Finite oriented tree in each depth-n slot (vertices n-cells with common lower boundary, edges (n+1)-cells), nested via strings; K^lin replaces each tree by a forward string.

name: Prop 3.7 Contractibility of tree diagrams via J_{n+1} duplication (generator-homotopy promotion)
statement: Under E(q,j) for j>n, F_q(K) is contractible for each depth-n tree diagram K: compare with the string model L via f,g; get edge homotopies alpha_e: e -> gf(e); adjoin duplicates e' with delta_e: e -> e' (J_{n+1} attachments), maps a_0,a_1: A->Q, common retraction r, h: Q->A with h a_0 = id, h a_1 = gf; 2-out-of-3 makes gf in W; gf factors through contractible L.

name: whiskered shapes H_eps(S) and Prop 3.8 Contractibility after adjoining whiskers
statement: H_eps(S): adjoin to F_q(S), for each n-cell x, a duplicate x' and one (n+1)-cell joining them (orientation eps, or chosen per cell). Contractible: reduce to T_n(S) (a tree diagram) and push along the upper J-cellular map H(T_n S) -> H(S).

name: partial cylinder objects P_j (coglobular), endpoints e_0,e_1, P(S)=colim P_j, domains A_j^eps (one-sided) and A_j^{01} (two-sided)
statement: P_j = D_j for j<n (stationary, both endpoints identity); P_n = D_{n+1} (endpoints source/target n-faces); for n<j<=q, P_j = small-object completion of A_j^{01} against upper I_k. A map P_j -> Y is a j-cylinder: endpoints agree below n, are joined by one (n+1)-cell at n, and are made compatible above.

name: Lemma 4.1 Exact skeletal gluing C_l(S) and its identities C_n(S)=H_eps(S), C_{j-1}(d_j)=A_j^eps, C_dim(S)(S)=P(S)
statement: C_l(S) = F(S) amalg_{F(sk_l S)} P(sk_l S) is built from C_{l-1}(S) by pushing out coproducts of A_l^eps -> P_l.

name: Prop 4.2 Cylinder contractibility (P_j, A_j^eps, P(S) contractible; A_j^eps -> P_j upper cellular weak equivalence)
statement: Induction on j>n: A_j^eps from H_eps(d_j) by pushing out earlier A_l^eps -> P_l; Lemma 3.6 keeps everything in W; P_j inherits low fillers and has upper fillers by construction.

name: Prop 4.3 Partial path functor P: A_q -> A_q with endpoints p_0,p_1; each p_eps lifts all I_j; (p_0,p_1) lifts J_n
statement: (PY)_j = Hom(P_j, Y); interpret each generator theta (in the original free order) by extending the prescribed map A_j^{01} -> P(S) over P_j using contractibility of P(S); individual lifting from retractions of A_j^eps -> P_j; joint lifting via the 4-vertex tree B (y0-x0-x1-y1) and B -> A_{n+1}^{01} -> P_{n+1}.

name: Completion of the descending induction: endpoint-section retract argument (h, u=p_1 h, u-bar = u r, v = i u-bar; iu retract of v)
statement: Section h of p_0 over cellular X; u=p_1h in W; joint lifting gives f: Y -> PY with p_0 f = id, p_1 f = i u r; v in W; iu is a retract of v; 2-out-of-3 gives i in W.

name: Theorem 1.1 (main): elementary expansions of cellular C-groupoids are weak equivalences
statement: For any Grothendieck coherator C, cellular X, n>=0, a: D_n -> X, the pushout i: X -> X^+ of s_n: D_n -> D_{n+1} along a is a weak equivalence.

name: Cor 5.1 canonical cofibrantly generated left semi-model structure on Mod(C)
statement: W, cofibrations I-cof, fibrations J-inj, trivial fibrations I-inj; cofibrant = retracts of cellular; all objects fibrant.
cited_or_new: cited reduction (Henry 2016 Thm 5.3.5), proof spelled out

name: Cor 5.2 Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis: Mod(C) Quillen equivalent to Spaces
statement: |-| : Mod(C) <-> Spaces : Pi_infty is a Quillen equivalence; Mod(C)[W^-1] ~ Ho(Spaces).

name: ExpansionContraction q r: J_{>=r}-cofibrations from cofibrant contractible objects in A_q have contractible targets
statement: forall i: X -> Y in (sourceClass q r).rlp.llp, Cofibrant X, HasFillers X -> HasFillers Y.

name: CutoffPathData q r Y and cylinderPathData
statement: Object P with p_0,p_1: P -> Y each lifting all I_k, jointly lifting J_k for all k>=r. cylinderPathData builds it as the cutoff reflection of the full cylinder model.

name: Index-n partial cylinders bootstrapped by descending induction at a fixed coskeletal cutoff (scheme E1)
statement: Fix a cutoff q (models with unique fillers above q). Prove 'J_n-expansions are weak equivalences' for n = q, q-1, ..., 0. At index n, build coglobular objects P_j: P_j = D_j for j<n (stationary), P_n = D_{n+1} (one joining cell), and for n<j<=q a small-object completion of the two-sided boundary datum against upper I_k. Their contractibility (and that of P(S)) follows from the already-proved higher-index expansions via whiskered shapes and skeletal gluing. Contractibility lets every coherator o…
why: Eureka CANDIDATE only. 2026-10-12 full-text re-check cleared the two named downgrade risks (Lanari 2018, Taylor 2609.20860), so confidence rises 0.35 -> 0.45; it does not rise further because Test 4 is not run, no expert has classified the scheme, and the templated-IH-strengthening reading (falls_to (d)) is untouched by literature checks. Non-analytic in its partial/descending form (test 2) though the path-object strategy is in L; strongly load-bearing (test 3, 65% dominated share). F3: P_j are…

name: Partial cylinder objects P_j as objects (I25 alone, without the bootstrap)
statement: Coglobular diagram P_0..P_q with endpoints e_0,e_1: D_j for j<n, D_{n+1} at n, small-object completion above n.
why: As an object it is a close variant of Lanari's cylinders combined with relative (stationary) homotopies; its value appears only inside C1.

name: Descending induction on the expansion index at a fixed coskeletal cutoff q (I19; Lean ExpansionContraction q r by strong induction on q-r)
statement: E(q,n) for all cellular X in A_q, proved for n = q down to 0; top case by unique fillers.
why: Templated strengthening (add a parameter q; reverse order): capped at N2 per PLAN. Its non-template value is counted in C1.

name: Cylinder contractibility from higher-index cases (I27, Prop 4.2) taken alone
statement: Under E(q,j) for j>n: A_j^eps -> P_j are upper-cellular weak equivalences and P_j, A_j^eps, P(S) are contractible.
why: Graded as part of C1 (the analyst's separate provisional N3 is merged into C1 to avoid double counting). Taken alone, given C2 and C3, it is an application of the IH plus skeletal gluing.

name: Promotion of generator homotopies through already-covered J_{n+1} expansions; tree and whisker contractibility (E2: I23, I24)
statement: Compare a tree model with a string; edge homotopies alpha_e; duplicate top generators via J_{n+1} attachments to get a cylinder-like Q with two inclusions and common retraction; two-out-of-three gives contractibility.
why: Left-homotopy/cylinder trick adapted to the descending induction.

name: Lean invariant ExpansionContraction (I33): contractibility preservation for the saturated J_{>=r} class
statement: J_{>=r}-cofibrations from cofibrant contractible objects have contractible targets; avoids the W calculus.
why: Weakening plus saturation of the IH ('strengthen to all substructures'): templated, capped at N2. Notable as evidence that the paper's W calculus is unnecessary.

name: Cutoff reflector R_q built in the coherator's free order (I15)
statement: Left adjoint A_q -> A, bijective on cells through q, unique fillers above q.
why: Standard coskeletal reflection; new only in checking compatibility with the free order under the arity bound.

name: Partial path functor: interpret every generator on Hom(P_j, -) in free order (I28/I34)
statement: Contractible coglobular object => interpretation of the coherator => path functor with endpoint lifting properties.
why: Application of the known contractible-coglobular-object interpretation once C1 supplies contractibility; the analyst's N2 is lowered because Bourke 2016 (in L) gives the mechanism.

name: Endpoint-section retract argument (I29)
statement: h section of p_0, u = p_1 h, v = i u r in W, iu retract of v, so i in W.
why: Folklore retract argument.

name: Spines T_m(S) (I17)
statement: Height-(m+1) spine of a pasting scheme with a source-inclusion filtration.
why: Elementary tree recursion; Lanari already proves the consequence.

name: E1 = I19 + I25 + I27 (+ I28): cutoff q, descending induction on n, and index-n partial cylinders whose representing objects are contractible by the higher-inde…
why: Henry's conjecture was open since 2016 (Lanari's full path object stalled on interpreting all higher operations; Henry-Lanari and Lanari only reached dimension 3; Taylor 2026 still assumes a generalized form). The fix is non-analytic: neither the cutoff, nor 'partial' cylinders stationary below n, nor the downward order occur in the goal or in L. Once in place, contractibility of P(S) makes the interpretation of every operation automatic, and the theorem follows by a retract argument. In Lean t…

name: E2 = I23/I24: promote edge-wise homotopies alpha_e to a weak equivalence gf via a duplicate object Q built from J_{n+1} attachments (Lean: free_hasFillers_of_t…
why: This is the step that turns 'each generator is homotopic to its image' into a statement about all freely generated coherences, which is precisely the difficulty of the conjecture; it uses only already-covered indices.

name: E3 = I33 (Lean only): ExpansionContraction - induct on contractibility preservation of the saturated class of J_{>=r}-cofibrations
why: Shows the paper's IH is stronger than needed; removes the whole W calculus (division lemma, 2-out-of-3) from the proof of Thm 1.1; a cleaner invariant for downstream reuse.

name: E4 = I15 cutoff reflector R_q interpreted in the original free order (needs generator arity height <= output dimension)
why: Makes the top case trivial and keeps all low cells; shows exactly where the Ara-Henry admissibility convention is used.

name: E5 = I17 spine T_m(S) and its source-inclusion filtration
why: Gives a uniform reduction of shape questions to height m+1 arities used twice (free shapes, whiskers).

name: Unit sphere S_X with inherited metric; surjective sphere isometry
statement: S_X={x: ||x||=1} with the distance of X; f:S_X->S_Y a surjective isometry.

name: Radial (natural positive-homogeneous) extension T
Mazur-Ulam property
statement: Every surjective sphere isometry from the given space onto the sphere of an arbitrary real Banach space extends linearly.

name: Support at a vector
statement: A linear functional φ with ||φ||<=1 and φ(a)=||a|| (on a finite-dimensional span).

name: Supports exist, extend; common support for norm-additive pairs (lem:support)
statement: Finite-dim Hahn-Banach with norm bound; if ||αv+βw||=α+β (α,β>0, v,w unit) then v,w have a common support.

name: Radial contact from an interior point (lem:radial)
statement: If ||c||<1 each ray c+R_+v meets S_X at a unique c+ρ(v)v; ρ continuous, 1-||c||<=ρ<=1+||c||.

name: Cross-radius defect D_q(x,y)=||f(x)-q f(y)||-||x-qy||, M=sup|D_q|
